  answer is current (values kept, rules unchanged); a `qr` with no text draws nothing.
  <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/settings-form/#status-hide>
- `qrScan` → `kino.qr.scan({ title })` only from an `action` or `panelAction`; `unavailable` on a TV; handle `null`,
  `timeout`, `permission_denied`, `busy`. A `qr` setting (no capability) shows a code from `settingsStatus()`, refreshed
  every `refreshMs`. <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/qr/>
- `imageSource` → `poster`/`backdrop`/`still`/hero `image` may be `{ source: "plugin", handle }` only when no public URL
  exists; export `image({ handle })` answering `{ bytes: <base64>, mime }` (JPEG, PNG or WebP, ≤ 256 KB); try it with
  `node sdk/run.mjs --out poster.jpg . image <handle>`. Never put a secret in a handle: it is saved and synced like a
  poster URL. <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/images/>

**Configuration aids and action answers (Kino 0.9.74)**: a `"type": "link"` setting (`label`, `url`
`https://` only, no user info, ≤ 2,048; a button that opens it through the system only on the person's tap;
on a TV, the address and a QR; Kino makes no request to it) and a `"type": "help"` setting (optional
`label`, `title` ≤ 60, `body` ≤ 2,000 plain text, `titleEn`/`bodyEn`; a modal titled with the plugin's
name), at most 4 of each, no value, apiVersion 12. Keep a help short: what the plugin needs and where to get
it; link to a full guide. An `action` may answer `setSettings: { key: "value" }` (≤ 8 of the plugin's own
`text`/`select` settings, and from apiVersion 13 a `password` (sealed, never logged, scrubbed from the answer), never
`url`, `toggle`, `list`; saved and synced like typed values,
without `validateSettings`; any bad entry refuses the whole field) and `link: { candidate, confirm }` (Kino
asks "¿Eres tú, <candidate>?" in its own words; `candidate` 1 to 64 plain characters; `confirm` is
**another** `action` key without its own `confirm` question; only "Sí, soy yo" runs it, once). Both are
ignored by older Kino: also say in `message` what to do. Mark that confirm action `"linkOnly": true`
(apiVersion 12) so it is never drawn and the person sees one button. Any settings item may carry
`"devices": ["phone"]` or `["tv"]` (apiVersion 12): it is drawn only there, but its value is still stored,
synced, provisioned and read through `kino.config`; a sync provider draws its setup on the phone only,
because the TV receives it with "Recibir configuración". Kino itself puts a "Sincronización ▸
Proveedor" button at the top of every provider's page and a per-device "Sincronizar cada" on its card
(`pullEveryMs` is only the default).
[The settings form](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/settings-form/#aids).

**Feature-detect what older Kino lacks**: `kino.meta` and `kino.tmdb` (Kino 0.9.53, no new apiVersion)
only behind `typeof kino.meta === "function"` / `typeof kino.tmdb === "function"`; the hidden
browser's `captureAll`, `alsoMatch`, `waitForCookie` and `returnCookiesOnTimeout` options (Kino 0.9.54) only when
`kino.browser.captureAll === true`. TMDB goes through `kino.tmdb`: never put a TMDB key in the code.

<a id="errors"></a>
**Errors**: `throw kino.error(code, detail)` with one of these codes; the person reads Kino's Spanish
sentence, your detail (cut at 200 characters) goes to the log.

| Code | The person sees |
| --- | --- |
| `auth_required` | "Configura {plugin} en Ajustes ▸ Plugins" (from Kino 0.9.50 "… Ajustes ▸ {plugin}" when it has settings: its own tab), with a button to Configurar |
| `not_found` | "No se encontró en {plugin}" |
| `geo_blocked` | "Este contenido no está disponible en tu región" |
| `rate_limited` | "{plugin} está limitando las peticiones; intenta en unos minutos" |
| `unavailable` | "{plugin} no está disponible ahora" |

**`userMessage` (apiVersion 6)**: `throw kino.error("not_found", "E100006", { userMessage: "Este capítulo
ya no está disponible." })` shows "Mensaje de <plugin name>: <sentence>" **instead of** Kino's line,
only for the five codes above and only if the sentence passes every safety rule; otherwise Kino's line
shows and the sentence is dropped silently. The rules, in short: 1 to 160 characters of Spanish/Latin-1
letters, digits and plain punctuation (no emoji, `@`, other scripts or invisible characters); at least
two words; no URL, domain, `www` or "punto com"; fewer than 6 digits in all, no digit glued to a
letter; never spells "Kino"; never asks for money, credentials, codes or contact (`pag…`, `recarg…`,
`transfer…`, `contraseñ…`, `clave…`, `token…`, `tarjeta`, `PIN`, Nequi, Daviplata, WhatsApp, Telegram,
SMS/verification codes); never contains a password the person typed or a sealed value. The plugin
name itself must be plain (no `:`, no digit glued to a letter). **A plugin that uses `userMessage` to
ask for money, credentials or contact outside Kino breaks the rules for plugins.** Each author is responsible
for their own plugin; Kino only lists community plugins (no recommendation or promotion), and removes one
that breaks the rules (asking for money, passwords or contact data, malware, rights claims) from the
community index through [`community-blocklist.json`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugins/blob/main/community-blocklist.json); anyone can report it with the
["Reclamo / retiro de plugin"](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugins/issues/new?template=reclamo-retiro-plugin.yml) issue template. An installed copy stays installed, shows
"Retirado del índice de la comunidad." and gets no more updates; a fork needs its own report. Build it where you
throw, write it in Spanish, and never echo what the person typed. Full rules:
[Your own sentence](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/contract/#user-message).

`kino.fetch` does not throw on non-2xx (check `r.ok`); it throws with `e.code` one of
`host_not_allowed`, `timeout`, `network`, `too_large`, `invalid_request`. `kino.crypto` errors carry
`code: "crypto_error"`.

**The unhandled-rejection trap**: in Kino 0.9.49 and older a `throw` inside an `async` function
**before its first `await`** aborts the whole call even if the caller wraps it in `try`/`catch` (also
`return Promise.reject(e)` and a `new Promise` rejected at once). Kino 0.9.50 catches it like Node; only a
rejection nobody ever handles still fails the call. The Node kit does not show the old behaviour.
Since people update late, keep `await`ing first (a fetch, or `await null;`) and validate after.

**Language**: everything the person sees (the manifest's `name` and `description`, settings `label`
and `hint`, Home row titles, error details, badges) is **Spanish from Bogotá, with tuteo** ("Configura",
"Escribe tu usuario"), **never voseo** ("Configurá", "Escribí" are wrong). From Kino 0.9.54 the app may
speak English, and `kino.lang` is then `"en-US"` (before, always `"es-CO"`): texts your code builds
at run time (row titles, a `userMessage`) follow `kino.lang`'s language. Code, identifiers and
comments may be English.

**Secrets**: never hardcode a password, token, API key or cookie in `plugin.js` or the repository;
ask for it in a `settings` entry of type `password`, keep derived tokens in `kino.storage` keyed by
user and server, and never log a setting. A `url` setting cannot have a `default` (use `hint`).
A fixed key that belongs to the plugin's author (not the person) can be **sealed** instead:
`node sdk/seal.mjs --repo owner/repo --name apiKey` prints `kino-sealed:v1:…` for the manifest's
`"secrets"` (apiVersion 4); the code uses `kino.secret("apiKey")` (fine at module top level too),
a marker Kino swaps for the
value only inside `kino.fetch`, toward the manifest's `hosts` over https, and redacts from everything
the code reads back. It is obfuscation, not secrecy; seals only open when the plugin is installed
from its default branch (no `@ref`); the Node kit reads plain values from `.kino-secrets.json`
(never commit it). Full rules: [Sealed secrets](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/manifest/#secrets).

**Downloads are declarative.** `"download"` in `capabilities` (apiVersion 2) is a flag the app acts
on: export nothing extra, there is no separate "resolve for download" call (Kino calls your
`resolve(ref)` when the queued download actually runs). Progressive files and non-live HLS save;
DASH, live, SAMPLE-AES and DRM never do. Phones only.

**Signing (apiVersion 5, Kino 0.9.45+, optional).** The author signs `plugin.js` with their own
Ed25519 key; the manifest carries `"signature": { "authorKey": <64 hex>, "value": <128 hex> }`;
Kino checks it at install and at every update (never at runtime), pins the key at the first install
(trust on first use) and refuses an update signed with another key or no longer signed. People see
"Firmado por su autor" and a "Firmado" badge. It does not hide the code. Full page:
[Signed plugins](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/signed/). When the person wants it:

1. Explain it in plain Spanish first. Then `node sdk/seal.mjs --keygen` **once** (writes
   `kino-author-key.pem`; refuses to overwrite). Add `*.pem` to `.gitignore` **before any commit**
   (the scaffold's `.gitignore` does not have it). Tell them to back the key up and never share it:
   there is no recovery, and a new key makes every existing install refuse the update (they must
   uninstall and reinstall). **Never put the key in the repository, the chat or a log.**
2. Set `"apiVersion": 5`, then `node sdk/seal.mjs --sign --repo owner/repo[/folder]` **after the last
   change** to `plugin.js` or `version`, and **again after every later change** (the signature covers
   the exact entry file, repo, `id` and `version`).
3. `node sdk/validate.mjs . --repo owner/repo` verifies it and fails if a `.pem` is tracked.
4. If it says "La firma del autor no es válida…", the code, `id`, `version` or repo changed after
   signing: sign again. If a person reports "firmada con otra clave de autor", the key changed.

**apiVersion 6 (Kino 0.9.50+): every widening, when to use it, its limits.** Declare `"apiVersion": 6`
only when you use one of these.

- **Typed / larger sealed secrets.** Values up to 8,192 bytes; a key for `kino.crypto` can be sealed as
  `{ "seal": "kino-sealed:v1:…", "use": "cipher-key", "encoding": "hex"|"base64" }`
  (`seal.mjs --use cipher-key --encoding hex`), 16/24/32 bytes, usable as the whole key of any cipher
  (DES-EDE3 too) and **nothing else**: never HMAC/PBKDF2 input, never in `kino.fetch`. Use it when a
  site's own player ships a fixed cipher key.
- **`migrate`** (capability + export, needs approval): Kino asks it about saved library titles,
  chapters and live favorites it can no longer open; answer what `search()` would return today, or
  `null`. 10 s each; avoid fetching; never return a `plg1:` ref. Use it only when the plugin replaces
  an older source or changes its ref format.
- **Request-signed streams** (`signing: "request"` + export `sign`): only for an HLS origin that wants a
  fresh signature on every playlist/segment request. `sign()` runs in a separate **signing lane**: only
  `kino.crypto`, `kino.secret`, `kino.config`, `kino.html`, `kino.log`; no network, no storage, no
  cookies, no sleep, no memory shared with the main runtime; 1.5 s per call; three failures stop the
  video. Everything it needs travels in `signContext` (a string ≤ 4,096 chars, never a `kino.secret`
  marker: call `kino.secret()` inside `sign`). No `drm`, no `audioTracks`, not downloadable, not for an
  inline channel stream. `resolve(ref, { retry: { reason: "conflict"|"expired", attempt, status } })`
  is called again on 409 or repeated 401/403 (3 tries). `alternateHosts` (≤ 6, same host rules as `url`)
  are other hosts serving the same stream. Casting works through the phone, which must stay on the
  same Wi-Fi. [Signing every request](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/signed-streams/).
- **Settings form**: `section` (heading), `status` (needs export `settingsStatus()` → `{ key: text }`,
  10 s) and `action` (needs export `action(key)` → `{ message?, refresh?, clearSettings? }`, 30 s,
  optional `confirm`) hold no value; at most 16 on top of the 12 valued settings. `clearSettings`
  empties up to 12 of the plugin's own optional valued settings (never `required` ones); use it for
  "Cerrar sesión". Optional `validateSettings(values)` (20 s) returns `null` to accept, a text, or
  `{ key: "message" }` to refuse. Every plugin with settings gets its own Ajustes tab; settings sync
  between paired devices and arrive **without** `validateSettings`, so key any `kino.storage` session
  by account and never store a device identity in a setting. A `toggle` without `default` reads
  `false`, a `select` without one its first option, a `list` an array of `{ [field key]: string }`;
  `confirm` only on `action`, `fields`/`max` only on `list`, `options` only on `select`. There are no
  conditional fields: group with a `section` and check combinations in `validateSettings`. Every type
  and attribute: [The settings form](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/settings-form/#types).
- **`debug: true`**: on-screen error panels and a "Registro" page (last 200 events); logcat tag
  `KinoPlugin/<id>` (and `KinoPlay` for playback metrics). Development only: **remove before
  publishing** (`validate.mjs` warns).
- **`telemetry: true | "verbose"`**: asks the person (consent line, and an update that adds it waits
  for approval) to share the failed call's scrubbed `kino.log` lines with Kino's error tracker; only
  plugins that declare it ever send lines (recommended or not). From Kino 0.9.54 each such plugin's
  Ajustes tab has an "Enviar registros de errores y de reproducción" switch, on by default and synced
  across the person's devices; older Kino always sends. `"verbose"` adds playback metrics of a sample of good plays and
  edge cases (60 events per run). `kino.log.report("myplugin:area", "code", "count=2")` flags a
  degraded-but-working result (area: lowercase namespaced word with `_` or `:`, ≤ 24 chars; 1/hour per
  area, 3 per run). Log codes and counts, never values from a response, never what the person typed.
  [Logs and telemetry](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/diagnostics/).
- **`section`** (`"section": { "label": "…" }` ≤ 20 chars + export `section({ tab })` →
  `{ tabs?, tab, hero?, rows }`, 20 s): a section of its own (TV sidebar, max 3 plugins; phone chip strip,
  max 8). **`categories()`** (needs `browse`, 20 s): up to 24 tiles in Categorías, each opening
  `browse(ref, null)`. **`theme`**: up to five `#RRGGBB` colors (`accent`, `onAccent`, `background`,
  `surface`, `highlight`); dark backgrounds only, contrast 3:1 / 4.5:1, nothing close to Kino's red
  `#E50914`; a failing color falls back to Kino's (accent+onAccent as a pair); errors are always Kino's
  red. Preview with `node sdk/run.mjs . theme`.
- **`scopedSearch`** (capability, needs `search`): your `search` gets `query.within` (the browse `ref`
  of a "Ver más" page) and answers inside that category; `null` means "let Kino filter". Kino gives up
  on you after 6 s. Without it Kino filters the loaded titles itself.
- **`adult: true`** on items, Categorías tiles, live categories and channels: kept and shown only while
  the person's 18+ code is unlocked (Ajustes ▸ Adultos). Below apiVersion 6 they are dropped. With an
  18+ live category, mark **every** `liveSearch` hit with `adult` or its `categoryId` (unmarked hits
  count as 18+). Never try to detect or bypass the lock: always send the mark.
- **Live channels in Home rows**: `kind: "live"` items now stay in `home` rows (a country's channels,
  for example); below 6 they are dropped from Home.
- **`kino.crypto` key pairs**: `generateKeyPair` (`ec` P-256/P-384, `ed25519`, `x25519`), `sign`,
  `verify`, `importKey`, `deriveSharedSecret`; private keys are handles that live only in the sandbox
  that made them (not in `sign()`'s lane), at most 64. For a player that proves itself by signing a
  challenge. Map Node/WebCrypto calls with the table in
  [The kino API](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/kino-api/#key-pairs).
- **`Stream.label` and labelled lazy copies**: `label` (≤ 48 chars, e.g. `"Latino · Servidor 1"`) names
  a copy in the player's **Servidor** menu; an alternative may be `{ label, ref }` (ref ≤ 512 chars) that
  Kino passes to `resolve(ref)` only when needed: the person picks it (whole `resolve` limit; if it fails
  they keep watching the copy they had), the automatic fallback reaches it (≤ 20 s, then the next copy),
  or a download's copy choice probes it (inside its 30 s budget). From that answer only `url`,
  `headers`, `mime`, `subtitles`, `expiresInSeconds` and `skip` are used; its own `alternatives` are
  ignored. Use it for **every** source with several servers or languages: never resolve all of them up
  front. [Labelled and lazy copies](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/contract/#lazy-copies).
- **`"browser": true`** (`kino.browser.capture`) or **`"browser": "pages"`** (capture plus `kino.browser.page`): see "The hidden browser"
  below.
- **`meta`** (capability + export `meta(query)`, no consent line, 6 s): fill a title's info page when
  TMDB/AniList have nothing (e.g. `kitsu:` anime); return `null` for titles you do not know.
- **Kino 0.9.53, no new apiVersion, always behind `typeof kino.<name> === "function"`**: `kino.meta(query)` asks Kino
  what it knows about a title (its own TMDB lookup, AniList, the person's other `meta` plugins; 30/min; `null` when
  unknown). `kino.tmdb(path, params)` is read-only TMDB v3 with **no key in your code**: Kino's own key first (behind its
  cache and limits: 20/10 s per plugin, 60/10 s for all), the person's key (Ajustes, or a Stremio addon's key they agreed
  to share) only when Kino's fails: never put a TMDB key in the code, and for a TMDB-based catalog prefer it
  over a `tmdbKey` setting (keep the setting only as the fallback for older Kino). Catch `no_tmdb_key` where an empty
  answer is better than an error (Home rows); uncaught, the person reads Kino's own sentence telling them where to add
  the key. [The `kino` API](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/kino-api/#tmdb).
- **Kino 0.9.54, no new apiVersion**: `kino.browser.capture` takes `captureAll`, `alsoMatch`,
  `waitForCookie` and `returnCookiesOnTimeout`, only behind `if (kino.browser.captureAll)` (older Kino ignores them).
  `kino.lang` follows the app's language (`"es-CO"` or `"en-US"`; before 0.9.54 always `"es-CO"`): word your
  `userMessage` and send `Accept-Language` from it. Kino's own error messages become English and may change: match on
  `e.code`, never on the text. [What's new](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/changelog/#v0954).
- **Any apiVersion**: `Stream.alternatives` (≤ 8 `{ url, mime?, headers? }`, other copies of the same
  video **in the same language** (never a dub next to the original: offer another language as another stream), best
  first; name the resolution in a `label` ("720p", "4K") so Kino 0.9.54 can move to a lighter copy after stalls; Kino switches when one cannot decode or is gone; ignored with `drm`, `signing` and
  for live). `Stream.skip` (`{ openingStartMs?, openingEndMs?, endingStartMs? }` for this exact file:
  "Saltar intro"/"Saltar outro"; wins over AniSkip, a hand correction wins over it). The `subtitles`
  export (10 s, background): tracks for any title Kino knows by IMDb/TMDB id, alongside your videos or
  as a pure subtitle provider (`"capabilities": ["subtitles"]` alone). The manifest's `categories`
  field (`movies`, `series`, `anime`, `live`, `radio`, `subtitles`, `utilities`, `adult`) only tags the
  plugin in the marketplace; it is not the `categories()` export. `settingsStatus()` is asked again after
  every `action` (no need for `refresh: true`).

**The hidden browser (`"browser": true` or `"pages"`, apiVersion 6, Kino 0.9.50+).** Rules, in order:

1. **Prefer `kino.fetch`.** Use the browser only for a server whose embed builds the video address by
   running its own scripts, after you checked the HTML, JSON and scripts with `curl`. It costs the
   person a red consent line ("Puede abrir páginas web ocultas para encontrar el video"), 5-25 s per page,
   and it never runs in the Node kit (`browser_unavailable` there): keep a `kino.fetch` path wherever one
   exists.
2. **`kino.browser.capture(url, { timeoutMs, headers, match, autoplay })` only inside `resolve`**, and
   only a `resolve` the person started (play or a download); anywhere else `not_allowed`. The start
   `url` must be on your `hosts`, https, public. It returns `{ media: [{ url, mime?, headers }],
   subtitles, finalUrl }`: return `media[0].url` with **its `headers`** (Referer, User-Agent, cookies…)
   as the Stream's `headers`. Add `"streamHosts": "any"` because the video lives on hosts you cannot list.
   An approved plugin's `resolve` gets 75 s: plan for two or three servers, not all of them.
3. **`kino.browser.page(url, { waitFor, timeoutMs })`**, only with `"browser": "pages"` (its own red line,
   "Puede abrir páginas web ocultas para mostrar contenido y encontrar el video"; `true` is capture-only and
   gets `not_allowed`; an update from `true` to `"pages"` asks the person again), returns `{ html, finalUrl, status, truncated }` for
   a site whose plain fetch only gets its automatic check page ("Just a moment…"): only from `search`,
   `home`, `browse`, `episodes`, `section` or `resolve` while the person is using the app (never
   background calls; **never from `categories`**, which is always Kino's own call), 20 reads a minute,
   Kino never touches the page. The top document must stay on your hosts: every redirect or navigation
   hop is checked, and the first one off your hosts ends the read with `blocked` (no HTML). Kino cuts
   `timeoutMs` to the call's remaining time minus 1.5 s; still pass ~12000 in `search`. Try `kino.fetch`
   first and cache with `kino.storage`.
4. **Never try to defeat a captcha or bot protection.** Kino never solves, clicks or ticks a CAPTCHA,
   Turnstile, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA or "verify you are human": the call ends with `blocked`. Do not add
   solver services, fingerprint spoofing, stealth tricks, or retry loops; on `blocked`, `timeout` or
   `busy` move to the next server or return nothing. The author is responsible for their own plugin;
   Kino only lists community plugins (community search), it does not recommend or promote them (see
   "Community takedowns" for what happens to a plugin that breaks the rules).
5. **One page at a time in the whole app** (`busy`); a device without WebView gets
   `browser_unavailable`. Each page starts with no cookies and is wiped after; it never reaches the
   home network.
6. **Combine it with labelled lazy copies**: capture the first server in `resolve`, list the other
   servers/languages as `{ label, ref }`, and capture each only when its `ref` comes back. (Maratón,
   a signed community plugin, works this way; "Tu servidor" stays the complete
   reference for everything else.) Full page:
   [Hidden browser](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/browser/).

<a id="api15"></a>
**apiVersion 15 (Kino 0.9.77; every older Kino refuses it and none of these is offered
through `enhancements`)**. Each has its own page, read it whole before using it:

- `pluginStore` → a **store**: the plugin is a source of plugins for Kino's store. Kino keeps one local index of every
  store's entries, paints the store from it (cards, search, categories, sort, pagination, a "de <store>" badge and a store
  filter), applies its own blocklist and the 18+ code, and installs through its own consent sheet: **a store only hands over
  addresses and never installs anything**. Authors answer for the plugins they list; Kino only lists them. The store view
  has three tabs: "De Kino" (EN "From Kino"), Kino Plugins' default list; "De la comunidad" (EN "Community"), everything
  else from every store **without Kino's list**, with the "Populares"/"Recientes" sort, the store filter and the live
  stores; and "Instalados" (EN "Installed"). A reload icon syncs every store and ends with a toast, "Se actualizaron N
  plugins" or "Tus plugins están al día". Manifest:
  `"capabilities": ["pluginStore"]` (may stand alone: no `resolve`, no `search`) and an optional
  `"pluginStore": { "mode": "local" | "live", "name": 1..60 chars }` (the block without the capability is refused).
  - `storeSync({ reason: "schedule" | "reload", since?, state? })` → `{ full, entries, removed?, state? }`: `full: true`
    is the whole list (Kino replaces the store's rows), `full: false` is upserts plus `removed` addresses (an empty change
    means nothing changed); `state` (<= 16 KB of JSON) comes back on the next call. It runs only in the background (every
    2 h by default, Wi-Fi only) and on reload: at most 60 s, 40 `kino.fetch` requests and 8 MB downloaded. At most 5,000
    entries and 4 MB of JSON per answer. **`since` (and `state`) may be absent at any time, not only the first time:** when
    Kino loses a store's rows (a restore, a rebuilt database) it syncs that store from scratch, with no `since` and no
    `state`, and the store must then answer its whole list (`full: true`). Never rely on a stored cursor.
  - A **live** store (`"mode": "live"`) must export all three: `storeSync` (a base list), `storeList({ category?, sort:
    "popular" | "recent", cursor? })` and `storeSearch({ q, category?, cursor? })`, each answering `{ entries, next? }`, at
    most 5 s per call and 20 calls a minute per store, cached 30 minutes. Kino paints local entries first and appends live
    ones at the end as they arrive (nothing on screen moves, repeats of an address are skipped); a live store picked in the
    filter shows only its live answers. The person reads an extra red line (what they search reaches its servers).
  - `StoreEntry`: `address` (`owner/repo`, `owner/repo/path`, `owner/repo@ref` or `url:https://.../kino-plugin.json`; required
    unless `stremio`), `id` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$`), `name` (1..60), `description` (<= 300), `longDescription`
    (<= 4000), `categories` (`movies`, `series`, `anime`, `live`, `radio`, `subtitles`, `utilities`, `adult`), `tags`,
    `icon` and `screenshots` (https), `version`, `author`, `popularity` (number), `updatedAt` (ms), `stremio`, `requires`,
    `needsSetup`, and the hints `signed`/`authorKey` (Kino re-checks at install). `recommended` is honoured only from
    Kino's own store (Kino Plugins). Invalid entries are dropped, long texts cut.
  - **One plugin per `id` across all stores.** If two repositories claim an id, the one in Kino Plugins' list wins; if none is
    there, one is kept deterministically and the rest are dropped. No store may list the id `kino-plugins` (Kino's own store).
    "De la comunidad" leaves out what "De Kino" shows. Leaving a store never uninstalls anything. 18+ entries stay hidden
    while the person's 18+ code is locked.
  - Consent lines: a store shows «Agrega plugins de sus servidores a tu tienda» and, if live, also in red «Lo que busques en la
    tienda llegará a sus servidores». The owner's blocklist is applied by Kino to every entry and refreshed with every store
    sync; Kino Plugins' daily index already leaves blocked repositories out. Kino Plugins ships inside Kino (version 1.0.2),
    signed with Kino's author key.
  - Kit: `node sdk/init.mjs my-store --host store.example.org --store local|live` scaffolds one;
    `node sdk/run.mjs . storeSync [--since <ms>] [--state '<json>']`, `storeList [popular|recent] [category]` and
    `storeSearch "<q>" [category]` print the answer as Kino's index keeps it and report what it drops. Copyable examples
    with offline tests: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/store-examples/> (a local store over a static JSON file, a live
    store over its own API). <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/plugin-stores/>
- `identity` → declarative, never alone: `await kino.identity.telegram({ challenge? })` answers `{ id, token }` (`id` a
  per-plugin pseudonym of the person, `token` Kino's bot's signed token: a credential, **never log or show it**); with a
  `challenge` (16..128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, a nonce from the plugin's server) also `deviceKey`, `signature`, `author` and
  `codeHash`, so the server can bind a session to this device and require its own author fingerprint. **Only plugins
  signed with Kino's own author key get an answer**; any other gets `permission_denied`, so a community plugin must not
  depend on it. Only inside a call the person started (`screen`, `screenEvent`, `panelAction`), 10 a minute. Red consent line
  ("Podrá saber tu usuario de Telegram y enviarlo a sus servicios"), switchable in Ajustes. Kit: `KINO_IDENTITY_TG`,
  `KINO_IDENTITY_TOKEN`, `KINO_IDENTITY_AUTHOR`, `KINO_IDENTITY_REVOKED=1`. <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/identity/>
- `notifications` → declarative, never alone: `await kino.notifications.post({ id, title, titleEn?, text?, textEn?, go? })`
  and `clear(id?)` leave short notices in the Home bell. `id` is 1..64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -` and replaces an earlier notice
  with the same id (group news under one id); `title` 1..80, `text` <= 160, plain one-line text; `go` is `{ screen: {
  route?, args? } }` (the plugin's own screen). From `screen`, `screenEvent` or the plugin's `job`; 20 posts an hour, 30
  kept, 30 days. Not synced between devices. Plain consent line ("Podrá mostrarte avisos en la campanita"), switchable in
  Ajustes. Kit: `node sdk/run.mjs . notifications` (it keeps `.kino-notices.json`), `KINO_NOTIFICATIONS_REVOKED=1`.
  <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/notifications/>
- `kino.library.watched()` also carries `season` and `episode` (the latest chapter played) on a watched series, never on a
  movie.

**apiVersion 16 (Kino 0.9.78) and the Kino 0.9.78 sync switch.** `coins` is not offered through `enhancements`:

- `coins` → declarative, never alone, red consent line («Podrá ver tu saldo de kinos y regalar tus kinos»), no switch of its
  own (the person revokes it by disabling or removing the plugin). `await kino.coins.balance()` → `{ balance, earnedToday,
  capToday }`; `await kino.coins.give({ to, postId })` gives ONE coin to the coins account `to` (1..128 characters, which your
  own server hands you) for the post `postId` (1..64) → `{ balance, postTotal }`. Kinos are Kino's free coin: 1 every 10
  minutes watched, at most 20 a UTC day. `give` only from `screen`, `screenEvent` or `panelAction` after the person's action;
  `balance` also from a timer tick and a job. 30 calls a minute. Errors: `permission_denied`, `not_available` (service down or
  this device never validated: keep working without coins), `rate_limited`, `bad_request`, `disabled` (the person switched
  Kinos off: show nothing about kinos at all), and `no_balance`, `self_gift`, `unknown_account`. Feature-detect
  `typeof kino.coins === "object"`. Your plugin never learns the service's address or session.
  <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/kino-api/#coins>
- `kino.sync.active()` and `kino.sync.setActive(on)` (Kino 0.9.78, no apiVersion, `syncProvider` only): read or change whether
  this plugin is the device's sync provider; `true` asks the person in Kino's own dialog (a decline answers `false`), `false`
  asks nothing. Changes only from a tap (`action`, `panelAction`, `screenEvent`), never a job; up to 120 s; errors `busy`,
  `timeout`, `unavailable`, `invalid_request`, `not_allowed`. Feature-detect `typeof kino.sync.setActive === "function"`.

**apiVersion 17 (Kino 0.9.81).**

- `kino.library.stats({ month? })` (with `library`; only a plugin declaring 17 has the function, and an update that raises a
  `library` plugin to 17 asks the person again): one month's aggregates of the active profile, every device summed:
  `{ month, estimated, seconds, secondsByKind: { movie, series, live }, secondsByBand: { morning, afternoon, night, lateNight }
  | null, titles, episodes, activeDays, longestStreakDays, top: [{ title, year?, kind, ids, poster?, genres?, seconds }] }`.
  `month` `yyyy-mm` (the current one by default); `top` ≤ 20; never 18+; live channels counted, never named; nothing finer
  than the month. Shares the 30 calls a minute of `watched`/`saved`. Feature-detect `typeof kino.library.stats === "function"`.
- Jobs: `perProfile: true` (with `runOn: "any"`, never with `enabledBy`) runs `job(ctx)` once per profile of the device that has
  your plugin on, each its own run with that profile's storage, library, shared values and config (ctx gives no profile id);
  `kino.notifications`, `kino.coins`, `kino.seed` and `kino.progress` answer `not_allowed` there. Its consent is Kino's own job row (off by
  default, each profile may leave itself out), with a longer red line. `kino.tmdb` is allowed in any job (each call one of
  the run's requests). A plugin with `ai` approved gets 60 s and 20 requests per run.
- Screens: `kino.jobOn("<jobId>")` (only in `screen`/`screenEvent`) says whether a job's row is on, and the answer
  `enableJob: "<jobId>"` turns it on after the person's tap (never off; a row the person switched off stays off). The `pages`
  widget, the `hero` text style, the `share` answer and `go.search` with `"scope": "all"` (see "The screen UI in one place"). A
  lower apiVersion gets each of these dropped, logged.

<a id="api18"></a>
**apiVersion 18: app themes (Kino 0.9.81; not offered
through `enhancements`).** A plugin may restyle the **whole app** on the phone and the TV, as data in the manifest: no code,
no network, no capability, no consent line (turning a theme on is the person's consent). Full page:
<https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/themes/>.

- **The plugin.** `"appThemes": [ … ]` (1..8 themes). A plugin whose only content is themes may leave `capabilities` out (or
  declare only `screen` for a presentation page), may have `"hosts": []` (its card says it does not connect), should declare
  `"categories": ["themes"]` (Kino's store lists it under Temas; `themes` is the ninth marketplace value) and ships an entry
  file that does nothing (`export {};`). It plays nothing, so it does not get the person past Kino's first source picker. Any
  other plugin may carry `appThemes` too. Below apiVersion 18 the field is ignored.
- **A theme** is `{ id, name, colors?, background?, shape?, typography?, elevation?, motion?, player?, tv?, phone?,
  adjustable?, pluginColors?, price?, experience?, logo? }`. `id` `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$`, unique, never changed after
  release; `name` `{ es, en }` (one missing takes the other) or one string, ≤ 40 characters. Every token is optional: what is
  missing stays Kino's. A format error (an unknown field or token, a wrong type, a bad or repeated id, more than 8 themes,
  `background.image`) **refuses the manifest**; a value out of range **only drops that token**, with a warning.
- **Tokens (45)** and ranges (`contract.json` `manifest.appThemes`):
  `colors.` `accent` (Kino's `#E50914`), `onAccent` (`#FFFFFF`), `background` (`#0E0E0E`), `surface` (`#181818`),
  `surfaceHigh` (`#242424`), `textPrimary` (`#F5F5F5`), `textSecondary` (`#B3B3B3`), `focus` (`#FFFFFF`), `onFocus`
  (`#000000`), `outline`, `railPanel`, `placeholderTop`, `placeholderBottom`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `favorite`,
  `scrim` and (Kino 0.9.82) `border`, all `#RRGGBB`; `shape.` `cardRadius`, `channelRadius`, `buttonRadius`, `chipRadius`, `dialogRadius`, `inputRadius`
  0..32; (Kino 0.9.82) `dialogBorder`, `menuBorder`, `headerBorder`, `cardBorder`, `panelBorder` 0..4 dp, drawn in `colors.border`
  (`outline` when absent; Kino has no borders by default: dialogs and sheets, menus, headers' lower edge, cards, panels); `typography.` `scale`, `titleScale`, `bodyScale` 0.85..1.3; `elevation.` `cardShadow` 0..1, `heroScrim` 0.3..1,
  `dialogShadow` 0..1; `motion.` `focusZoom` 1..1.15, `crossfadeMs` 0..800, `heroDrift` `"on"`/`"off"`; `player.` `buttonScale`
  0.8..1.4, `playButtonScale` 0.8..1.6, `seekBarScale` 0.8..2, `labelScale` 0.85..1.3, `buttonShape`
  `"circle"`/`"rounded"`/`"square"`. `background` is `{ type: "solid", colors: [one] }` or `{ type: "gradient", colors: [2..8],
  angle }` (whole degrees, default 180); an image arrives in a later Kino. `tv` and `phone` take the same groups and
  `background` and override the theme on that form.
- **Resolution, low to high**: Kino's value < the theme < its `tv`/`phone` block < the person's adjustments (only tokens in
  `adjustable`, clamped to it and to the ranges) < **the device** (reduced effects make `motion` do nothing; the person's
  "Esquinas redondeadas" switch decides whether TV cards are rounded at all). A player button may look smaller on the phone but
  its touch target stays ≥ 48 dp; the TV focus treatment stays, only recoloured.
- **Legibility guardrails** (the apiVersion 6 `theme` numbers, on the effective colours): the background (every gradient stop)
  must be dark, relative luminance ≤ 0.05 (light themes come later); `accent` ≥ 3:1 on the background and `onAccent` ≥ 4.5:1 on
  `accent` (else both fall back, as a pair); Kino's accent must stand out 3:1 on your background (else your background falls
  back); `textPrimary`/`textSecondary` ≥ 4.5:1 on the background, `surface` and (`textPrimary`) `surfaceHigh`; `focus` ≥ 3:1 on
  the background and `onFocus` ≥ 4.5:1 on `focus`. A failing pair falls back on the side your theme set. There is no
  "far from Kino's red" rule for `appThemes`.
- **`adjustable`** (≤ 40 entries, keyed by token path, `background` included): `true`, `{ "swatches": ["#RRGGBB", …] }`
  (colours only) or `{ "min", "max" }` (numbers only). Ajustes ▸ Apariencia ▸ Personalizar shows only these (swatches work with
  a remote; a hex field and a stepper too) and «Volver a los valores del tema».
- **`pluginColors`**: `"respect"` (default: other plugins keep their own apiVersion 6 `theme` colours on their pages and player
  accent) or `"override"` (the theme's colours win everywhere). The person always has a «Colores de los plugins» switch.
- **`price`** `{ "kinos": 1..1000, "payTo": "<the author's coins account: 64 lowercase hex>" }`; no `price` = free. Before a
  priced theme turns on (from Apariencia, the plugin's manage sheet or `go.useTheme`) Kino shows **its own** sheet: the price,
  the person's balance, «Comprar por N kinos» enabled only when the balance covers it («Te faltan N kinos…» otherwise). Bought
  once per theme and account, valid on all their devices; the kinos go to `payTo`; a failed purchase charges nothing. The
  plugin never sees the purchase and **needs no `coins` capability** to sell. The price lives in a public manifest: it is what
  Kino charges and pays, not DRM over your files.
  `payTo` is the 64-hex coins account of whoever is paid: the same id Kino Social calls the author's `user_key` (derived from
  their Telegram identity; the Telegram id is never stored; from Kino 0.9.81 the author reads
  and copies it in Ajustes ▸ App ▸ Tu cuenta de kinos, which needs the Kinos switch on and a Telegram sign-in). Buyer and `payTo` being the same account is refused
  (`self_purchase`, nothing charged), so test the flow with a second account or the kit mocks. There are **no refunds**: a
  purchase is final; a failed one charges nothing and buying the same theme twice charges once.
- **`experience`** `"light"` (no shadows, no effects, square corners) or `"full"` (every effect, rounded corners): when the
  theme is turned on Kino asks («Este tema se ve mejor con la experiencia completa. ¿La usamos también?») and changes nothing
  without a yes, nor asks when the app already has it.
- **`logo`** `{ wordmark?, mark? }` (at least one): each `{ size: [w, h], paths: [{ d, fill }] }`, `w`/`h` whole 1..1000 and
  at most 8 times wider than tall, 1..8 paths, `d` ≤ 2,000 characters of SVG path data (`MmLlHhVvCcSsQqTtAaZz`, digits, `e`,
  `.`, `,`, spaces, signs), `fill` `accent`/`onAccent`/`textPrimary`/`textSecondary` or `#RRGGBB`. The wordmark replaces Kino's
  in the phone's menu and header and the TV's open rail; the mark in the TV's collapsed rail. Vector only: no image, no network.
- **What a theme never restyles**: Ajustes ▸ Apariencia itself and its preview, the purchase and experience questions, the
  install and update consent sheets, the 18+ code and setting locks, the `go.url` sheet, the lock screen and every other
  screen that asks the person for a decision keep Kino's own look; the splash, the gate and those screens keep Kino's logo; QR
  codes stay black on white; what is drawn over video or artwork keeps its colours.
- **On your own screen**: `screen` and `screenEvent` receive `activeTheme` (your active theme's id or `null`; Kino calls
  `screen` again after any change, Apariencia's too). A button `{ go: { useTheme: { theme: "<your id>" | null } } }` turns
  your theme on (`null`: back to Kino's, only while one of yours is active), exactly as Apariencia does, with Kino's toast
  «Tema aplicado» / «Volviste al tema de Kino»; refused, logged, for an id Apariencia does not list as yours (another
  plugin's, yours switched off in this profile, 18+ while locked). `{ go: { setExperience: "light" | "full" } }` asks for that
  experience with Kino's own question («Tu plugin» pide la experiencia completa. ¿La usamos?). Both only from the person's own
  press or submit on your screen (never `open`, a timer, a change, a load-more, an `onClose`, a panel or a notice); below
  apiVersion 18 dropped. A presentation screen usually opens from the settings page only: `"screen": { "label": …,
  "opensFrom": ["settings"], "settingsButton": { "label": "Ver presentación", "labelEn": "See presentation" } }`.
- **The person's side**: one theme active per profile, picked in Ajustes ▸ Apariencia (Tema de Kino, a built-in theme plugin,
  is always first; a preview shows a Home row, a dialog and the player controls before «Usar este tema»); choice and
  adjustments sync both ways between linked devices; disabling or removing the plugin returns to Kino's theme (the choice
  comes back on reinstall); an update re-resolves the theme and drops adjustments no longer `adjustable`; any failure gives
  Kino's look, never a crash.
- **Kit**: `node sdk/validate.mjs .` checks the format with the app's parser and prints each theme's dropped tokens for the
  phone and the TV, word for word as the app logs them (`appThemes neon (tv): shape.cardRadius: 40.0 is outside 0.0..32.0;
  Kino's is used`); `node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"activeTheme":"<id>"}' . screen` and `. screenEvent <name> --trigger tap`
  check the screen and say what Kino does with `go.useTheme` / `go.setExperience`. The kit draws no colours: look at the theme in
  Kino's preview.
- **Level 2, painted themes (`apiVersion` 26, Kino 0.9.87, provisional, not published yet).** A theme that declares 26 may add the
  keys below; a Kino that does not know 26 refuses the manifest as a whole (never put these keys in a theme that declares a lower
  apiVersion: an older Kino refuses an unknown field):
  - `surfaces`: keys `button`, `buttonGhost`, `navItem`, `navActive`, `rail`, `iconButton`, `card`, `cardFocus`, `focus`, `hero`,
    `progress`; each `{ fill?, stroke?, glow? }`. `fill` is `{ type: "solid", color }` or `{ type: "gradient", colors: [2..8],
    angle? }`; `stroke` is `{ width: 0..4, color }` **or** `{ width, gradient: { type: "gradient", … } }` (exactly one); `glow` is
    `{ color, radius: 0..24, alpha: 0..1 }`. `focus` has a stroke and a glow, never a fill; a `card` has no fill (the picture is
    the fill). `tv` and `phone` blocks may carry their own `surfaces` and `layout`.
  - `style.gloss` (0 to 1): an element with no explicit `fill` gets a lighter-top, darker-bottom gradient from its base colour,
    and `button`, `navActive`, `cardFocus` a glow from the accent; explicit values win.
  - `layout`: `hero` `"fullBleed"` | `"framed"` and `rail` `"strip"` | `"floating"`, TV only (the phone ignores them); with
    `shape.heroRadius` (0 to 32) and `shape.railItemRadius` (0 to 24).
  - `assets` (at most 16 `{ id, path, sha256, bytes }`, files of the plugin's own repository, fetched and hash-checked at
    install: a picture at most 2,000,000 bytes and 3,840 x 2,160, a font at most 1,000,000, 6,000,000 in all; a file that fails
    is left out and the theme still installs, so every effect needs a fallback) with `background.image` `{ asset, fit: "cover" |
    "top", dim: 0.3..1 }` (`colors.background` stays required as the fallback; contrast is measured on it darkened by `dim`) and
    `typography.fontFamily` `{ regular, bold? }` (asset ids of TTF or OTF files). `.kinoplugin` files and packaged plugins do not
    carry theme assets yet.
  - Guardrails (each drops **that value** with a warning, never the manifest): text on a fill keeps 4.5:1 on every gradient stop;
    a `focus` or `cardFocus` stroke too close to the page colour is dropped (focus is never invisible); ranges are clamped or
    dropped. The kit's `validate.mjs` checks the format of these keys; replay of the contrast and range warnings for them is not in the
    kit yet, so check them in Kino.
  - The person can turn each of seven effects off on its own (Ajustes ▸ Experiencia visual ▸ Personalizar uno por uno, or the
    Rendimiento tile of the TV's plugins panel): glows, gradient fills, gradient strokes, the background picture, the framed hero,
    the floating rail, the theme font. The device wins, so design every effect as an addition. A complete example:
    <https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-theme-crimson>.

<a id="protocol"></a>
**apiVersion 20: the plugin protocol (Kino 0.9.81; `provides`/`consumes` also work inside
`enhancements["20"]`).** One plugin (the **provider**) opens named **doors**; another (the **consumer**) uses them. Kino is
the only middleman: plugins never call each other, share memory or see each other's storage, settings or secrets. Full
page: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/>. Reference pair: the provider TMDB
(`kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb`, TMDB 1.3.0 and later, door `movies` in `enhancements["20"]`) and the consumer Cine Trivia
(`kinotvapp/kino-plugin-cine-trivia`, `apiVersion` 20, a `screen` game).

- **Neither block is a capability.** A provider or a consumer keeps the capabilities of the kind of plugin it is (a catalog
  keeps `search`/`home`/`resolve`, a game keeps `screen`). Never add a capability called `provides`, `consumes` or
  `protocol`: there is none.
- **Where to declare them.** `"apiVersion": 20` with `provides`/`consumes` at the top level, or a lower `apiVersion` with
  `"enhancements": { "20": { "provides": { … }, "consumes": { … } } }` (the block replaces the manifest's and is checked as
  apiVersion 20; an older Kino ignores it and keeps the plugin working). A top-level block below apiVersion 20 refuses the
  manifest (`The "provides" block needs apiVersion 20`). A provider with existing users uses `enhancements["20"]`.
- **Names.** Door, call, stream and alias names match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,31}$` (no `_`, no `-`); type names
  `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,31}$`, local to their door; a call and a stream of one door never share a name.
- **The provider's manifest** (at most 4 doors; each at most 16 calls and 8 streams):

  ```json
  "provides": { "movies": {
    "summary": "Movie records from TMDB",
    "calls": {
      "byId":   { "in": { "id": "number" }, "out": "Movie" },
      "random": { "in": { "fromYear": "number?", "toYear": "number?" }, "out": "Movie" },
      "search": { "in": { "q": "string" }, "out": "Movie[]" }
    },
    "streams": { "trending": { "out": "Movie", "everySeconds": 60 } },
    "types": { "Movie": { "id": "number", "title": "string", "year": "number", "director": "string?", "overview": "string?", "posterUrl": "string?" } }
  } }
  ```

  `summary` (optional, ≤ 120 characters, one text for both languages, no `summaryEn`) is what the person reads in the
  consumer's consent line. `out` is required for every call and stream; `in` may be left out (no argument). A stream's `out`
  is the type of ONE item. `everySeconds` is clamped to 30..86,400 (60 when omitted).
- **The provider's exports, exact names**: `proto_<door>_<call>(arg)` for each call, `proto_<door>_<stream>(cursor)` for
  each stream, spelled exactly as in the manifest, case included (`proto_movies_byId`, `proto_movies_trending`). A call
  returns JSON matching `out` (or a promise of it); a stream returns `{ items: [...], cursor }`, where `items` are the new
  ones since `cursor` (`null` the first time) and `cursor` is any small JSON you want back next poll (a number, a date
  string, a list of the last ids: all fine). The cursor travels **inside** that answer, so items and cursor together must fit
  in 64 KB; keep the cursor to a few KB at most and never put the items in it. To fail, `throw`: the
  consumer gets `provider_failed` and never your message (put nothing private in it). A missing export is also
  `provider_failed`. Map your rows to the declared type yourself; Kino only drops extra fields as a safety net.
- **The type language** (closed): `string`, `number` (finite), `boolean`, `T?` (absent or null), `T[]`, a door type name,
  or an inline object `{ "field": "type" }`. Suffixes combine (`"string[]?"`). No `any`, union, enum or map. Requests are
  checked **strictly** (an extra field, a missing required one or a wrong type is `bad_input`; nothing is coerced:
  `"1990"` is not a number; no argument reads as `{}` only when every `in` field is optional). Answers are checked
  **loosely** (undeclared fields dropped; a missing required field or a wrong type is `bad_output`). JSON, ≤ 64 KB
  (65,536 UTF-8 bytes) each way.
- **The consumer's manifest** (at most 8 entries; each lists at most 16 calls and 8 streams):

  ```json
  "consumes": { "tmdb": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb", "door": "movies", "calls": ["random", "byId"], "streams": ["trending"] } },
  "recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb"]
  ```

  The key (`tmdb`) is a local alias. `repo` is the provider's plain GitHub `owner/name` (no URL, sub-path or `@ref`; a fork
  does not stand in). List only the calls and streams the code really uses: an unlisted one answers `not_declared`.
  **Always put the same repository in `recommends`**: that is what gives `screen`/`screenEvent` the `installed` map
  (`recommends` does nothing else: Kino shows the person no list for it).
- <a id="consumer-hosts"></a>**The consumer's `hosts`: a screen-only consumer declares none.** Data from a door needs no host.
  A **screen-only consumer** (`"apiVersion": 20` or later, a non-empty `consumes`, `capabilities` exactly `["screen"]`;
  `contract.json` `protocol.screenOnlyConsumer`) declares **`"hosts": []`**, as Cine Trivia does. With no host its own
  `kino.fetch` is refused unless it declares `"fetchHosts": "any"` or has a `url` setting (alone or in a `list`). An `Image`
  needs **no** host declaration (any public https address,
  [Image](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/screen-components/#image)): TMDB's `posterUrl` draws without
  `image.tmdb.org`. With `"hosts": []` and **no setting at all** its card says it does not connect to the internet; any setting
  rules that out. If the screen does fetch something itself, declare that real host (it stays screen-only). Any other
  capability (`tracking`, a catalog, `playerPanelTab`...), an empty `consumes` or apiVersion 19 (`consumes` only in
  `enhancements["20"]`) bring back the ordinary rule: at least one host unless a `url` setting exists
  (`The "hosts" field can only be empty if the plugin has a setting of type "url"`). Never a placeholder: `validate.mjs` warns
  (`!`) on `example.com`, `*.example.com`, `example.org`, `example.net` and anything under `.test`, `.invalid`, `.example`, and
  tells a screen-only consumer `a screen-only consumer needs no host: declare none ("hosts": [])`; any other plugin is told
  `declare a host the plugin really loads from`. Full text:
  <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/#consumer-hosts>.
- <a id="text-only-consumer"></a>**A consumer that shows only text** (or public pictures) and loads nothing of its own is a
  screen-only consumer: `"hosts": []`, nothing to invent or replace. Never a made-up host (`images.my-recipes.test`, a domain
  nobody runs) and no `.invalid` name. Full text: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/#text-only-consumer>.
- **The call**: `await kino.plugins.call(alias, call, arg?)` resolves to the checked answer or rejects with an `Error`
  whose `code` is exactly one of `provider_missing` (not installed, off, needs setup, or 18+ while the consumer is not),
  `not_declared`, `bad_input`, `bad_output` (also: the answer held one of the provider's sealed secrets), `rate_limited`
  (more than 30 calls in any 10 s to one provider door, whatever alias), `timeout` (10 s) or `provider_failed`; in a
  background `job` it rejects with `not_allowed`. Usable in `screen`, `screenEvent` and the other exports that use Kino's
  services; **never in `job` or `sign()`**. Feature-detect with `typeof kino.plugins === "object"` when the consumer is
  below apiVersion 20. Always `try`/`catch` it and show a Spanish + English sentence per case; never retry in a loop;
  never cache answers in module variables (keep them in `state`, `kino.storage` or `kino.shared`).
- **The install gate (mandatory for a consumer that cannot work without its provider)**: Kino never installs anything on
  its own. While `installed["<owner/name>"] !== true`, `screen` returns **only** an install view with one primary,
  `autofocus` button whose action is `{ go: { installPlugin: { repo: "<owner/name>" } } }`, and `screenEvent` does nothing.
  Kino opens its normal install sheet over the screen; when the person taps Instalar, `installed` flips and Kino calls
  `screen` again, so the real UI appears in place. `go.installPlugin` is honoured from apiVersion 19, only from the person's
  own press or submit (never `open`, a timer, a change, an `onClose`, a panel or a notice), one repository per button; its
  only field is `repo`. **What `installed` means**: `true` while a plugin from that repository is installed, **even when the
  person switched it off or it needs its settings**; `false` only when none is installed (never installed, or removed). So also
  handle `provider_missing` at call time: with `installed` `true` it means the provider is off, needs setup or is 18+ while
  your plugin is not; keep the code in `state` and draw a sentence ("TMDB está apagado o le falta configurarse: revísalo en
  Plugins") with a retry button, not the install button. Keep a **default sentence** for any other code (a newer Kino may add
  one); a missing case must never throw out of `screenEvent`.
- **The reserved `open` event in a gated consumer**: answer `null` while `installed[repo] !== true` (an `open` answer cannot
  carry `go.installPlugin`, and `open` drops every `go` but `go.screen`). With the provider installed, `open` may load the first
  data or answer `null`. After the install Kino calls `screen` again with the new `installed` and sends **no** new `open`, so
  the main view must work with an empty `state` (a button, or a `Skeleton` and a load on the first press).
- **Consumer recipes** (<https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/#consumer-recipes>): a **search box** is
  `{ type: "TextField", key: "q", kind: "search", labelText: "Buscar", labelTextEn: "Search", onSubmitted: "search" }`; the
  `search` event gets the typed text as its `value` (not `arg`). A **detail** is `route: { push: "detail", params }` from the
  press, `screen` then gets `route.name === "detail"`, and its `AppBar` `leading` is a back whose event answers
  `{ route: { pop: true } }`. An answer's `focus` on a key inside a `ListView` item is **not guaranteed**: Kino moves focus only
  to a focusable node drawn at that moment, and a `ListView` draws its items lazily (an off-screen item is not drawn; the
  request is then ignored with no log; the kit accepts any key).
- **Streams**: switch one on from a `screenEvent` answer with the state flag
  `{ state: { protocol: { "<alias>": { "<stream>": true } } } }` (`false` switches it off; the `protocol` key is replaced
  whole, so send every flag together). While that screen is open, shown and Kino in front, Kino polls the provider every
  `everySeconds` and sends the new, checked items to `screenEvent` as the event **`protocol`** with
  `arg = { alias, stream, items }` (an object, not a string). Its answer keeps only `state`, `toast`, `close` and `config`.
  At most 4 live subscriptions per plugin and 16 flags read; polls are 8 in any 10 s per door (separate from the 30 calls);
  three failures in a row switch it off for that opening; leaving the screen or Kino leaving the front ends it; after a
  return the cursor restarts from `null`, so **items may repeat**: make the handler idempotent. Not for player-panel sessions.
- **Provides-only plugin**: `"apiVersion": 20`, a non-empty `provides`, no `capabilities` at all (the field may be left out),
  no settings. Kino derives this from the manifest: **there is no `providesOnly` field** (validate warns if you write one).
  It may declare `"hosts": []`; then it plays nothing, is no source, and reaches the world only through Kino's services such
  as `kino.tmdb`. A provider that later needs `kino.fetch` adds those hosts to `hosts` and **stays** provides-only (no
  `resolve`/`search`/`home` to write); its consent sheet then lists the hosts. Any capability or setting brings the ordinary
  rules back (`resolve`, `search`/`home`, at least one host). The consumer side has the same freedom: a screen-only consumer
  may declare `"hosts": []` too ([above](#consumer-hosts)).
- **Security and privacy rules you must follow**: every argument reaches the provider, which may send it to its own hosts
  (or any host with `"fetchHosts": "any"`): never pass tokens, passwords, the person's private input or anything from a
  `password` setting. An 18+ provider answers only an 18+ consumer (`provider_missing` otherwise). An answer holding a
  sealed secret (or a marker) is `bad_output`: never return `kino.secret()` values or anything derived from them. A plugin
  cannot call its own door (`not_declared`); two plugins must not call each other back from inside an answer (it waits
  until `timeout`). Receiving data never widens the consumer's own `hosts`.
- **What the person sees**: one plain line per door on the consumer's install sheet, «Usa datos de <provider name>
  (<door summary>)» («Usa datos de kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb» while the provider is not installed), marked new on an
  update that adds it; no prompt per call; removing the provider leaves the consumer installed and its calls answer
  `provider_missing`. The protocol stores nothing, so nothing new is synced.
- **Evolving a door**: Kino re-reads the provider's door at every call. Only add (new calls, optional fields). Removing or
  renaming a call breaks every consumer with `not_declared`; a new required `in` field breaks old consumers with
  `bad_input`. For a breaking change open a new door (`movies2`) and keep the old one.
- **Kit** (full page: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/#kit>):
  - **Scaffolds**: `node sdk/init.mjs my-provider --kind provider --door <door> --call <call>`, `node sdk/init.mjs
    my-consumer --kind consumer --repo <owner/name> --door <door> --call <call>` (section 3, step 1; the consumer gets
    `"hosts": []`, `--host` adds a real one). Each comes with a test that passes as written (the consumer's shows `todo 0`),
    and the consumer's `test/provider` is a STAND-IN to replace with a copy of the real provider.
  - **A provider on its own**: `node sdk/run.mjs <provider folder> proto <door>.<call> '<arg json>'` (a call) and
    `node sdk/run.mjs <provider folder> proto <door>.<stream> ['<cursor json>']` (one poll; it prints `{ items, cursor }` and the
    command for the next poll). Same checks and codes as the app. Exit 0 with the answer on stdout; 1 with `✗ <code>: <message>`
    when Kino would reject the call (your thrown message follows on a `·` line; the consumer never sees it); 2 for a wrong
    command (unknown door or call, which it lists; bad JSON; a folder without `provides`).
  - **A consumer with its provider**: `node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"installed":{"<owner/name>":true}}' --provider <provider
    folder> <consumer folder> screen` draws past the gate (without `--context` every `recommends` entry is `false`: that draws
    the gate); pass the same `--context` to `screenEvent <name>` too, or a gated consumer answers nothing. `--provider` is
    repeatable; without it every call is `provider_missing`. `screenEvent protocol <alias>.<stream>` (with `--state
    '{"protocol":{"<alias>":{"<stream>":true}}}'`) polls a stream once and sends the `protocol` event; `--cursor '<json>'`
    polls from a cursor the provider already returned, to try repeated items. `--lang en` draws the English texts and
    `--device tv` the TV. A clean run prints no `dropped` line on stderr (the exit code is 0 either way).
  - **A detail route**: `--context '{"installed":{"<owner/name>":true},"route":{"name":"detail","params":{"id":1}}}'` (with
    `--state` for what the route shows) draws it. **A typed value**: `screenEvent search "" '"tomate"' --trigger submit`: the
    value is the **third** word after `screenEvent` (`<name> [arg] [value]`, `""` for no arg) and must be JSON (`'"tomate"'`,
    never `tomate`: `the value must be JSON`).
  - **Error codes**: the kit can provoke only `provider_missing` (run without `--provider`) and `provider_failed` (the provider
    throws, e.g. an id it lacks; `proto` also shows `bad_input`). `not_declared`, `bad_output`, `rate_limited`, `timeout` (and
    your default) are tested by **drawing** them: `--state '{"error":"rate_limited"}' . screen`, no `dropped` line.
  - **Was a prop accepted?** The printed tree is the checked one and does not echo every flag (an `AppBar`'s `dense: true` is
    not printed). A wrong value prints `· dropped: screen: appBar dense "yes" is not true or false, ignored`, so no `dropped`
    line means accepted; `--raw` prints the tree as your plugin returned it. Kino draws `dense` on a phone (4 dp above and below
    the bar's row) and ignores it on a TV and in a player panel.
  - **validate**: `node sdk/validate.mjs .` checks both blocks (top level and `enhancements`) like the app. It **fails** (`✗`,
    exit 1) when a declared call or stream has no `proto_<door>_<name>` export (Kino would install it, but every call to it
    answers `provider_failed`). It **warns** (`!`, exit 0) when a consumed repo is missing from `recommends`, when
    `everySeconds` is outside 30..86,400 (it says the value Kino uses), when the manifest has a `providesOnly` field and when a
    `hosts` entry is a placeholder (`example.com`, `.test`, `.invalid`...; a screen-only consumer is told to declare none).
  - **What the kit does not check**: it has no repositories, so it serves an entry with the **first provider that has the
    door and ignores `repo`**: check by hand that `repo` is the provider's exact GitHub `owner/name`, the same string in
    `recommends` and in your `installed[...]` key. It does **not** apply the 18+ rule, the sealed-secret check or the
    self-call refusal: test those in Kino 0.9.81+, with the provider installed, switched off and removed.
  - The provider's own services need their usual kit setup (`KINO_TMDB_KEY` or `KINO_TMDB_FIXTURE` for `kino.tmdb`).
    `--provider` needs a kit with `sdk/protocol.mjs`, and `proto`, `--cursor`, `--lang` and `init.mjs --kind` a recent copy:
    if `run.mjs`/`validate.mjs`/`init.mjs` do not know them, tell the person their copy of `sdk/`, `contract.json` and
    `kino.d.ts` is old (get it again from kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk); never delete the blocks to silence it.

<a id="minimal-consumer"></a>
**A minimal consumer screen that draws clean (apiVersion 20).** Start a consumer from this shape (or from `init.mjs --kind
consumer`). It is checked: with the kit's example provider (`fixtures/protocol/provider` in kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk),
`node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"installed":{"kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb":true}}' --provider <provider folder> . screen` prints
no `dropped` line, with `installed` `true` and `false`, with `--lang en` and with `--device tv`.

```json
{
  "id": "mini-trivia",
  "name": "Mini Trivia",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": 20,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Una pregunta de cine con las películas del plugin TMDB",
  "hosts": [],
  "capabilities": ["screen"],
  "screen": { "label": "Trivia", "labelEn": "Trivia" },
  "recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb"],
  "consumes": { "tmdb": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb", "door": "movies", "calls": ["random"], "streams": ["trending"] } }
}
```

```js
const TMDB = "kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb"; // exactly as written in "recommends"

const ERRORS = {
  provider_missing: ["TMDB está apagado o le falta configurarse: revísalo en Plugins.", "TMDB is off or needs setting up: check it in Plugins."],
  rate_limited: ["Demasiadas preguntas seguidas. Espera un momento.", "Too many questions in a row. Wait a moment."],
};
const OTHER = ["No se pudo traer la película. Intenta otra vez.", "Could not get the movie. Try again."];

const text = (es, en, more = {}) => ({ type: "Text", text: es, textEn: en, ...more });
const page = (children) => ({
  type: "Scaffold",
  appBar: {
    type: "AppBar", title: "Mini Trivia", titleEn: "Mini Trivia", mergeWithKinoBar: true, dense: true,
    leading: { type: "IconButton", icon: "close", labelText: "Cerrar", labelTextEn: "Close", onPressed: { close: true } },
  },
  body: { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Column", padding: 16, gap: 12, children }] },
});

export async function screen({ state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (installed[TMDB] !== true) {
    return page([
      text("Para jugar necesitas el plugin TMDB.", "To play you need the TMDB plugin."),
      { type: "ElevatedButton", key: "install", labelText: "Instalar TMDB", labelTextEn: "Install TMDB",
        onPressed: { go: { installPlugin: { repo: TMDB } } }, autofocus: true },
    ]);
  }
  const kids = [];
  if (state.movie) {
    if (state.movie.poster) kids.push({ type: "Image", url: state.movie.poster, aspect: "2:3", width: 160 }); // image.tmdb.org
    kids.push(text(`¿De qué año es ${state.movie.title}?`, `What year is ${state.movie.title} from?`, { style: "h3" }));
  }
  if (state.error) kids.push(text(...(ERRORS[state.error] || OTHER), { color: "error" }));
  kids.push({ type: "ElevatedButton", key: "play", labelText: "Otra película", labelTextEn: "Another movie", onPressed: "play", autofocus: true });
  kids.push({ type: "Switch", key: "live", labelText: "Tendencias en vivo", labelTextEn: "Live trending",
    value: state.protocol?.tmdb?.trending === true, onChanged: "live" });
  if (state.trending) kids.push(text(state.trending, state.trending, { style: "caption" }));
  return page(kids);
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, value, arg, state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (installed[TMDB] !== true) return null; // the gate: nothing works until the provider is installed
  if (name === "play") {
    try {
      const m = await kino.plugins.call("tmdb", "random", {});
      return { state: { movie: { title: m.title, year: m.year, poster: m.posterUrl ?? null }, error: null } };
    } catch (e) {
      return { state: { error: e.code || "provider_failed" } }; // provider_missing, rate_limited, timeout...
    }
  }
  if (name === "live") return { state: { protocol: { tmdb: { trending: value === true } } } };
  if (name === "protocol" && Array.isArray(arg?.items)) {
    return { state: { trending: arg.items.map((m) => m.title).slice(0, 5).join(", ") } };
  }
  return null;
}
```

Three silent traps (a Flutter habit writes them; the kit and Kino do not draw them):

- `SingleChildScrollView` takes **`children`** (a list), never `child`: with `child` the scroll is **empty and no `dropped`
  line warns you**.
- A `Scaffold`'s `appBar` must be an **`AppBar` node**, `{ "type": "AppBar", "title": …, "titleEn": … }`: without `type` the
  whole bar is dropped (`scaffold appBar must be AppBar`).
- There is **no `FilledButton`** (`unknown widget "FilledButton"`, dropped): use `ElevatedButton` or `TextButton` with
  `labelText` + `labelTextEn` and `onPressed`. Also, a `Text` with `text: ""` is dropped (`text is empty`).

What Kino 0.9.50 does for every plugin, with no field: plays a plugin title on the paired TV through
the TV's own copy of the plugin (keep `id` and refs identical across devices), checks followed series
for new chapters through `episodes(ref)` (keep series refs stable), saves "Para ti" picks by `ref`,
and treats a **signed** plugin installed from two repos with the same `id` and author key as one
plugin across devices.

<a id="share"></a>
**Sharing: Kino Social's `wall` door (Kino 0.9.81, Kino Social 0.9.7) and share cards (Kino 0.9.84).** Recommend a
**Compartir** action in **every** plugin. Full page: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/share/>. Published example:
Megaplay (`xuper-plugin/kino-plugin-megaplay`, `src/browse/share.js` and `test/share.test.mjs`).

- **Manifest** (top level with `"apiVersion": 20`, or `consumes` inside `enhancements["20"]` at a lower apiVersion, the feature
  behind `typeof kino.plugins === "object"`; the plugin needs a screen):

  ```json
  "consumes": { "social": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-social", "door": "wall", "calls": ["share"] } },
  "recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-social"]
  ```

  No host is needed for it.
- **The call**: `await kino.plugins.call("social", "share", { text?, title?, link?, from? })` from the person's press or submit
  (never `open`, a timer or a `job`). `text` ≤ 500 characters (longer is cut); `title` is `{ kind: "movie" | "series", tmdb:
  <positive whole TMDB id>, season?, episode? }` (season and episode only on a series); `link` https only (≤ 500); `from` your
  plugin's name (≤ 40), shown in the bell notice. At least one of `text`, `title`, `link`; **text only is fine** (no `title`).
  Any other field is `bad_input`; an empty proposal, a bad `kind` or a non-https link is `provider_failed`. Answer:
  `{ status: "draft", draftId, pending }`.
- **What happens**: Kino Social **publishes nothing**. It keeps a draft (at most 5, the oldest goes; the same proposal twice
  keeps one; 14 days), rings the bell («<from> quiere publicar en tu muro») and shows it at the top of its wall with Revisar /
  Descartar; the person posts it. **Never publish on the person's behalf, and never say it was posted**: say it waits in Kino
  Social.
- **The UI**: a share `IconButton` in the bar (text only) and/or a «Compartir» button on a title page (with the title); the
  press opens a declared `BottomSheet` (from the answer: `ui: [{ open }]`) with a `Form`: a `TextField` (prefilled «Estoy viendo
  «…»», editable, `maxLength` 500), a `Switch` «Adjuntar el título» when there is a title, a caption saying it arrives as a
  draft, and a submit button; the form's values come as the event's `value` (merge `state.inputs` too). ES + EN texts.
- **Errors**: no `kino.plugins` (Kino before 0.9.81) → a toast «Actualiza Kino…», do not call; `provider_missing` with
  `installed["kinotvapp/kino-social"] !== true` → answer `{ go: { installPlugin: { repo: "kinotvapp/kino-social" } } }` (Kino's
  install sheet; the person decides); `provider_missing` while installed → «Kino Social está apagado o le falta configurarse»;
  `not_declared` → Kino Social older than 0.9.7 (or your `consumes` lacks `share`): ask to update Kino Social; anything else →
  «No se pudo enviar a Kino Social. Inténtalo de nuevo.» (a default sentence for unknown codes). Never retry in a loop. Nothing
  private in the arguments.
- **Share cards (Kino 0.9.84, not published yet; no new apiVersion).** Kino Social will show cards in a later version; until
  then senders use `share`. The pieces:
  - `go.plugin` `{ repo, route?, args?, query? }` (apiVersion 20, the person's press or submit only): `repo` a GitHub
    `owner/name[/path]` ≤ 200 (a URL or `@ref` drops it), `route` a `go.screen` route, `args` ≤ 4 KB JSON, `query` ≤ 200. Kino,
    in order: not installed → its install sheet, then continues; 18+ and locked → nothing opens, Kino's toast; off → «¿Activar?»;
    `route` in the target's `openFrom.routes` → that screen with `args`; else with a `query` and a search → Kino's search scoped
    to that plugin; else its section or screen default page; else a toast. An unlisted route never opens.
  - `"openFrom": { "routes": ["detail"] }` in the target's manifest (apiVersion 20 at the top level, or `enhancements["20"]`;
    needs `screen`; 1 to 16 names `^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,64}$`; a bad list refuses the manifest). It says what may be opened, not
    how. The target's `screen({ route })` gets `route.name` and `route.args`, and the `open` event comes with the same `route`:
    load there, and **check the `args`** (they come from another plugin).
  - `ctx.caller` `{ id, repo, name, adult }`: the second argument of every `proto_` export (Kino sets it; an older Kino sends
    none, so read `ctx && ctx.caller`). `repo` is `owner/name[/path][@ref]` or `null`; **cut the `@ref` off** before using it in
    `go.plugin`. Kit: `node sdk/run.mjs --repo me/my-game <provider folder> proto <door>.<call>`.
  - `kino.image.thumbnail(url, { maxWidth?, maxBytes? })` → `"data:image/jpeg;base64,…"`: https only, under the plugin's own
    `kino.fetch` rules (hosts, budget, never the home network), download ≤ 5 MB, `maxWidth` 32..400 (200), `maxBytes`
    2,048..32,768 (16,384), 20 a minute; errors `bad_request`, `host_not_allowed`, `not_found`, `network`, `timeout`,
    `too_large`, `not_image`, `rate_limited`, `not_allowed` (from `sign()`). Feature-detect `typeof kino.image === "object"`;
    show the card without a picture on any error. The kit has no codec (`kit_unsupported` unless the bytes are already a small
    JPEG/PNG; `KINO_THUMBNAIL_FIXTURE=<file>` answers a file).

<a id="visual-browser"></a>
**apiVersion 20: a browser window the person drives (`visualBrowser`, Kino 0.9.81).** When the
person has to sign in, solve a challenge or accept a site's terms, the hidden `kino.browser` cannot help: with
`"apiVersion": 20` and `"visualBrowser": true` (also `"enhancements": { "20": { "visualBrowser": true } }` at an older
`apiVersion`) the plugin calls `kino.visualBrowser.open({ url, title?, doneWhen?, collect?, userAgent?, timeoutMs? })` and
gets `{ status: "done" | "closed" | "timeout", finalUrl?, cookies?, html?, stored?, storedNames?, userAgent? }`. Full page and
the "Vincular cuenta" recipe: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/visual-browser/>.

- **Check first**: `kino.visualBrowser?.available` (undefined on an older Kino; false on the desktop and on a device without
  a WebView). Keep another way in (a `password` setting the person pastes the cookies into). Phone and tablet; Android TV is
  experimental.
- **Only from the person's own press**: a settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a `screenEvent` after a tap or submit; anything
  else throws `forbidden`. Other errors: `bad_args`, `unavailable`, `busy` (one window in the whole app), `store_failed`.
- **Your `hosts` only**: the first `url` and every page the window goes to must be https on the default port on a declared host.
  Kino asks the person in its own sheet at every open (the sites, the cookie names, the user agent); the manifest carries one
  plain consent line.
- **Cookies**: `collect.cookies` (at most 32 names; 64 cookies and 16,384 characters back, only with `done`), `collect.html`
  (2,000,000 characters), `collect.finalUrl`. `collect.storeAs: { setting, format: "header" | "json", spill?, thenEvent? }` makes Kino write
  the cookies into your declared `password` setting (500 characters) after your call ends; you get `stored` and `storedNames`,
  never a value; `thenEvent` names a `screenEvent` Kino sends your open screen once they are written. `spill` (1 to 3 more
  declared, distinct `password` settings) takes a longer text: Kino cuts it at 500 characters over `setting` then each `spill`
  setting in order, in one save, all or nothing (`store_failed` if it does not fit); read it back with
  `[kino.config.cookieA, kino.config.cookieB, ...].join("")`, no separator, never trimming a piece.
- **localStorage** (additive inside apiVersion 20, Kino 0.9.87, provisional; an older Kino ignores it and answers no
  `localStorage`, so check the answer): `collect.localStorage` (at most 32 keys of 1 to 256 characters, no control character) returns
  `localStorage: { key: value }` for the keys the page's own `localStorage` holds, read from the page the window ends on (a declared
  host), only with `done`, at most 65,536 characters of keys and values together; a missing key is absent. Kino's sheet lists the keys.
  `storeAs` covers only cookies, so these values reach your script: keep them in `kino.storage`, never log them.
  `doneWhen.localStorage` closes the window once every named key exists.
- **`doneWhen`** `{ cookies?, localStorage?, urlMatches? }` closes the window by itself; `timeoutMs` 5,000 to 600,000; `userAgent` is `"browser"`
  or your own string (1 to 300 printable ASCII characters). The window's own `timeoutMs` is its only time bound: the opening
  call's time bound does not run while it is up, and the call has at least 10 seconds after `open` resolves. The window starts with a clean cookie jar.
- **Test**: the Node kit has no window; `validate.mjs` checks the key and prints a note, and `kino.visualBrowser.open` answers
  `unavailable` unless a test of yours gives `createKino` a `visualBrowser` option (answer `{ status: "done", localStorage: { … } }` to test `collect.localStorage`). Try the real window on a phone or a TV.

<a id="files"></a>
**apiVersion 21: files on the device (`files`, Kino 0.9.82).** A plugin that reads books, plays music or shows videos the
person already keeps on the device declares `"apiVersion": 21` and `"capabilities": [..., "files"]` (declarative: nothing to
export; a plain consent line; it may stand alone, and an enhancement may add it). The person picks a file or a folder with the
system picker; the plugin gets an opaque **handle** (`{ id, name, size, mime, kind, copied, addedAt, folder? }`), never an
address. Nothing is uploaded or sent by this capability. Full page: <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/files/>.

- **Calls.** `kino.files.pick({ kinds?, multiple?, copy? })` (handles, `[]` on cancel; `kinds` from `video`, `audio`, `book`,
  `image`, `subtitle`, `other`), `pickFolder({ kinds? })`, `list({ folder?, kinds? })`, `folders()`, `info(id)`,
  `read(id, { start?, end? })` (a `Uint8Array`, ≤ 2,000,000 bytes a call: read a big file by parts), `readText(id, range)`,
  `forget(id)` and `url(id)`, which returns `kino-file:<id>` for a stream's or an audio track's `url` (the player plays the file;
  the host rules do not apply; it cannot be cast to a Chromecast or DLNA by address).
- **A press.** `pick` and `pickFolder` only run from a settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a `screenEvent` that follows the
  person's own tap or submit (the rule of `kino.qr.scan`); anywhere else (`open`, a timer, Home, `playerEvent`) they reject with
  `not_allowed`. Everything else needs no press.
- **`copy: true`** copies the bytes into the plugin's own store (≤ 64 MB a file, 1 GB in all); the default keeps a reference that
  stops working when the person moves or deletes the file.
