- **Errors** (`err.code`): `unavailable`, `not_allowed`, `busy`, `timeout` (the picker closes at 3 minutes), `invalid_request`,
  `gone` (moved, deleted or the grant lost: say so in a line and offer to pick again, no error screen), `too_large`, `denied`
  (not your handle), `quota`. Limits: 500 handles, 20 folders, 5,000 files from a folder, 50 in one pick.
- **Not synced.** A handle means nothing on another device: sync what you save *about* a file (reading place, play position)
  under its name and size, not under the handle. To draw a cover, read the bytes and give an `Image` a `data:image/png;base64,…`.
- **Kit.** `kino.files` in `sdk/run.mjs` answers from the folder named by `KINO_FILES_DIR` (default `./.kino-files`): `pick`
  hands out the files that are there, in name order.

<a id="progress"></a>
**apiVersion 22: where the person is (`progress`, next Kino release, not published yet).** A plugin whose items are not videos
(a manga reader, a book reader, a podcast it plays itself) declares `"apiVersion": 22` and `"capabilities": [..., "progress"]`
(declarative: nothing to export; **no consent line, no approval**; it may stand alone, beside `screen` (`["screen", "progress"]`
is valid) or beside any capability, and the plugin stays that kind; an enhancement may add it: `enhancements["22"]`). Full page:
<https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/progress/>.

- **Calls.** `kino.progress.set({ id, fraction, title?, poster?, label?, labelEn?, resume?, done?, doneAt? })` (`id` matches
  `^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,128}$`, yours: a chapter, a book, a manga; `fraction` 0 to 1; resolves when Kino has taken it),
  `get(id)` (the entry, or **`null`** when there is none: always handle it), `list({ limit?, sinceMs? })` (most recently set
  first; `limit` 1..100, default 50; `sinceMs` a finite number >= 0; finished ones included with `done: true`) and `clear(id)`.
  An entry is `{ id, fraction, title?, poster?, label?, labelEn?, resume?, done, updatedAtMs }`: **every `list` entry carries its
  `id`**.
- **Kino draws nothing.** No Home row, no card, no "Continuar viendo": the plugin builds its own "keep reading" shelf from
  `list` (in `home()` or on its screen). It is kept apart from the library, the watch time, `kino.library` and `tracking`.
- **`resume` is opaque.** Any JSON value (string, number, boolean, object, array) of ≤ 1024 bytes once serialized (else
  `too_large`); Kino stores, syncs and hands it back unchanged and **never reads it**. Put the exact place there
  (`{ cap: 87, pag: 12 }`, or a screen route and its args); `fraction` is only an approximation. Keep a margin below 1024: Kino
  counts U+2028/U+2029 as 6 bytes where `JSON.stringify` writes them raw. Validate its shape when you read it back (another
  device, maybe another version of the plugin, wrote it).
- **Texts.** `title` ≤ 200 characters; `label` and `labelEn` ≤ 80 each ("Cap. 87 · hoja 12 de 40"); `poster` an https address
  under the screen `Image` rule or a `KinoImageRef` of `imageSource` (a bad poster costs only the poster). A `set` that leaves
  `title`/`poster` out keeps what was there.
- **Finished** at `done: true` or when `fraction >= doneAt` (default 0.9); it stays in `list`; a later `set` with a lower
  fraction reopens it; an identical `set` changes nothing.
- **Call it on every page turn if you like**: Kino keeps the latest per element in memory and writes at most every 2 s (and
  when the screen closes or the app goes to the background); more than 20 calls a second are coalesced, never an error. 500
  elements per plugin (the oldest by last activity dropped).
- **Per profile, synced, backed up.** Each element is the plugin's and the profile's (another plugin or profile never sees it);
  it syncs per profile between the person's linked devices both ways (the latest `set` wins) and travels in backups.
- **Jobs.** A scheduled job may call it, but **not a job that runs for a profile other than the active one** (`perProfile`):
  there it rejects with `not_allowed`, like `kino.notifications`, `kino.coins` and `kino.seed`.
- **Errors** (`err.code`): `bad_request` (a bad `id`, `fraction`, `done`, `doneAt`, text or option), `too_large` (`resume` over
  1024 bytes), `not_allowed` (capability not declared, a job for another profile, or Kino could not keep it right now).
- **Feature-detect** with `typeof kino.progress === "object"`.
- **A `home()` built from it** returns an **array of rows**, each with its own `id`, and every item needs an `id` (plus `ref`,
  `title`, `kind`):

```js
async function home() {
  const rows = [];
  if (typeof kino.progress === "object") {
    const reading = (await kino.progress.list({ limit: 15 })).filter((e) => !e.done);
    if (reading.length) rows.push({ id: "keep-reading", title: "Seguir leyendo",
      items: reading.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, ref: e.id, title: e.title || e.id, kind: "series", poster: e.poster })) });
  }
  return rows; // a KinoRow[], never a single row object
}
```

- **Kit.** `kino.progress` in the Node kit keeps the elements in memory for the run, with Kino's checks and error codes
  (`node --test sdk/test/progress.test.mjs`).

<a id="player-slot"></a>
**apiVersion 23: the player slot (`playerSlot`, next Kino release, provisionally 0.9.83, not published yet).** Up to three
small elements in the **top-right corner of the TV player** (never on a phone), on movies, series and En vivo channels; three
on screen in all across every plugin (`fixed` first, then the person's plugin order). Declare `"apiVersion": 23`,
`"capabilities": [..., "playerSlot"]` and a `slot` block (each needs the other; `playerSlot` may be the plugin's only
capability: it plays nothing, so no `resolve`/`search`; an older Kino gets it through `enhancements["23"]` with both). No new
host: an `image` is loaded by Kino from any public https address. Full page:
<https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/player-slot/>.

- **`slot.elements`**: 1 to 3 `{ id, kind, mode }`; `id` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,23}$`, unique; `kind` `text` | `icon` |
  `image` | `button`; `mode` `overlay` (shows with the controls; on a channel, with the channel card) or `fixed` (always
  there). The count, kinds and modes are fixed in the manifest: answers change content only.
- **`playerSlot(context)`** answers `{ items: [{ id, text } | { id, icon } | { id, image } | { id, label?, icon? }], refreshMs? }`.
  `text`: at most 2 lines (newlines split), 2,000 characters; `icon`: one of Kino's 50 icon names; `image`: https on a public
  host (no IP, `localhost` or local name); `button`: `label` ≤ 40 characters and/or `icon`. Nothing is repaired: an undeclared
  id, a wrong kind, an unknown icon or a bad image drops that item; a repeated id keeps the first valid one; items come out in
  declared order; an answer without an `items` list keeps the last good frame. `refreshMs` is clamped to 2,000..60,000 and
  counted from the end of the last call; absent = never called again.
- **Look and place (no new apiVersion).** A `text` item may carry `size` (`small`, `normal`, `large`, `xlarge`: 12, 14, 18, 24 sp),
  `weight` (`extralight`, `light`, `normal`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`: Inter 200..700, every line), `color` and `background`
  (`#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`; alpha 0 on `background` draws no pill); any item may carry `left` and `top` (whole dp, clamped to
  -400..200 and -40..300). An invalid field is ignored on its own; the letters are never under half opacity, a `color` under 2:1
  contrast on an opaque pill (or on Kino's dark one) is dropped, white letters turn black on a light opaque pill. Offer them as
  ordinary `select` settings read with `kino.config.get`; a time zone is a fixed UTC offset (no daylight saving), the device's own
  by default (the player-clock example, `docs/slot-examples/player-clock`; <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/player-slot/#dress>).
- **Timing.** 5 s a call, one at a time per plugin; until the first good answer a failed call is retried every 5 s, 4 more
  times; calls never count toward "No responde" (a press does); no call while Kino is in the background.
- **`playerSlotAction({ id, context })`** runs on OK on a declared button on screen; answer `null`/`{}` or
  `{ openPanel?: true, player?: KinoPlayerAction }`. `openPanel` opens your player panel (needs a `panel` or a contributed tab;
  ignored and logged otherwise). `player` follows a panel press's rules: the plugin of the title playing keeps its fields, any
  other plugin only `seekToMs` (with approved `playerControl`: also `pause` and `speed`), through Kino's gate. A slot-only
  plugin cannot declare `playerControl` (it needs a `panel`).
- **`context`** = the panel's context plus `live`: full for your own title; the contributed one (`foreign: true`, opaque
  `ref`, `source`) for another plugin's; the **bare** one (`live`, `foreign`, `device`, `lang`, `features`, **no `kind`**)
  for an 18+ title, one no plugin owns or one Kino cannot confirm, and for an unconfirmed channel; the live panel's
  (`kind: "live"`, `channel`) for a confirmed channel. Read `live` and `lang`; treat the rest as possibly missing.
- **Live.** Up/Down still zap, so the **Menu** key reaches the buttons (a remote without Menu cannot: never make a live-only
  function depend on a button). `seekToMs`, `seekStepMs`, `speed`, `skip`, `markers`, `autoNext` are dropped; only `pause`
  survives, and only with approved `playerControl`. On a movie, Up from the progress bar reaches the first button.
- **Consent.** Only a `fixed` element asks: a red line ("Mostrará algo suyo de forma permanente en el reproductor mientras ves
  un video"), asked again by an update that adds one, never auto-approved, approved again on each device (never carried by
  sync or a backup). Overlay-only asks nothing. The person's switch "Dejar que muestre algo en el reproductor" stops the calls.
- **Look.** Kino draws everything (no `padding`, `color`, `style`, `ring`): a text on a translucent dark pill, white with a
  shadow, the first line Medium and the second Regular, tabular figures; buttons round (icon) or a pill (label). Kino's own
  type gets lighter in this release; plugin screens keep their old scale (headings still bold).
- **Kit.** `node sdk/run.mjs <folder> playerSlot [ref]`, `node sdk/run.mjs <folder> playerSlotAction <ref> <button id>`,
  with `--context '<json>'`, `--foreign <id>[:<name>]`, `--live-channel <provider>:<code>[:<name>]` and `--bare` (ref `-`
  with the last two); `node sdk/validate.mjs <folder>` checks the block and both exports and prints the red line
  (`--run playerSlot` calls it). A minimal clock (one `fixed` text, no network):

```json
{ "id": "player-clock", "name": "Reloj del reproductor", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 23, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": ["kinotvapp.github.io"], "capabilities": ["playerSlot"],
  "slot": { "elements": [{ "id": "clock", "kind": "text", "mode": "fixed" }] } }
```

```js
export async function playerSlot(context) {
  const now = new Date();
  const pad = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
  return { items: [{ id: "clock", text: pad(now.getHours()) + ":" + pad(now.getMinutes()) + "\n" + now.toDateString() }],
    refreshMs: 60000 };
}
export async function playerSlotAction() { return null; } // no button, but the capability requires the export
```

<a id="player-panel"></a>
**The player panel (apiVersion 9, Kino 0.9.55).** `"panel": { "label", "labelEn?", "icon" | "iconFile" }` adds a
button in the player, only while a title of the plugin plays, and requires exporting `panel(context)`; optional
`panelAction(event, context)` answers presses, changes and submits, and `playerEvent(event, context)` hears
started/paused/resumed/ended/failed/copyChanged. `settingsLayout` arranges the settings form in rows, columns and
cards. Playback must never depend on any of it (older Kino refuses apiVersion 9). Full reference:
<https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/player-panel/>.

**Nuvio scrapers as a link source (apiVersion 11, Kino 0.9.71, experiment).** Many Nuvio repositories hold dozens of working scrapers; a plugin can use them instead of writing its own scraper per site. Declare `"nuvio"` in `capabilities` and `"nuvioRepos": ["owner/repo"]` (1 to 4 GitHub `owner/repo` or https addresses of a Nuvio `manifest.json`; each requires the other; `kino.nuvio` refuses any repository not listed with `not_allowed`), plus `"streamHosts": "any"` because the videos come from each scraper's own hosts. Inside your functions (never at module load) call `kino.nuvio.available({ repo })` (what is offered: `id`, `name`, `types`, `languages`, `compatible`, `installed`), `kino.nuvio.use({ repo, scrapers })` (installs up to 12, 45 s each; `{ ready, failed }`), `kino.nuvio.scrapers({ repo })` (the installed ones) and `kino.nuvio.streams({ repo, type, tmdbId, season?, episode?, scrapers?, timeoutMs? })`, which answers `{ results, truncated }` with ONE entry per scraper (`{ scraper, ok: true, stream }` or `{ scraper, ok: false, code, message }`; a failing or slow scraper is never a throw). You turn those into one `Stream` (main copy + `alternatives`) in your `resolve`, deciding order, labels and what to drop. Limits: 20 calls a minute per plugin, up to 12 scrapers per call (`streams` asks 4 at a time), 60 s per scraper (`timeoutMs` 2000 to 60000), `resolve` gets 75 s. Torrent-only scrapers are never installed. The scrapers you install belong to your plugin: not listed in Instalados, removed with it. Always check `typeof kino.nuvio === "object"` first. The Node kit (`kino-plugin-sdk`, current version) knows `nuvio`: `validate.mjs` checks `nuvioRepos`, and `run.mjs` answers `kino.nuvio` from a fixture you write (`KINO_NUVIO_FIXTURE`, sample at <https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk/blob/main/fixtures/nuvio.json>), with the app's checks and limits, so you can test your own logic offline. If the person's copy of the kit says `Unknown capability: "nuvio"`, it is old: have them copy `sdk/`, `contract.json` and `kino.d.ts` again from that repository; never remove the capability to silence it. The kit has no scrapers, so tell the person the real ones are only tested by installing the plugin in Kino 0.9.71 or newer. The catalogue still comes from you (for example `kino.tmdb` and `kino.meta`). Copy the shape of the example in <https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/nuvio-plugins/#example>. This is NOT the person-side Nuvio import (<https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/nuvio/>): that needs no plugin at all.

**Community takedowns**: each author is responsible for their own plugin; Kino only lists community
plugins (no recommendation or promotion). A plugin that breaks the rules for plugins (a `userMessage`
asking for money, passwords or contact data, malware, a rights claim) is removed from the community
index through `community-blocklist.json` at the root of `kinotvapp/kino-plugins` (reasons `claim`,
`malware`, `broken`, `rules`, `author_request`); anyone can report one with the "Reclamo / retiro de
plugin" issue template. Installed copies stay installed, show "Retirado del índice de la comunidad."
and stop updating; a fork needs its own report. Do not build anything that infringes rights or harms
people. See
[Claims and plugin takedowns](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/claims/).

**Sending to the TV** needs nothing from the plugin; it casts best with a correct `mime` and no
`headers` (see [What people see](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/what-people-see/#cast)).

## 5. Checklist before publishing

- [ ] `node sdk/validate.mjs .` exits 0, and `node sdk/validate.mjs . --run <fn> …` passes for every
      declared capability.
- [ ] `node --test test/plugin.test.mjs` passes offline from recorded fixtures.
- [ ] Every host the code, the stream, its segments, subtitles and redirects touch is in `hosts`,
      with the bare domain next to its `*.` form.
- [ ] No missing global (`setTimeout`, `fetch`, `Buffer`, `process`, `require`, `crypto`, `Intl`…)
      in `plugin.js`; no `import`.
- [ ] No `throw` before the first `await` in any async function.
- [ ] Every declared capability is an exported async function (except `download`/`drm`); nothing
      exported that the manifest does not declare is ever called.
- [ ] `id`s are stable and match the pattern; `ref`s keep working when replayed later.
- [ ] User-facing text in Spanish (Bogotá, tuteo), and texts built at run time in `kino.lang`'s
      language (it may be `"en-US"` from Kino 0.9.54); no secrets in the repository.
- [ ] `version` raised; `apiVersion` is the lowest that works (6 only for an apiVersion 6 feature:
      it needs Kino 0.9.50+; 7 only for `tracking` or `segments`: it needs Kino 0.9.51+; 8 only for
      `music`/`podcast` items or `details`: it needs Kino 0.9.54+; 10 only for the `playlists`
      capability: it needs Kino 0.9.65+; 11 only for the `externalResolve` capability (Kino 0.9.66+) or the `nuvio` capability (Kino 0.9.71+);
      12 only for `syncProvider`, the `sync` block or a `link`/`help` setting: it needs Kino 0.9.74+;
      13 only for `socket`, `byteSource`, `storageLarge`, `catalog`, `qrScan`, `imageSource` or a `qr` setting:
      Kino 0.9.74+; 14 only for screens and their capabilities (Kino 0.9.74+); 15 only for `identity`, `notifications`
      or `pluginStore` (Kino 0.9.77+); 16 only for `coins` (Kino 0.9.78+); 17 and 18 only for what section 2 lists for them:
      Kino 0.9.81+; 21 only for `files`: Kino 0.9.82+; 22 only for `progress`: the next Kino release, or `enhancements["22"]`;
      23 only for `playerSlot`: the same release, or `enhancements["23"]`).
      A plugin that uses `kino.nuvio` declares `nuvioRepos`, `"streamHosts": "any"` and checks
      `typeof kino.nuvio === "object"`.
- [ ] A plugin with no video of its own declares `"catalogOnly": true` and still exports a `resolve`
      that throws `not_found` (for Kino 0.9.53 and older).
- [ ] Audio: every audio item has `kind` `"music"` or `"podcast"` and `"apiVersion": 8`; with
      `episodes` declared, `episodes(ref)` answers every audio ref, even a single track.
- [ ] Playlists: if you export any of `playlists`, `playlistItems`, `playlistCreate`,
      `playlistAddItem`, `playlistRemoveItem` or `playlistReorder`, declare the `playlists`
      capability and `"apiVersion": 10`; export only the functions your service actually supports --
      none is required.
- [ ] External resolver: a plugin that hands a title to another app declares `"apiVersion": 11` and the
      `externalResolve` capability (nothing to export), optionally `externalResolver` (`{ package, apk?, fdroid?, downloader? }`) in the
      manifest, and `resolve()` (or one `alternatives` entry) answers `{ external: { protocol, ref, resolver? } }` with no
      `url`; the plugin does not promise an app is installed, keeps a fallback copy when it can, and never uses `external`
      when it can produce the URL itself. Its `hosts` list only what the plugin's own code fetches, not what the resolver
      app reaches.
- [ ] Sync provider: `"apiVersion": 12`, `syncProvider` declared, `syncPull` and `syncPush` exported with one
      object argument, the blob stored and returned byte for byte, `conflict` thrown when the remote moved,
      `sync.maxBlobBytes` ≤ 4194304, `keySecret` (required) a long random token in a `password` setting with no
      `default`, `provision` lists what a second device needs, no token in any error/status/log, offline tests
      with a 4 MiB blob both ways, and the person was told in plain Spanish who can read the data.
- [ ] apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74): `byteSource` exports `read` and answers exactly the range asked as base64,
      with no JavaScript loop over the bytes; `imageSource` exports `image` and puts no secret in a handle;
      `kino.ws` only to declared hosts, every socket closed; `kino.qr.scan` only from an `action`/`panelAction`;
      `storageLarge` and `kino.catalog` hold nothing that must survive a restore; a `"sync": false` password is a
      one-device value (in `sync.provision` only as a one-shot secret the plugin clears once used, never as
      `keySecret`) and a `"sync": false` text is not in `sync.provision`; `run.mjs . read` and a Node test
      (`askRead`) cover `read`, `run.mjs . image` covers `image`; every `kino.crypto` byte operation you use is
      feature-detected (they depend on the Kino version, not on the manifest).
- [ ] apiVersion 14 / screens: `node sdk/run.mjs . screen` and `node sdk/run.mjs --device tv . screen` print the tree
      with nothing dropped; every screen's `AppBar` has `mergeWithKinoBar: true` and `dense: true` and a `leading` that is a real
      exit (`{ close: true }` on the front page); every event name the tree uses is handled in `screenEvent`; no state kept in module
      variables; a node the TV must stop on to read has `canRequestFocus`; below apiVersion 14 the screen and its
      capabilities come through `enhancements` and `validate.mjs` reports no dropped block; nothing secret in
      `kino.shared`, a room message or an AI prompt; the AI reply and `kino.shared.get` values are validated.
- [ ] apiVersion 15 / a store: `node sdk/validate.mjs .` shows the consent lines and no problem; `node sdk/run.mjs . storeSync`
      prints entries with nothing reported as `[dropped by Kino]` (every entry has a valid `address`, `id` and `name`);
      a live store exports `storeSync`, `storeList` and `storeSearch`; the list is complete (`full: true`) or the change is
      right (`removed`); `state` is small; no secret in an entry; the store never claims to install or approve anything.
- [ ] apiVersion 15 / `identity`, `notifications`: the plugin works with them switched off or refused (`permission_denied`); no
      token logged or shown; a notice's `id` groups events, its `go` points to the plugin's own screen.
- [ ] apiVersion 16 / `coins`: feature-detected (`typeof kino.coins === "object"`); on `disabled` nothing about kinos shows;
      `give` only after the person's tap; the screen works when the call answers `not_available`.
- [ ] apiVersion 17: `kino.library.stats`, `perProfile`, `pages`, `hero`, `share`, `enableJob` and `go.search` `scope` used
      only with `"apiVersion": 17` or more; `share` hidden on a TV; a `perProfile` job has `runOn: "any"` and no `enabledBy`, and
      catches `not_allowed` from `kino.notifications`/`kino.coins`/`kino.seed`.
- [ ] apiVersion 18 / `appThemes`: `node sdk/validate.mjs .` prints no theme warning you did not expect (phone and TV); the
      background is dark and every text, accent and focus pair reads; ids are final; `name` has `es` and `en`; `adjustable`
      offers swatches; a `price` carries the author's real `payTo` and the plugin does not declare `coins` just to sell; a
      themes-only plugin has `"categories": ["themes"]`, no capabilities (or only `screen`) and `"hosts": []`; a screen that
      turns the theme on reads `activeTheme` and sends `go.useTheme` only from a tap.
- [ ] apiVersion 20 / provider: `provides` at the top level with `"apiVersion": 20` or in `enhancements["20"]`; one export
      `proto_<door>_<name>` per call and stream, spelled exactly (`node sdk/validate.mjs .` fails a missing one); every answer
      matches `out` (a stream answers `{ items, cursor }`, the cursor small JSON); nothing private in answers or thrown
      messages; a short `summary`; the door documented in the README; a published door only grows (new calls, optional
      fields); each call tried with `node sdk/run.mjs . proto <door>.<call> '<json>'` (and a bad argument), each stream with
      `proto <door>.<stream>` and again from the cursor it printed. Provides-only: no capability, no setting, no
      `providesOnly` field, `everySeconds` within 30..86,400.
- [ ] apiVersion 20 / consumer: `consumes` with the provider's exact `repo` and `door` and only the names used (checked by
      hand: the kit ignores `repo`); the same repo in `recommends` (no `!` from validate about it); `hosts` `[]` for a
      screen-only consumer (or only real hosts its own `kino.fetch` reaches), never `example.com` (no `!` about a placeholder host); `test/provider` replaced by a copy of the
      real provider; an install view with `go.installPlugin` while `installed[repo] !== true`, and a
      sentence for `provider_missing` while it is `true`; every `kino.plugins.call` in `try`/`catch` with ES + EN messages; no
      call from a `job`; a `protocol` handler that tolerates repeated items (tried with `--cursor`); the screen drawn with
      `installed` `true` and `false`, `--lang en` and `--device tv` with no `dropped` line; tried with
      `node sdk/run.mjs --provider …` and in Kino 0.9.81+ with the provider installed, switched off and removed.
- [ ] Sharing (every plugin, recommended): a «Compartir» button in the plugin's screen (a title page with the title and/or the
      bar, text only) that opens a sheet with an editable text and an «Adjuntar el título» switch and calls
      `kino.plugins.call("social", "share", …)`; `consumes` `social` → `kinotvapp/kino-social` door `wall` call `share` and the
      same repo in `recommends`; `provider_missing` answered with `go.installPlugin` (or a sentence when it is installed but
      off); no `kino.plugins` → a toast; the person told the post waits in Kino Social as a draft (nothing published on their
      behalf); ES + EN texts. From Kino 0.9.84, `openFrom.routes` declared for the routes a card may open, and each such route
      checks its `route.args`.
- [ ] apiVersion 22 / `progress`: `"apiVersion": 22` or `enhancements["22"]`; `typeof kino.progress === "object"` checked;
      the exact place in `resume` (well under 1024 bytes); `get` answering `null` handled; the plugin's own "keep reading" row
      built from `list()` (Kino draws none) inside a `home()` that returns an array of rows with `id`s and items with `id`s;
      every call in `try`/`catch`. `Image` `headers` only on pictures whose hosts (and the Referer's) are in `hosts`.
- [ ] apiVersion 23 / `playerSlot`: the capability and the `slot` block together; both `playerSlot` and `playerSlotAction`
      exported; answers use declared ids and their kinds; `refreshMs` 2,000..60,000 (60,000 for a clock in minutes); code copes
      with a context without `kind`; no live-only function behind a button; `node sdk/run.mjs . playerSlot` and
      `node sdk/validate.mjs .` pass.
- [ ] `sdk/test/` is not in the plugin's repository (the kit's own suite).
- [ ] No helper exported under the name `details` unless it is the real `details` export (reserved
      from apiVersion 8).
- [ ] `kino.meta`, `kino.tmdb` and the `captureAll` options are used only behind their feature checks
      (`typeof kino.meta === "function"`, `typeof kino.tmdb === "function"`,
      `kino.browser.captureAll === true`); no TMDB key in the code.
- [ ] No `"debug": true` in the manifest unless the person asked for it (every plugin has a
      "Modo debug" switch in Kino's Ajustes; `true` only turns it on by default for everyone). If `telemetry` is declared, the person agreed and
      the logs hold codes and counts only.
- [ ] Every `userMessage` passes the rules (Spanish, ≤ 160, no URL/digits/money/credentials/contact)
      and `run.mjs` shows it; 18+ content carries `adult: true`.
- [ ] `"entry"` and `"icon"` have **no leading `./`** (`"plugin.js"`).
- [ ] If `"browser": true`: every server that works with `kino.fetch` uses it; `kino.browser.capture`
      is only called from `resolve`; nothing tries to solve, click or bypass a captcha or bot check;
      `blocked`/`timeout`/`busy`/`browser_unavailable` move on to the next server or end cleanly; the
      captured `headers` are returned with the Stream; several servers are labelled lazy copies.
- [ ] If signed: `"apiVersion": 5`, `signature` present, `node sdk/validate.mjs . --repo owner/repo`
      verified it after the last edit, `*.pem` in `.gitignore`, no `.pem` tracked, the person knows to
      back the key up.
- [ ] Public repository, manifest at the root, topic `kino-plugin` on THAT repository (mandatory: without it the
      app never finds the plugin), not a fork. Manifest `description` written (the card shows it);
      the GitHub About description is optional and not read by the app.
- [ ] The person installed it in Kino and it searched, listed episodes or tracks and played.

## 6. Being discovered ("De la comunidad")

**From Kino 0.9.77 (apiVersion 15)** the app no longer searches GitHub by itself: the community
list comes from the built-in store, Kino Plugins (a `pluginStore` plugin), which reads an index built every day from the
repositories with the `kino-plugin` topic plus what changed since. The rules below are still what gets a plugin into that list.
People see it in the store view's "De la comunidad" tab (the old "Buscar en GitHub" tab is gone), beside "De Kino" and
"Instalados". There is one plugin per `id` across stores.
Anyone can also publish a store of their own (see apiVersion 15 above).

Kino lists community plugins itself; nobody approves them. The step-by-step for the person, with
exact clicks and how to check it, is [Get listed in Kino](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/listed/).
Every rule, as the app applies it (full detail:
[Publishing › Get found](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/publish/#get-found)):

1. Public GitHub repository at `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (owner `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}$`,
   repo `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$`), **not a fork** (use the template's "Use this template").
2. Topic exactly `kino-plugin`, **mandatory**, on the repository that holds `kino-plugin.json`
   (`gh repo edit owner/repo --add-topic kino-plugin`). Verify:
   `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo | tr -d ' \n' | grep -o '"topics":\[[^]]*\]'` must list it. The card shows the
   manifest `description`; the GitHub About description is optional and does not affect discovery.
3. `kino-plugin.json` at the repository **root on the default branch**
   (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/HEAD/kino-plugin.json`), at most 16 KB, valid
   by the installer's rules, `apiVersion` not above the person's Kino (17 to 20 from Kino 0.9.81;
   16 from Kino 0.9.78; 15 on 0.9.77; 14 on 0.9.74 to 0.9.76, 11 on 0.9.66 to 0.9.73, 10 on 0.9.65, 9 on 0.9.55 to 0.9.64, 8 on 0.9.54, 7 on 0.9.51 to 0.9.53, 6 on 0.9.50, 5 on 0.9.45 to 0.9.49; a signed plugin needs Kino 0.9.45+), and not
   `"discoverable": false`.
4. An `id` of your own: never a recommended plugin's id from another repo (today `internet-archive`,
   `own-server`), never the template's `archive-org`; the same id installed from
   another repo hides it on that device.
5. Order and reach. **From Kino 0.9.54** the app reads one page of 100 results at a time
   (`https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=topic:kino-plugin+fork:false&sort=stars&order=desc&per_page=100`,
   or `sort=updated`), in the order the person picks ("Populares", most stars, the default; or
   "Recientes", most recently updated); "Cargar más" reads the next 100 (up to GitHub's 1,000), and
   "Buscar en GitHub" adds the typed words matched against the repository's name and description
   (`in:name,description`), so a plugin with no stars is found too. **Kino 0.9.53 and older** make one
   request with `per_page=50` sorted by stars, keep the first 30 well-formed results, then drop the
   ones whose manifest fails (they still used a slot): below the top 30 a plugin is not listed there.
6. Timing: each device searches when its plugins screen opens and its copy is older than 12 hours,
   or on "Actualizar" (never twice within 60 s); 403/429 means waiting `Retry-After` /
   `X-RateLimit-Reset` / 15 min (1 min to 24 h). GitHub indexes new topics on its own schedule;
   raw files are cached about 5 minutes.
7. If GitHub cannot answer, a backup list published by the Kino team is used; it is rebuilt from the
   same search, so nothing needs requesting. A repository in `community-blocklist.json` (a claim was
   upheld) never shows, in either list. From Kino 0.9.77 the list is refreshed with every store sync.
8. Nothing installs by itself: the person always sees the consent sheet ("Plugin no verificado…").
9. Where to look in the app (before Kino 0.9.77, apiVersion 15): Plugins (phone: menu ☰ → Plugins; TV: Ajustes → Plugins), the "De la
   comunidad" tab, beside "Recomendados" ("Plugins de la comunidad — Kino no los revisa ni responde por
   su contenido.") with its "Actualizar" button (from Kino 0.9.54 also "Populares"/"Recientes",
   "Cargar más" and "Buscar en GitHub"); also the first-run "Elige tus fuentes", which has the same
   tabs. On the web: <https://github.com/topics/kino-plugin>.

To debug "it does not appear": open the search URL in a browser and find the repo in `items`; open
the raw manifest URL; run `node sdk/validate.mjs .`; check the id; tap "Actualizar" after 60 s.

## 7. Common mistakes

- A screen with two bars (no `mergeWithKinoBar: true` + `dense: true` on its `AppBar`), the booleans on only some screens, or a
  merged bar whose `leading` is not a real exit (`{ close: true }` on the front page, a back elsewhere).
- Treating a screen opened from Kino's Home as if it always had a route: `route.name` is `"main"` there, your front page; and
  giving a Home row item a route instead of `open: { screen: { args } }`, so Back has no front page to return to (push the
  detail from the `open` answer).
- A reader that measures bytes or sizes pictures by hand instead of `Image` `fit: "width"`, a scroll with `zoom` and `onScroll`, and
  `pages` with `reverse`/`progress`; a spinner where a `Skeleton` keeps the layout; thirty chips where a bottom sheet with a
  search field fits; a screen that goes past its 600 nodes.
- `kino.progress`: waiting for Kino to show a "keep reading" row (it draws none: build it from `list()`); reading
  `here.resume` without checking that `get` did not answer `null`; putting the page's content in `resume` (≤ 1024 bytes, else
  `too_large`); expecting it to work in a `perProfile` job run for another profile (`not_allowed`); a `home()` that returns one
  row object instead of an array, a row or an item without `id`.
- `playerSlot`: a `slot` block without the capability (or the reverse); leaving out `playerSlotAction` because there is no
  button; answering an id that is not declared, or a kind other than the element's (dropped, never repaired); a fourth
  element; reading `context.kind` without checking it (the bare context has none); a `refreshMs` below 2,000 expecting faster
  updates; expecting it on a phone; relying on a live button reachable only with Menu; expecting `seekToMs` to work on a
  channel.
- `Image` `headers` on a picture whose host is not in `hosts` (they are not sent, the site answers 403), a `Referer` on an
  undeclared host (left out), or other header names (dropped).

- Declaring `*.site.com` only, then failing on `site.com` (or the reverse after a redirect).
- A CDN, a subtitle host or a license server missing from `hosts`: playback stops with an error.
- Using `fetch`, `setTimeout` or `Buffer` because the Node kit ran fine.
- Writing `plugin.js` with an `import`/`require` of a second local file: Kino only loads `entry`,
  there is nothing for it to resolve on-device. Bundle to one file first (section 3, step 3).
- Validating arguments with `throw` before the first `await` in a helper wrapped in `try`/`catch`.
- Returning ids with `/`, `:` or spaces (dropped), or ids that change between calls (the library
  loses the title).
- Returning `next` or a row `ref` without declaring and exporting `browse` (they are dropped).
- Putting expiring links in `ref` instead of resolving them fresh in `resolve`.
- Network calls at the top level of the module (install fails).
- Forgetting to raise `version`, so the fix never reaches anyone.
- Writing `"entry": "./plugin.js"` (or `"icon": "./icon.png"`): refused by Kino 0.9.45 and older.
- Signing, then editing `plugin.js` or `version` without signing again; committing the `.pem`; making
  a new key for an already published plugin (everyone must reinstall).
- Declaring `apiVersion` 2 or 3 without needing it (older Kino builds cannot install it); declaring
  6 for nothing (Kino 0.9.49 and older refuse it).
- Publishing with `"debug": true` without being asked (it turns error panels on by default for everyone).
- Calling `kino.fetch`, `kino.storage` or a private-key handle from `sign()`, or putting a
  `kino.secret()` marker in `signContext`.
- A `userMessage` with a URL, a phone number, "WhatsApp", "paga"/"recarga" or the person's own input:
  dropped silently at best, the plugin removed at worst.
- A `status` or `action` setting without exporting `settingsStatus` / `action`; `"section"` without
  exporting `section` (install fails).
- `kino.html.select` "failing" under Node: it only exists in the app; test that part in Kino.
- Forking the template: forks never appear in "De la comunidad".
- Keeping the template's `"id": "archive-org"`: install refused ("Ya hay un plugin con ese id") and
  hidden from the community list wherever the Internet Archive plugin is installed.
- English or voseo in what the person reads.
- Copying a browser's `Accept-Encoding` or `Host` header and expecting it to be sent.
- Pasting a secret into `kino-plugin.json` or `plugin.js` instead of sealing it (author keys) or
  asking for it in a `password` setting (the person's credentials); committing `.kino-secrets.json`.
- A sync provider that decodes, re-encodes or trims the blob, keeps extra copies of it (memory), puts the
  token in an error or status text, uses a password a person picks as `keySecret`, or promises the plugin
  "cannot read" the data (with `keySecret`, always required, it can).
- `setSettings` on a `url` setting (or a `password` below apiVersion 13), or a `link` whose `confirm` is the answering action or an
  action with its own `confirm` question: refused whole.
- Keeping screen state in a module variable (it is gone when the runtime closes), fetching inside `screen()` instead of the
  `open` event, or naming a node's event `open`.
- Free values in a screen tree (`"padding": 10`, `"color": "#FF0000"`, `"width": 300`): off-scale values are dropped; use the
  spacing and size scales and the colour roles. A node invalid in one size class is dropped whole.
- Sending a person-only `go` (`url`, `copy`, `titleByIds`, `liveChannel`, `syncProvider`, `useTheme`, `setExperience`, `installPlugin`) or
  `share`/`enableJob` from `open`, a timer, a change or an `onClose`, or more than 5 s after the tap: dropped.
- A TV screen where a status card cannot be reached with the remote (no `canRequestFocus`), or a `share` button shown on a TV.
- A theme with a light background, grey text on a grey surface or an accent that does not stand out: Kino drops those tokens
  and the theme looks like Kino's. Run `validate.mjs` and read its warnings for the phone and the TV.
- `background.image`, an unknown token (`colors.primary`), a number given as a string, or a theme `id` with capitals: the whole
  manifest is refused.
- Declaring `coins` to sell a theme (not needed: Kino sells it), a `price` without `payTo` or with someone else's account, or
  promising the person a theme "unlocks" anything beyond the look.
- Changing the light/full experience or the theme without the person's tap (`go.useTheme` from `open`), or expecting
  `go.useTheme` to turn on another plugin's theme: refused.
- Confusing the apiVersion 6 `theme` (your own pages' colours) with `appThemes` (the whole app).
- Plugin protocol: calling another plugin's exports, `import`ing its code or fetching its hosts instead of using
  `kino.plugins.call` through a declared `consumes` entry; declaring `provides`/`consumes` as capabilities; naming exports
  `proto_movies_by_id` or `movies_byId` instead of exactly `proto_<door>_<name>`; an alias, door or call name with `_` or
  `-`; a `repo` given as a URL or with `@ref`; forgetting `recommends`, so `installed` never arrives and the install gate
  cannot work; drawing the game (or anything interactive) while the provider is missing, or sending `go.installPlugin` from
  `open` or a timer; one button that "installs everything"; sending a number as a string (`"1990"`: `bad_input`, never
  coerced); calling `kino.plugins.call` from a `job`; retrying `rate_limited` in a loop; assuming stream items never repeat;
  passing a token or the person's private input as an argument; a provider that returns a sealed secret or throws messages
  with private data; a top-level `provides` below apiVersion 20 (refused: use `enhancements["20"]`); removing or renaming a
  published call.
- Plugin protocol, kit and manifest: a screen-only consumer with a placeholder (`example.com`, a `.invalid` name) or an
  invented host instead of `"hosts": []` (a lie on the consent sheet); `"hosts": []` in a consumer that also declares another
  capability (refused: it needs a real host); declaring `image.tmdb.org` only to draw posters (not needed); trusting the scaffold's stand-in `test/provider`
  as if it were the real provider; writing `"providesOnly": true` (no such field: it is derived); a declared call whose
  `proto_` export is missing or misspelled (validate fails it; Kino would answer `provider_failed`); `everySeconds` below 30
  (clamped); a cursor that carries the items (the answer passes 64 KB: `bad_output`); running `screenEvent` in the kit
  without `--context '{"installed":{…:true}}'`, so the gated consumer answers nothing and looks broken; trusting the kit to
  check `repo` (it serves the first provider with the door); treating `installed === true` as "the provider works" (it is
  also `true` when the provider is off).
- Screen trees that look right and draw nothing: `SingleChildScrollView` with `child` instead of `children` (an empty
  scroll, no warning); `appBar: { title }` without `"type": "AppBar"` (the bar is dropped); `FilledButton` (unknown: use
  `ElevatedButton`/`TextButton` with `labelText`/`labelTextEn` and `onPressed`); a `Text` with `text: ""`. Read stderr: a
  `dropped` line never changes the exit code.
- Copying `sdk/test/` into the plugin (more than 60 files nobody needs) and then running a bare `node --test`.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/ (docs/index.en.md) -->

# Writing a Kino plugin

A Kino plugin is a video source that anyone can publish as a small GitHub repository: one JSON
manifest and one JavaScript file. A person types `owner/repo` in Kino, sees which sites the plugin
will talk to, accepts, and from then on the plugin is one more source: its results show up in
search and on Home, and its titles open, list episodes, play in Kino's player, keep progress and
appear in "Continuar viendo" and the library like any other title.

You can write, run and test a plugin on your computer with Node before you ever touch the app. This
guide has everything you need: the file layout, the manifest, the contract your code must meet, the
API Kino gives you, every limit, the quirks of the JavaScript engine, and how to publish.

The complete API demo is [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server)
("Tu servidor" 1.5.0: every feature up to apiVersion 7 working end to end); [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive)
(Internet Archive) is the simplest starting template, and
[kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio)
(Internet Archive Audio) is the reference for [music and podcasts](music.md) (apiVersion 8, Kino
0.9.54). The first two carry the `sdk/` folder, the Node kit; the kit alone is in [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk). Two more files describe the contract for machines (both on the [Reference](reference/index.md)
page): `contract.json` holds every number and rule the app enforces (the tables in this guide are
generated from it, and the app's tests pin its own constants to it), and `kino.d.ts` declares the
whole `kino` API for your editor (`/// <reference path="./kino.d.ts" />` at the top of `plugin.js`).

## The 5-minute path { #five-minutes }

1. **Start from the template.** Create your repository from
   [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive) -- the
   simplest one -- or from [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server)
   if you need settings, a session, downloads or live channels, or from
   [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio) for
   music and podcasts ("Use this template" on any of them,
   or clone it and copy `sdk/`). Do not *fork* it: Kino's community search leaves forks
   out ([Get found](publish.md#get-found)). Or let the kit write a skeleton:
   `node sdk/init.mjs my-plugin --host example.com`.
2. **Declare what you need** in `kino-plugin.json`: an `id`, the `hosts` you will call and the
   `capabilities` you export ([The manifest](manifest.md)).
3. **Write the functions** in `plugin.js`: `search` and/or `home`, and `resolve` at least
   ([The contract](contract.md), [The `kino` API](kino-api.md)).
4. **Check it the way Kino does:** `node sdk/validate.mjs .`, then
   `node sdk/run.mjs . search "algo"` ([Test it locally](test-locally.md)).
5. **Publish** it as a public repository with the topic `kino-plugin` (mandatory: without it Kino cannot find it), and install it in Kino from
   Ajustes > Plugins by typing `owner/repo` or pasting the URL of its `kino-plugin.json`
   ([Publishing](publish.md)).
6. **Get Kino to show it by itself** in "De la comunidad": the topic, name and description, and how
   to check it, in [Get listed in Kino](listed.md).

Using an AI assistant? Give it [the ready-made prompt](ai.md): it reads this whole guide from
`llms-full.txt` and follows `AGENTS.md`.

## What a plugin is { #what-a-plugin-is }

A public GitHub repository, or a folder inside one, with:

```
kino-plugin.json   the manifest (required)
plugin.js          the code: a single ES module (required; its name is set by "entry")
icon.png           optional, square, at most 128 KB
README.md          for humans
```

Kino runs your code in a sandbox: no filesystem, no timers, no other plugins, no access to the
person's data. The only way out is `kino.fetch`, which can reach only the hosts your manifest
declares and the person approved on screen, plus the servers the person typed in your plugin's
settings (see [The manifest](manifest.md)). Plugins never reach each other directly: from Kino 0.9.81 one can use the
**doors** another one opens, always through Kino, which checks every request and answer ([The plugin protocol](protocol.md)).

Kino loads exactly one JavaScript file, so there is nothing for an `import` to resolve to. If you
use a build step or a library, bundle everything into that single file -- see
[Splitting your code across files](engine-limits.md#splitting-files) for a worked example.

**How people install it.** In Kino, Ajustes > Plugins, they type the address of your repository:

| They type | Kino reads |
| --- | --- |
| `owner/repo` | the repository root, default branch |
| `owner/repo/sub/dir` | a folder inside the repository |
| `owner/repo@v1.2.0` | a branch, tag or commit (the name cannot contain `/`); also works with a folder |
| `https://github.com/owner/repo` or `.../tree/<ref>/<path>` | the same, pasted from the browser |
| `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/<ref>/<path>/kino-plugin.json` (or a `github.com/.../blob/<ref>/.../kino-plugin.json`, also `/raw/`) | the folder that `.json` file is in, at that ref; any other kind of file is refused |
| `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/owner/repo[@<ref>]/<path>/kino-plugin.json` (also `fastly`, `gcore`, `testingcf` and `quantil.jsdelivr.net`) | the same repository folder, read from GitHub: no `@ref` or `@latest` is the default branch; the ref must be an exact branch, tag or commit (`@main`, `@v1.2.0`), so a version range (`@1`, `@^1.2`, `@1.x`) is refused |
| `https://<any public server>/<path>/kino-plugin.json` | a plugin hosted outside GitHub: see [Installing from a manifest URL](#manifest-url) |

The field in Kino says "Escribe usuario/repositorio de GitHub o pega la URL del manifest
(kino-plugin.json)". A `?query` or `#fragment` in a pasted URL is ignored. A ref that only comes from a
pasted URL (`tree`, `blob`, `raw`, `raw.githubusercontent.com` or jsDelivr's `@ref`) is not a pin: a
plugin with [sealed secrets](manifest.md#secrets) pasted that way installs from the default branch.

For a repository address, Kino downloads `kino-plugin.json`, your entry file and the icon from
`raw.githubusercontent.com`, which is why the repository has to be public. A URL of a repository's
`kino-plugin.json` (on GitHub, raw.githubusercontent.com or jsDelivr) always becomes that repository's
address, so sealed secrets, signatures and community search keep working for it.

### Installing from a manifest URL { #manifest-url }

Your plugin does not have to live on GitHub (new in the Kino version after 0.9.49). People can paste the
`https` URL of its `kino-plugin.json` on any public server: your own site, GitHub Pages, a CDN such as
jsDelivr's `npm/`. Kino stores it as the address `url:https://…/kino-plugin.json` (scheme and host
lowercased, default port, query and fragment dropped): that URL is the plugin's identity, and it
travels as is to the person's other devices with plugin sync.

- `entry` and `icon` are read relative to the manifest URL: `"entry": "plugin.js"` next to
  `https://example.com/kino/kino-plugin.json` is `https://example.com/kino/plugin.js`.
- `https` only (`http://` is refused with "Kino solo instala plugins desde direcciones https…"), on a
  public name: no IP addresses, no `localhost`, no single-label or `.local`/`.lan` names, no
  user:password in the URL, and the file has to be named exactly `kino-plugin.json`. A name that
  resolves to a private address, and a redirect off `https` or to such a host, are refused too.
- **No sealed secrets**: seals are bound to a GitHub repository, so a manifest with `secrets`
  installed from a URL is refused ("Este plugin trae datos sellados, y esos solo funcionan si lo
  instalas desde su repositorio de GitHub…"). Publish such a plugin on GitHub.
- **Unsigned**: a `signature` is bound to `owner/repo`, so it is not checked and the plugin installs
  (and shows) as unsigned.
- Everything else is the same as a repository install: the consent sheet, `hosts` and every approval
  rule, and updates: Kino re-reads the same URL and applies a higher `version`, asking again when it
  needs more than was approved. The plugin is never listed by community search (that only finds
  GitHub repositories with the `kino-plugin` topic).

**Stremio addons** are a Kino feature for people, not something you write: in the same field a person
can paste the address of a Stremio addon's `manifest.json` (or a `stremio://` link) and Kino generates
a plugin for it. Nothing in this guide changes for your plugin.

!!! tip "New: identity, notices and plugin stores (apiVersion 15, with Kino 0.9.77)"
    A plugin can know who the person is without a sign-up ([Identity](identity.md)), leave notices in the Home bell
    ([Notices](notifications.md)) and be a **store**: a source of plugins for Kino's store, backed by GitHub, by its own
    server or by a JSON file ([Plugin stores](plugin-stores.md), with two [example stores](store-examples.md)). What
    changed: [What's new](changelog.md#v15).

!!! tip "New: Kino coins (apiVersion 16, with Kino 0.9.78) and apiVersion 17"
    The `coins` capability lets a plugin show the person's Kino coin balance and give coins away (`kino.coins`), and
    `kino.sync.setActive` lets a sync provider switch itself on or off. `apiVersion` 17 (with Kino 0.9.81) brings
    `kino.library.stats`, per-profile jobs, the `pages` widget and more. What changed: [What's new](changelog.md#v17).

!!! tip "New: your plugin's own screens (apiVersion 14, with Kino 0.9.74)"
    A plugin can draw its own full screen inside Kino: columns, cards, lists, tabs, forms, pop-ups and Kino's own poster
    rows, with Kino's look, on the phone and on the TV from the same JSON tree. Start with [Screens](screens.md) and the
    [component catalogue](screen-components.md); rooms over the Internet, background jobs, results shared between
    devices and Kino's text AI arrive too. What changed: [What's new](changelog.md#v14).

# A first plugin

Two files. `kino-plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "hello-archive",
  "name": "Hola Archive",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Películas de archive.org, en veinte líneas",
  "hosts": ["archive.org", "*.archive.org"],
  "capabilities": ["search", "resolve"]
}
```

`plugin.js`:

```js
const BASE = "https://archive.org";

export async function search(query) {
  const q = "title:(" + query.q + ") AND mediatype:(movies)";
  const url = BASE + "/advancedsearch.php?q=" + encodeURIComponent(q) +
    "&fl%5B%5D=identifier&fl%5B%5D=title&rows=10&output=json";
  const r = await kino.fetch(url);
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error("archive.org respondió " + r.status);
  return r.json().response.docs.map((d) => ({
    id: d.identifier,
    ref: d.identifier,
    title: String(d.title),
    kind: "movie",
    poster: BASE + "/services/img/" + encodeURIComponent(d.identifier),
  }));
}

export async function resolve(ref) {
  const r = await kino.fetch(BASE + "/metadata/" + encodeURIComponent(ref));
  const file = r.json().files.find((f) => f.name.endsWith(".mp4"));
  if (!file) throw new Error("este item no tiene un mp4");
  const path = file.name.split("/").map(encodeURIComponent).join("/");
  return { url: BASE + "/download/" + encodeURIComponent(ref) + "/" + path };
}
```

Run it (needs Node 18 or newer; see [Test it locally](test-locally.md)):

```
node sdk/run.mjs ./plugin.js search "metropolis"
node sdk/run.mjs ./plugin.js resolve TheGiantOfMetropolis1961
```

Or let the kit write the skeleton for you: `node sdk/init.mjs my-plugin --host example.com` creates
`my-plugin/` with a manifest, a `plugin.js` with every function, a README and a replay-based test. Add
`--with byteSource,images,catalog,socket` (any of them) for an apiVersion 13 skeleton (Kino 0.9.74
and later) that declares those capabilities and carries a working, commented example of each.

This one is deliberately naive (a query with a `/` or a lone `AND` makes archive.org answer with
an error, and nothing checks the shape of the reply). The reference plugin,
[kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive), is the robust
version of the same idea; read [how it is built](examples.md#reference-plugin) before you build on it.

## Where the `sdk/` comes from { #get-the-sdk }

The **kit** is the `sdk/` folder inside the example plugins. Nothing to install with npm or anything
else: they are `.mjs` files you run with Node 18 or newer. The easiest way to get it is to create
your plugin from a template, so the kit is already inside.

**Steps (recommended):**

1. Open the template closest to what you want to build:
    - [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server): the
      complete example, "Tu servidor" 1.5.0 (settings, user and password, downloads, live channels, and
      every feature up to apiVersion 7).
    - [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive): the
      simplest, for a site with search and videos.
    - [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio):
      music and podcasts (apiVersion 8, Kino 0.9.54; see [Music and podcasts](music.md)).
2. Top right, press the green **Use this template → Create a new repository** button. Name your
   repository and keep it **public**.
3. Download it to your computer and check the kit works:

    ```
    git clone https://github.com/<your-user>/<your-repository>.git
    cd <your-repository>
    node sdk/validate.mjs .
    ```

    If you see `✓ Kino would accept this plugin`, you are ready to start changing `plugin.js` and
    `kino-plugin.json`.

**Already have a plugin, or an old copy of the kit?** The kit alone is in
[kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk). Copy its `sdk/` folder,
`contract.json` and `kino.d.ts` into your plugin (the three go together: the kit reads `contract.json`, and
`kino.d.ts` is what your editor shows for `kino`). An out-of-date copy is one reason a plugin that
passes the kit fails in the app, or the editor offers an API that has changed.

!!! warning "Use the template, not the Fork button"
    **Use this template** creates a new, independent repository that is yours. **Fork** creates a
    copy linked to the original, and Kino **does not show forks** in "De la comunidad"
    ([Get found](publish.md#get-found)). If you fork, your plugin will never show up in the app's
    search.

**Already have your own repository?** Copy just the `sdk/` folder from either template into it (for
example by downloading the ZIP from **Code → Download ZIP**). The commands are the same:
`node sdk/validate.mjs .`, `node sdk/run.mjs …`.

## Next steps { #next }

- [The manifest](manifest.md): every field and what the person approves.
- [The contract](contract.md): the shapes you return and the rules Kino checks them with.
- [Limits and engine quirks](engine-limits.md): read [the rejection trap](engine-limits.md#rejection-trap)
  before you write a helper (it matters on Kino 0.9.49 and older).
- [Get listed in Kino](listed.md): once it works, the five steps for people to find it in the app
  without knowing its address.

# Example plugins

Three published plugins, all public, all installable in Kino, and all usable as a template. Start
from **Internet Archive** for the simplest possible template; start from **Tu servidor**, the
complete API demo, when your source is a server the person owns, or when you want to see every
feature up to apiVersion 7 working end to end; start from **Internet Archive Audio** for music and
podcasts ([apiVersion 8](music.md), Kino 0.9.54).

<div class="grid cards" markdown>

-   ![](assets/own-server-icon.png){ .card-icon } **Tu servidor** · `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server`

    ---

    **The complete API demo.** A media server at home (Jellyfin, Emby, a NAS…): the person types its
    address, user and password. Version 1.5.0, apiVersion 7: `"hosts": []`, every setting type and the
    full settings form, a session kept with `kino.storage`, `kino.rank`, seasons, `download`, copies,
    request signing, `channels` in every shape, a section and Categorías tiles, `migrate`, `meta`,
    `subtitles`, `tracking` and `segments`, plus a reference server (`server.mjs`) to run it against
    with nothing of your own.

    [:octicons-repo-template-16: Use as template](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server/generate){ .md-button .md-button--primary }
    [:octicons-mark-github-16: View on GitHub](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server){ .md-button }

-   ![](assets/archive-icon.png){ .card-icon } **Internet Archive** · `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive`

    ---

    Public-domain films and classic TV from archive.org. **The simplest template to start from**:
    one manifest, one JavaScript file, no build step, all five capabilities plus `download`, and one
    `list` setting for the person's own archive.org addresses (apiVersion 4), with the `sdk/` kit,
    `GUIDE.md`, `contract.json` and `kino.d.ts`.

    [:octicons-repo-template-16: Use as template](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive/generate){ .md-button .md-button--primary }
    [:octicons-mark-github-16: View on GitHub](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive){ .md-button }

-   ![](assets/archive-audio-icon.png){ .card-icon } **Internet Archive Audio** · `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio`

    ---

    **The reference audio plugin.** Free music, live concerts, audiobooks and old-time radio from
    archive.org, as `music` and `podcast` items: apiVersion 8, Kino 0.9.54 or newer. `episodes`
    answers for every album, audiobook and show (even a single track), `resolve` offers each audio
    format as a labelled lazy copy, plus `download`, a section of its own and Categorías tiles. See
    [Music and podcasts](music.md).

    [:octicons-repo-template-16: Use as template](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio/generate){ .md-button .md-button--primary }
    [:octicons-mark-github-16: View on GitHub](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio){ .md-button }

</div>

To try one in Kino, open Ajustes > Plugins and type `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive`,
`kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server` or `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio`.

**Use the template, don't fork.** "Use as template" creates a fresh repository of your own with the
same files. A fork would work as a plugin too, but Kino's community search leaves forks out
([Get found](publish.md#get-found)). Then change `id`, `name`, `homepage`, `hosts` and
`capabilities` in `kino-plugin.json`, rewrite `plugin.js`, and keep `sdk/`.

!!! note "Plugins that use each other (apiVersion 20, Kino 0.9.81): TMDB and Cine Trivia"
    [**Cine Trivia**](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-cine-trivia) (`kinotvapp/kino-plugin-cine-trivia`) is the
    reference **consumer** of the [plugin protocol](protocol.md): a five-question movie game (a `screen` plugin, phone and TV)
    that takes every movie from the `movies` door of [**TMDB**](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb), the reference
    **provider** (TMDB 1.3.0 and later, door in `enhancements["20"]`). It shows the whole pattern: `consumes` + `recommends`,
    an install screen with `go.installPlugin` until TMDB is installed, `kino.plugins.call` with every error code handled, and a
    live `trending` stream. Both need Kino 0.9.81 or newer for the door.

!!! note "A real-world example: a plugin that uses the hidden browser"
    **Maratón** (signed, `apiVersion` 6, `"browser": "pages"`) is a real-world plugin, by someone else, that
    finds its video with [`kino.browser.capture`](browser.md) and offers each episode's other servers
    and languages as [labelled lazy copies](contract.md#lazy-copies). It is an example of those two
    features only (Kino just lists community plugins: each author is responsible for theirs); "Tu servidor" stays the complete reference plugin.

!!! note "Sync providers: Sync-Gram, Sync Servidor and Sync-Gram Cuenta"
    The references for a [sync provider](sync-providers.md) (apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74) are three public
    repositories: **Sync-Gram** ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram), a Telegram bot of the person's own; unofficial, not
    affiliated with Telegram; recommended in Kino) and **Sync Servidor** ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-server), a single-file
    Node server the person runs; not listed in Kino, installed by pasting its repository address) and **Sync-Gram Cuenta**
    ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram-account](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram-account), the person's own
    Telegram account over a WebSocket, apiVersion 13; unofficial; not listed in Kino, installed by pasting
    `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram-account`). Each has a guide in English and Spanish
    and offline tests. See [The three example providers](sync-providers.md#examples).

!!! note "Kino Sync (experimental): sync through your own Google Drive"
    **Kino Sync** ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gdrive](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gdrive)) is a
    [sync provider](sync-providers.md) that keeps the encrypted copy in **the person's own Google Drive**: no server of
    yours and no tokens to paste. The person taps **Connect with Google**, types a code at `google.com/device` (the same step
    TV apps use) and that is it. It is an experiment: not part of Kino, not recommended, and unofficial (not affiliated with
    Google). It draws a [screen](screens.md) (`settingsIn: "screen"`) with the steps, a banner with «Try again», the state of
    the copy in Drive and an accordion of questions; the copy lives in a «Kino Sync» folder as a single file,
    `kino-sync.bin`, with the `drive.file` permission (the plugin only sees what it created). The Google client is built in
    as a sealed secret, and since Drive cannot write «only if the version is X», the plugin checks, writes and checks again
    to detect a `conflict`. It ships offline Node tests with an imitation of Google.

!!! note "Screens (apiVersion 14, with Kino 0.9.74): three examples"
    - **UI gallery** ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-ui-gallery](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-ui-gallery)): every
      [screen](screens.md) component drawn on the device, in seven tabs (layout, content, actions, forms, overlays, navigation and data), including the
      latest pieces: full-screen `pages`, a `PageView` carousel, `ListTile`, `CircleAvatar`, the floating button, a `Scaffold`
      route, animations and a `settings` node with `autoSave`; the [component catalogue](screen-components.md)'s
      captures come from it.
    - **Solo noticias** ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-news](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-news)): a screen of news
      cards about what you watch and a [background job](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs) that refreshes them; code in `src/`
      bundled with esbuild ([Structure a bigger plugin](structure.md)).
    - **Party Chat** ([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-watch-party](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-watch-party)): a
      [player-panel](player-panel.md#contributed-tab) tab to watch a title with friends, with [rooms](rooms.md#room),
      a chat and the video in sync through [`playerControl`](rooms.md#player-control).

!!! note "apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74): a byte-stream example"
    No published example plugin uses apiVersion 13 yet. The guide has a complete
    `socket` + `byteSource` plugin, a video library behind a WebSocket, with the Node test that checks every range it
    serves: [A complete example](bytes.md#example). The catalog, image and QR pages each carry a complete example too.

## The reference plugin { #reference-plugin }

For the basics -- `search`, `home`, `browse`, `episodes` and `resolve` over a public site, with no
settings or session -- the reference is `kino-plugin.json` and `plugin.js` in
[kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive), the Internet
Archive plugin, with all five capabilities. It reads about like this:

1. It declares `archive.org` **and** `*.archive.org`: a download URL on `archive.org` redirects to a
   storage node such as `dn720705.ca.archive.org`, and the wildcard does not cover the bare domain.
2. `getJson` does the `await` first and throws afterwards (the rule of
   [the rejection trap](engine-limits.md#rejection-trap)).
3. `search` cleans what the person typed: archive.org answers 200 with an error body when the query
   has a stray `/`, `-`, `&` or `'` or a dangling `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, so it keeps letters, digits and
   apostrophes inside words, drops the operator words, and asks both collections (films and classic
   TV) whatever `type` says, using it only to decide which group comes first; an item that is in both
   is listed once.
4. `home` builds three rows (films, classic TV, classic animation) and wraps each row in its own
   `try`/`catch`, so one failing row does not lose the others; it reports it with `kino.log`. Each row
   carries its own id as `ref`, and `browse(ref, cursor)` pages through the same query 50 at a time
   with the page number as the cursor (`"2"`, `"3"`, …), throwing `kino.error("not_found")` for a row
   it does not know.
5. `episodes` reads the item's file list, keeps the video originals in natural order (a small
   `natural()` comparator, because `localeCompare` cannot be trusted), numbers them from `S01E02`
   in the file name or 1, 2, 3, and uses `"<item>|<file name>"` as each episode's `ref`.
6. `resolve` picks the best playable file (an mp4 derived from the original, or the mp4/webm itself),
   turns sibling `.vtt`/`.srt` files into `subtitles`, and sets `durationMs`.
7. Every URL it builds is `https` on a declared host; posters use
   `https://archive.org/services/img/<id>` and are not host-checked.

`README.md` in that repository says what it does not do (a collection is exposed as a single movie,
episodes numbered 0 are dropped), so do not copy those as intended behavior.

For everything else, up to apiVersion 7 (Kino 0.9.51) -- settings, a session, downloads, `live`
items, `channels`, the apiVersion 6 set, `tracking` and `segments` -- the reference is
[kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server) ("Tu servidor"
1.5.0): its
[`kino-plugin.json`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server/blob/main/kino-plugin.json)
and its [`plugin.js`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server/blob/main/plugin.js) use
nearly everything that exists, and its
[`README.md`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server/blob/main/README.md) maps every
feature to the title of its test server that exercises it:

| What it shows | Where in the code | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"hosts": []`, the server the person types and its other addresses (a `list` of `url` fields) | `kino-plugin.json`; `base()`, `addresses()`, `reach()` | [The person's own servers](manifest.md#own-servers) |
| Every setting type: `url`, `text`, `password`, `toggle`, `select`, `list`, `section` (a 300-character hint), `status`, `action` | `kino-plugin.json`: `settings` | [The settings form](settings-form.md#types) |
| Status lines, buttons (`confirm`, `clearSettings`) and a check before saving | `settingsStatus()`, `action()`, `validateSettings()` | [The settings form](settings-form.md) |
| A login and a token kept in `kino.storage`, retried once on a 401; `kino.sleep` on a short `Retry-After` | `token()`, `api()` | [`kino.storage`](kino-api.md#storage) |
| Typed errors (`kino.error`) and your own sentence (`userMessage`) | `api()`, `resolveCopy()` | [Errors people understand](contract.md#errors) |
| A cache with `ttlMs` the person picks, and the last copy when the server is down; `telemetry` + `kino.log.report` | `home()`, `reach()` | [`kino.storage`](kino-api.md#storage), [Telemetry](diagnostics.md#telemetry) |
| Title search over a backend that matches any word; a `Page` with `next`; `scopedSearch` | `search()`, `kino.rank.*` | [`kino.rank`](kino-api.md#rank), [Searching inside "Ver más"](contract.md#scoped-search) |
| Cursor paging, rows with `genre` | `browse()`, `refFilter()`, `ROWS` | [Paging](contract.md#paging) |
| Seasons as separate titles | `episodes()` | [Seasons](contract.md#seasons) |
| `ids.tmdb` + `ids.imdb`, item fields, `adult: true` entries | `item()`, `categories()` | [`ids.tmdb`](contract.md#tmdb), [18+ content](contract.md#adult) |
| A section with tabs and a hero, Categorías tiles, `theme` | `section()`, `categories()`; `kino-plugin.json` | [Section, categories and colors](section-theme.md) |
| Downloads (`download`) | `kino-plugin.json`; `resolve()` returns a progressive mp4 | [Downloads](manifest.md#downloads) |
| `audioTracks`, `subtitles`, `durationMs` and `skip` on the Stream | `resolve()` | [The `Stream` rules](contract.md#stream) |
| Labelled and lazy copies, the same file at the other addresses | `withCopies()`, `resolveCopy()`, `withAddresses()` | [Labelled and lazy copies](contract.md#lazy-copies) |
| Signing every request (`signing`, `signContext`, `sign`, `alternateHosts`, `resolve(ref, { retry })`) | `signedStream()`, `sign()`, `resolve()` | [Signing every request](signed-streams.md) |
| `live` items (apiVersion 2) | `item()`, `resolve()` | [Live channels (apiVersion 2)](live-channels.md#live-items) |
| `channels`: a `ref`, an inline `stream`, an M3U list with an XMLTV guide, a `resolve: true` list, `liveSearch`, paging | `liveCategories()`, `channel()`, `liveChannels()`, `liveSearch()`, `resolveListEntry()` | [Channels in the En vivo tab](live-channels.md#en-vivo-tab), [Three recipes](live-channels.md#recipes) |
| A User-Agent the channels insist on: `headers` on a Stream, `streamHeaders` on a playlist | `agentHeaders()` | [Channels in the En vivo tab](live-channels.md#en-vivo-tab) |
| A guide for its own channels | `guide()` | [The channel functions](live-channels.md#live-contract) |
| Moving saved titles from the server's older ids | `migrate()`, `movedTable()` | [Moving saved titles](migrate.md) |
| `meta` with `logo`, `ratings` and `cast` (Kino 0.9.51) | `meta()` | [Describing other titles](contract.md#meta) |
| `subtitles` with the `file` hint (Kino 0.9.51) | `subtitles()` | [Subtitles for any title](contract.md#subtitles) |
| `tracking` (apiVersion 7): idempotency by `event.id`, `{ skipped: true }` | `track()` | [Telling a tracker](contract.md#tracking) |
| `segments` (apiVersion 7) | `segments()` | [Where the intro and credits are](contract.md#segments) |

Its core, line by line, is in the cookbook:
[The person's own server](cookbook.md#own-server).

## Install it and see it work { #own-server-demo }

[kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server) bundles a
reference server with no dependencies
(`node server.mjs [--port 8096] [--user ana] [--password s3cr3t] [--live-agent VLC]`) whose catalog exercises one
feature per title, so you can install the plugin in Kino and watch every row of the table above work,
with no real server of your own.

A few powers are deliberately **not** in it, because a server at home never needs them: Widevine DRM
([recipe](cookbook.md#widevine)), a declared host over plain `http`
([recipe](cookbook.md#insecure-site)), streams on any server
([recipe](live-channels.md#recipe-m3u)), sealed secrets ([`kino.secret`](kino-api.md#secret)), the
author's signature ([Signed plugins](signed.md)), the hidden browser and `kino.html.select`
([Hidden browser](browser.md)), and key pairs ([Key pairs](kino-api.md#key-pairs)).

## Example plugin stores { #store-examples }

To **publish your own store** (apiVersion 15, with Kino 0.9.77) there are two complete, copyable plugins: a
**local** store whose list is a static JSON file and a **live** store with its own API. Both pass the kit and ship tests
that run without a network: [Example stores](store-examples.md). The store that ships in the app, Kino Plugins, is another
real example ([Plugin stores](plugin-stores.md#kino-plugins)).

# Build a plugin with AI

An AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Aider…) can write a
Kino plugin for you if it reads the rules first, **even if you cannot program**: you say which source
you want and try the result in Kino; the assistant writes the code, tests it with the kit and tells
you what to do at each step. This site publishes the rules in the shapes those tools read best:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`AGENTS.md`](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/AGENTS.md) | The instructions for the assistant: its role, what to read, the step-by-step workflow, the hard rules with their exact numbers, a checklist and the usual mistakes. Also in [the repository](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugins/blob/main/AGENTS.md). |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/llms-full.txt) | This whole guide as one text file (English), plus `AGENTS.md`, `contract.json` and `kino.d.ts`. Built with the site, so it is always the same version as these pages. |
| [`llms.txt`](https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/llms.txt) | The short index, in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) format. |

!!! tip "Want to use a Nuvio scraper?"
    To **add** scrapers to Kino you do not need this prompt: Kino installs the scrapers of a Nuvio repository directly,
    converting them on the device. See [Nuvio scrapers](nuvio.md).

!!! tip "Want a plugin that finds its links through Nuvio scrapers?"
    That is a plugin of your own, and an assistant writes it well if it reads [Plugins that use Nuvio scrapers](nuvio-plugins.md)
    (`kino.nuvio`, Kino 0.9.71). Use [the short Nuvio prompt](#nuvio-prompt) or, in the prompt below, fill in the «Nuvio scrapers» line.

!!! tip "Want to use a Stremio addon?"
    You do not need this prompt either. In Ajustes ▸ Plugins, "Agregar plugin", choose **Stremio** and paste
    the address of the addon's `manifest.json`: Kino reads it and generates, on the device, a plugin that talks to the
    addon's server. See [Stremio addons](stremio.md).

!!! tip "Want to use a CloudStream plugin?"
    No prompt needed (Kino 0.9.54). In "Agregar plugin", paste the address of a CloudStream repository, or its short
    code, and Kino converts the plugins the person picks. **One thing to know: it needs an auxiliary app.**
    CloudStream code never runs inside Kino; it runs in a small separate app, the **CloudStream complement** (an extra
    APK). The first time, Kino offers to install it ("Instalar complemento"): it downloads it from the same servers as
    Kino's own updates, checks that it is Kino's copy (package, version, sha256 and signature) and Android asks for
    permission to install it. The complement has no internet permission: every request goes through Kino. Until it is
    installed, those plugins say "Necesitas el complemento de CloudStream" with a button to install it. See
    [CloudStream plugins](cloudstream.md) and [the complement](cloudstream.md#complement).

!!! tip "Want a plugin that uses another plugin's data, or offers its own to other plugins?"
    From Kino 0.9.81 plugins can use each other through Kino: one opens **doors**, another asks them (a movie trivia that
    takes its movies from the TMDB plugin, say). An assistant gets it right if it reads [The plugin protocol](protocol.md).
    Use [the short protocol prompt](#protocol-prompt).

## Before you start { #before }

You need five things. All are free except, sometimes, the assistant.

1. **A GitHub account** ([github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup)). Your plugin lives in a
   public GitHub repository; Kino installs it from there.
2. **Node.js 18 or newer** ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/), the "LTS" version). It runs the test
   kit. To check, in a terminal: `node --version` must answer `v18` or a higher number.
3. **Git** ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/downloads)), to download and upload the repository.
   Optional but handy: [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (`gh`), with which the assistant can
   create the repository and set its topic for you (the first time, `gh auth login`).
4. **An assistant that can use the terminal**, that is, one that runs commands and reads what they
   answer:
    - in the terminal: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider;
    - in an editor: Cursor, or VS Code with GitHub Copilot in agent mode.

    **How to open a terminal:** on Windows, Start menu → type "Terminal" (or "PowerShell"); on a
    Mac, Cmd + Space → type "Terminal"; on Linux, Ctrl + Alt + T. Create an empty folder, go into it
    and start the assistant there.

    A chat in the browser, with no terminal, works too, but then you copy each command, run it and
    paste what it answers back into the chat.
5. **Kino on a phone or a TV**, to try the plugin for real before sharing it.

And one more thing: **the right to use the source.** A plugin can only reach what the person could
watch anyway; do not ask an assistant to get around a paywall, someone else's login or DRM.

## The prompt { #prompt }
