Copy it (the copy button is at the top right of the block), change what is between `<<<` and `>>>`
and paste it into your assistant. If you do not know what to put on a line, leave it as it is: the
assistant will ask you.

```text
You are going to write a Kino plugin: a public GitHub repository with kino-plugin.json and one
JavaScript ES module (plugin.js) that the Kino app (video, live TV, music and podcasts) runs in a
QuickJS sandbox.

I may not know how to program. Explain each step in plain words, run the commands yourself (tell
me first which one and why), ask me before anything that cannot be undone (deleting, publishing,
pushing to GitHub) and, when I have to do something on GitHub or in Kino, give me the exact clicks.

The plugin's UI (this rule comes first): for any plugin that needs its own screen, configuration,
onboarding, dashboard or panel, build it with Kino's screens UI: apiVersion 14, the "screen" capability with the
screen() and screenEvent() exports, Flutter-style components (Scaffold, AppBar, TabBar, ListTile, Card, Form,
TextField, the "settings" node...), per-size values, the phone and the TV drawn from the same tree. Keep the old
settings form and the legacy panel format only for compatibility. apiVersion 14 arrives with Kino 0.9.74: to stay installable on older Kinos keep your apiVersion and offer the screen through
"enhancements". Put the code in src/ and bundle it to plugin.js with esbuild (generated, committed, checked with
check:built). Validate with node sdk/validate.mjs . and node sdk/run.mjs . screen (also with --device tv). Follow
the component catalogue (https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/screen-components/, https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/screen-forms/, https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/screen-reference/) and the TV focus rules
(https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/screens/#tv-focus): Kino draws its focus ring only on nodes the person can press; a node the remote must stop on
just to read it gets "canRequestFocus": true.
Every screen of the plugin uses one compact bar: its AppBar sets mergeWithKinoBar: true and dense: true, with a leading
that is a real exit ({ close: true } on the front page, a back elsewhere). The unnamed route is "main", the front page. A Home
row item that opens a screen uses open: { screen: { args } } and the detail is pushed from the open answer, so Back returns
to the front page. A reader uses Image fit: "width", a scroll with zoom and onScroll, and pages with reverse and progress.
If the site's pictures answer only to its own page, each Image takes headers { Referer, User-Agent }, sent only to hosts
in the manifest's hosts. To remember where the person stopped, use kino.progress (apiVersion 22, next Kino release): the
exact place goes in resume (opaque to Kino, at most 1024 bytes), get(id) answers null when there is none, and Kino draws
no row: the plugin builds its own "keep reading" row from list() (https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/progress/).
For something small that stays on the TV player (a clock, a score, a button that opens my panel), use the player slot
(apiVersion 23, next Kino release): the "playerSlot" capability, a "slot" block of 1 to 3 elements (text, icon, image,
button; "overlay" with the controls or "fixed", which asks me in red), and both exports playerSlot(context) and
playerSlotAction({ id, context }); context may lack kind, and refreshMs is 2000 to 60000. A text accepts size, weight, color
and background, and any element left and top; offer them as ordinary settings, and Kino ignores what is invalid and keeps the
text readable (https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/player-slot/#dress).
If the sign-in keeps its token in the page's localStorage (not in a cookie), open the window with kino.visualBrowser.open and
collect.localStorage: ["access_token"] plus doneWhen.localStorage (next Kino release, 0.9.87, no new apiVersion): the answer's
localStorage holds only the keys named, with "done"; an older Kino answers none, so check it, keep the values in kino.storage and
never log them (storeAs covers cookies only; https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/visual-browser/#rules).
For a look for the whole app (app themes), the manifest's appThemes (apiVersion 18) holds colours, shapes and type; from
apiVersion 26 (next Kino release, 0.9.87) a theme may also paint: surfaces (fill, stroke and glow per element), style.gloss,
layout (a framed hero and a floating rail, TV only), assets with background.image and typography.fontFamily. Never put those keys in
a theme that declares a lower apiVersion, give every asset its exact sha256 and bytes (a picture at most 2 MB), make the theme look
right with each effect off, and keep text readable on every gradient stop (https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/themes/#level2).
Prefer a Skeleton to a spinner and a bottom sheet with a search field to many chips; a screen has a 600-node budget.
(https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/screen-components/#one-compact-bar)

Before writing anything:
1. Read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/AGENTS.md completely and follow it as your
   instructions.
2. Read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/llms-full.txt (the whole guide, contract.json and
   kino.d.ts). If you cannot open URLs, tell me and I will paste them.
3. Start from a template, with "Use this template" (never Fork): kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive if my
   plugin is simple, kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server if it needs settings, a session, downloads or
   live channels (its plugin.js and kino-plugin.json, "Tu servidor" 1.5.0, are the complete API
   reference, up to apiVersion 7). The template's sdk/ folder is the Node test kit. If my plugin is
   music or podcasts, also read the "Music and podcasts" section of the contract (apiVersion 8, Kino
   0.9.54: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/contract/#music-podcasts) and use
   kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive-audio as the reference audio plugin.
4. If my plugin cannot turn what it finds into a playable URL itself and instead hands it to another app
   installed on the phone or TV (a "resolver app"), read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/resolver/ and
   "Letting another app resolve what you found" in the contract (apiVersion 11, Kino 0.9.66). In that case the
   plugin only declares "externalResolve" and answers { external: { protocol, ref } } from resolve(); it never
   touches the content itself.
5. If I named a Nuvio repository, read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/nuvio-plugins/ (kino.nuvio,
   apiVersion 11, Kino 0.9.71) and copy the shape of its complete example.
6. If my plugin is a sync provider (it carries Kino's own sync between my devices through a service: a bot,
   a storage API, a server of mine), read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/sync-providers/ first
   (apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74). Its references are three public repositories: Sync-Gram
   (https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram, a Telegram bot of the person's own) for a third-party
   service, Sync Servidor (https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-server, a single-file Node
   server) for a server of my own, and Sync-Gram Cuenta
   (https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sync-gram-account, the person's own Telegram account over a
   WebSocket, apiVersion 13: sync.generateKey, a one-shot 2FA password in provision, settingsStatus hide) for
   an account of my own.
7. If my plugin is a store (a source of plugins for Kino's store), or uses identity or notifications, read
   https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/plugin-stores/, /en/store-examples/, /en/identity/ and
   /en/notifications/ first (apiVersion 15, Kino 0.9.77) and start from an example
   store with node sdk/init.mjs my-store --host <host> --store local|live.
8. If my plugin uses another plugin's data, or opens a door for other plugins, read
   https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/ first (the plugin protocol: apiVersion 20, Kino
   0.9.81) and copy the patterns of Cine Trivia (https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-cine-trivia, a
   consumer with the install gate) and TMDB (https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb, a provider). Start
   from the kit's scaffold: node sdk/init.mjs my-plugin --kind provider, or --kind consumer --repo owner/name
   --door <the real door> --call <a real call> (it writes "hosts": []); its test/provider is a
   stand-in to replace with a copy of the real provider. One-page summary:
   https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol-quick/.
9. For the Share button (it goes in every plugin, see the rules), read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/share/
   and copy Megaplay's shape (https://github.com/xuper-plugin/kino-plugin-megaplay, src/browse/share.js and
   test/share.test.mjs).

What I want:
- Source: <<< the site or API, e.g. https://example.com >>>
- Content: <<< movies / series / anime / live TV / music / podcasts or audiobooks / a catalog that plays nothing (lists or ratings); language and country >>>
- Access: <<< none / my username and password on the site / an API key of mine (the developer's) that I do not want to publish / the address of a server each person types >>>
- What Kino asks the person when setting it up: <<< nothing / their username and password / their region / their server's address >>>
- Offline downloads: <<< yes / no >>>
- Another app resolves the playable stream (a separate resolver app on the device): <<< no / yes: the app's package name, the protocol name it answers, what "ref" it expects, and how people get it: a GitHub release APK (with its sha256), F-Droid, a Downloader code for TV >>>
- Nuvio scrapers: <<< none / the Nuvio repository (owner/repo) the plugin gets its links from >>>
- Sync provider (the plugin carries Kino's sync between my devices instead of the local network): <<< no / yes: the service, whether it gives each person a long random token, and whether the service may read the synced data >>>
- Name in Kino and a short description: <<< e.g. "Mi fuente": "Películas de …, en español" >>>
- Its own screen (a dashboard, a setup flow, a panel tab...): <<< no / yes: what it shows and what the person does there >>>
- A store (a source of plugins for Kino's store, apiVersion 15): <<< no / yes: local (a list it hands over in the background, from GitHub, my server or a static JSON file) or live (also answers while the person browses: storeList and storeSearch, so what they search reaches my server), the hosts it uses, and the plugins it lists >>>
- Identity or notices (apiVersion 15): <<< no / yes: who needs the person's Telegram pseudonym (only plugins signed with Kino's author key get an answer) and what notices to leave in the Home bell >>>
- Other plugins (the plugin protocol, apiVersion 20, Kino 0.9.81): <<< no / it uses the door of another plugin: its repository and door (e.g. kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb, "movies") / it opens a door: what other plugins could ask it >>>
- Files on the person's device (apiVersion 21, Kino 0.9.82): <<< no / yes: what kinds (books, music, videos, pictures, subtitles), one file or a whole folder, and whether it only reads them or plays them >>>
- Remember where the person stopped (apiVersion 22, next Kino release, not published yet): <<< no / yes: what the person goes through page by page or chapter by chapter (a manga, a book, a podcast it plays itself), the unit to remember (chapter and page, a position in the book) and what to keep in resume to come back to the exact place (e.g. { cap: 87, pag: 12 }), and whether my plugin shows its own "keep reading" row (Kino draws none) >>>
- Pictures from a site that only answers to its own page (an Image's headers, next Kino release): <<< no / yes: the site, the Referer it wants (e.g. https://mangasite.example/) and whether it needs a browser User-Agent; its picture hosts go in hosts >>>
- Something always on the TV player (the player slot, apiVersion 23, next Kino release, not published yet): <<< no / yes: what it shows (a clock, a score, a logo, a button that opens my panel), whether it stays the whole time (fixed: Kino asks me in red) or only with the controls (overlay), and how often it changes >>>
- Sign-in that keeps its token in the page's localStorage (kino.visualBrowser, next Kino release): <<< no / yes: the site, the localStorage keys that hold the token (e.g. access_token) and where to keep them (kino.storage) >>>
- A look for the whole app (app themes; painted surfaces from apiVersion 26, next Kino release, not published yet): <<< no / yes: the mood (colours, dark or light), whether it needs surfaces (gradient or glossy buttons, glows), a background picture (my own file, at most 2 MB, in the plugin's repository), its own font (TTF or OTF), a framed hero and a floating rail (TV only) >>>
- Share to Kino Social (recommended in every plugin): <<< yes, from each title page and from the bar / only from the bar (text only) / no >>>
- Sign the plugin with my own key, so people know every update is mine: <<< yes / no >>>
- My GitHub user: <<< e.g. my-user >>>

Rules you cannot break (the detail and exact numbers are in AGENTS.md):
- Declare in "hosts" every host you know: the API's and the video's, subtitles', audio's, segments'
  and redirects' (*.x does not cover x). If one is missing, Kino asks the person once when a title
  is opened or played; do not rely on it. If the video comes from changing CDNs, use
  "streamHosts": "any" (apiVersion 4; the person approves it at install); for live channels,
  "liveStreamHosts": "any" (apiVersion 3, needs the "channels" capability). If the site or its
  extractors rotate domains and you cannot list them, use "fetchHosts": "any" (apiVersion 9, Kino
  0.9.55; the person approves it in red; https on port 443 only, under a request budget, never the home network) and check kino.fetchAnyHost.
  There is no maximum number of hosts from Kino 0.9.45; Kino 0.9.44 and older refuse more than 20, so
  if you declare more than 20, tell me.
- In kino-plugin.json write "entry": "plugin.js" and "icon": "icon.png", NEVER "./plugin.js": Kino
  0.9.45 and older refuse a leading "./" and the plugin does not install.
- It is neither Node nor a browser: no fetch, setTimeout, Buffer, process, require, crypto or Intl;
  use kino.fetch, kino.sleep, kino.crypto, kino.storage. URL, URLSearchParams, atob, btoa,
  TextEncoder, TextDecoder and console do exist. One file, no import.
- Never throw before the first await of an async function (await first, validate after): Kino 0.9.50
  catches it, but 0.9.49 and older abort the whole call, and people update late.
- Use kino.fetch whenever it can find the video. Only if a server's embed builds the address by
  running its own scripts, use the hidden browser ("browser": true, apiVersion 6; it asks me in red)
  and call kino.browser.capture only inside resolve. Never try to solve or get around a captcha or a
  "verify you are human" check: on blocked, move to the next server. If a title has several servers
  or languages, resolve one and list the others as alternatives { label, ref }.
- Limits: search 15 s and the other calls 20 s; 60 requests per call (every redirect hop counts,
  refused ones too) and at most 6 at once; 5 MB bodies; 256 KB of
  kino.storage; 100 search results; Home with 20 rows of 60.
- Errors for the person: kino.error("auth_required" | "not_found" | "geo_blocked" |
  "rate_limited" | "unavailable"). With apiVersion 6 you may add a sentence of your own,
  kino.error(code, detail, { userMessage: "…" }): in Spanish (or in kino.lang's language, see the
  language rule), at most 160 characters, no URL or
  domain, no long numbers, never asking for money, passwords, codes or contact outside Kino, and never
  echoing what the person typed (Kino shows it as "Mensaje de <plugin>: …" only if it passes all its
  rules; a plugin that uses it to ask for money or data breaks the rules and is taken out of the community index).
- Home categories: preferably group the content in Kino's categories
  (https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/categories/): declare "genre" on each home() row and "genres"
  on each item using ids from that list (peliculas, series, anime, accion, comedia, drama...), also send
  "year" and ids.tmdb, and invent a new category only when nothing fits.
- 18+ content: mark it with adult: true (apiVersion 6; Kino shows it only with the 18+ code
  unlocked). Never try to get around that lock.
- Everything the person reads is in Spanish from Bogotá with tuteo, never voseo, and the texts the
  code builds (row titles, userMessage) are in kino.lang's language: from Kino 0.9.54 kino.lang may be
  "en-US", and then they go in English (before 0.9.54 it is always "es-CO").
- Music and podcasts (apiVersion 8, Kino 0.9.54): kind "music" is an album, a playlist or a track;
  kind "podcast" is a show, an audiobook or a radio program; "artist" is optional (the artist, or the
  host or author). If the plugin declares "episodes", episodes() must answer for every music and
  podcast ref, even a single track; without "episodes", the item's own ref goes to resolve. Below
  apiVersion 8 such items are dropped.
- The person's playlists on your plugin (apiVersion 10, Kino 0.9.65): if the service has the
  person's OWN playlists (their account, not your catalog), you may declare the "playlists"
  capability; its six functions are each independently optional, including playlists() itself. It
  is a contract not yet wired into any Kino screen, so do not present it as something already live
  in the app. Read it at https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/contract/#playlists before
  using it; most plugins do not need it.
- Another app resolving what you found (apiVersion 11, Kino 0.9.66): when a source cannot be turned into a
  URL by the plugin itself and a separate, independently-installed resolver app does it, declare the
  "externalResolve" capability (and, to name the app, the manifest's "externalResolver") and answer
  { external: { protocol, ref } } from resolve() instead of a url. Kino never interprets the protocol or the
  ref; it asks the person's permission, shows the app's progress and plays what it returns. Use it only when the
  plugin truly cannot produce a url, give it a fallback when possible, and do not promise a resolver app exists.
  Read https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/resolver/ before using it.
- Sync providers (apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74), only if I asked for one: declare the "syncProvider"
  capability (it may be the only one) and export syncPull({ maxBlobBytes }) -> { blob, version } or null,
  syncPush({ maxBlobBytes, blob, expectedVersion }) -> { version } and, optionally, syncStatus(null) ->
  { ready, message? }. The blob is opaque base64 ciphertext made by Kino: store it and give it back byte
  for byte, never decode it. Throw kino.error("conflict", …) when the remote copy changed since
  expectedVersion, and kino.error("auth_required", …) when settings are missing or refused. The manifest
  MUST have a "sync" block with "keySecret" (a provider without it is refused): "keySecret" = the key of a
  "password" setting holding a long random token (never a password a person picks, no "default"); Kino
  derives the sync key from it on each device, so a second device only needs the same settings and no key
  travels, BUT the plugin and its service can read the data and the one consent line says so in red: tell
  me. "provision" (required) = the settings a second device needs, including "keySecret". "maxBlobBytes"
  at most 4194304 (4 MiB; only inside syncPull and syncPush may kino.fetch move that much). If the token
  changes, every other device needs the new one. Never put the token in an
  error, a status line or a log.
- Configuration aids (apiVersion 12): a short "help" setting (what the person needs and where to get it)
  and a "link" setting (an https button, e.g. https://t.me/BotFather). From Kino 0.9.74 an action may
  answer link: { candidate, confirm } (Kino asks "Is this you, <candidate>?" before running the confirm
  action) and setSettings: { key: value } to fill the plugin's own "text" or "select" settings (never a
  "url"; a "password" only from apiVersion 13). The confirm action carries "linkOnly": true, so the person sees one button.
  Setup a TV cannot do (a token pasted on the phone) carries "devices": ["phone"]: the TV receives it with
  "Recibir configuración" ("Receive settings"), sent from the phone with "Enviar configuración".
- apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74; older Kinos refuse it), only if my source needs it: a service that speaks over a WebSocket ("socket", kino.ws, wss:// to
  my declared hosts, frames as hex/base64 strings), video the plugin serves itself ("byteSource":
  resolve answers { source: "plugin", handle, size, mime } and read({ handle, offset, length }) answers
  { bytes: base64 } of exactly that range, built with kino.crypto.convert, never a JavaScript loop over
  the bytes), thousands of records to search ("catalog", kino.catalog), a bigger device-only storage
  ("storageLarge"), a QR on the settings form ("qr" setting) or the phone's scanner from an action
  ("qrScan", kino.qr.scan), a password that must stay on one device such as a 2FA password sent once ("sync": false
  on that password setting; sync.provision may carry it once to a new device, never as keySecret), a sync
  provider next to "socket"/"storageLarge"/"catalog"/"qrScan" with no resolve or search, a key Kino makes
  (sync.generateKey), a form that hides what a step does not need (settingsStatus answering hide: [keys]), pictures only the plugin can fetch ("imageSource" and an image export). Read
  https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/bytes/, /en/catalog/, /en/images/ and /en/qr/ first; test read
  with node sdk/run.mjs --size <bytes> . read <handle> <offset> <length> and a Node test (askRead or a fake
  WebSocket); feature-detect every kino.crypto byte operation you use (they depend on the Kino version).
- Feature-detect what older Kino lacks: kino.meta and kino.tmdb (Kino 0.9.53) only behind
  `typeof kino.meta === "function"` / `typeof kino.tmdb === "function"`, and the hidden browser's
  captureAll options (Kino 0.9.54) only when `kino.browser.captureAll === true`. kino.device (Kino 0.9.55)
  is "tv" or "phone" and undefined on an older Kino: use it only for what really differs on a TV box and
  treat anything but "tv" as the phone. Add kino.seed(session) (Kino 0.9.55, behind
  `typeof kino.seed === "function"`) ONLY to a plugin whose source hands out anonymous guest sessions and
  blocks regions from logging in: one brand-new session you just proved works, never the person's own, at
  most every few hours, behind a setting the person can turn off. TMDB goes through
  kino.tmdb, never with a key in the code. Never export a helper named "details": from apiVersion 8
  it is a reserved export.
- Nothing secret in the code or the repository. Each person's username and password go in a
  "password" setting. An API key of mine is sealed: "secrets" in the manifest, sealed with
  `node sdk/seal.mjs --repo USER/REPO --name name`, and kino.secret("name") in the code
  (apiVersion 4).
- Downloads are declarative: if the source allows it, add "download" to "capabilities" (apiVersion
  2) and export nothing extra; Kino calls resolve itself when the download runs. Movies and
  episodes are saved from a plain file (mp4, mkv…) or from HLS that is not live; live channels,
  DASH and anything with DRM, never.
- Signing (only if I said yes): "apiVersion": 5 (needs Kino 0.9.45+). Tell me, in plain words, what
  it is for, and walk me through it: `node sdk/seal.mjs --keygen` ONCE (it writes
  kino-author-key.pem), add `*.pem` to .gitignore BEFORE any commit, and tell me to back the key up
  and never share it (if it is lost, everyone who installed the plugin must uninstall and reinstall
  it). Then `node sdk/seal.mjs --sign --repo USER/REPO` AFTER the last change to plugin.js or
  "version" and again after every later change, never commit the .pem. Never print the key's
  contents in the chat.
- apiVersion: the lowest that works (3 for channels, 4 only for secrets, "streamHosts": "any" or a
  "list" setting, 5 only for a signed plugin, 6 only if you use an apiVersion 6 feature: status lines
  and buttons in the settings, a section of its own, colors, telemetry, migrate, request signing,
  userMessage, adult, channels in Home rows; 6 needs Kino 0.9.50 or newer; 7 only for "tracking" or
  "segments", and it needs Kino 0.9.51 or newer; 8 only for "music" or "podcast" items or the details
  export, and it needs Kino 0.9.54 or newer; 9 for the player panel or a hand-written "fetchHosts":
  "any" (Kino 0.9.55); 10 only for "playlists" (Kino 0.9.65); 11 only for "externalResolve" (Kino 0.9.66);
  12 only for "syncProvider", the "sync" block or a "link"/"help" setting (Kino 0.9.74; Kino 0.9.73 and
  older refuse it); 13 only for "socket", "byteSource", "storageLarge", "catalog", "qrScan", "imageSource"
  or a "qr" setting (Kino 0.9.74); 14 for screens and their capabilities (Kino 0.9.74); 15 for "identity",
  "notifications" or "pluginStore" (Kino 0.9.77); 16 for "coins" (Kino 0.9.78); 17 to 20 only for what AGENTS.md
  section 2 lists for them (Kino 0.9.81); 21 for "files" (Kino 0.9.82); 22 for "progress" and 23 for "playerSlot"
  (the next Kino release, not published yet; to keep older Kinos, the feature goes in "enhancements")). A catalog that plays nothing declares "catalogOnly": true
  (Kino 0.9.54) and still exports a resolve that fails with not_found, for older Kino. A new id of my own (never
  "archive-org").
- Sharing (recommended in EVERY plugin, unless I say no): a "Compartir" button in the plugin's screen (on a title page, with
  the title, and/or in the bar, text only) that opens a sheet with a text I can change and an "Adjuntar el título" switch, and
  sends the text, plus the title when there is one ({ kind: "movie" | "series", tmdb }), to Kino Social's "wall" door with
  kino.plugins.call("social", "share", { text, title, from }). In the manifest:
  "consumes": { "social": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-social", "door": "wall", "calls": ["share"] } } and
  "recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-social"] (apiVersion 20, or inside enhancements["20"] and behind
  typeof kino.plugins === "object"; Kino 0.9.81 and Kino Social 0.9.7). If it answers provider_missing and Kino Social is not
  installed, answer go: { installPlugin: { repo: "kinotvapp/kino-social" } }; without kino.plugins, an "Actualiza Kino" toast.
  Never publish on my behalf: Kino Social only keeps a draft I review and post there, and you tell me so. From Kino 0.9.84
  (not published yet) the plugin can also declare "openFrom": { "routes": [...] } with the routes of its screen that other
  plugins' cards may open (read route.args in the open event and check them)
  (https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/share/).
- No "debug": true in a published plugin unless I ask for it: every plugin already has a "Modo debug"
  switch in Kino's Ajustes, and "debug": true only turns it on by default for everyone. "telemetry" only if I agree that the
  plugin's errors reach Kino; log steps and counts, never what the person types.

Work step by step: first explore the source with real requests, then the manifest, then each
function. After each step run `node sdk/validate.mjs .` and `node sdk/run.mjs . <function> …` and
fix everything Kino would drop. Record fixtures with --record and make
`node --test test/plugin.test.mjs` pass offline. Finish with the AGENTS.md checklist, and before
you hand the plugin over run this self-check and tell me the result of each line:
- `node sdk/validate.mjs .` exits 0 with no problems;
- kino-plugin.json: "entry" and "icon" have no leading "./"; "version" raised; apiVersion is the
  lowest that works; no "debug": true unless I asked for it;
- if signing: "signature" is in kino-plugin.json, `validate.mjs` verified it AFTER the last edit, and
  no .pem is tracked (`.gitignore` has *.pem);
- every host (video, subtitles, segments, redirects) is in "hosts" or covered by an "any" field;
- for discovery: the repository is public and not a fork, the topic kino-plugin is set, and the
  manifest has a Spanish "name" and "description";
- if it plays nothing: "catalogOnly": true, and a resolve that fails with not_found for older Kino;
- if it uses Nuvio scrapers: "apiVersion": 11, the "nuvio" capability and "nuvioRepos" (1 to 4), "streamHosts": "any",
  kino.nuvio only inside functions and behind `typeof kino.nuvio === "object"`; the Node kit answers it
  from a fixture (KINO_NUVIO_FIXTURE; if it says `Unknown capability`, my kit is old: update it, do not remove the
  capability), and the real scrapers are only tested in Kino 0.9.71 or newer;
- if it has music or podcasts: "apiVersion": 8, every audio item has kind "music" or "podcast", and
  (with "episodes") episodes() answers every audio ref, even a single track;
- if it is a sync provider: "apiVersion": 12, "syncProvider" declared, syncPull and syncPush exported,
  "sync.maxBlobBytes" at most 4194304, tests that push and pull a 4 MiB blob and throw "conflict",
  "sync.keySecret" and "sync.provision" declared, and you told me in plain words that the plugin and its
  service can read the data;
- if it uses apiVersion 13: read is covered by a Node test
  that checks every range byte for byte, no handle holds a secret, and every socket is closed;
- the Share button: consumes "social" (kinotvapp/kino-social, door "wall", call "share") and the same repository in
  recommends, provider_missing answers go.installPlugin, the text can be changed before sending, the title can be dropped,
  and the final message says the draft waits in Kino Social (nothing is published on its own);
- if it has a player slot: "playerSlot" and the "slot" block together, both exports present, node sdk/run.mjs . playerSlot
  prints the frame with nothing dropped (also with --bare), and node sdk/validate.mjs . passes;
- if it has a screen: every screen's AppBar has mergeWithKinoBar: true and dense: true with a real-exit leading,
  node sdk/run.mjs . screen and --device tv . screen print the tree with nothing dropped, every
  event name you use answers in screenEvent, and, if its apiVersion is below 14, the screen comes through
  "enhancements" and node sdk/validate.mjs . reports no dropped block;
- apiVersion 15 (Kino 0.9.77 or later).
  A store: "capabilities": ["pluginStore"] (it may stand alone) and optionally "pluginStore": { "mode": "local" | "live",
  "name" }. storeSync({ reason, since, state }) answers { full, entries, removed?, state? } and since/state may be
  absent at any time: when Kino loses a store's rows it syncs it again from scratch, so the store must then answer
  its whole list (full: true) and never rely on a saved cursor. A live store (mode "live") also exports storeList({
  category, sort, cursor }) and storeSearch({ q, category, cursor }), 5 s and 20 calls a minute. Each entry has an
  address (owner/repo, owner/repo/path, owner/repo@ref or url:https://...), an id, a name (1 to 60 characters) and
  optional description, categories, icon, popularity, updatedAt, signed/authorKey (hints only); "recommended" is
  ignored outside Kino Plugins. At most 5,000 entries and 4 MB. One plugin per id across all stores: if two repos
  claim an id the one in Kino Plugins' list wins, otherwise one is kept deterministically, and no store may list the
  id kino-plugins. The store only hands over addresses: it never installs anything and never claims to approve a
  plugin; Kino applies its blocklist and the 18+ code, and shows the consent lines (a red one for a live store). The
  people who publish a plugin answer for it; Kino only lists it. The store view has the tabs "De Kino" (Kino Plugins'
  default list), "De la comunidad" (everything else from every store) and "Instalados". Check with node sdk/validate.mjs
  . and node sdk/run.mjs . storeSync (and storeList / storeSearch for a live store) with nothing reported as [dropped by
  Kino]. identity: kino.identity.telegram({ challenge? }) answers { id, token } only to plugins signed with Kino's author
  key and only inside a call the person started; never log or show the token; the plugin works with it refused
  (permission_denied). notifications: kino.notifications.post({ id, title, text?, go? }) and clear(id?), 80-character
  titles, 160-character texts, 20 posts an hour, from a screen or the job. library: kino.library.watched() carries
  season and episode on series. All of it declarative, tested with node sdk/run.mjs . notifications and the KINO_IDENTITY_*
  variables.

At the end, walk me through:
1. Publishing it: a public repository (never a fork) with the files at the root; the topic
   kino-plugin and a GitHub description (About → ⚙ → Description and Topics → Save changes, or
   `gh repo edit USER/REPO --add-topic kino-plugin --description "…"`); and a good "name" and
   "description", in Spanish, in kino-plugin.json, because that is what people see in Kino.
2. Installing it in Kino: on a phone, menu ☰ → Plugins → + button; on a TV, Ajustes → Plugins →
   Agregar. Type USER/REPO → Agregar → read the sheet → Instalar (and Configurar if it asks for data).
3. What to try by hand in Kino, and what to do if something fails.
```

## A filled-in example { #example }

This is the "What I want" part for a simple public source. Paste it instead of the prompt's if you
want to rehearse the whole path before making your own:

```text
What I want:
- Source: https://archive.org, only the film noir collection (https://archive.org/details/Film_Noir)
- Content: movies; in English
- Access: none
- What Kino asks the person when setting it up: nothing
- Offline downloads: yes
- Name in Kino and a short description: "Cine negro": "Películas clásicas de cine negro de archive.org, de dominio público. No pide cuenta."
- My GitHub user: my-user
```

## Short prompt: a plugin with Nuvio scrapers { #nuvio-prompt }

If all you want is a plugin whose catalogue is yours and whose links are found by the scrapers of a Nuvio
repository, this prompt is shorter (the assistant still reads `AGENTS.md`):

```text
You are going to write a Kino plugin that finds its links with the scrapers of a Nuvio repository.

I may not know how to program: explain every step in plain English, run the commands yourself (tell me
which one and why first) and ask me before anything that cannot be undone.

Read, in this order:
1. https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/AGENTS.md (your instructions).
2. https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/nuvio-plugins/ (kino.nuvio: the manifest, the four
   calls, the limits and a complete example you must follow).
3. https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/llms-full.txt (the whole guide, contract.json and kino.d.ts).

What I want:
- Nuvio repository: <<< owner/repo, or the https address of its manifest.json >>>
- Catalogue: <<< movies / series / anime; where it comes from (e.g. TMDB with kino.tmdb) >>>
- Which scrapers to ask first: <<< e.g. the Spanish-speaking ones / anime ones only for animation / the plugin decides >>>
- Name in Kino and a short description: <<< e.g. "Mi todo en uno": "Películas y series, enlaces de Nuvio" >>>
- My GitHub user: <<< e.g. my-user >>>

Rules: "apiVersion": 11, "nuvio" in "capabilities", "nuvioRepos" with that repository, and
"streamHosts": "any". Call kino.nuvio only inside your functions and behind
`typeof kino.nuvio === "object"`. Ask few scrapers at a time (start with 4 to 6), lower timeoutMs so a
hung one does not spend the resolve's 75 s, and remember in kino.storage which ones worked. A scraper
that fails is an entry with ok: false, not an error. Return one Stream with the best copy and the rest
in alternatives. Every text for the person in Bogota Spanish with tuteo (or kino.lang's language).

The Node kit (the current one) knows "nuvio": `node sdk/validate.mjs .` checks nuvioRepos and `node sdk/run.mjs`
answers kino.nuvio from a fixture you write (KINO_NUVIO_FIXTURE; sample at
https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk/blob/main/fixtures/nuvio.json), so test it that way. If validate
says `Unknown capability: "nuvio"`, my copy of the kit is old: tell me to copy sdk/, contract.json and
kino.d.ts again from kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk (do not remove the capability). When you finish, tell me how to test
the real scrapers by installing the plugin in Kino 0.9.71 or newer, with the exact clicks.
```


## Short prompt: plugins that use each other { #protocol-prompt }

For a plugin that **uses** another plugin's door (a consumer) or **opens** one for other plugins (a provider). The
[plugin protocol](protocol.md) arrives with Kino 0.9.81: the plugin will only install, or only
open its door, on Kino 0.9.81 or newer. Fill in the part that applies and delete the other:

```text
You are going to write a Kino plugin that uses the plugin protocol (apiVersion 20, Kino 0.9.81):
plugins that use each other through Kino.

I may not know how to program: explain every step in plain English, run the commands yourself (tell me
which one and why first) and ask me before anything that cannot be undone.

Read, in this order:
1. https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol-quick/ (the protocol on one page: shapes, a minimal
   screen, the test commands, the five traps), then https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/AGENTS.md (your
   instructions; its contents table at the top gives the line where each part starts; section 4,
   "apiVersion 20: the plugin protocol", is the part that matters most here).
2. https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/ (provides, consumes, kino.plugins.call, the types,
   the seven error codes, the limits, streams, the install gate, and the TMDB + Cine Trivia example).
3. https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/llms-full.txt (the whole guide, contract.json and kino.d.ts:
   the "protocol" section of contract.json has every number).
Study the two reference plugins before writing anything: https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-cine-trivia
(a consumer) and https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb (a provider, TMDB 1.3.0 and later).

What I want:
- Role: <<< consumer (uses another plugin's door) / provider (opens a door for others) / both >>>
- If consumer: the provider's repository and door: <<< e.g. kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb, door "movies" >>>
  and what my plugin does with that data: <<< e.g. a movie quiz / a "random movie tonight" screen >>>
- If provider: what other plugins could ask for: <<< e.g. "a song's lyrics by title and artist", "today's matches" >>>
  and where that data comes from: <<< e.g. kino.tmdb / my site https://example.org/api >>>
- Should my plugin stay installable on older Kinos? <<< yes (use enhancements["20"]) / no (apiVersion 20) >>>
- Name in Kino and a short description: <<< e.g. "Cine Trivia": "Preguntas de cine con películas de TMDB" >>>
- My GitHub user: <<< e.g. my-user >>>

Rules:
- Kino is the only middleman: never import, fetch or copy the other plugin; a consumer only uses
  `await kino.plugins.call(alias, call, arg)` with a "consumes" entry; a provider only answers through
  exports named exactly proto_<door>_<call>(arg) and proto_<door>_<stream>(cursor) -> { items, cursor }.
- Names of doors, calls, streams and aliases: letters and digits, starting with a letter, at most 32. Types
  only from the closed language (string, number, boolean, T?, T[], a door type, an inline object).
- Consumer: list in "consumes" only the calls and streams it uses, put the same repository in "recommends",
  and while installed["owner/name"] is not true draw ONLY an install screen with one button
  { go: { installPlugin: { repo: "owner/name" } } }; never install anything yourself. Every
  kino.plugins.call goes in try/catch and shows a short message for each code (provider_missing,
  not_declared, bad_input, bad_output, rate_limited, timeout, provider_failed); no retry loops, no calls from
  a background job. Arguments never carry tokens, passwords or anything private: they reach the provider.
- Provider: answer only what the door declares, nothing private in answers or thrown errors, never a sealed
  secret; a short "summary" the person understands; once published, a door only grows (new calls,
  optional fields).
- Limits: 64 KB per request and answer, 10 s per call, 30 calls in any 10 s per door, 4 doors per plugin,
  16 calls and 8 streams per door, 8 consumes entries, streams polled every 30 s at least.
- Every text for the person in Spanish (neutral, tuteo, never voseo) and English (text + textEn).
- A screen-only consumer (apiVersion 20, a non-empty "consumes", "capabilities" exactly ["screen"]) declares
  "hosts": [] (an Image needs no host declaration; its own kino.fetch is refused with no host unless it declares
  fetchHosts "any" or a url setting). Any other capability brings back "at least one host": then list only the real
  hosts its kino.fetch reaches. Never example.com or an invented host (validate warns on a placeholder). See
  https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol/#consumer-hosts. A provides-only plugin (apiVersion 20,
  provides, no capabilities, no settings) may also have "hosts": []; there is no "providesOnly" field.
- Screen trees: a Scaffold whose appBar is { "type": "AppBar", ... }; SingleChildScrollView takes "children"
  (a list), never "child"; buttons are ElevatedButton/TextButton with labelText + labelTextEn and onPressed
  (FilledButton does not exist). Copy the minimal consumer screen of AGENTS.md section 4.

Start from the kit's scaffold, not from a blank file: `node sdk/init.mjs my-plugin --kind provider` or
`node sdk/init.mjs my-plugin --kind consumer --repo owner/name --door <door> --call <call>` (`"hosts": []`)
(`node sdk/init.mjs --help`), replace its stand-in `test/provider` with a copy of the real provider, then copy `sdk/`
without `sdk/test/` and `contract.json` next to it (`kino.d.ts` is optional, only editor typings). Test it offline before anything else:
`node sdk/validate.mjs .` (no ✗, and read every ! line); for a provider
`node sdk/run.mjs . proto <door>.<call> '<json>'` and `node sdk/run.mjs . proto <door>.<stream> ['<cursor>']`;
for a consumer `node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"installed":{"owner/name":true}}' --provider <provider folder> . screen`
(also with false, with --lang en and with --device tv: no "dropped" line on stderr), the same --context and
--provider with `screenEvent <event>`, and `screenEvent protocol <alias>.<stream>` (with --cursor '<json>' to
try repeated items). The kit ignores "repo" (it uses the first provider with the door): check it by hand.
If run.mjs does not know --provider or proto, or init.mjs does not know --kind, tell me how to get a newer kit
instead of working around it. The kit does not check the 18+ rule, sealed secrets in answers nor self-calls:
when you finish, tell me how to try it in Kino 0.9.81 or newer with both plugins installed, then with the
provider switched off and removed, with the exact clicks.
```

## Getting Kino to find your plugin { #listed }

Installing it by typing its address works from the start. For it to also show up by itself in Kino,
in the "De la comunidad" tab of the Plugins screen, the repository must:

1. be **public** and **not a fork** (create it with "Use this template");
2. have `kino-plugin.json` at its root, valid for `node sdk/validate.mjs .`, with a `name` and a
   `description` in Spanish (that is what the card shows);
3. carry the topic **`kino-plugin`** (About → ⚙ → Topics) and, better, a GitHub description;
4. on Kino 0.9.53 and older, be among the 30 with the most stars on the topic.

From Kino 0.9.54 the app reads the matches 100 at a time, in the order the person picks ("Populares"
or "Recientes"), "Cargar más" reads the next 100, and "Buscar en GitHub" finds a plugin by its
repository's name and description, so a plugin with no stars is found too. Each device searches again
every 12 hours, or when "Actualizar" is tapped. The exact clicks and how
to check it: [Get listed in Kino](listed.md).

With Kino 0.9.77 (apiVersion 15) the app no longer searches GitHub by itself: the "De la
comunidad" tab of the store view (beside "De Kino" and "Instalados") is filled by Kino Plugins, whose daily index is built
from the repositories with the `kino-plugin` topic; the rules above still apply. There is one plugin per `id` across stores,
and a reload icon ends with a toast ("Se actualizaron N plugins" or "Tus plugins están al día").

## Signed plugins { #signed }

If you want people to know that every update comes from you, ask for a [signed plugin](signed.md)
(`"apiVersion": 5`, Kino 0.9.45+): you make a key once, the assistant signs `plugin.js` with it
after every change, and Kino checks the signature at install and at each update. The private key
stays on your computer: it must **never** go to GitHub (`*.pem` in `.gitignore`), and you should back
it up, because if it is lost, everyone who installed the plugin has to uninstall and reinstall it.
It is optional: an unsigned plugin works the same. [Read the whole page](signed.md).

## If something fails { #troubleshooting }

Paste **the full text** the terminal printed into the assistant (not a summary) and say what you
expected. Some common cases:

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `node: command not found`, "node is not recognized…" | Node is not installed, or you opened the terminal before installing it: install it and open a new terminal. |
| `✗ kino-plugin.json: …` | The manifest breaks a rule; the message is the one Kino gives. Ask the assistant to fix it following AGENTS.md. |
| `[dropped by Kino] …` | Kino would drop those results. Ask which rule of [the contract](contract.md) they break, instead of accepting a blind patch. |
| `[host_not_allowed] …` | A host missing from `hosts`: have it declared. |
| `El campo "entry" debe ser una ruta relativa a un archivo .js` (Kino) or `Quita el "./" del campo "entry"` (kit) | `"entry"` (or `"icon"`) starts with `./`. Write `"plugin.js"`: Kino 0.9.45 and older refuse the `./` ([why](manifest.md#entry-dot-slash)). |
| `La firma del autor no es válida…` | The plugin is [signed](signed.md) and `plugin.js` or `version` changed after signing: run `node sdk/seal.mjs --sign --repo owner/repo` again. |
| `[timeout] …` | The source is slow or there are too many requests: have it make fewer requests per call. |
| Works in the kit but fails in Kino | The Node kit is more permissive than the app ([what it does not reproduce](test-locally.md#differences)): missing globals, a `throw` before the first `await` (on Kino 0.9.49 and older), `kino.html.select`. Give the assistant the exact message Kino shows (or a photo of the screen). |
| Kino says "Configura … en Ajustes ▸ Plugins" | The plugin needs data: tap the message's Configurar button, or go to Plugins → Instalados → your plugin → Configurar. |
| It does not show in "De la comunidad" | See [Get listed in Kino](listed.md). |

**Kino's logs** (for someone with a computer connected to the phone with `adb`):
`adb logcat -s KinoPlugin` shows what the plugin writes with `kino.log`. Never paste passwords or
keys into the chat.

## Tips { #tips }

- **Give the assistant a terminal.** The kit only helps if the assistant can run
  `node sdk/validate.mjs .` and `node sdk/run.mjs …` and read what they print.
- **Try it in the app.** The Node kit is more permissive than Kino
  ([what it does not reproduce](test-locally.md#differences)): install the plugin and check that it
  searches, lists episodes, plays (and downloads, if you declared it) before sharing it.
- **Ask for the reasons.** When the kit reports a dropped item, ask the assistant which rule of
  [the contract](contract.md) it broke, instead of accepting a patch.
- **Raise the version on every change.** Kino only installs an update whose `version` is higher
  ([Publishing](publish.md#updates)).
- **Mind the rights.** A plugin can only reach what the person could watch anyway; do not ask an
  assistant to get around a paywall, a login or DRM.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/manifest/ (docs/manifest.en.md) -->

# The manifest

`kino-plugin.json`, at most 16 KB:

```json
{
  "id": "archive-org",
  "name": "Internet Archive",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 1,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Películas de dominio público y televisión clásica de archive.org",
  "author": "kinotvapp",
  "homepage": "https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-archive",
  "hosts": ["archive.org", "*.archive.org"],
  "capabilities": ["search", "home", "browse", "episodes", "resolve"],
  "color": "#E0A030",
  "icon": "icon.png"
}
```

If a rule below is broken, Kino refuses to install the plugin and shows a message in Spanish that
names the field.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Required. `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` (2 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, not starting with a hyphen). Not one of `live`, `local`, `unknown`, `plugin`, `own`, `subtitle-keys`, `subtitle-prefs` (Kino's own names; older versions reserve a few more: if one says "El id … está reservado por Kino", pick another). It is the plugin's identity: never change it once people have installed it. |
| `name` | Required. 1 to 40 characters. |
| `version` | Required. `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and nothing else (no `-beta`, no `+build`), each number up to 6 digits and without leading zeros. |
| `apiVersion` | Required. `1` to `26` (`26` adds to `appThemes` the painted [surfaces, gloss, layouts, assets, background picture and font](themes.md#level2), in the next Kino release (provisionally 0.9.87), not published yet; `25` lets a stream subtitle carry its own decrypted `text` instead of a `url`, Kino 0.9.86; `24` lets a stream's `drm` be a list and adds the `clearkey` type, Kino 0.9.85; `23` adds the [`playerSlot`](player-slot.md) capability and the [`slot`](#slot) block, in the next Kino release (provisionally 0.9.83), not published yet; `22` adds the [`progress`](progress.md) capability, in the next Kino release, not published yet; `21` adds the [`files`](files.md) capability, Kino 0.9.82): `12`, `13` and `14` arrive together in Kino 0.9.74. A higher number than Kino supports is refused with "Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino". Declare the lowest number that has what you use, so your plugin also runs on older Kino builds: `2` for `download`, `drm`, `insecureHttp`, `"hosts": []` or `live` items; `3` for `channels`/`liveStreamHosts`; `4` for a `list` setting, `streamHosts` or `secrets`; `5` only for a [signed plugin](signed.md) (Kino 0.9.45+); `6` (Kino 0.9.50+) for anything on the [apiVersion 6 list](changelog.md#v0950): typed or larger sealed secrets, `migrate`, `scopedSearch`, request-signed streams, the settings form's `section`/`status`/`action`, `debug`, `telemetry`, `section`, `categories`, `theme`, `userMessage`, `adult` entries, channels in Home rows, `kino.crypto`'s key-pair calls, the `meta` capability, [`"browser": true`](browser.md) with `kino.browser.capture` (and `"browser": "pages"` with `kino.browser.page` too), and [labelled and lazy copies](contract.md#lazy-copies); `7` (Kino 0.9.51+) for the [`tracking`](contract.md#tracking) and [`segments`](contract.md#segments) capabilities; `8` (Kino 0.9.54+) for [`music` and `podcast` items](contract.md#music-podcasts) and the [`details`](contract.md#details) export; `9` (Kino 0.9.55+) for `section.labelEn`, the [player panel](player-panel.md#manifest), `settingsLayout` and a hand-written plugin's `fetchHosts: "any"`; `10` (Kino 0.9.65+) for the [`playlists`](contract.md#playlists) capability (still just a contract -- no plugin uses it today); `11` (Kino 0.9.66+) for the [`externalResolve`](resolver.md) capability and the manifest's [`externalResolver`](#external-resolver); `12` (Kino 0.9.74+) for the [`syncProvider`](sync-providers.md) capability, the manifest's [`sync`](#sync) block and the settings form's [`link` and `help`](settings-form.md#aids) types; `13` (Kino 0.9.74+) for the `socket` and `byteSource` capabilities ([Sockets and plugin-served bytes](bytes.md)), `storageLarge` and `catalog` ([Catalog and large storage](catalog.md)), `qrScan` and the settings form's `qr` type ([QR codes](qr.md)), `imageSource` ([Images from the plugin](images.md)); `14` (Kino 0.9.74+) for the [`screen`](screens.md) capability with its [`screen`](#screen) block, the `library`, `room` and `playerControl` capabilities ([Rooms, the library and player control](rooms.md)), `playerPanelTab` ([The player panel](player-panel.md#contributed-tab)), `schedule` with [`jobs`](#jobs), `ai` and `shared` ([Background jobs, shared results and AI](jobs-and-shared.md)), a setting's [`unlockWith`](settings-form.md#unlock-with) and [`kino.fetch`](kino-api.md#fetch)'s `maxBytes` and `stopAt` options; `15` (Kino 0.9.77) for the [`identity`](identity.md), [`notifications`](notifications.md) and [`pluginStore`](plugin-stores.md) capabilities with their [`pluginStore`](#plugin-store) block, and for `season` and `episode` in `kino.library.watched()`; `16` (Kino 0.9.78) for the [`coins`](kino-api.md#coins) capability (`kino.coins`: the person's Kino coins balance, and giving one coin for a post) and for [`kino.sync.setActive`](kino-api.md#sync-active), which is not an `apiVersion`; `17` for [`kino.library.stats`](kino-api.md#library-stats) (a month's aggregates of what the person watched, for the `library` capability; Kino 0.9.81), a job's `"perProfile"` ([Background jobs](jobs-and-shared.md)), `kino.tmdb` inside a job and 60 s and 20 requests for a job with `ai`; `18` (Kino 0.9.81) for [`appThemes`](#app-themes) (whole-app themes), `go.useTheme`, `go.setExperience` and `activeTheme` ([App themes](themes.md)); `19` (Kino 0.9.81) for the [`lyrics`](contract.md#lyrics) capability and [`go.installPlugin`](screen-forms.md#go-install-plugin); `20` (Kino 0.9.81) for the [plugin protocol](protocol.md): [`provides`](#provides), [`consumes`](#consumes) and `kino.plugins.call` (both blocks also work inside `enhancements["20"]` without raising yours), and for [`visualBrowser`](#visual-browser) and `kino.visualBrowser.open` ([a browser window the person drives](visual-browser.md)); the [`enhancements`](#enhancements) block is read by Kino 0.9.74 at any `apiVersion` (`kino.crypto`'s byte operations come with the same Kino version at any `apiVersion`; a stream's advisory `media` and its `portable` copy are read at any `apiVersion`). |
| `entry` | Required. Relative path of the JavaScript file: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and `/` only, no `..`, at most 200 characters, ends in `.js`. The file is at most 1 MB. **Write `"plugin.js"`, never `"./plugin.js"`**: Kino 0.9.45 and older refuse a leading `./` (see the warning [below](#entry-dot-slash)). |
| `signature` | Optional, from apiVersion 5: `{ "authorKey": "<64 hex>", "value": "<128 hex>" }`, written by `node sdk/seal.mjs --sign`: your signature over the entry file. Needs Kino 0.9.45+. See [Signed plugins](signed.md). Below apiVersion 5 it is ignored. <a id="signature"></a> |
| `hosts` | Required. at least 1 entry, with no upper limit from Kino 0.9.45 (only the manifest's 16 KB bounds it). Kino 0.9.44 and older refuse more than 20, so with more than 20 hosts the kit warns "Más de 20 hosts: Kino 0.9.44 o anterior rechaza este plugin; necesita Kino 0.9.45 o superior". From apiVersion 2 it may be empty, `[]`, when the plugin has a `url` setting: see [The person's own servers](#own-servers)). From apiVersion 18 it may also be empty in a plugin that only ships [`appThemes`](themes.md): it reaches nothing, and its card says it doesn't connect to the internet. From apiVersion 20 it may also be empty in a plugin that only opens doors with [`provides`](protocol.md#provides-only), and in a [screen-only consumer](protocol.md#consumer-hosts): a non-empty `consumes` and `capabilities` exactly `["screen"]` (its own `kino.fetch` is then refused unless it declares `fetchHosts: "any"` or a `url` setting; pictures from public https addresses need no host; with no setting at all its card says it doesn't connect to the internet). Never a placeholder such as `example.com`: `sdk/validate.mjs` warns on one. Each a lowercase DNS name (`archive.org`), `*.` plus a DNS name (`*.archive.org`), or (apiVersion 2 only) an object `{ "host": "…", "insecureHttp": true }` (below). Host names only: no scheme, port or path. No bare `*`, no IP addresses, no `localhost`, nothing ending in `.local`, `.lan`, `.internal`, `.localhost` or `.home.arpa`, and at least one dot. **`*.x` covers subdomains only, not `x` itself**: if you need both, list both. The hosts a person approves later, one by one, while your plugin runs ([A host you forgot](contract.md#forgotten-host)) are not counted against the manifest. |
| `capabilities` | Required. A subset of `search`, `home`, `browse`, `episodes`, `resolve`, `download`, `drm`, `channels`, `migrate`, `scopedSearch`, `meta`, `subtitles`, `tracking`, `segments`, `lyrics`, `playlists`, `externalResolve`, `nuvio` (apiVersion 11, with `nuvioRepos`), `syncProvider`, from apiVersion 13 `socket`, `byteSource`, `storageLarge`, `catalog`, `qrScan`, `imageSource`, and from apiVersion 14 `screen`, `library`, `playerPanelTab`, `playerControl`, `room`, `schedule`, `ai` and `shared`, and from apiVersion 15 `identity`, `notifications` and `pluginStore`, and from apiVersion 16 `coins`, and from apiVersion 21 `files`, and from apiVersion 22 [`progress`](progress.md) (declarative, no consent line; it may stand alone or sit beside any other capability and the plugin stays that kind of plugin), and from apiVersion 23 [`playerSlot`](player-slot.md) (the exports `playerSlot` and `playerSlotAction` and the [`slot`](#slot) block; it may be the plugin's only capability; red consent line only with a `fixed` element). Must include `resolve` and at least one of `search` or `home`, except in a [catalog-only plugin](contract.md#catalog-only) (`"catalogOnly": true`, Kino 0.9.54) and a plugin that declares only `subtitles`, `tracking`, `segments` and/or `syncProvider` (below); from apiVersion 13 such a plugin may also declare `socket`, `storageLarge`, `catalog` and `qrScan` and stay that kind of plugin (a sync provider that talks over `kino.ws`, `["syncProvider", "socket"]`), while those four alone, with none of the four above, still need `resolve` and `search` or `home`. `search`, `home`, `browse`, `episodes` and `resolve` must each be an exported function of the entry file, or the install fails with "El plugin no carga: le falta ...". `download` and `drm` need `apiVersion: 2` and are declarative flags instead — the app acts on them, not your code, so nothing extra to export; declaring one shows its consent line ("Puede descargar videos para verlos sin conexión" / "Reproduce video protegido (DRM)") and needs approval again on an update that adds it. `download` gives your titles offline downloads (see [Downloads](#downloads)); `drm` lets a `Stream` carry a Widevine license (see [A Widevine-protected stream](cookbook.md#widevine)). `channels` needs `apiVersion: 3` and the exports `liveCategories` and `liveChannels` (see [Channels in the En vivo tab](live-channels.md#en-vivo-tab)). `migrate` needs `apiVersion: 6` and the export `migrate`; declaring it shows "Revisar lo que tienes guardado (biblioteca, historial, favoritos) para pasarlo a este plugin" and needs approval again on an update that adds it (see [Moving saved titles](migrate.md)). `scopedSearch` needs `apiVersion: 6` and `search` (refused otherwise with "La capacidad \"scopedSearch\" necesita también \"search\""); it exports nothing of its own: your `search` gets `within` when the person searches inside a "Ver más" page (see [Searching inside a "Ver más" page](contract.md#scoped-search)). `meta` needs `apiVersion: 6` and the export `meta`, no consent line (see [Describing other titles](contract.md#meta)). `subtitles` needs the export `subtitles`; `["subtitles"]` alone is a subtitle provider; a plugin that declares only `subtitles`, `tracking` and/or `segments` (a subtitle provider, a tracker, a segment source or a mix of them) is also an exception to "`resolve` and `search` or `home`" (see [Subtitles for any title](contract.md#subtitles)). `tracking` needs `apiVersion: 7` and the export `track`; declaring it shows a red line naming your hosts ("Le contará a seenr.app qué ves y cuándo lo terminas") and needs approval again on an update that adds it, even when Kino approves other updates on its own (see [Telling a tracker what the person watches](contract.md#tracking)). `segments` needs `apiVersion: 7` and the export `segments`; declaring it shows "Agrega el botón para saltar la intro y los créditos", not in red and with no approval of its own (see [Where the intro and credits are](contract.md#segments)). `playlists` needs `apiVersion: 10`; unlike the others, none of its six exports (`playlists`, `playlistItems`, `playlistCreate`, `playlistAddItem`, `playlistRemoveItem`, `playlistReorder`) is required -- declare only the ones your service supports; no consent line of its own; still no installed or announced plugin uses it, and Kino doesn't wire it into any screen yet (see [Playlists](contract.md#playlists)). `externalResolve` needs `apiVersion: 11`, a declarative flag like `download` and `drm` (nothing to export): it lets a `resolve()` answer (or one of a Stream's `alternatives`) be `{ external: { protocol, ref } }` instead of a playable `url`, so Kino hands `ref` to an independently-installed resolver app; it adds no consent line to your install sheet (the only consent is per app, asked the first time one is needed; see [External resolver apps](resolver.md) and [the contract](contract.md#external-resolve)). `syncProvider` needs `apiVersion: 12` (Kino 0.9.74) and the exports `syncPull` and `syncPush` (`syncStatus` optional); it may be the plugin's only capability. The plugin becomes the transport of the person's cross-device sync: Kino encrypts the snapshot and hands the plugin an opaque base64 blob to store and give back byte for byte. It requires the manifest's [`sync`](#sync) block with `keySecret`. Declaring it shows one consent line, always in red, "Sincronizará tus datos a través de su servicio: el plugin y su servicio podrán leerlos", and needs approval again on an update that adds it (never approved on its own). See [Sync providers](sync-providers.md). The six of apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74) show no consent line and need no approval of their own: `socket` is declarative and unlocks `kino.ws`, WebSockets to your declared hosts only; `byteSource` needs the export `read` and lets a stream be `{ source: "plugin", handle, size, mime }` ([Sockets and plugin-served bytes](bytes.md)); `storageLarge` is declarative and makes `kino.storage` 16 MB, device-only; `catalog` is declarative and unlocks `kino.catalog` ([Catalog and large storage](catalog.md)); `qrScan` is declarative and unlocks `kino.qr.scan` ([QR codes](qr.md)); `imageSource` needs the export `image` and lets a `poster`, `backdrop`, `still` or section hero `image` be `{ source: "plugin", handle }` ([Images from the plugin](images.md)). Each one below `"apiVersion": 13` is refused ("The \"catalog\" capability needs apiVersion 13"). The eight of apiVersion 14 (Kino 0.9.74): `screen` needs the exports `screen` and `screenEvent` and the [`screen`](#screen) block, may be the plugin's only capability and shows no consent line ([Screens](screens.md)); `library` (declarative, may stand alone) reads what the person watched and saved ([`kino.library`](rooms.md#library)); `playerPanelTab` needs the export `panel` and `"panel": { "contributes": true }`, may stand alone and adds a tab to the player panel of any plugin's title ([The player panel](player-panel.md#contributed-tab)); `playerControl` (declarative, never alone, needs a `panel`) lets your player actions pause and move the video on their own ([Player control](rooms.md#player-control)); `room` (declarative, never alone) unlocks [`kino.room`](rooms.md#room), rooms over the Internet hosted on the person's device; `schedule` needs the export `job` and the [`jobs`](#jobs) block, never alone ([Background jobs](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs)); `ai` (declarative, never alone) unlocks [`kino.ai.ask`](jobs-and-shared.md#ai); `shared` (declarative, never alone) unlocks [`kino.shared`](jobs-and-shared.md#shared). `library`, `playerPanelTab`, `playerControl`, `room`, `schedule` and `ai` each show a red consent line and need approval at install and on the update that adds them (never approved by Kino on its own), and the person can switch them off in your tab in Ajustes; `shared` shows a plain line, not red, and waits for no approval. A plugin that stays on a lower `apiVersion` can offer them through [`enhancements`](enhancements.md). The three of apiVersion 15 (Kino 0.9.77) are not offered through `enhancements`: `identity` (declarative, never alone) unlocks [`kino.identity.telegram`](identity.md), with a red consent line, and answers only plugins signed with Kino's own author key; `notifications` (declarative, never alone) unlocks [`kino.notifications`](notifications.md), with a plain line; `pluginStore` needs the export `storeSync` (and `storeList` and `storeSearch` for a live store), may stand alone and makes your plugin a source of plugins for Kino's store, with a plain line and, for a live store, a red one ([Plugin stores](plugin-stores.md)). All three need approval at install and on the update that adds them, and the person can switch `identity` and `notifications` off in your tab in Ajustes. `coins` (apiVersion 16, Kino 0.9.78; declarative, never alone and not offered through `enhancements` either) unlocks [`kino.coins`](kino-api.md#coins), the person's Kino coins balance and giving one coin, with a red consent line («Podrá ver tu saldo de kinos y regalar tus kinos»); it needs approval the same way and has no switch of its own: the person revokes it by disabling or removing your plugin. From apiVersion 20 a plugin whose only purpose is a non-empty [`provides`](#provides) may declare no capability at all (the field may be left out): see [A plugin that only provides](protocol.md#provides-only). `provides` and `consumes` are not capabilities: a provider or a consumer keeps the capabilities of the kind of plugin it is. |
| `settings` | Optional. What the person fills in on your plugin's "Configurar" screen: see below. |
| `permissions` | Optional. A list of names from the closed list in `contract.json`. **The list is empty in this version**: any name is refused with "permiso desconocido: …". It exists so a later version can add permissions (each one shown on the consent screen) without a new `apiVersion`. |
| `color` | Optional `#RRGGBB`: the accent of your plugin's tab and chips. A neutral color by default. |
| `icon` | Optional relative path to a square `.png`, at most 128 KB. An icon that is missing or too big is skipped without failing the install. |
| `discoverable` | Optional `true` or `false` (default `true`), at every `apiVersion`. `false` keeps the plugin out of Kino's community search (see [Get found](publish.md#get-found)); people can still install it by typing its address. Any other value is refused with "El campo \"discoverable\" debe ser true o false". |
| `categories` | Optional, at every `apiVersion`: what your plugin offers, for the category chips of Kino's plugin marketplace (Recomendados, "De la comunidad", "Elige tus plugins"). A list without repeats of `movies`, `series`, `anime`, `live`, `radio`, `subtitles`, `utilities`, `themes`, `adult` (`themes`: a plugin that offers [app themes](themes.md), listed under Temas), or of a **new type** of your own (`manga`, `audio-books`): 2 to 24 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. A new type needs no change in Kino: its chip (the id with hyphens as spaces and a capital first letter: "Manga", "Audio books") shows up by itself while some listed plugin carries it. Declare a new type in the **catalog entry** whenever you can: a Kino that predates new types refuses a manifest that names one, while it silently drops the id from a catalog entry. When present it replaces Kino's guess from your capabilities (`channels` is `live`, `episodes` is `series`, anything that lists and plays is `movies`); an `adult` plugin's chip only shows while the person's 18+ code is unlocked. Any other value is refused with "El campo \"categories\" debe ser una lista sin repetidos de: movies, series, anime, live, radio, subtitles, utilities, themes, adult, o un tipo nuevo (de 2 a 24 letras minúsculas, dígitos y guiones, empezando por una letra)". Not the same as the `categories()` export (tiles inside Kino's Categorías, see [Section, categories and colors](section-theme.md)). |
| `catalogOnly` | Optional `true` or `false` (default `false`), at every `apiVersion`, from Kino 0.9.54 (older Kino ignores it). `true` says the plugin lists and describes titles but plays none: `resolve` is no longer required, and Kino never calls it; its titles go to "Buscar dónde verlo". It needs one of `home`, `browse`, `search` or `meta`, and refuses `download`, `drm`, `channels`, `streamHosts` and `"browser": true`. To stay installable on Kino 0.9.53 and older, keep declaring and exporting `resolve` (failing with `not_found`) and `search` or `home`. See [Catalog-only plugins](contract.md#catalog-only). Any other value is refused with "El campo \"catalogOnly\" debe ser true o false". |
| `recommends` | <a id="recommends"></a>Optional (Kino 0.9.81), at every `apiVersion` (an older Kino ignores it; it has no `apiVersion` of its own): a list of at most 8 plain GitHub `owner/name` strings, the plugins yours works better with (no URL, no sub-path, no `@ref`, at most 100 characters each; the case you write is kept, repeats ignoring case collapse). Anything else is refused: `The "recommends" field must be a list of at most 8 plain GitHub owner/name repositories`. Your `screen` and `screenEvent` get `installed`, `{ "<repo as written>": true \| false }` for these entries only, to offer a [`go.installPlugin`](screen-forms.md#go-install-plugin) button for each missing one: see [Recommended plugins and `installed`](screen-forms.md#recommends-installed). A protocol consumer names its provider here too ([the install gate](protocol.md#install-gate)). |
| `creator` | Optional, at every `apiVersion` (Kino never reads it; no `apiVersion` of its own). Your Kino Social handle (3 to 20 characters: letters, digits and `_`), e.g. `"lordmacu"`. It only rides along in the published `kino-plugin.json` so Kino Social's community-plugin index can attach the plugin to your profile there. Leave it out and the plugin simply appears on no Kino Social profile. A value that does not match that shape is ignored. |
| `provides` | <a id="provides"></a>Optional, `apiVersion` 20 (Kino 0.9.81; also inside `enhancements["20"]`, which keeps your `apiVersion`): the doors this plugin opens to other plugins, `{ "<door>": { "summary", "calls", "streams", "types" } }`: at most 4 doors, each with a `summary` of at most 120 characters, at most 16 calls and 8 streams, answered by your exports `proto_<door>_<call>(arg)` and `proto_<door>_<stream>(cursor)`. Kino checks every request and answer against the declared types. A malformed block refuses the manifest with a message naming the door and the field; a top-level block below `apiVersion` 20 is refused with `The "provides" block needs apiVersion 20`. A plugin with only `provides` needs no capability and may have `"hosts": []`. See [The plugin protocol](protocol.md#provides). |
| `consumes` | <a id="consumes"></a>Optional, `apiVersion` 20 (Kino 0.9.81; also inside `enhancements["20"]`): the doors of other plugins this one uses, `{ "<alias>": { "repo", "door", "calls", "streams" } }`: at most 8 entries; `repo` the provider's plain GitHub `owner/name` (a fork does not stand in), `door` its door, `calls` (at most 16) and `streams` (at most 8) the names you use. Your code calls `await kino.plugins.call("<alias>", "<call>", arg)`; the consent sheet shows «Usa datos de <provider> (<door summary>)». Pair it with `recommends` and `go.installPlugin` to invite the person to install the provider. See [The plugin protocol](protocol.md#consumes). |
| `openFrom` | <a id="open-from"></a>Optional, `apiVersion` 20 (Kino 0.9.84, not published yet; also inside `enhancements["20"]`): `{ "routes": ["detail", …] }`, the names of your own screen routes that other plugins' cards may open with [`go.plugin`](share.md#go-plugin). It needs the `screen` capability. 1 to 16 different names, each 1 to 64 letters, digits or `. _ ~ -` (the same names a `go.screen` `route` takes). It says what may be opened, not how: you decide later, in your screen, how each route reaches its content. A card whose route you do not list falls back to a search. A bad list refuses the manifest with a message naming `openFrom.routes`. See [Sharing](share.md#open-from). |
| `visualBrowser` | <a id="visual-browser"></a>Optional `true` or `false` (default `false`), `apiVersion` 20 (Kino 0.9.81; also inside `enhancements["20"]`, which keeps your `apiVersion`); below it the key is ignored and any other value is refused (`The "visualBrowser" field must be true or false`). `true` lets the plugin open `kino.visualBrowser.open`, a web window the person drives on the plugin's own `hosts`. Not a capability: nothing is approved at install except a plain consent line, and Kino asks in its own sheet at every open. See [A browser window the person drives](visual-browser.md). |
| `browser` | Optional `true`, `false` or `"pages"`, from `apiVersion` 6; ignored below. `true` lets the plugin open pages in a hidden web view on the device with `kino.browser.capture` (in `resolve`), shown in red as "Puede abrir páginas web ocultas para encontrar el video"; `"pages"` adds `kino.browser.page`, shown as "Puede abrir páginas web ocultas para mostrar contenido y encontrar el video". An update that adds it, or moves `true` to `"pages"`, waits for approval again; an approved plugin's `resolve` gets 75 s. See [Hidden browser](browser.md). Any other value is refused with "El campo \"browser\" debe ser true, false o \"pages\"". |
| `externalResolver` | <a id="external-resolver"></a>Optional, from `apiVersion` 11, and only with the `externalResolve` capability (otherwise the manifest is refused: `The "externalResolver" field needs the "externalResolve" capability`): `{ "package": "com.example.resolver", "apk"?: { "url": "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>.apk", "sha256": "<64 hex characters>", "label"?: "..." }, "fdroid"?: true, "downloader"?: { "code": "<3 to 10 digits>" } }`. `package` is the one resolver app this plugin wants its `external` answers handed to; with it set, no other app is ever asked, whatever else declares the protocol (a stream's own `external.resolver` overrides it). `apk`, `fdroid` and `downloader` are optional and independent ways to get that app when it is not installed: `apk` is where Kino may offer to download it. Only a GitHub release asset (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<file>`) or an archive.org file (`https://archive.org/download/<item>/<file>`) is accepted (https, no query), at most 300 MB, and the downloaded file must have exactly that `sha256` or nothing is offered; `label` is the app's name for the person (at most 40 characters). `fdroid: true` says the same `package` is listed in F-Droid (Kino opens F-Droid for exactly that package; only `true` is accepted). `downloader.code` is a Downloader (TV sideloading app) code of 3 to 10 digits that Kino only shows. Anything malformed refuses the manifest (`The "externalResolver" field must be an object with a "package" (an Android package name) and, optionally, an "apk" with a GitHub release "url" ... and a 64-character hex "sha256"; "fdroid" may only be true and "downloader" an object with a "code" of 3 to 10 digits`). Older Kino ignores the field. See [External resolver apps](resolver.md). |
| `sync` | <a id="sync"></a>From `apiVersion` 12 (Kino 0.9.74), **required** with the `syncProvider` capability and only with it (otherwise the manifest is refused: `The "sync" field needs the "syncProvider" capability`; a provider without it or without `keySecret`: `The "syncProvider" capability needs a "sync" field whose "keySecret" is the key of one of the plugin's own "password" settings`): `{ "mode"?: "poll" \| "realtime", "pullEveryMs"?: 600000, "pushDebounceMs"?: 300000, "maxBlobBytes"?: 4194304, "keySecret": "<setting key>", "provision": ["<setting key>", ...] }`. `mode` defaults to `poll` (Kino pulls when it comes to the front and every `pullEveryMs`, and pushes `pushDebounceMs` after a change); `realtime` lets the provider call [`kino.sync.remoteChanged()`](kino-api.md#sync) when it learns the remote moved. The times are positive whole milliseconds that Kino clamps to its own floors. `maxBlobBytes` is the largest blob the provider accepts (default and maximum 4194304, 4 MiB); it also sets how big `syncPull`/`syncPush`'s `kino.fetch` requests, responses and answers may be (ceil(maxBlobBytes × 4/3) + 64 KB). `keySecret` names one of your own `password` settings (with no `default`): Kino derives the sync key from its value on each device, so the key never travels, and the plugin and its service **can** read the synced data (red consent line). `provision` lists at most 8 of your own valued settings (secret or not) that "Enviar configuración" ("Send settings") hands to a second device; it must include `keySecret`, and from apiVersion 13 it may name a `"sync": false` password as a one-shot secret (never as `keySecret`), never a `"sync": false` text. From apiVersion 13, `"generateKey": true` makes Kino create the `keySecret` value itself (32 random bytes as hex) while it is empty ([A key Kino makes](sync-providers.md#generate-key)); anything but a boolean is refused. Every rule, message and trade-off: [Sync providers](sync-providers.md#sync-block). Older Kino ignores the field. |
| `screen` | <a id="screen"></a>From `apiVersion` 14 (Kino 0.9.74), required with the `screen` capability: the menu entry and the options of the plugin's full-screen canvas, `{ "label": "Noticias", "labelEn": "News", "icon": "list", "menuOpens": "screen" }`. Every field and rule: [The manifest's `screen` block](screens.md#manifest). |
| `jobs` | <a id="jobs"></a>From `apiVersion` 14 (Kino 0.9.74), required with the `schedule` capability and refused without it: 1 to 3 background jobs, each `{ "id": "refresh", "label": { "es": "Actualizar noticias", "en": "Refresh news" }, "everyMin": 60, "everyOptions": [15, 30, 60, 180, 720, 1440] }`, with an optional `runOn` (`"any"` or `"preferPhone"`) and `perProfile` (apiVersion 17, `true` or `false`, always with `runOn: "any"`): one run per profile of the device with your plugin on. Every field and rule: [Background jobs](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs). |
| `slot` | <a id="slot"></a>From `apiVersion` 23 (the next Kino release, provisionally 0.9.83, not published yet), with the `playerSlot` capability (each needs the other): `{ "elements": [ { "id", "kind", "mode" } ] }`, 1 to 3 elements; `id` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,23}$` and is unique; `kind` is `text`, `icon`, `image` or `button`; `mode` is `overlay` (shows with the controls) or `fixed` (always there; a red consent line). Up to three small elements in the top-right corner of the TV player: see [The player slot](player-slot.md). |
