2. **The person's own key, only when Kino's fails**: TMDB refuses Kino's key (401/403), TMDB rate-limits it (429), or one
   of Kino's two limits above is spent. Then the same request goes again with the key the person typed in **Ajustes de todos los perfiles
   ▸ Llaves ▸ Tu llave de TMDB** (optional; a v3 API key, 32 hexadecimal characters, or a v4 read access token; synced between their
   devices), else the key they configured in an **installed Stremio addon** (Kino looks in each addon's saved
   configuration for a field whose name contains "tmdb", no addon is listed by name, and uses it only after the person said
   yes once to "Usar la llave de TMDB de tu addon <name>", also synced).
3. **With neither**: a copy from the cache up to 7 days old when there is one; otherwise `rate_limited` (Kino's limit, or
   TMDB's 429) or `unavailable` (TMDB refused Kino's key).

`no_tmdb_key` is left for a Kino build with no key of its own and a person with none either: `e.userMessage` is then Kino's
own sentence for the person, in their language: "Agrega tu llave de TMDB en Ajustes de todos los perfiles ▸ Llaves" /
"Add your TMDB key in Settings for all profiles ▸ Keys" (Kino 0.9.53 also pointed to a Stremio TMDB addon). Uncaught,
the person reads that same sentence. On such a build, a person's key TMDB refuses is `no_tmdb_key` too.

A key your plugin keeps in its own settings (a `tmdbKey` setting) stays your plugin's business: Kino never reads it for
`kino.tmdb`. Kino adds the key itself (`api_key` for a v3 key, an `Authorization: Bearer` header for a v4 token): your code
never sees any key, Kino's or the person's, and answers, errors and logs never carry one. You do not declare
`api.themoviedb.org` in `hosts` for it.

- **`path`**: starts with `/discover`, `/trending`, `/search`, `/movie`, `/tv`, `/find`, `/genre`, `/configuration`,
  `/person` or `/collection` (`"/movie"` or `"/movie/603/credits"`), without the `/3` version, without a query string,
  no `..` and no `//`. Anything else (an account, a list, a rating: what writes or reads the person's account) is
  `invalid_request`. GET only.
- **`params`**: a plain object of at most 20 strings, numbers or booleans, each at most 500 characters as text, names
  like `language`, `page`, `with_genres`, `vote_count.gte`, `append_to_response`. Never `api_key`, `session_id`,
  `guest_session_id`, `request_token` or `access_token` (`invalid_request`).
- **The answer**: the body as parsed JSON. `404` is `not_found`, a body over 2 MiB is `too_large`; when TMDB does not
  answer in 15 s (`timeout`), cannot be reached (`network`) or answers 5xx (`unavailable`), the cached copy (up to 7 days)
  is served instead when there is one. Anything else that is not a 2xx with JSON is `unavailable`.
- **Limits**: at most 40 calls per 10 s per plugin whichever key answers (a token bucket), and the two limits on Kino's
  key above; a fresh cached answer counts against neither of Kino's. Cached 10 minutes in memory by path and params (so per
  `language`; only bodies up to 512 KiB), and on disk with Kino's TMDB cache (from 1 hour for lists and searches to 7 days
  for `/find` and `/genre`), whichever key fetched it. Not counted in `kino.fetch`'s 60 requests per call. Not from
  `sign()` (`not_allowed`). Kino's telemetry counts calls by how they were served (cache, Kino's key, the person's key) and
  error codes, never a path or a key.
- **A call Kino stopped waiting for** (a bug fixed in Kino 0.9.54): when Kino gives up on one of your calls (the person
  left the screen, it timed out) but still hands its late answer on to an identical call that is waiting for it,
  `kino.tmdb` and `kino.meta` keep answering until your code finishes. Kino 0.9.53 answered `not_allowed` from that
  moment, so a Home built from many `kino.tmdb` calls could come back with only its first row until a restart.
- **No new apiVersion**: Kino 0.9.53 and later; feature-detect it (`typeof kino.tmdb === "function"`) and keep your own
  key setting only as the fallback for older Kino, as above. A plugin that builds its catalog from TMDB no longer needs
  to ask each person for a key. A complete example: [A TMDB catalog with no key in the
  plugin](cookbook.md#tmdb-catalog).

Under the Node kit, `kino.tmdb` uses your key from `KINO_TMDB_KEY` (or `"tmdbKey"` in `sdk/config.json`) where the app uses
Kino's, with the stricter limit on Kino's key (20 per 10 s; the kit has no person's key to fall back to), and with
`KINO_TMDB_FIXTURE` it answers offline from a JSON file keyed `"<path>?<params sorted by name>"` or `"<path>"`. Without
either, it throws `no_tmdb_key`, as a Kino build without a key does.

## `await kino.image.thumbnail(url, { maxWidth?, maxBytes? })` (Kino 0.9.84, not published yet) { #image-thumbnail }

Kino downloads an `https` picture under **the same network rules as your `kino.fetch`** (your `hosts`, https only, never the
home network, your request budget; at most 5 MB) and answers a small JPEG as `"data:image/jpeg;base64,…"`, so a card can carry
its picture inside a message. `maxWidth` 32 to 400 (default 200), `maxBytes` 2,048 to 32,768 (default 16,384), at most 20
calls a minute. Errors: `bad_request`, `host_not_allowed`, `not_found`, `network`, `timeout`, `too_large`, `not_image`,
`rate_limited`, `not_allowed` (from `sign()`). No new `apiVersion`: check `typeof kino.image === "object"`. The full guide,
with the kit: [`kino.image.thumbnail`](share.md#thumbnail).

## `kino.nuvio` (apiVersion 11, Kino 0.9.71) { #nuvio }

Experiment. With the `nuvio` capability and `nuvioRepos` in the manifest, your plugin asks Kino to install and use the scrapers of a Nuvio repository: `kino.nuvio.available({ repo })`, `use({ repo, scrapers })`, `scrapers({ repo })` and `streams({ repo, type, tmdbId, season?, episode?, scrapers?, timeoutMs? })`. Only inside your functions; 20 calls a minute; detect it with `typeof kino.nuvio === "object"`. Everything, with a complete example, in [Plugins that use Nuvio scrapers](nuvio-plugins.md).

## `kino.seed(session)`: share one anonymous guest session (Kino 0.9.55) { #seed }

Some sources give an anonymous, free guest session to anyone who asks and block whole regions from logging in.
`kino.seed` lets your plugin hand Kino **one** such session so people in those regions have live sessions to fall back
on. It is best-effort and synchronous: it answers nothing and never throws into your plugin, so call it and carry on.

```js
if (typeof kino.seed === "function") {
  kino.seed({ sn, userId, userToken, jwtToken, mintedAt });   // a brand-new guest session, already proven to work
}
```

- **What to send.** A session you just created for this and nothing else, never the person's own, and only after you
  checked it works (for example by reading one catalog page with it). If a device cannot create a working guest session
  (a blocked region, a refusal, an empty answer), it sends nothing at all.
- **What Kino keeps.** Only these keys, each a short string (at most 2,048 characters) or a finite number: `sn`,
  `userId`, `userToken`, `jwtToken`, `mintedAt`, `customer`, `activeTime` and `availableTime`. Any other key is dropped.
  If `sn`, `userId` and `userToken` are not all present and non-blank, the whole session is dropped. The cleaned session
  is at most 8,192 characters, and a session whose JSON is over 16,384 characters never crosses.
- **Consent.** Kino sends it to its own error board only when the person's plugin-telemetry consent is on for your plugin
  (the one [`kino.log.report`](#log) rides on, with `"telemetry": true` in your manifest); with it off, nothing leaves the
  device. It is anonymous: it names no account and carries nothing about the person. Say so in your plugin's
  description and give the person a setting to turn the contribution off.
- **Rate.** Do not mint on every Home. Keep a timestamp in [`kino.storage`](#storage) and share at most one session
  every few hours per device.
- **Feature-detect it.** An older Kino has no `kino.seed`; the check above is the whole compatibility story. The
  contract's `kinoSeed` section carries the same keys and limits ([`contract.json`](reference/index.md)).
- **In the Node kit** `kino.seed` is there too: it sends nothing, applies the same filter and logs which keys Kino
  would keep (never the values), noting when your manifest lacks `"telemetry"` and the app would send nothing.

## `kino.sync.remoteChanged()`: tell Kino the remote copy moved (Kino 0.9.74) { #sync }

Only for a [sync provider](sync-providers.md) that declares `"sync": { "mode": "realtime" }`. When your
code learns that another device stored a new copy, it tells Kino, and Kino pulls at once instead of
waiting for the next `pullEveryMs`:

```js
export async function syncStatus() {
  const head = await readRemoteHead();                       // one cheap request, never the blob
  if (typeof kino.sync === "object" && head.version !== kino.storage.get("lastSeen")) {
    kino.storage.set("lastSeen", head.version);
    kino.sync.remoteChanged();
  }
  return { ready: true };
}
```

- **Synchronous and cheap**: it answers nothing. Kino accepts at most one signal every 30 seconds and
  drops one that arrives while a pull is already running (that pull sees the remote), so call it when
  you notice a change, never in a loop.
- **Signal from `syncStatus`, not from `syncPull`**: a signal sent during a pull is dropped. Your code
  only runs while Kino calls it, so you cannot hold a connection open between calls; Kino keeps pulling
  every `pullEveryMs` anyway.
- **`not_allowed` for any other plugin**: it throws `{ code: "not_allowed" }` unless the plugin declares
  the `syncProvider` capability with `mode: "realtime"`.
- **Feature-detect it** with `typeof kino.sync === "object"`: an older Kino has no `kino.sync`.

## `kino.sync.active()` and `kino.sync.setActive(on)` (Kino 0.9.78) { #sync-active }

Additive, for a plugin with the approved `syncProvider` capability. Kino keeps one sync provider at a time, so your plugin can
let the person switch to it, or away from it, from its own screen, instead of sending them to Ajustes ▸ Conectar:

```js
if (typeof kino.sync.setActive === "function") {
  const on = await kino.sync.active();   // is this plugin the provider on THIS device?
  await kino.sync.setActive(!on);        // from a button the person pressed: true asks them first, false returns to local sync
}
```

- `setActive(true)` shows Kino's own question (your installed name and Kino's words; you cannot change them) and, if the person
  accepts, makes your plugin the only provider on: the current one is turned off. Declined: it resolves `false` and nothing changes.
  Already on: it resolves `true` and asks nothing.
- `setActive(false)` asks nothing and returns the person to Kino's local sync, only when your plugin is the one on.
- Both only run from a call the person started with a tap (a settings `action`, a `panelAction`, or a screen's `screenEvent` after their
  own press), never from a job, a timer or a screen's `open`: they reject with `not_allowed` there. Reading `active()` works in any call.
- Rejections carry `code`: `not_allowed`, `unavailable` (the plugin cannot be a provider now), `busy`, `timeout` (two minutes without an
  answer) and `invalid_request` (not a boolean).
- Set the key your provider needs (`sync.keySecret`) before offering the switch: a provider with no key shows "not set up".
- It is not an `apiVersion`: an older Kino has neither function, so feature-detect with `typeof kino.sync.setActive === "function"` and
  keep `go: { syncProvider: true }` (opens Kino's provider settings; see [Screen reference](screen-reference.md)) as the way for older builds.

See [Sync providers](sync-providers.md).

## `kino.ws`: WebSockets (apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #ws }

With the `socket` capability: `await kino.ws.open(url, { protocol? })` opens an outbound WebSocket and answers a socket
with `send(data, { encoding? })`, `recv(timeoutMs?, { encoding? })` and `close()`. `wss://` on port 443 to a host your
manifest declares and the person approved, never the local network or an IP literal; at most 4 open sockets per plugin,
8 MiB queued unread per socket, 786,000 bytes per frame sent, 60 s per `recv`. Frames are `Uint8Array`, or `hex` /
`base64` strings with `{ encoding }` (the fast path: no JavaScript loop over the bytes). Errors: `not_https`,
`host_not_allowed` (with `host`), `limit`, `closed`, `network`, `timeout`, `too_large`, `invalid_request`. The whole
guide: [Sockets and plugin-served bytes](bytes.md#ws).

## `kino.catalog` (apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #catalog }

With the `catalog` capability: `upsert(items)`, `search({ q?, limit?, offset?, order? })`, `get(ids)`, `remove(ids)`,
`clear()` and `count()` over a SQLite catalog of your own items (up to 100,000, in one 64 MiB file for your plugin alone,
on the device only). Every call is `async`; there is no SQL. The whole guide, with every rule, limit and error:
[Catalog and large storage](catalog.md).

## `kino.qr.scan(options?)` (apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #qr }

With the `qrScan` capability: opens Kino's camera scanner full screen on the phone and resolves with the scanned text (1
to 4,096 characters) or `null` when the person closes it. `{ title?, titleEn? }`, at most 80 characters each. Only from a
settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a `screenEvent` that follows the person's tap or submit (apiVersion 14; `not_allowed` from anything else); `unavailable` on a TV or without a camera;
`busy`, `timeout` (120 s), `permission_denied`, `invalid_request`. Showing a QR needs no capability: the settings form's
`qr` type. See [QR codes](qr.md) for the rules, the errors and a two-device login recipe.

## `kino.files` (apiVersion 21, Kino 0.9.82) { #files }

With the `files` capability: files that are on the person's device. `pick({ kinds?, multiple?, copy? })` and
`pickFolder({ kinds? })` open the picker (only from a press of the person's; `not_allowed` from anything else) and answer opaque
handles, never an address; `list`, `folders`, `info`, `read`, `readText` (at most 2,000,000 bytes a call), `forget` and `url`
(`kino-file:<id>`, for a stream's or an audio track's `url`) need no press. Errors: `unavailable`, `not_allowed`, `busy`,
`timeout`, `invalid_request`, `gone`, `too_large`, `denied`, `quota`. Nothing is uploaded or sent. The full guide, with every rule
and limit: [Files on the device](files.md).

## `kino.progress` (apiVersion 22, next Kino release) { #progress }

With the `progress` capability (no consent line): where the person is in an element your plugin owns (a manga chapter and
page, a book position). `set({ id, fraction, title?, poster?, label?, labelEn?, resume?, done?, doneAt? })`, `get(id)` (the
entry or `null`), `list({ limit?, sinceMs? })` (most recently set first, each entry with its `id`; `limit` 1 to 100, default 50)
and `clear(id)`. `resume` is any JSON value up to 1024 bytes serialized that Kino never reads. An element is finished at
`done: true` or when `fraction >= doneAt` (default 0.9). Kept per profile, synced between the person's devices and in backups;
**Kino draws nothing from it**, your plugin builds its own shelf from `list`. Refused (`not_allowed`) in a job that runs for a
profile other than the active one. Errors: `not_allowed`, `bad_request`, `too_large`. The full guide:
[Saving where the person is](progress.md).

## `kino.screen` (apiVersion 14, Kino 0.9.74) { #screen }

What this Kino's screen canvas draws, for feature detection: `kino.screen.names` (the node types as this guide spells
them, `Column`, `TextField`, `titleRail`...), `kino.screen.widgets` (the same by their older names) and
`kino.screen.version` (the screen contract's own number, 1 for now). `undefined` on an older Kino. See
[Screens](screens.md).

## `kino.library`, `kino.room`, `kino.ai` and `kino.shared` (apiVersion 14, Kino 0.9.74) { #api14 }

Each needs its capability: what the person watched and saved ([`library`](rooms.md#library); from apiVersion 17 also [`kino.library.stats`](#library-stats)), a room over the Internet
hosted on the device ([`room`](rooms.md#room)), one ask to Kino's text AI ([`ai`](jobs-and-shared.md#ai)) and a few small
results synced between the person's devices ([`shared`](jobs-and-shared.md#shared)). A background `job(ctx)`
(`schedule`) is described in [Background jobs](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs).

## `kino.identity` and `kino.notifications` (apiVersion 15) { #api15 }

Each needs its capability (declarative, you export nothing): `kino.identity.telegram({ challenge? })` answers a pseudonym of
the person for your plugin and the signed token that proves it, only to plugins signed with Kino's own author key
([`identity`](identity.md)); `kino.notifications.post({ id, title, titleEn?, text?, textEn?, go? })` and `clear(id?)` leave
and remove notices in the Home bell ([`notifications`](notifications.md)). Detect them with
`typeof kino.identity === "object"` and `typeof kino.notifications === "object"`. On a watched series,
`kino.library.watched()` also carries `season` and `episode` ([Rooms, the library and player control](rooms.md#library)).
A plugin that is a store does not call `kino`: it exports `storeSync` ([Plugin stores](plugin-stores.md)).

## `kino.coins` (apiVersion 16, Kino 0.9.78) { #coins }

`coins` (apiVersion 16, a declarative capability that never stands alone and is not offered through `enhancements`) lets your
plugin show the person's Kino coins and give them away. Kino coins are a free currency shared by all of Kino: the person earns 1
coin every 10 minutes watched, at most 20 a UTC day, and gives them one at a time. `await kino.coins.balance()` answers
`{ balance, earnedToday, capToday }`; `await kino.coins.give({ to, postId })` gives ONE coin to the account `to` (1 to 128
characters: the coins service's id of the recipient, which your own server hands you, e.g. Kino Social's `coinsAccount`) for
the post `postId` (1 to 64 characters) and answers `{ balance, postTotal }` (the balance left, the coins the post holds now).

Kino's own client talks to the coins service, signed in with the device's Telegram validation: your plugin never learns the
service's address nor its session, and never needs `hosts` for it.

- **When:** `give` works only inside a call the person started from `screen`, `screenEvent` or `panelAction` (never a timer tick
  nor a job); `balance` also from a timer tick and from your scheduled `job` (a daily balance notice through
  [`kino.notifications`](notifications.md)). 30 calls a minute per plugin.
- **Errors:** both reject with a KinoError whose `code` is `permission_denied`, `not_available` (the service is down or slow, or
  this device was never validated with a Telegram account: keep your screen working without coins), `rate_limited`,
  `bad_request`, `disabled` (the person switched Kinos off in Kino's Ajustes, message "kino.coins is switched off in Kino's
  settings": show nothing of coins, no button, no balance, no notice), or the service's own `no_balance` (nothing to give),
  `self_gift` (to yourself) and `unknown_account`.
- **Approval:** a red consent line («Podrá ver tu saldo de kinos y regalar tus kinos»), never approved by Kino on its own and
  unticked in a kit import. There is no switch of its own: the person revokes it by disabling or removing your plugin.
- **Detect it** with `typeof kino.coins === "object"`: an older Kino has no `kino.coins`, so hide your coin button there
  (`kinoCoins` in the contract, [`contract.json`](reference/index.md)).
- **Selling a theme needs none of this:** a priced [app theme](themes.md#price) (apiVersion 18) is bought through Kino's own
  sheet, which shows the price and the balance and pays the author; your plugin never sees the purchase.

## `kino.library.stats` (apiVersion 17): a month's habits { #library-stats }

```js
const s = await kino.library.stats({ month: "2026-10" }); // default: the current month
// { month, estimated, seconds, secondsByKind: { movie, series, live },
//   secondsByBand: { morning, afternoon, night, lateNight } | null,
//   titles, episodes, activeDays, longestStreakDays,
//   top: [{ title, year?, kind, ids: { tmdb?, imdb? }, poster?, genres?, seconds }] /* at most 20 */ }
```

Same capability (`library`) and the same switch as `watched` and `saved` ([Rooms, the library and player control](rooms.md#library)),
but **only a plugin that declares `"apiVersion": 17` or later has the function** (feature-detect with
`typeof kino.library.stats === "function"`). Because the red consent line now says the plugin can read **how much and at what
time of day** the person watches, an update that raises a plugin already holding `library` to apiVersion 17 asks the person again.

- **Active profile only**, every device of the person summed. Nothing finer than the month's aggregates: no per-day series and no
  timestamps. `month` is `yyyy-mm` (a real month); any other value, or any other option, is `bad_request`.
- **Never 18+**: a title Kino knows to be 18+ when you ask leaves the totals and `top`. A title Kino merely cannot place now (its
  plugin is gone) stays in the totals and is not in `top`. Live channels are in the totals and never named.
- `titles` counts distinct movies and series; `episodes` the distinct chapters of series played in the month (a rewatch does not add).
- `poster` and `genres` are only what Kino already holds for the item, with no network call; a field Kino does not have is left out.
  Kino holds no genres for its library items today, so `genres` is usually absent: fill the gaps with `kino.tmdb`.
- **Before the counter existed**: Kino counts the seconds really played from the release that brought it. A month before it is
  estimated from the play history (`estimated: true`, `secondsByBand: null`); the month of the release mixes both, and its
  `secondsByBand` covers the counted part only.
- Same call rules, rate limit (30 a minute together with `watched` and `saved`) and error codes as the rest of `kino.library`;
  it also answers from a job.
- Kit: the fixture's `stats` is `{ "2026-10": { seconds, secondsByKind, secondsByBand, titles, episodes, activeDays, longestStreakDays, top } }`.

## `kino.plugins.call(alias, call, arg?)` (apiVersion 20, Kino 0.9.81) { #plugins }

Asks a **door another plugin opens**, through Kino: the [plugin protocol](protocol.md). `alias` is a key of your manifest's
[`consumes`](manifest.md#consumes), `call` a name listed there, `arg` JSON (at most 64 KB) that matches the call's `in`.

```js
if (typeof kino.plugins === "object") {                 // absent on a Kino older than 0.9.81
  try {
    const movie = await kino.plugins.call("tmdb", "random", { fromYear: 1990 });   // the provider's answer, checked against "out"
  } catch (e) {
    // e.code: provider_missing, not_declared, bad_input, bad_output, rate_limited, timeout or provider_failed
  }
}
```

- Resolves to the provider's answer checked against the call's `out` (fields the door does not declare are dropped).
- Rejects with an `Error` whose `code` is `provider_missing`, `not_declared`, `bad_input`, `bad_output`, `rate_limited`
  (more than 30 calls in any 10 s to one provider door), `timeout` (10 s) or `provider_failed`; in a background `job`,
  `not_allowed`. What each one means and what to do: [Errors](protocol.md#errors).
- Usable wherever the other Kino services are (`screen`, `screenEvent`, a panel's exports...); never in a `job` or in `sign()`.
- `arg` reaches the provider, which may send it to its own hosts: put nothing private in it.
- A provider's **streams** are not called with this function: your screen switches them on with
  `state.protocol.<alias>.<stream> = true` and receives the event `protocol` ([Streams](protocol.md#streams)).
- From Kino 0.9.84 the provider knows who calls: its `proto_` exports get `ctx.caller`
  ([`ctx.caller`](share.md#ctx-caller)). To share to Kino Social with this function, see [Sharing](share.md#social).

## `kino.visualBrowser.open(options)` (apiVersion 20, Kino 0.9.81) { #visual-browser }

With `"visualBrowser": true` in the manifest: opens a web window **the person sees and drives** (to sign in, solve a challenge, accept
terms) on your declared `hosts`, and resolves with `{ status: "done" | "closed" | "timeout", finalUrl?, cookies?, html?, stored?,
storedNames?, userAgent? }`. Kino asks the person in its own sheet at every open. Only from a settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a
`screenEvent` the person pressed (`forbidden` from anything else); errors `bad_args`, `forbidden`, `unavailable`, `busy` and
`store_failed`. `kino.visualBrowser` is `undefined` without the manifest key or on a Kino before 0.9.81, and
`kino.visualBrowser.available` is `false` on the desktop and on a device without a WebView (Android TV has one: experimental there).
The rules, the cookie caps, `storeAs` and the "Vincular cuenta" recipe are on
[A browser window the person drives](visual-browser.md).

## `kino.sleep(ms)` and `kino.error(code, message?, { userMessage }?)` { #sleep-error }

`await kino.sleep(1500)` waits 0 to 5000 ms (for a site that rate-limits you); the time counts
inside the call's own limit. `kino.error` builds the typed errors of
[Errors people understand](contract.md#errors); its optional `{ userMessage }` (apiVersion 6) is your
own sentence for the person, shown under [its rules](contract.md#user-message) as "Mensaje de <your
plugin>: …".

### Errors your code can catch { #catch }

Every failure a `kino.*` call reports is an ordinary `Error` your `try`/`catch` receives (your own
`throw`s still have [the rejection trap](engine-limits.md#rejection-trap)). Test `e.code`, never the
text of `e.message`: that is for the log, and may change (Spanish up to Kino 0.9.53, English from Kino 0.9.54).

| Where | `e.code` |
| --- | --- |
| `kino.fetch` | `host_not_allowed`, `timeout`, `network`, `too_large`, `invalid_request`, and `rate_limited` under `fetchHosts` ([the table](#fetch)) |
| `kino.crypto` | `crypto_error` |
| `kino.browser.capture` | `browser_unavailable`, `timeout`, `blocked`, `busy`, `not_allowed`, `invalid_request` |
| `kino.browser.page` | the same, plus `rate_limited` ([Hidden browser](browser.md#page)) |
| `kino.plugins.call` | `provider_missing`, `not_declared`, `bad_input`, `bad_output`, `rate_limited`, `timeout`, `provider_failed`; `not_allowed` in a `job` ([the plugin protocol](protocol.md#errors)) |
| inside [`sign()`](signed-streams.md#rules) | `host_not_allowed` from `kino.fetch`; `not_allowed` from `kino.storage`, `kino.cookies` and `kino.sleep` |
| `kino.storage` over 256 KB or a bad `ttlMs`, `kino.html.select` over its limits, `kino.secret` with an undeclared name | no `code`: a plain `Error` with a message (Spanish up to Kino 0.9.53, English from Kino 0.9.54) |

From Kino 0.9.50 a **synchronous** `kino.*` call that fails (a full `kino.storage`, a bad cipher key, a
selector that is too long) is caught by your `try`/`catch` like any other error. Kino 0.9.49 and older
ended the whole call there even inside a `try`/`catch`, so on those versions keep an eye on what you
store.

`kino.error(code, message?, { userMessage }?)` builds an `Error` whose `name` is `KinoError_<code>`
(`KinoError_not_found`), with `code` and, when you passed one, `userMessage`. A code that is not one of
the five becomes `code: "unknown"`, and the person reads a plain error. Throw it as it is, or rethrow a
caught one: the code reaches the person only when the error leaves your function with it. Whatever you
throw (an `Error`, a string, anything) reaches Kino as text, cut at 2,000 characters.

```js
try {
  kino.storage.set("cache:" + key, JSON.stringify(rows), { ttlMs: 3600000 });
} catch (e) {
  kino.log("cache: not saved", e.message);   // full storage: keep going without the cache
}

try {
  return await api("/play/" + encodeURIComponent(ref));
} catch (e) {
  if (e.code === "timeout" || e.code === "network") return backupStream(ref);
  throw e;                                     // a kino.error keeps its code and its userMessage
}
```

## `kino.config` { #config }

```js
kino.config.get("server")   // text, url, password, select: a string; toggle: true/false
kino.config.get("sources")  // list (apiVersion 4): [{ url: "https://…", category: "Noticias" }, …]
kino.config.all()           // every setting that has a value, as an object
```

Read-only: the values the person saved, or the `default` of a setting they left alone. A `toggle`
without a `default` is `false` and a `select` without one is its first option, so both always have a
value. A `text` or `password` with no value and no `default`, a `url` the person left empty (it never
has a default) and an empty `list` are `undefined`. A `list` is an array of objects, one per entry,
keyed by its `fields`' keys, trimmed, without all-blank entries. The `section`, `status` and `action`
types hold no value and never appear here. Every type is on [The settings form](settings-form.md#types).

## `kino.html.select(html, css)` { #html }

Parses `html` and returns `[{ text, html, attrs }]` for every element matching the CSS selector
(Jsoup's selector syntax): `text` is its text, `html` its inner HTML, `attrs` an object of its
attributes. Only the first 2,000,000 characters of `html` are read, at most 500 elements come back,
and it throws if the combined text and HTML of the matches goes over 5,242,880 characters (5 MB). A
selector longer than 10,000 characters throws `Error("CSS selector too long (over 10000 characters)")` (Kino 0.9.53 and
older: `"selector CSS demasiado largo (más de 10000 caracteres)"`). **It
exists only inside Kino**: the Node kit's version throws, so test anything that uses it in the app.

## `kino.storage` { #storage }

```js
kino.storage.get("key")                          // the string, or null
kino.storage.set("key", "v")                     // values are converted to strings
kino.storage.set("key", "v", { ttlMs: 3600000 }) // expires after that many milliseconds
kino.storage.remove("key")
kino.storage.keys()                              // every key, as an array (expired keys are already gone)
```

Synchronous, private to your plugin, and it survives restarts of the sandbox and of the app. At most
256 KB in total (measured as the JSON of all keys and values); going over throws
`Error("plugin storage full (256 KB)")` (Kino 0.9.53 and older: `"almacenamiento del plugin lleno (256 KB)"`). It is deleted when the person uninstalls the
plugin, and it is **not** cleared when they change your settings.

**A bigger store (`storageLarge`, apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74).** A plugin that declares `storageLarge` gets the same
API with 16 MB in total, at most 2 MB per value and at most 1,000 keys of at most 256 characters, kept one file per value
**on the device only: never synced and not in any backup** (declaring it moves your existing keys there too). Keep
credentials in sealed secrets or settings, and shard big data into values of about 512 KB. To search thousands of
records use `kino.catalog` instead. [The rules](catalog.md#storage-large).

`set`'s third argument is optional: leave it out for a permanent entry, exactly as before this option
existed. Give `{ ttlMs }` to make the entry expire -- after that many milliseconds `get` returns `null`
and `keys()` no longer lists it, even across a restart of the app. `ttlMs` must be a whole number
greater than 0 and at most 2,592,000,000 (30 days); anything else throws before your entry is
touched, the same way an oversized value already does. An expired entry never counts against the
256 KB cap (16 MB with `storageLarge`): it is dropped the next time your plugin reads or writes storage. Example, a Home row
cached for an hour:

```js
export async function home() {
  const cached = kino.storage.get("home-rows");
  if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached);
  const rows = await buildHomeRows();
  kino.storage.set("home-rows", JSON.stringify(rows), { ttlMs: 60 * 60 * 1000 });
  return rows;
}
```

## `kino.log(...args)` { #log }

Also `console.log`, `console.info`, `console.warn` and `console.error`: they all go to the log
(tag `KinoPlugin` in `adb logcat`; `KinoPlugin/<your id>` in a debug build of Kino, or in any build
while your plugin's [Modo debug](diagnostics.md#debug) switch is on: `"debug": true` only makes that the default), objects are written as JSON, and a message is cut at 2000
characters. Under the Node kit they go to stderr.

When a call of a plugin whose manifest says `"telemetry": true` or `"verbose"` (apiVersion 6) **fails**
(it throws, times out, returns something unusable, including `sign`, `settingsStatus`, `action` and
`validateSettings`), the lines it logged during that call (the last 30, each cut at 300
characters) travel with the failure report to the maintainers' error tracker as `plugin_log`, so a
`kino.log("home: status", r.status)` before the throw is how you see why it failed on someone else's
phone. Each report is tagged with your plugin's id and version; at most one report per function and
kind of failure an hour. Nothing is sent for a call that succeeds, and no line of any plugin that does
not declare `telemetry` (recommended or not, a converted Nuvio scraper): for those Kino only notes that
the call failed (your id and version, the function, the kind of failure). Up to Kino 0.9.53 a declared plugin's lines
are always sent; from Kino 0.9.54 the person can turn "Enviar registros de errores y de reproducción" off in your
plugin's tab in Ajustes (see [Logs and telemetry](diagnostics.md#telemetry)), and then nothing is sent while it is off. Before it leaves the device
every line has URLs, hostnames, IPs, e-mails, long ids, long hex/base64 runs, credential-shaped text,
the person's setting values and the text of their search or title removed, and the whole is capped at
2 KB (the newest lines win). Still: log what happened (a status, a step, a count), never what the
person typed or a secret, and never a setting's value. Works on every `apiVersion`.

**`kino.log.report(...args)`** (apiVersion 6, with `telemetry`) writes a line like `kino.log` and also
tells the error tracker that your plugin served a **degraded** result even though the call worked: it
fell back to a shared account, used a backup source, trimmed a list. The details (the area, the caps)
are on [Logs and telemetry](diagnostics.md#report).

## `kino.rank` { #rank }

For a search backend that only matches a loose bag of shared words rather than a title as a whole:
asking it a long title can return twenty unrelated results that merely share one common word, with
the real match buried on page two. These three pure functions make a backend like that behave like a
title search, without touching its own JSON shape.

```js
kino.rank.shortQuery(query)
kino.rank.sortBySimilarity(items, query, getTitle?)
kino.rank.filterRelevant(items, query, getTitle?)
```

- **`shortQuery(query)`** returns the title's HEAD, up to its first `:`, `,`, `|`, en dash or em
  dash: ask your backend that instead of the whole title, so its own ranking has less noise to sort
  through. A one- or two-letter head ("El", "A") identifies nothing, so the whole (trimmed) text
  comes back instead; a plain `-` is never a cut point (it would split "Spider-Man"). Try it against
  your backend first -- some do worse with a short query, not better.
- **`sortBySimilarity(items, query, getTitle?)`** reorders `items` so the ones sharing the most words
  with `query` come first; ties keep the backend's own order.
- **`filterRelevant(items, query, getTitle?)`** drops items that only share a stray word with
  `query`. Reordering alone still shows a full page of near-misses when the title genuinely is not on
  the backend; this makes an absent title come back with 0 results instead.

`query` is a title, or an array of several forms of one worth trying together --
`[query.q, query.originalTitle, ...query.altTitles]`, since a backend may only know a title in one
language. `getTitle` reads a title off one of your own `items`; it defaults to
`(item) => item.title`, and may itself return an array the same way `query` can, when an item keeps
a title in more than one field or language (every form's words are combined). Matching folds accents
and case and ignores words of 1-2 letters (the "el", "de", "of" that make unrelated titles look
alike); `filterRelevant` keeps an item once it shares at least 60% of a requested title's distinctive
words.

**Bad input never throws.** Unlike `kino.fetch`/`kino.crypto`/`kino.sleep`, these three never raise a
`kino.error` for a malformed argument: `items` that is not an array answers `[]` from either
function. An item with no usable title -- `null`, `undefined`, `getTitle` returning something that is
not a string (or an array with none in it), or `getTitle` itself throwing -- is treated as "no title"
rather than crashing your call: `filterRelevant` drops it like an actual near-miss, and
`sortBySimilarity` sorts it after every item that does have one, in your list's own order among
themselves.

```js
export async function search(query) {
  const titles = [query.q, query.originalTitle, ...query.altTitles];
  const r = await kino.fetch(BASE + "/search?q=" + encodeURIComponent(kino.rank.shortQuery(query.q)));
  const found = r.json().results; // whatever shape your backend answers with
  const relevant = kino.rank.filterRelevant(found, titles, (x) => x.name);
  return kino.rank.sortBySimilarity(relevant, titles, (x) => x.name).map(toItem);
}
```

If your backend already ranks a full title well, skip `shortQuery` and run only
`filterRelevant`/`sortBySimilarity`, on what it gives you for `query.q` as typed.

Two things left out on purpose. Neither retries with the full title: if `shortQuery`'s head happens
to be a common word (e.g. "Love, Death & Robots" -> "Love") and the backend returns nothing relevant
for it, retry `search` with the full title yourself when the short one comes back empty. And neither
does anything with season numbers or ordering: how a backend spells "season 2" in its own titles
("T2", "Temporada 2", …) is specific to that backend, not something these can fold in.

# Limits and engine quirks

## Every number in one place { #limits }

<!-- contract:limits:start -->
| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Manifest / entry file / icon | 16 KB / 1 MB / 128 KB |
| Memory / stack, per plugin | 64 MB / 1 MB |
| Time per call | `search` 15 s; `home`, `browse`, `episodes`, `resolve` 20 s each (`resolve` of a plugin Kino itself generates, from a Nuvio scraper or a Stremio addon: 75 s); `liveCategories`, `liveChannels`, `guide` 20 s each; `liveSearch` 15 s; `subtitles` 10 s; `track` 10 s (apiVersion 7); `segments` 8 s (apiVersion 7); `lyrics` 10 s (apiVersion 19); `meta` 6 s (apiVersion 6; past it, no answer); `section`, `categories` 20 s each (apiVersion 6); `details` 20 s (apiVersion 8); `migrate` 10 s; `sign` 1.5 s (and 3 s counting its wait); counting all your fetches and sleeps together, but not the time the person spends answering a host question for that call |
| Loading the module (its top level) | 10 s |
| Idle sandbox | closed after 5 minutes without calls |
| Consecutive timeouts | 3 in a row and Kino disables the plugin ("No responde") |
| `kino.fetch` | https only (or the person's own server as typed, or `http` on a host declared `insecureHttp`); 15 s default, 30 s maximum; response body at most 5 MB; the request (URL, headers and body) at most 1,048,576 characters; inside a sync provider's `syncPull` and `syncPush` only, both the request and the response body may reach the declared blob's base64 plus 64 KB (ceil(`sync.maxBlobBytes` × 4/3) + 65,536); at most 60 requests per call, every hop counted, refused ones included (250 for a plugin converted from a Nuvio scraper); at most 6 fetches in flight at once; at most 3 host questions per call; at most 10 redirects per request; under `"fetchHosts": "any"`, a host reached only through it: https on port 443, a dotted name or public IPv4 address, at most 60 requests a minute per site and 600 every 10 minutes per plugin (250 / 2,500 for a converted Nuvio scraper), else `rate_limited` |
| Cookies | 50 per domain, 64 KB in total per plugin |
| `kino.storage` | 256 KB per plugin (with `storageLarge`, apiVersion 13: 16 MB in total, 2 MB per value, 1,000 keys of at most 256 characters); an entry's optional `ttlMs` is 1..2,592,000,000 ms (30 days) |
| `kino.sleep` | 0 to 5,000 ms per call |
| `kino.meta` (Kino 0.9.53) | at most 30 calls a minute per plugin; 8 s at most (each other `meta` plugin 6 s), inside your call's own limit; the query at most 4,096 characters; the answer at most 1,000,000 characters; cached 30 minutes |
| `kino.tmdb` (Kino 0.9.53) | at most 40 calls per 10 s per plugin; on Kino's own key at most 20 per 10 s per plugin and 60 per 10 s for all plugins (then the person's key, else the cache or `rate_limited`); 15 s per call; a body at most 2 MB; at most 20 params of at most 500 characters; cached and shared by all plugins, per route (12 hours for a series by id and its seasons and episodes; 30 days for a movie, person or collection by id, any title's credits, images and the like, and for `/find`, `/genre`, `/configuration`; 24 hours for `/search`; 3 hours for `/trending`, `/discover` and the lists; 10 minutes for anything else, an empty answer or a 404), bodies up to 512 KB; a cached answer does not count against these limits, and when TMDB fails (not when it refuses the key) the last copy is served; not counted in `kino.fetch`'s requests per call |
| `kino.crypto` | data at most 5 MB per call; PBKDF2 at most 100,000 iterations and 64-byte keys; `randomBytes` at most 1,024 |
| `kino.ws` (apiVersion 13) | at most 4 open sockets per plugin (the fifth is refused with `limit`); at most 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) of received messages queued unread per socket, past that the socket closes with `limit`; a frame to send at most 786,000 bytes once decoded, also when sent as a `hex` or `base64` string (`too_large`); one `recv` waits at most 60 s; `wss://` to a declared, approved host only; memory: what is queued unread sits on Kino's heap (up to 32 MiB with every socket full), what you keep from it counts in your 64 MB sandbox; not measured on 1 GB TV boxes, so read what arrives and keep little |
| `byteSource` (apiVersion 13) | at most 2 open streams at once on the device (another is refused), and apart from them at most 2 served to TVs (one per Chromecast and DLNA cast); each `read` asks for 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) at an offset that is a multiple of 1,048,576 (so always a multiple of 4,096), the last one running past `size`; 3 chunks ahead are read while one plays; Kino keeps the last 8 chunks read per stream; `handle` 1 to 512 characters; memory: each open stream holds up to about 12 MiB of Kino's heap (the chunks kept, the ones read ahead and the one in flight), so 2 on the device plus 2 served to TVs can reach about 48 MiB, besides your 64 MB sandbox; not measured on 1 GB TV boxes |
| `kino.catalog` (apiVersion 13) | at most 100,000 items per plugin (then `limit`), as long as they fit in the file: about 670 bytes per item on average, so keep `data` small; `id` 1 to 128 characters, `title` at most 300 characters, `data` at most 4,096 bytes of JSON; at most 500 items or ids per call; `search`: `q` at most 256 characters, `limit` default 50, at most 100, `offset` at most 1,000,000; the database file at most 64 MiB (then `limit`); one SQLite file per plugin, on the device only |
| `kino.qr.scan` (apiVersion 13) | one scanner on screen at a time (another scan, from any plugin, is `busy`); it closes after 120 s (`timeout`); `title` and `titleEn` at most 80 characters; the scanned text 1 to 4,096 characters (a longer code is ignored); only from a settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a `screenEvent` that follows the person's tap or submit (else `not_allowed`), never on a TV or a device without a camera (`unavailable`); a settings `qr` setting's text at most 512 characters, asked again every 2,000 to 60,000 ms (`refreshMs`) |
| `kino.files` (apiVersion 21) | `pick` and `pickFolder` only from a press of the person's (else `not_allowed`); the picker closes after 180 s (`timeout`); `read` and `readText` 2,000,000 bytes a call; 500 handles, 20 folders, 5,000 files read from a folder, 50 in one `pick`; `copy: true` up to 64 MB a file and 1 GB in all ([Files on the device](files.md)) |
| `kino.progress` (apiVersion 22) | `id` 1 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`; `resume` 1024 bytes serialized; `label` and `labelEn` 80 characters each, `title` 200; 500 elements per plugin (the oldest by last activity dropped); `list` 100 at most, 50 by default; written to disk at most every 2 s; 20 `set` calls a second, the rest coalesced; finished at `done: true` or `fraction` >= `doneAt` (0.9); refused in a job for a profile other than the active one ([Saving where the person is](progress.md)) |
| `kino.image.thumbnail` (Kino 0.9.84) | `url` https of at most 2,048 characters; `maxWidth` 32 to 400 (default 200); `maxBytes` 2,048 to 32,768 (default 16,384); a download of at most 5 MB under your `kino.fetch` rules; 20 calls a minute per plugin; never from `sign()` ([`kino.image.thumbnail`](share.md#thumbnail)) |
| Images from the plugin (`imageSource`, apiVersion 13) | `handle` 1 to 512 characters, no control character; `image` answers at most 256 KB once decoded (262,144 bytes), canonical base64, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp` only; 10 s per call; at most 1 image call in flight per plugin, none while one of your byte streams is open or your `read` is queued or running or ended less than 2 s ago (an image waits up to 20 s, then is skipped); a timed-out call discards your sandbox (QuickJS cannot be interrupted); a failed handle is not asked again for 5 minutes; 2 timeouts in a row pause your images for 5 minutes; each image asked once, then kept in Kino's image disk cache per plugin, version and handle |
| `kino.log` / `console.*` | 2,000 characters per message; when a call of a plugin whose manifest declares `telemetry` fails, its last 30 lines (each cut at 300 characters, scrubbed, 2,048 characters in all) go with the failure report |
| What a function returns | at most 2,000,000 characters once turned into JSON (a sync provider's `syncPull` and `syncPush`: up to ceil(`sync.maxBlobBytes` × 4/3) + 65,536, set by its declared blob) |
| Results | `search` 100 items; `home` 20 rows of 60; `browse` 100 per page; `episodes` 5,000 (and 50 `seasons`); `ref` 4,096 characters; `next` 2,048 characters; `id` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,128}$` |
| Live channels (apiVersion 3) | `liveCategories` 200; `liveChannels` 500 per page, 10 pages at first and 5 more per scroll, 10,000 channels (200 pages) per category; `liveSearch` 100 channels, asked from 2 characters; `guide` 50 channels and 24 h per call, 100 entries per channel; `number` 1..9999 |
| Tracking (apiVersion 7) | `progress` at most every 5 minutes of playback; `watched` once, with 3 minutes or less left and at least 90% played; at most 200 events waiting per plugin; an event not delivered within 7 days is dropped; a retryable failure waits 30 s, doubling up to 6 h, 12 tries at most |
| Settings | at most 12 with a value, plus at most 16 `section`/`status`/`action`/`link`/`help` (apiVersion 6; `link` and `help` apiVersion 12, at most 4 of each) and `qr` (apiVersion 13); `text` 500, `url` 2,048, `password` 500 characters; a `link`'s address 2,048, a `help`'s title 60 and body 2,000 |
| Error messages | your `kino.error` message is a detail for the log, cut at 200 characters; a `userMessage` for the person is at most 160 |
| `hosts` | at least 1 entry, no upper limit from Kino 0.9.45 (only the manifest's 16 KB; Kino 0.9.44 and older refuse more than 20); from apiVersion 2, none (`[]`) when a `url` setting exists; from apiVersion 20, none in a provides-only plugin or a screen-only consumer (a non-empty `consumes` and `capabilities` exactly `["screen"]`) |
| `secrets` (apiVersion 4) | at most 16; names match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}$`; a value is 1..4,096 bytes (1..8,192 from apiVersion 6); from apiVersion 6 a cipher key may be typed: `{ seal, use: "cipher-key", encoding: "hex" | "base64" }`, 16/24/32 bytes |
| `kino.fetch` `maxBytes` (apiVersion 14) | 1 to 2,000,000 bytes of the body are read, the answer's `truncated` says whether it was cut; out of range: `invalid_request` |
| Screens (`screen`, apiVersion 14) | depth 10, 600 nodes, 500 items per list, state 64 KB, a text 2,000 characters; `screen` and `screenEvent` 20 s each; every number in [Screen limits](screens.md#limits) |
| `kino.library` (apiVersion 14) | `limit` default 50, at most 100; at most 30 calls a minute per plugin; times rounded to the day, `progress` to 0.01 |
| `kino.library.stats` (apiVersion 17) | one month's aggregates (`month` as `yyyy-mm`, the current one by default), nothing finer; `top` at most 20 titles; shares the 30 calls a minute of `watched` and `saved`; never 18+, live channels in the totals and never named |
| `kino.room` (apiVersion 14) | a payload at most 8,192 bytes and 4 levels; 5 messages a second, 100 and 256 KB a minute per member; 2 to 8 members; 10 to 240 minutes (default 120); mailbox 200 events or 15 minutes; 2 joined and 1 hosted per device, 2 per plugin; 5 wrong codes lock joins for 60 s, doubling up to 30 minutes; closed after 30 minutes in the background (a hosted room shows Kino's notification meanwhile) |

| `kino.ai` (apiVersion 14) | a prompt at most 8,192 bytes, `system` 2,048; the reply cut at `maxChars` (1 to 4,096, default 2,048); 10 asks in any minute, 100 a day and 1 at a time per plugin; 300 a day and 2 at a time for every plugin of the device together; 20 s an ask |

| `kino.plugins.call` (apiVersion 20) | a request and an answer at most 64 KB of JSON; 10 s a call; 30 calls in any 10 s per door; a manifest holds at most 4 doors (each 16 calls and 8 streams) and 8 `consumes` entries; a stream polls every 30 s at least; 4 live subscriptions per plugin; not in a background job |

## How your code lives { #lifecycle }

- **One call at a time.** Calls to the same plugin run one after another. The sandbox is reused
  between calls, but Kino throws it away after 5 idle minutes, after a timeout, when a call is
  cancelled (for example a newer search replaces an older one), when the plugin is updated or
  disabled, and (Kino 0.9.54) when the person switches the app's language, so the next call gets the new
  [`kino.lang`](kino-api.md#lang). Module-level variables are a cache at best: keep anything that must survive in
  `kino.storage`.
- **Load-time code.** When it installs your plugin, Kino loads the module once in a throwaway sandbox
  without network access, to check that every declared capability is an exported function. Keep the
  top level to declarations: a network call there fails, and the install with it.
- **Errors reach people.** If your function throws, that call fails and the person sees an error that
  names your plugin, and the text of your `Error` can be part of it. Write those messages for a
  person, in Spanish, short.
- **Memory over a long call (Kino 0.9.74).** Each plugin has 64 MB of engine
  memory. Before Kino 0.9.74 the answer of every awaited `kino.*` call (a `kino.fetch` body, a socket frame) stayed in
  that memory until the sandbox closed, so a plugin that moved many megabytes in one sandbox's life could run out of it
  on its second video. From Kino 0.9.74 an answer is freed once your code has it, and after a call that leaves the
  engine over half its limit Kino runs its garbage collector, so only what your code still holds counts. It applies at
  every `apiVersion`. Still keep few big strings alive at once: a hex string costs 2 bytes per byte, then its base64.
- **Runaway code.** Running out of memory or stack fails the call. A synchronous infinite loop
  (`while (true) {}`) **cannot be interrupted**: at the time limit Kino stops waiting for the call
  and discards the sandbox, but the loop keeps spinning on its own thread until it ends, which for a
  real infinite loop means until the app is closed. Three timeouts in a row disable the plugin.
- **App closed during a call.** A crash inside the engine, or being killed for memory, can take the
  whole app down mid-call, and nothing in-process can catch that. Kino notices at the next start:
  whichever plugins were mid-call at that moment each get an unclean exit counted against them —
  **including a healthy plugin that simply happened to be running at the same time**, not only the
  one that actually caused the crash. Two unclean exits in a row for the same plugin, with no call
  finishing normally in between, switch it off ("No responde") exactly like three timeouts in a
  row; a call that completes normally resets its count.

## The engine is not Node and not a browser { #not-node }

Plugins run in QuickJS. It handles modern JavaScript: `async`/`await`, classes with fields, `?.` and
`??`, regular expressions with lookbehind, named groups and `\p{L}` under the `u` flag, template
literals, spread, `replaceAll`, `Array.prototype.at` and `flat`, `Object.fromEntries`,
`Promise.allSettled`, `Map`, `Set`, `BigInt`. It does **not** have the platform around it:

- **Missing globals** (`typeof` is `"undefined"` inside Kino): `setTimeout`, `setInterval`,
  `setImmediate`, `queueMicrotask`, `Buffer`, `process`, `require`, `fetch`, `AbortController`,
  `structuredClone`, `performance`, `crypto`, `WeakRef` and `Intl`. Use `kino.sleep` to wait,
  `kino.fetch` instead of `fetch` and `kino.crypto` instead of `crypto`. `URL`, `URLSearchParams`,
  `atob`, `btoa`, `TextEncoder`, `TextDecoder` and `console` do exist: Kino provides them.
- **The kit now removes them:** `run.mjs` and `validate.mjs` load your plugin in an isolated environment
  where those names do not exist (using one is a `ReferenceError`, as in Kino), and `validate` flags
  with `!` the line that uses one and what to use instead. It also refuses any `import`: Kino loads a
  single file (bundle it with esbuild).
- **Locale-aware methods do not localize:** `localeCompare` ignores its locale and options (so
  `{ numeric: true }` and `{ sensitivity: "base" }` do nothing; it compares code units), and
  `(1234.5).toLocaleString("es-CO")` gives `"1234.5"`. Write the comparison you need; the reference
  plugin has a small `natural()` for numbered names.
- **Keep function names short.** A function name of millions of characters makes the engine's
  native code crash the whole app. As a best-effort guard, `kino.*`, `console.*`, the web globals and
  the other functions Kino provides are frozen, and on any function `Object.defineProperty`,
  `Object.defineProperties`, `Reflect.defineProperty` and `__defineGetter__`/`__defineSetter__`
  refuse to set `name` to a string longer than 1000 characters, to a getter or setter, or to make
  it writable: they throw a `TypeError` (`Reflect.defineProperty` returns `false`). The guard is not
  airtight (a huge computed key still names a function); a plugin that crashes the app anyway is
  switched off (see "App closed during a call" above). Setting `name` on ordinary objects, and
  `this.name = "MyError"` in an `Error` subclass, work as usual.

## What the kit cannot copy { #kit-differences }

The kit runs your plugin in Node's V8 inside a sandbox that imitates Kino's engine, and a test compares both on
about a hundred language probes (`plugins/sdk/test/engine-probes.js` in the Kino repo, measured against the real
engine). The kit copies what it can: `Error.stack` lines, `Date#toLocale*String` (they ignore their arguments and
print `01/15/2024` and `01:05:09 PM`), the three-line `toString` of native functions, `[object global]`, no
`ArrayBuffer#resize`/`transfer`, `console` with only `log`, `info`, `warn` and `error`, `TextDecoder` with utf-8 only.

What it **cannot** copy, so a plugin can pass in the kit and still fail in Kino:

| What | In Kino | In the kit |
|---|---|---|
| Memory | 64 MB per plugin. A 1e7-element array, an object with 1e6 keys or a `Map` with 1e6 entries fails the call | no limit |
| Stack | 1 MB: about 5000 nested calls already throw `InternalError` (runaway recursion is `InternalError`, not `RangeError`) | V8 allows about 10000 and throws `RangeError` |
| `/x/v` flag | `SyntaxError` | accepted |
| `sort` with a comparator that contradicts itself (`() => -1`) | a different order | V8's order. Consistent comparators, and stability, are identical |
| `new URL("http://münchen.de")` | `TypeError` (no punycode): write the host as `xn--mnchen-3ya.de` | turns it into `xn--...` |
| `Error.stackTraceLimit` | does not exist | exists (V8 needs it to build `stack`) |

If something behaves in Kino unlike in the kit, that is a probe to add: the list of known differences is
`plugins/sdk/test/engine-probes.known.json`, one reason per line.

### The plugin protocol: what only the app checks { #kit-protocol }

`node sdk/run.mjs --provider <folder>` answers [`kino.plugins.call`](protocol.md#kit) from a provider on your computer with the
app's own type checks, sizes, error codes and rate buckets. Some rules need the person's installed plugins, which only Kino has,
so **the kit does not apply them**:

| Rule | In Kino | In the kit |
|---|---|---|
| Which plugin answers an entry of `consumes` | the installed plugin of that exact `repo` (never a fork) | the first `--provider` folder that has the door |
| An 18+ provider and a consumer that is not 18+ | `provider_missing` | answered |
| An answer that holds one of the provider's sealed secrets (or a marker) | `bad_output` | passed on |
| A plugin calling its own door | `not_declared` | answered (if you pass the plugin as its own `--provider`) |
| A provider that is off or needs setup | `provider_missing` | answered |
| The consent line «Usa datos de …» and the install sheet of `go.installPlugin` | shown by Kino | `run.mjs` only says what Kino would do |

Try those cases in Kino 0.9.81 or newer with both plugins installed.

## Splitting your code across files { #splitting-files }

Kino loads exactly one file (the manifest's `entry`), and the engine has no `require` and no
module resolver, so an `import` from `plugin.js` to a second file has nothing to resolve against on
the device. That does not mean you must write the whole plugin in one file -- just that the file you
publish has to be the finished, single-file result.

Write it split, normally, then bundle it before you publish:

```
src/
  animeav1.js       a helper module
  plugin.js         the entry point; imports from animeav1.js
kino-plugin.json
package.json
```

```js
// src/animeav1.js
export async function searchAnimeAV1(query) {
  const res = await kino.fetch(`https://animeav1.com/api/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query.q)}`);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error("animeav1 respondió " + res.status);
  return res.json().results.map((r) => ({ id: r.slug, ref: r.slug, title: r.title, kind: "series", poster: r.image }));
}
```

```js
// src/plugin.js -- this import is fine: it runs through the bundler, never on the device
import { searchAnimeAV1 } from "./animeav1.js";

export async function search(query) {
  return searchAnimeAV1(query);
}
```

Bundle with [esbuild](https://esbuild.github.io/) (`npm i -D esbuild`), targeting ES module output
(Kino runs the published file as one):

```bash
npx esbuild src/plugin.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=plugin.js
```

`plugin.js` at the repo root is what comes out of that command, with `src/animeav1.js` inlined into
it and its `export async function search` intact -- that is the file `entry` names and the one Kino
fetches. Add it as an npm script
(`"build": "esbuild src/plugin.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=plugin.js"`) and run it before
every `sdk/` test or publish. Rollup and webpack work the same way; esbuild needs the least
configuration for a plugin this size. For a bigger plugin (folders by responsibility, a generated `plugin.js` checked with `check:built`), see [Structure a bigger plugin](structure.md).

## The trap: a rejection nobody is listening to yet (Kino 0.9.49 and older) { #rejection-trap }

**From Kino 0.9.50** a rejection behaves as in Node: a `throw` inside an `async` function is caught
by the caller's `try`/`catch`, `.catch()`, `Promise.all` or `Promise.allSettled`, however early it
happens -- even before the function's first `await`, and even when the handler is attached a few
`await`s later. What still fails the call is a rejection **nobody ever handles**: one still without a
handler once the plugin is only waiting on Kino (a `kino.fetch`, a `kino.sleep`, ...). For example a
helper called without `await` that throws, or a promise you keep and only `await` after a
`kino.fetch`. The call then fails with that error, as Node would stop with an `unhandledRejection`.
Await what you start, or give it a `.catch()` right away.

**Kino 0.9.49 and older** abort the **whole call** when a promise is rejected before anything has a
handler on it, even if your code is inside `try`/`catch`. The Node kit cannot show you this. If your
plugin must work there too (people update late), follow these rules:

- **Aborts the call:** a `throw` inside an `async` function **before its first `await`**, while the
  caller is wrapped in `try`/`catch`. A `.catch()` on that call, or `Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled`
  around it, do not rescue it either. Also aborts: `new Promise((_, reject) => reject(e))` rejected
  right away, and `return Promise.reject(e)` from an `async` function.
- **Is caught normally:** a `throw` after any `await` (even `await null;`), a rejection coming from
  `kino.fetch` or `kino.sleep` (for example a refused host), and `await Promise.reject(e)` or
  `Promise.reject(e).catch(...)` (those builds delay `Promise.reject` by one tick so a handler can
  attach in time).
- **A synchronous `kino.*` call that fails** (`kino.storage.set` over 256 KB, a `kino.crypto` error,
  a selector `kino.html.select` refuses) is caught normally from Kino 0.9.50. Kino 0.9.49 and older
  ended the whole call there, even inside `try`/`catch` ([Errors your code can catch](kino-api.md#catch)).
- If nobody catches the error anyway, it is harmless: the call fails with that error either way, and
  a `kino.error` code still reaches the person correctly.
- **Nuvio-converted scrapers get a workaround:** when Kino converts a [Nuvio scraper](nuvio.md) it
  rewrites the async helpers bundlers emit (esbuild's `__async`, TypeScript's `__awaiter`, Babel's
  `_asyncToGenerator`) so a transpiled function's body starts one tick later, and a throw before its
  first `await` is caught normally. A native `async` function (yours, or an untranspiled scraper's)
  still needs the `await` before anything that can throw.

So, for those builds, in a helper that a caller may wrap in `try`/`catch`, do the `await` first and
validate afterwards:

```js
// Wrong before Kino 0.9.50: this throw is NOT caught by the caller's try/catch; it aborts the whole call.
async function getJson(url) {
  if (!url.startsWith("https://")) throw new Error("dirección inválida");
  const r = await kino.fetch(url);
  return r.json();
}

// Right everywhere: the first await comes before anything that can throw.
async function getJson(url) {
  const r = await kino.fetch(url);
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error("archive.org respondió " + r.status);
  return r.json();
}
```

(If a helper has nothing to await, start it with `await null;`, or check the input in the caller
before it calls the helper. The examples on this site do, so they run on older builds too.)

# Structure a bigger plugin in files and bundle it { #structure }

Kino loads exactly one file, your manifest's `entry`; [Splitting your code across files](engine-limits.md#splitting-files)
shows the basic idea (write `src/`, bundle with esbuild). This page is the recipe for a plugin that has grown: a screen, a
player-panel tab, a background job, a protocol of its own. It works at any `apiVersion`.

Two published plugins are built this way and are worth reading whole:

- [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-watch-party](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-watch-party) (**Party Chat**): a
  player-panel tab with [rooms](rooms.md#room) and failover.
- [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-news](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-news) (**Solo noticias**): a
  [screen](screens.md) and a [background job](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs).

## The recipe { #recipe }

- **One responsibility per file, grouped in folders** (`util/`, `protocol/`, `ui/`, `exports/`...), a short comment at
  the top of each file saying what it owns, and imports that only go one way: no import cycles (a cycle bundles, but it
  makes the order code runs in depend on who imported whom first).
- **`src/plugin.js` only re-exports** what Kino calls (`search`, `screen`, `panel`, `job`...) and what your tests use.
  The bundle keeps exactly those named exports.
- **One shipped file, generated and committed.** Kino installs `plugin.js` straight from your repository and the
  [signature](signed.md) covers its exact bytes, so the generated file is committed, never edited by hand, and signed
  after every build. Keep it readable (do not minify): people review what they install.
- **Deterministic.** The same sources must give the same bytes: no timestamps, no absolute paths (run esbuild from the
  plugin's folder), one esbuild version (`"esbuild": "^0.21.0"`). A header line says the file is generated.
- **`check:built`.** A script rebuilds in memory and fails when the result is not exactly the committed `plugin.js`, so
  nobody ships a hand-edited or stale bundle; a test does the same, so `npm test` catches it too. Your other tests load
  the built `plugin.js` with the kit, which is what Kino will run.

## The build script { #build-script }

The build script both examples use (`scripts/build.mjs`, esbuild's JS API, so the banner needs no shell quoting):

```js
import * as esbuild from "esbuild";
const result = await esbuild.build({
  absWorkingDir: ROOT, entryPoints: ["src/plugin.js"], outfile: "plugin.js",
  bundle: true, format: "esm", target: "es2020", charset: "utf8",
  banner: { js: "// Generated by `npm run build` from src/. Do not edit this file: edit src/ and rebuild." },
  write: false,
});
const text = result.outputFiles[0].text;   // write it (build), or compare it with plugin.js (--check)
```

```json
"scripts": {
  "build": "node scripts/build.mjs",
  "check:built": "node scripts/build.mjs --check",
  "test": "node --test test/*.test.mjs",
  "validate": "node sdk/validate.mjs .",
  "sign": "node scripts/sign.mjs"
},
"devDependencies": { "esbuild": "^0.21.0" }
```

## The workflow { #workflow }

Edit `src/`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, raise `version` (and your changelog), `npm run sign`, `npm run validate`, then
commit `src/` and `plugin.js` together. Keep `node_modules/` in `.gitignore`. esbuild drops most comments, so the bundle
is readable but bare: point people at `src/` in your README.

See also [Test it locally](test-locally.md) and [Signed plugins](signed.md).

# Cookbook

Three complete shapes, then two short recipes for the apiVersion 2 powers that need a line on the
consent sheet. The three recipes for live channels (apiVersion 3) are on
[Live channels](live-channels.md#recipes). The first and the third shapes are, nearly line for line,
the two reference plugins Kino's own tests run end to end against a fake server.

## An HTML site with a login and hidden links { #html-login }

The site has a login form, keeps the session in a cookie, lists titles as HTML with a "next" link,
and hides each video URL with AES-128-CBC. The person's user and password are settings.

```json
{
  "id": "mi-sitio", "name": "Mi sitio", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 1, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": ["sitio.example", "cdn.example.com"],
  "capabilities": ["search", "home", "browse", "resolve"],
  "settings": [
    { "key": "user", "label": "Usuario", "type": "text", "required": true },
    { "key": "password", "label": "Contraseña", "type": "password", "required": true }
  ]
}
```

```js
const BASE = "https://sitio.example";
const KEY = "0123456789abcdef";
const IV = "abcdef9876543210";

// The cookie jar keeps the session between calls (and across restarts): log in only when needed.
async function login() {
  const probe = await kino.fetch(BASE + "/session", { redirect: "manual" });
  if (probe.status === 200) return;
  const r = await kino.fetch(BASE + "/login", {
    method: "POST",
    body: { form: { user: kino.config.get("user"), password: kino.config.get("password") } },
    redirect: "manual",
  });
  if (r.status === 401) throw kino.error("auth_required", "usuario o contraseña incorrectos");
  if (r.status !== 302) throw kino.error("unavailable", "el sitio respondió " + r.status);
}

function cards(html) {
  return kino.html.select(html, "a.card").map((a) => ({
    id: a.attrs["data-id"], ref: a.attrs["data-link"], title: a.text, kind: "movie",
  }));
}

async function page(path) {
  await login();
  const r = await kino.fetch(BASE + path);
  if (r.status === 429) throw kino.error("rate_limited", "demasiadas peticiones");
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", "el sitio respondió " + r.status);
  const html = r.text();
  const next = kino.html.select(html, "a.next").map((a) => a.attrs.href)[0];
  return { items: cards(html), next: next || undefined };
}

export async function search(query) {
  return (await page("/buscar?q=" + encodeURIComponent(query.q))).items;
}

export async function home() {
  const first = await page("/catalogo");
  return [{ id: "catalogo", title: "Catálogo", ref: "/catalogo", items: first.items }];
}

export async function browse(ref, cursor) {
  return page(cursor || ref);
}

export async function resolve(ref) {
  await null;
  const url = kino.crypto.decrypt("aes-128-cbc", { key: KEY, iv: IV, data: ref });
  return { url, mime: "video/mp4" };
}
```

`kino.html.select` exists only in the app, so test this one in Kino (or with `--replay` for the
parts that do not parse HTML).

## A JSON API with a token { #json-token }

The API wants a token it gives out for an API key. Keep the token in `kino.storage`, keyed by the
key it came from, and fetch a new one when the API says it expired.

```js
const API = "https://api.example.com/v1";
const tokenKey = () => "token:" + kino.config.get("apiKey");

async function token() {
  await null;
  const saved = kino.storage.get(tokenKey());
  if (saved) return saved;
  const r = await kino.fetch(API + "/token", { method: "POST", body: { json: { key: kino.config.get("apiKey") } } });
  if (r.status === 401) throw kino.error("auth_required", "la clave no sirve");
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", "la API respondió " + r.status);
  const t = r.json().token;
  kino.storage.set(tokenKey(), t);
  return t;
}

async function api(path) {
  const r = await kino.fetch(API + path, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer " + (await token()) } });
  if (r.status === 401) { kino.storage.remove(tokenKey()); throw kino.error("auth_required", "el token venció"); }
  if (r.status === 404) throw kino.error("not_found");
  if (r.status === 429) throw kino.error("rate_limited");
  if (r.status === 451) throw kino.error("geo_blocked");
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", "la API respondió " + r.status);
  return r.json();
}

export async function search(query) {
  const p = await api("/search?q=" + encodeURIComponent(query.q) + (query.cursor ? "&page=" + query.cursor : ""));
  return {
    items: p.results.map((x) => ({ id: String(x.id), ref: String(x.id), title: x.title, kind: "movie", ids: { tmdb: x.tmdb } })),
    next: p.nextPage ? String(p.nextPage) : undefined,
  };
}

export async function resolve(ref) {
  const s = await api("/play/" + encodeURIComponent(ref));
  return { url: s.url, expiresInSeconds: 3600 };
}
```

Manifest: `"hosts": ["api.example.com"]`, `"capabilities": ["search", "browse", "resolve"]` (a
`next` in a search page needs `browse`), and one setting
`{ "key": "apiKey", "label": "Clave de la API", "type": "password", "required": true }`. Since
`browse` is declared it must be exported too; `export async function browse(ref, cursor) { throw
kino.error("not_found"); }` is enough when only search pages.

## The person's own server { #own-server }

A media server at home (Jellyfin, Emby, a NAS…): the person types its address, user and password.
The address becomes an allowed host for that install, `http` and a LAN address included; streams,
posters and stills may point at it. This is the published demo plugin **Tu servidor** 1.5.0
([kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server), with a
reference server to run it against), which uses every feature up to apiVersion 7 (Kino 0.9.51) a
server of your own can: seasons, `download`, `audioTracks`, `subtitles`, `durationMs` and `skip`,
`live` items, `kino.storage` with a TTL, `kino.rank`, `ids`, `channels` in every shape (a `ref`, an
inline `stream`, an M3U playlist with an XMLTV guide, a `resolve: true` playlist, `liveSearch` and
paging), the apiVersion 6 set (a section with tabs, Categorías tiles, `scopedSearch`, `migrate`,
`adult` entries, labelled and lazy copies, request-signed HLS, the full settings form, `telemetry`,
`userMessage`) and the apiVersion 7 capabilities `tracking` and `segments`, plus `meta` with a logo,
ratings and cast and `subtitles` with Kino 0.9.51's `file` hint. It is the reference plugin for
anything beyond the five basic capabilities; [Example plugins](examples.md#reference-plugin) maps
every feature to its function. Its real
[`kino-plugin.json`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-own-server/blob/main/kino-plugin.json):

```json
{
  "id": "own-server",
  "name": "Tu servidor",
  "version": "1.5.0",
  "apiVersion": 7,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Ve el contenido de tu propio servidor de video, con sus canales y subtítulos, y cuéntale qué ves. Necesita que escribas su dirección.",
  "author": "kinotvapp",

    { "key": "userAgent", "label": "User-Agent de los canales", "type": "text", "hint": "VLC/3.0.20 LibVLC/3.0.20" },
```
