```js
  return { type: "Column", children: [
    { type: "SingleChildScrollView", flex: 1, children: [{ type: "Row", wrap: true, gap: 12, padding: 16, children: STORIES.map(card) }] },
    { type: "AlertDialog", key: "story", title: reading ? reading.title : "", onClose: "closed", children: [{ type: "Text", text: reading ? reading.source : "…" }] },
  ] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, arg }) {
  if (name === "read") return { state: { reading: arg }, ui: [{ open: "story" }] };
  if (name === "closed") return { state: { reading: null } };
  return null;
}
```

### Settings form with validation { #recipe-settings-form }

A form whose submit Kino checks first; the answer writes your settings with `config` (the manifest declares `greeting` as
a `text` setting and `density` as a `select`).

```js
export async function screen() {
  return { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Form", key: "prefs", onSubmitted: "save", gap: 12, padding: 16, children: [
    { type: "TextField", key: "greeting", labelText: "Saludo", labelTextEn: "Greeting", required: true, maxLength: 40, pattern: "^[A-Za-z ]+$", errorText: "Solo letras", errorTextEn: "Letters only" },
    { type: "RadioGroup", key: "density", labelText: "Densidad", value: "normal", options: [{ value: "compact", label: "Compacta" }, { value: "normal", label: "Normal" }, { value: "roomy", label: "Amplia" }] },
    { type: "ElevatedButton", labelText: "Guardar", labelTextEn: "Save", submit: true },
  ] }] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, value }) {
  if (name !== "save") return null;
  return { config: { greeting: value.greeting, density: value.density }, toast: "Guardado", toastEn: "Saved" };
}
```

### Confirmation pop-up { #recipe-confirm }

The quick way is a button's `confirm` (Kino asks, then runs the action); the custom way is a dialog from the answer.

```js
export async function screen({ state }) {
  return { type: "Column", gap: 12, padding: 16, children: [
    { type: "Text", text: state.deleted ? "Lista borrada" : "Tu lista" },
    { type: "TextButton", labelText: "Borrar (rápido)", confirm: "¿Borrar la lista?", confirmEn: "Delete the list?", onPressed: "delete" },
    { type: "Button", variant: "secondary", labelText: "Borrar (diálogo)", onPressed: "ask" },
  ] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name }) {
  if (name === "ask") return { dialog: { title: "¿Borrar la lista?", body: "No se puede deshacer.", buttons: [{ label: "Borrar", event: "delete", variant: "primary" }, { label: "Cancelar", variant: "text" }] } };
  if (name === "delete") return { state: { deleted: true }, toast: { text: "Borrada", role: "success" } };
  return null;
}
```

### Tabs with chips { #recipe-tabs-chips }

A `TabBar` whose value you keep in your state, and `Chips` filtering the tab's list.

```js
const ALL = [{ t: "Big Buck Bunny", k: "movies" }, { t: "Sintel", k: "movies" }, { t: "Una serie", k: "series" }];

export async function screen({ state }) {
  const tab = state.tab === "saved" ? "saved" : "all";
  const filter = typeof state.inputs?.kind === "string" ? state.inputs.kind : "any";
  const list = ALL.filter((x) => filter === "any" || x.k === filter);
  return { type: "Column", children: [
    { type: "TabBar", key: "tabs", value: tab, onChanged: "tab", tabs: [{ value: "all", label: "Todo", labelEn: "All" }, { value: "saved", label: "Guardado", labelEn: "Saved" }] },
    { type: "Chips", key: "kind", value: filter, padding: 8, options: [{ value: "any", label: "Todo" }, { value: "movies", label: "Películas" }, { value: "series", label: "Series" }], onChanged: "filter" },
    { type: "ListView", key: "list", flex: 1, items: list.map((x, i) => ({ type: "Text", key: "x" + i, text: x.t, padding: 12 })), empty: { type: "emptyState", title: "Nada", titleEn: "Nothing" } },
  ] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, value }) {
  if (name === "tab") return { state: { tab: value } };
  if (name === "filter") return { state: {} }; // the chip's value is already in state.inputs: just draw again
  return null;
}
```

### Button matrix (calculator style) { #recipe-matrix }

Buttons in a twelve-column row, three columns each (four to a line), each with its own `key`, sized per class: the
D-pad walks it as a matrix on a TV. A whole calculator plugin is built the same way.

```js
const KEYS = ["7", "8", "9", "÷", "4", "5", "6", "×", "1", "2", "3", "−", "C", "0", ".", "+"];

export async function screen({ state }) {
  const shown = typeof state.shown === "string" ? state.shown : "0";
  return { type: "Column", gap: 12, padding: 16, children: [
    { type: "Card", variant: "filled", children: [{ type: "Text", text: shown, style: "h1", crossAxisAlignment: "end" }] },
    { type: "Row", wrap: true, gap: 8, children: KEYS.map((k, i) => ({
      type: "Button", key: "k" + i, variant: /\d|\./.test(k) ? "secondary" : "primary", labelText: k,
      onPressed: "key", arg: k, span: 3, fill: true, height: { compact: 80, medium: 64, expanded: 48 },
    })) },
  ] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, arg, state }) {
  if (name !== "key") return null;
  const now = typeof state.shown === "string" ? state.shown : "0";
  return { state: { shown: arg === "C" ? "0" : (now === "0" ? "" : now) + arg } };
}
```

### A screen with an app bar, tabs and a floating button { #recipe-scaffold }

A `Scaffold` root: the bar with a back button, a search action and two tabs; a lazy list in the body; a «Nueva» button above
a bottom bar of three sections. Your state keeps the tab and the section (neither is in `state.inputs`).

```js
export async function screen({ state }) {
  const tab = state.tab === "saved" ? "saved" : "all";
  const section = ["home", "lists", "me"].includes(state.section) ? state.section : "home";
  const rows = (tab === "saved" ? ["Guardado 1"] : ["Uno", "Dos", "Tres"]).map((t, i) => ({ type: "ListTile", key: "r" + i, title: t, onTap: "show", arg: String(i) }));
  return {
    type: "Scaffold",
    appBar: {
      type: "AppBar", title: "Mis listas", titleEn: "My lists",
      leading: { type: "IconButton", icon: "arrow_back", labelText: "Atrás", labelTextEn: "Back", onPressed: { close: true } },
      actions: [{ type: "IconButton", icon: "search", labelText: "Buscar", labelTextEn: "Search", onPressed: "search" }],
      bottom: { type: "TabBar", key: "tabs", value: tab, onChanged: "tab", tabs: [{ value: "all", label: "Todo", labelEn: "All" }, { value: "saved", label: "Guardado", labelEn: "Saved" }] },
    },
    body: { type: "ListView", key: "rows", items: rows },
    floatingActionButton: { type: "FloatingActionButton", icon: "add", labelText: "Nueva", labelTextEn: "New", onPressed: "newList" },
    bottomNavigationBar: { type: "NavigationBar", value: section, onChanged: "section", items: [
      { key: "home", icon: "home", label: "Inicio", labelEn: "Home" },
      { key: "lists", icon: "list", label: "Listas", labelEn: "Lists" },
      { key: "me", icon: "person", label: "Yo", labelEn: "Me" },
    ] },
  };
}

export async function screenEvent(e) {
  if (e.name === "tab") return { state: { tab: e.value } };
  if (e.name === "section") return { state: { section: e.value } };
  return null;
}
```

### Tabs in the app bar { #recipe-app-bar-tabs }

Kino's own title bar already names the screen, so the app bar can hold the tabs themselves: a `TabBar` as the `title`, beside
the actions, one row tall.

```js
export async function screen({ state }) {
  const tab = ["account", "connection", "help"].includes(state.tab) ? state.tab : "account";
  return {
    type: "Scaffold",
    appBar: {
      type: "AppBar",
      title: { type: "TabBar", key: "tabs", value: tab, onChanged: "tab", tabs: [
        { value: "account", label: "Cuenta", labelEn: "Account" },
        { value: "connection", label: "Conexión", labelEn: "Connection" },
        { value: "help", label: "Inicio y ayuda", labelEn: "Start and help" },
      ] },
      actions: [
        { type: "IconButton", icon: "refresh", labelText: "Actualizar", labelTextEn: "Refresh", onPressed: "refresh" },
        { type: "IconButton", icon: "help", labelText: "Ayuda", labelTextEn: "Help", onPressed: "help" },
      ],
    },
    body: { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Column", padding: 16, gap: 12, children: [{ type: "Text", text: "Pestaña: " + tab }] }] },
  };
}

export async function screenEvent(e) {
  return e.name === "tab" ? { state: { tab: e.value } } : null;
}
```

### A search view that Back closes first { #recipe-search-back }

One bar (`mergeWithKinoBar`: your `leading` where Close was, your title in place of the plugin's name) and a Back that first
leaves the search, then the screen: while `state.searching` is true the tree declares `onBack`, and its answer turns the flag
off, so the next Back closes the screen.

```js
export async function screen({ state }) {
  const searching = state.searching === true;
  return {
    type: "Scaffold",
    // Declared only while there is something for Back to undo.
    onBack: searching ? "close_search" : undefined,
    appBar: {
      type: "AppBar", mergeWithKinoBar: true,
      title: searching ? "Buscar" : "Mis listas", titleEn: searching ? "Search" : "My lists",
      leading: searching
        ? { type: "IconButton", icon: "arrow_back", labelText: "Cerrar la búsqueda", labelTextEn: "Close search", onPressed: "close_search" }
        : { type: "IconButton", icon: "close", labelText: "Cerrar", labelTextEn: "Close", onPressed: { close: true } },
      actions: searching ? [] : [{ type: "IconButton", icon: "search", labelText: "Buscar", labelTextEn: "Search", onPressed: "open_search" }],
    },
    body: { type: "Column", padding: 16, gap: 12, children: [
      searching
        ? { type: "TextField", key: "q", labelText: "Buscar", labelTextEn: "Search", autofocus: true }
        : { type: "Text", text: "Tus listas", textEn: "Your lists" },
    ] },
  };
}

export async function screenEvent(e) {
  if (e.name === "open_search") return { state: { searching: true } };
  if (e.name === "close_search") return { state: { searching: false } };
  return null;
}
```

### A reader: pages that fit the width, zoom and a place that is kept { #recipe-reader }

For manga, webtoons, comics and long documents. Four small pieces, each useful alone:

- `Image` with `fit: "width"`: the picture takes the width of its box and its own height, so a page is never cut (no byte
  measuring, no size table). The `aspect` (any `"w:h"`, like `"1.4:1"`) only holds the place until it loads.
- `zoom: true` on the vertical scroll: pinch, double tap and drag; the content is laid out wider, so the picture stays sharp.
- `onScroll`: where the person stopped, `0` (top) to `1` (end), 0.3 s after they stop. Save it in `kino.storage`.
- `pages` with `reverse: true` and `progress: "bar"`: one page at a time, swiped left to right, or right to left for manga,
  up to 250 pages, with one thin bar instead of a segment per page. A page that holds a zoomable scroll zooms; one finger on
  an unzoomed page still swipes.

```js
export async function screen({ state }) {
  const pages = state.pages ?? []; // [{ url }]
  if (state.mode === "paged") {
    return { type: "pages", key: "pgs", flex: 1, reverse: state.rtl === true, progress: "bar", onPageChanged: "page",
      children: pages.map((p, i) => ({ type: "SingleChildScrollView", key: "z" + i, zoom: true, children: [
        { type: "Image", url: p.url, fit: "width", aspect: "2:3", alt: "Página " + (i + 1), altEn: "Page " + (i + 1) } ] })) };
  }
  return { type: "SingleChildScrollView", key: "strip", flex: 1, zoom: true, onScroll: "scrolled",
    children: [{ type: "Column", crossAxisAlignment: "center",
      children: pages.map((p, i) => ({ type: "Image", key: "p" + i, url: p.url, fit: "width", aspect: "2:3" })) }] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, value }) {
  if (name === "scrolled" || name === "page") { kino.storage.set("at", String(value)); return null; } // the place to resume
  return null;
}
```

- A `pages` node needs a `key` of its own and 2 or more children; with `progress: "segments"` (the default) at most 8.
- `onScroll` is for a vertical scroll that scrolls itself (the strip); inside `pages`, the page the person reached comes from `onPageChanged`.
- Resume a page with a `ui` `set` on the `pages` key in the answer that opens the chapter: `ui: [{ set: { key: "pgs", value: 4 } }]`.
- The vertical strip cannot be told to scroll to a saved position: keep the place, show it, and let the person scroll.

### A carousel at the top of a front page { #recipe-carousel }

`PageView` with `viewportFraction` below 1: the next page peeks at the side, it turns by itself and Kino draws the dots.

```js
const page = (it, i) => ({ type: "Card", key: "car-" + i, variant: "filled", radius: "large", margin: 8,
  onTap: { event: "series", arg: it.url },
  children: [{ type: "Row", gap: 16, padding: 16, crossAxisAlignment: "center", children: [
    { type: "Card", flush: true, radius: "medium", elevation: 6, children: [
      { type: "Image", url: it.poster, width: 120, aspect: "2:3", alt: it.title } ] },
    { type: "Column", gap: 8, flex: 1, crossAxisAlignment: "start", children: [
      { type: "Badge", text: "#" + (i + 1), color: "primary" },
      { type: "Text", text: it.title, style: "h3", maxLines: 3 },
      { type: "ElevatedButton", icon: "play", radius: "full", labelText: "Ver", labelTextEn: "See", onPressed: { event: "series", arg: it.url } },
    ] } ] }] });

// placeholders until your data loads: a PageView with no pages draws nothing
const DEMO = [{ url: "/a", title: "Uno", poster: "https://example.com/a.jpg" }, { url: "/b", title: "Dos", poster: "https://example.com/b.jpg" }];

export async function screen({ state }) {
  return { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [
    { type: "Text", text: "Tendencias", textEn: "Trending", style: "h3", padding: 16 },
    { type: "PageView", key: "carousel", viewportFraction: { compact: 0.9, medium: 0.6, expanded: 0.42 }, padEnds: false,
      autoPlayMs: 5000, children: (state.trending ?? DEMO).slice(0, 6).map(page) } ] };
}
```

Every page counts toward the 600 nodes of a screen: a page like this one is about 9 nodes, so six pages cost 54. Keep the
carousel to 6 to 8 pages and trim the rails under it.

### A card in Kino's Home that opens your screen, with a front page to go back to { #recipe-home-opens-screen }

A `home()` row item carries `open: { screen }`: tapping it opens your screen instead of the title page, from Kino's Home rows
and from its category shelves. Give it **`args`, not a route**, so the screen opens on your front page (route `main`) and
you push the detail over it: Back then lands on your front page instead of doing nothing.

```js
export async function home() {
  return [{ id: "trending", title: "Mangas populares", items: titles.map((t) => ({
    id: t.slug, ref: t.url, title: t.title, kind: "movie", poster: t.poster,
    open: { screen: { args: { open: t.url } } },          // no route: the screen opens as "main"
  })) }];
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, route }) {
  if (name === "open" && typeof route?.args?.open === "string") {
    const detail = await loadSeries(route.args.open);       // your own loader
    return { state: { detail }, route: { push: "detail", params: { url: route.args.open } } }; // front page below, detail on top
  }
  return null;
}
```

- A plugin that plays nothing declares `"catalogOnly": true`; give its items `kind: "movie"` (a `series` item needs `episodes`).
- Check `route.args.open` yourself (a path you recognise): it comes from a saved row that an older plugin version wrote.
- Kino keeps `home()` rows 6 hours and drops them when the plugin's version changes.

### Search inside the field, with skeletons while it loads { #recipe-search-field }

A `TextField` can carry its own search icon (`trailingIcon`, `trailingLabel`, `onTrailingTap`), so no separate button or `Form`
is needed. Show a hidden skeleton grid **at once** with a local `ui` operation, and hide it in the answer: the screen never
sits frozen while your `screenEvent` fetches.

```js
const SEARCH = { ui: [{ show: "loading" }, { hide: "results" }], event: "search" };
const card = (r) => ({ type: "Card", key: "r-" + r.id, onTap: { event: "series", arg: r.id }, children: [{ type: "Text", text: r.title, padding: 8 }] });

export async function screen({ state }) {
  return { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Column", children: [
    { type: "TextField", key: "q", kind: "search", padding: 16, labelText: "Buscar", labelTextEn: "Search",
      trailingIcon: "search", trailingLabel: "Buscar", trailingLabelEn: "Search", onSubmitted: SEARCH, onTrailingTap: SEARCH },
    { type: "Column", key: "loading", hidden: true, padding: 12, children: [{ type: "GridView", columns: 3, gap: 12,
      children: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((i) => ({ type: "Column", key: "sk" + i, gap: 8, children: [
        { type: "Skeleton", shape: "block", height: 200 }, { type: "Skeleton", shape: "line", lines: 2 } ] })) }] },
    { type: "Column", key: "results", children: (state.results ?? []).map(card) },
  ] }] };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, value }) {
  if (name !== "search") return null;
  const results = await find(String(value ?? "").trim());   // the field's text arrives as `value`
  return { state: { results }, ui: [{ hide: "loading" }, { show: "results" }] }; // also in the answer to a failure
}
```

Skeletons beat a spinner here: they keep the shape of the grid, so nothing jumps when the results arrive.

### Filters in a bottom sheet, with a search field { #recipe-filter-sheet }

Three or four filters as buttons (`Género: Todos ▾`) that open a `BottomSheet`; a long list (genres) gets a search field.
Picking a row closes the sheet and shows skeletons while the new page loads, all with local `ui` operations on the tap.

```js
const BUSY = [{ show: "skeleton" }, { hide: "grid" }];

const sheet = (key, title, options, current, event, q) => ({ type: "BottomSheet", key, title, children: [
  options.length > 8 ? { type: "TextField", key: "gq", kind: "search", value: q, padding: 8, labelText: "Buscar", onChanged: "gq" } : null,
  { type: "ListView", key: key + "-list", items: options.filter((o) => !q || o[1].toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase())).map((o) => ({
    type: "ListTile", key: key + "-" + o[0], dense: true, title: o[1],
    trailing: o[0] === current ? { type: "Icon", name: "check" } : undefined,
    onTap: { ui: [{ close: key }].concat(BUSY), event, arg: o[0] } })) },
].filter(Boolean) });

// the button that opens it
const button = (sheetKey, label, value) => ({ type: value ? "ElevatedButton" : "TextButton", radius: "full", icon: "expand_more",
  labelText: label + ": " + (value || "Todos"), onPressed: { ui: [{ open: sheetKey }] } });
```

- `gq` is your own state: `screenEvent` answers `{ state: { gq: value } }` and the next render filters the list; the sheet stays open.
- A `Chips` row is fine for 3 to 5 short options; with more, scrolling sideways hides most of them. Use a sheet.
- An option with an empty value cannot be a chip's `value`: use a word like `"all"` and read it back as empty.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/rooms/ (docs/rooms.en.md) -->

# Rooms, the library and player control { #rooms }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.74"
    Available from Kino 0.9.74. An older Kino refuses these plugins with
    «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino»; to keep reaching people on an older version use
    `enhancements` (see [Screens without raising your apiVersion](enhancements.md)).

Three capabilities give your plugin a reach beyond its own source:

- **`library`**: read what the person watched and saved in Kino ([below](#library)).
- **`playerControl`**: pause, resume and move the video by itself, not only right after the person presses a button
  ([below](#player-control)).
- **`room`**: open a room that other people reach over the Internet through the person's device ([below](#room)).

All three are **declarative** (you export nothing new: you declare them in `capabilities`) and all three have a **red**
consent line the person approves. A screen ([`screen`](screens.md)) or a tab of the
[player panel](player-panel.md#contributed-tab) is what uses them.

The reference example is **Party Chat** (<https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-watch-party>): a player-panel tab, on
any title of any plugin, that opens a room, shares it with a code and a QR, keeps everyone at the same point of the video
with `playerControl` and carries a chat. It shows everything on this page.

## Consent { #consent }

None of these capabilities is approved on its own. Kino asks the person **in its own words**, which you cannot change or
hide:

| Capability | What the person reads | Red, waits for approval | The person's switch (your tab in Ajustes) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `library` | «Podrá leer lo que has visto y guardado en Kino, cuánto lo ves y a qué hora, y enviarlo a sus servicios» ("Can read what you have watched and saved in Kino, how much and at what time of day, and send it to its services") | yes | «Dejar que lea lo que he visto y guardado» ("Let it read what I watched and saved") |
| `playerControl` | «Podrá pausar, reanudar y mover tu video por sí solo» ("Can pause, resume and move your video by itself") | yes | «Dejar que pause y mueva mi video» ("Let it pause and move my video") |
| `room` | «Podrá abrir una sala a la que se entra por internet a través de este aparato, y enviar los mensajes de la sala a quienes entren» ("Can open a room that people reach over the Internet through this device, and send the room's messages to whoever joins") | yes | «Dejar que abra salas por internet» ("Let it open rooms over the Internet") |

- A red line is asked at install and again on the update that adds it, and **Kino never approves it on its own**; the
  kit's import starts it unticked. Until the person approves it the API refuses (`permission_denied`), so always handle
  that refusal and work without it.
- Each switch is in your plugin's tab in Ajustes, covers the whole device and every profile, and syncs to the person's
  other devices. Off, the API refuses at once (a room closes).
- Kino lists your declared hosts beside the line: these lines are the safeguard, not a technical wall. A plugin that can
  `fetch` can send what it reads to its hosts.
- Be honest in your own UI too: say what you send and where.

The whole model, with the other capabilities that go with screens, is in [Screens](screens.md#consent).

## Reading what the person watched (`library`) { #library }

```json
"apiVersion": 14,
"capabilities": ["screen", "library"]
```

`library` may stand alone or beside `screen` (a plugin that declares only `library` is still valid, but can never read
it: see [when](#library-when)).

```js
const watched = await kino.library.watched({ limit: 20, kind: "movie", sinceMs: Date.now() - 30 * 86400000 });
const saved = await kino.library.saved({ limit: 50 });
```

`kino.library.watched({ limit?, kind?, sinceMs? })` and `kino.library.saved({ limit?, kind? })` answer what the **active
profile** watched and saved, newest first, one entry per title:

```ts
interface KinoLibraryEntry {
  title: string;                       // as Kino shows it (TMDB's when Kino identified it), at most 200 characters
  year?: number;                       // only when Kino knows it; usually absent on a watched one
  kind: "movie" | "series";
  ids: { tmdb?: number; imdb?: string }; // each only when Kino knows it; may be empty
  progress?: number;                   // watched only: 0..1 in steps of 0.01 (1 when finished)
  watchedAtMs?: number;                // watched only: rounded down to the day (UTC midnight)
  season?: number;                     // watched series only (apiVersion 15): the season of the latest chapter played
  episode?: number;                    // watched series only (apiVersion 15): the number of that chapter
}
```

- **`season` and `episode`** (from Kino 0.9.77): on a **watched series**, the latest chapter played, only
  when its source numbered it. Never on a movie or on a series with no numbered chapter.

- `kind` is `movie` or `series` and works as a filter; music and podcasts are left out.
- `limit`: default 50, at most 100 (above 100 gives 100). `sinceMs` keeps titles played on that day (UTC) or later. A
  number that is not finite is `bad_request`.

From apiVersion 17, `kino.library.stats({ month? })` answers a month's aggregates (seconds watched, by kind and by time of day,
titles, active days and a `top`) with this same capability and the same switch: see
[`kino.library.stats`](kino-api.md#library-stats).

### What never comes { #library-never }

- **Never**: a stream URL, a plugin ref, a Kino id, a position in seconds, a profile name, anything of another profile, or
  an 18+ title (always left out, even with the 18+ code unlocked; a title whose source this device cannot place is left
  out too: it fails closed).
- **Coarse on purpose**: `watchedAtMs` and `sinceMs` are rounded down to the day (UTC), `progress` to steps of 0.01, so
  nothing finer can be probed. Titles watched on the same day come in Kino's own order.

### When it can be read { #library-when }

- Only inside a call the person started: `screen`, `screenEvent` (timer ticks count while the screen is in front),
  `home`, `section`, `search`, and a [background job](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs) with this approval. Never in prewarm or
  sync calls. A plugin with only `library` can therefore never read it.
- At most **30 calls a minute** per plugin.
- Kino keeps nothing of an answer; a Home answer you build from it is cached like any Home answer.

### Errors and detection { #library-errors }

- `permission_denied` (not approved, or switched off), `rate_limited`, `bad_request`.
- Feature-detect with `typeof kino.library === "object"` and **still** catch `permission_denied`: a plugin whose `library`
  came through an [`enhancements`](enhancements.md) block on a Kino updated after the install is asked only with its next
  version.

```js
async function recentMovies() {
  if (typeof kino.library !== "object") return [];
  try {
    return await kino.library.watched({ limit: 20, kind: "movie" });
  } catch (e) {
    if (e && e.code === "permission_denied") return []; // not approved or switched off: work without it
    throw e;
  }
}
```

- Kit: `KINO_LIBRARY_FIXTURE=<json>` stands in for the person's data and `KINO_LIBRARY_REVOKED=1` plays the switch off.

## Moving the video (`playerControl`) { #player-control }

A declarative capability (no export) that **never stands alone**: only beside a panel, your own (`panel`) or a tab you
contribute to other plugins (`"panel": { "contributes": true }` with `playerPanelTab`, see
[the player panel](player-panel.md#contributed-tab)). Without a panel the manifest is refused with
"The \"playerControl\" capability needs a \"panel\" ...".

```json
"apiVersion": 14,
"capabilities": ["screen", "playerPanelTab", "playerControl", "room"],
"panel": { "contributes": true, "label": "Party Chat" }
```

With `playerControl` a `player` action may also carry `pause`: `true` pauses, `false` resumes (any other value is
dropped). It is a one-shot command: never stored.

### Without the capability and with it { #player-control-origins }

Every `player` action has an **origin**: `press`, `change` or `submit` (what the person does in the panel), `refresh` (a
panel result's own `player`: on open, on a tab, on a `refreshMs` tick, or a `playerEvent` answer's new panel) and `event`
(a `playerEvent` answer).

| Who | Without `playerControl` | With `playerControl` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The plugin whose title plays | The apiVersion 9 rules: every `player` field after the person's `press`, `change` or `submit` and in a `playerEvent` answer; `pause` only after a `press`; a panel result's own `player` never counts. | Every origin counts: `press`, `change`, `submit`, `refresh` and `event`. |
| A tab contributed to another plugin | Only `seekToMs`, only after a `press` in your tab. | `seekToMs`, `pause` and `speed`, from any origin. |

So a `refreshMs` tick can keep the video in step with the room without anybody touching anything.

### What Kino still enforces { #player-control-limits }

The same for every plugin (contract.json `kinoPlayerControl`):

- **One seek or pause a second per plugin**, always (the panel and its `playerEvent` calls together).
- An action kept only thanks to the capability is dropped while Kino is not in front (the player covered or in the
  background), while one of Kino's dialogs is up, or while the person is seeking.
- On a live stream, only `pause`.
- At most **30 a minute**.
- A pause is dropped while the phone's player is held for a cast (Chromecast or DLNA), and when it asks for the state the
  video is already in (no notice, no budget).
- A panel nested in an answer carries no `player` of its own.
- When the action does not come from the person's press (`refresh` or `event`), Kino shows a short notice naming your
  plugin, which you cannot word or suppress: «Party Chat: pausado», «Party Chat: reanudado, movido a 1:02:03» (in English
  "Party Chat: paused", "resumed", "moved to {time}", "speed {speed}"). A name that reads like "Kino" is shown qualified.
- A contributed tab's speed is never stored: it ends with the title, and the person's own speed wins.

The `player` properties (`seekToMs`, `speed`, `resize`…) and who wins against the person are in
[Driving the player](player-panel.md#player).

- Kit: `KINO_PLAYER_CONTROL_REVOKED=1` plays the switch off.

## Rooms over the Internet (`room`) { #room }

A declarative capability that **never stands alone**: a screen or a player-panel tab drives it. `kino.room` is a
short-lived mailbox **hosted on the person's own device** and reached from the Internet through the same Cloudflare quick
tunnel Kino opens for «Recibir configuración»: no server of yours or Kino's, and your code never sees an address.

```js
const { code, words, expiresAtMs } = await kino.room.open({ ttlMin: 120, max: 6, name: "Ana" }); // the host, from a press
const { handle, memberId } = await kino.room.join({ words, code, name: "Beto" });                // a guest, from a press
await kino.room.send({ t: "chat", text: "hola" });                                               // a JSON object
const { events, last, more, reachable } = await kino.room.inbox({ since: state.last });          // poll it from a timer
```

Feature-detect it with `typeof kino.room === "object"`.

### The functions { #room-api }

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `open({ ttlMin?, max?, name?, codeDigits?, code? })` | Opens the tunnel and the mailbox. `ttlMin` 10 to 240 (default 120); `max` members counting you, 2 to 8 (default 6); `name`, your name as the guests see it, up to 40 characters. Answers `{ code, words, expiresAtMs }`. |
| `join({ words, code, name? })` | Joins a room with the words and code the host shared; `name` up to 24 characters. Answers `{ handle, memberId, host: { name }, expiresAtMs }`. Keep `handle`: it names this session in the other calls. |
| `send(payload, { to?, session? })` | Sends a JSON object of at most 8192 bytes and 4 levels. The host writes to one `memberId` or everyone (`to` absent or `"all"`); a guest to the host (`to` absent or `"host"`) or to `"all"` through the host, never to another member directly. |
| `inbox({ since?, limit?, session? })` | Answers `{ events, last, more, reachable }`: the events after `since` (pass the answer's `last` next time), at most `limit` (1 to 50, default 50). |
| `members({ session? })` | `[{ memberId, name, host }]`: never an address. |
| `close({ session? })` | Closes the session (or the room, if you are the host). |
| `state()` | `{ role: "host" \| "guest" \| "none", joined: [...], hosted: { code, words, expiresAtMs, members } \| null }`: your plugin's sessions on this device. |

- `words` are **public** (`brave-river-cat-moon`): anyone may see them. The `code` is the room's **only secret**: 12
  digits, or the ones you ask for with `codeDigits` (4 to 12). Show it grouped, «1234 5678 9012», and as a QR; spaces and
  hyphens are ignored on `join`. `join` needs both.
- An event is `{ seq, from, kind, payload?, name? }`: `kind` is `msg`, `join`, `leave` or `closed`; `from` is a
  `memberId` or `"host"`; `payload` (`msg` only) is the object the sender passed, re-serialised by Kino; `name` (`join`
  only) is the member's name. `seq` only grows.
- `reachable: false` means a guest's last poll of its host got no answer: your failover cue. A guest asks its host at most
  once a second.
- `session` is `"hosted"` (the room this device hosts) or a `handle` from `join`. Absent: the first joined session, else
  the hosted one.
- A member the host has not heard from for 2 minutes is dropped (`leave`).

### A short code { #room-short-code }

`open({ codeDigits: 4 })` makes a code friends can type. It keeps strangers out **only because the words cannot be
guessed** and the room closes itself after 30 wrong codes (Kino tells the person; your next calls get `room_closed`).
Whoever captures the traffic and knows the words, the tunnel provider among them, recovers a 4-digit code offline in
milliseconds: such a room is not private from the provider. The default 12 digits makes that expensive, not impossible.
Keep a room's messages low-sensitivity either way.

### When it can be called { #room-when }

- `open` and `join` **only from the person's own press** (`screenEvent`, `panelAction`; never a tick or a refresh), so a
  plugin can never move a person into a room, or open one, behind their back.
- `send`, `inbox` and `members` from your screen's or panel's calls (`screen`, `screenEvent`, `panel`, `panelAction`,
  `playerEvent`), ticks included, only while Kino is in front.
- `close` and `state` from any live call.
- **Never from a [background job](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs)** (there `kino.room` answers `not_allowed`).

### Limits { #room-limits }

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| A message | at most 8192 bytes (UTF-8, as your plugin's JSON text) and 4 levels (the object itself is 1) |
| Rate per member | 5 messages a second; 100 messages and 256 KB a minute (checked by the sender's Kino and again by the host) |
| Members | 2 to 8 (default 6) |
| Lifetime | 10 to 240 minutes (default 120) |
| Mailbox | 200 events or 15 minutes per member |
| Sessions per device | 2 joined and 1 hosted; at most 2 of them for one plugin (`room_busy`) |
| Wrong codes | 5 lock joins for 60 s, doubling up to 30 minutes (`rate_limited`); 30 in all close the room |

A room closes at its lifetime, with `close()`, when the plugin is removed, disabled or the person switches it off, when
plugin screens are switched off in Kino, and after **30 minutes** of Kino in the background. While the device hosts a room,
Android shows Kino's own notification «Sala abierta · N personas» with «Cerrar sala» and keeps the room alive, so the host
can step out to paste the invitation; the person swiping Kino away closes it.

While the device hosts a room, your tab in Ajustes shows it with a button to close it.

### Errors { #room-errors }

`room_denied`, `room_closed`, `room_full`, `room_unreachable`, `room_busy`, `rate_limited`, `permission_denied`,
`bad_request`. `room_unreachable` (no internet, a network that blocks it, Cloudflare's rate limit) and the room refusals
carry Kino's own `userMessage`.

### Security, said plainly { #room-security }

- Every request is sealed (scrypt N=8192 r=8 of the code salted with the words, AES-256-GCM plus HMAC-SHA256, per-member
  keys) and messages are never stored, logged or executed by Kino.
- **The code protects against casual access, not against the tunnel provider.** A stranger can only guess online (and
  gets locked out), but the TLS-terminating provider, targeting a room, could crack a captured join offline (about 400
  GPU-days on average on one high-end GPU) and then read it; there is no forward secrecy. **Keep a room's messages
  low-sensitivity** (a chat, a position). A password-authenticated exchange (CPace or SPAKE2) is recorded as future
  hardening.
- **Payloads are untrusted**: check every message's kind, exact fields, sizes and types; scrub names; cap texts; never
  execute or render one as markup. Never put the code in a message or a log.

### What is yours { #room-yours }

Who leads, what a message means, history and failover are yours. With `open({ code })` a member opens a second door to
the same room with its own words (refused with `permission_denied` unless your plugin is in that room now or opened it;
its expiry is capped at the room's); publish its words a few seconds later (a fresh name takes a moment to resolve). Send
a goodbye before `close()`. Party Chat shows all of it.

- Kit: an in-memory room with two simulated members (`createKitRoom()` in tests: `say`, `leave`) and `KINO_ROOM_REVOKED=1`
  for the switch off.

## Trying it with the kit { #kit }

```
node sdk/validate.mjs <folder>                                    # the manifest, the exports, every consent line
node sdk/run.mjs --foreign latino:Latino <folder> panel <ref>     # a tab you contribute to another plugin's title
node sdk/run.mjs --state '{}' --screen <folder> panelAction <ref> <name> press
```

| Variable | What it plays |
| --- | --- |
| `KINO_LIBRARY_FIXTURE=<json>` | the person's data for `kino.library` |
| `KINO_LIBRARY_REVOKED=1` | `library` switched off |
| `KINO_PLAYER_CONTROL_REVOKED=1` | `playerControl` switched off |
| `KINO_ROOM_REVOKED=1` | `room` switched off |

In `node --test` files, import the kit's helpers (`createKino`, `createKitRoom`…) as Party Chat's tests do. More in
[Testing screens with the kit](screens.md#testing).

## Limits in one place { #limits }

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `kino.library` | `limit` default 50, at most 100; at most 30 calls a minute per plugin; times rounded to the day, `progress` to 0.01 |
| `playerControl` | one seek or pause a second per plugin; at most 30 actions a minute |
| `kino.room` | a message at most 8192 bytes and 4 levels; 5 messages a second, 100 and 256 KB a minute per member; 2 to 8 members; 10 to 240 minutes (default 120); mailbox 200 events or 15 minutes; 2 joined and 1 hosted per device, 2 per plugin; 5 wrong codes lock joins for 60 s, doubling up to 30 minutes; closed after 30 minutes in the background (a hosted room shows Kino's notification meanwhile) |


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/jobs-and-shared/ (docs/jobs-and-shared.en.md) -->

# Background jobs, shared results and AI { #jobs-and-shared }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.74"
    Available from Kino 0.9.74. An older Kino refuses these plugins with
    «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino»; to keep reaching people on an older version use
    `enhancements` (see [Screens without raising your apiVersion](enhancements.md)).

Three capabilities help your [screen](screens.md) open with fresh data without making anybody wait:

- **`schedule`** (with the manifest's `jobs` field and the `job` export): Kino runs your code in the background every so
  often ([below](#jobs)).
- **`shared`**: a few small results that sync between the person's linked devices, so the phone does the work and the TV
  reads it ([below](#shared)).
- **`ai`**: one short ask to Kino's text AI, to summarise or classify ([below](#ai)).

None stands alone: a job feeds what your screen or catalog shows.

The reference example is **Solo noticias** (<https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-news>): a news screen and a job that,
from the phone, fetches the headlines, sorts them with the AI and leaves the result in `kino.shared` so the TV's screen
reads it when it opens.

## Consent { #consent }

| Capability | What the person reads | Red, waits for approval | The person's switch (your tab in Ajustes) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule` | «Podrá ejecutarse en segundo plano cada cierto tiempo para actualizar sus datos, usando internet y batería» ("Can run in the background every so often to refresh its data, using your internet and battery") | yes | «Dejar que trabaje en segundo plano» ("Let it work in the background") |
| `ai` | «Podrá enviar texto a un servicio de IA de terceros (Kilo) para que lo resuma o clasifique; lo que envíe sale de tu aparato» ("Can send text to a third-party AI service (Kilo) to have it summarized or classified; what it sends leaves your device") | yes | «Dejar que use la IA de texto» ("Let it use the text AI") |
| `shared` | «Guarda unos pocos resultados que se sincronizan entre tus aparatos vinculados» ("Keeps a few small results that sync between your linked devices") | no | none |

- A red line is asked at install and again on the update that adds it, and **Kino never approves it on its own**; the
  kit's import starts it unticked. Until the person approves it the API refuses, so always handle the refusal and work
  without it.
- Each switch is in your plugin's tab in Ajustes, covers the whole device and every profile, and syncs to the person's
  other devices. Off, the API refuses at once (a job's work is cancelled).
- `shared` is a plain line: marked new on the update that adds it and never waiting for approval (it is the person's own
  data on the person's own devices). An update that adds only `shared` applies without a sheet.
- Be honest in your own UI: say what you send and where (Solo noticias' settings say «Los titulares se envían al servicio
  de IA de terceros de Kino»).

The whole model is in [Screens](screens.md#consent).

## Background jobs (`schedule`, `jobs`, `job(ctx)`) { #jobs }

The capability `schedule`, the manifest's `jobs` field and the export `job` need each other; a job never stands alone (it
feeds what your screen or catalog shows):

```json
"capabilities": ["screen", "schedule", "shared"],
"jobs": [{ "id": "refresh", "label": { "es": "Actualizar", "en": "Refresh" }, "everyMin": 60,
           "everyOptions": [15, 60, 180, 1440], "runOn": "preferPhone" }]
```

```js
export async function job({ id, reason, lastRunMs, attempt }) {
  const data = await refreshSomething(); // a few requests, one at a time
  kino.storage.set("feed", JSON.stringify(data)); // or kino.shared, for "preferPhone"
}
```

### The manifest's `jobs` field { #jobs-manifest }

Required with the `schedule` capability and refused without it: 1 to 3 jobs, each like this:

```json
{ "id": "refresh", "label": { "es": "Actualizar noticias", "en": "Refresh news" }, "everyMin": 60,
  "everyOptions": [15, 30, 60, 180, 720, 1440] }
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | 1 to 24 characters (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`), unique. |
| `label` | `{ es, en? }`: `es` 1 to 40 characters, `en` optional with the same limit (control and bidirectional characters are dropped). |
| `everyOptions` | 1 to 6 different whole minutes, from 15 (Android's floor for periodic work) to 1440. |
| `everyMin` | The default: one of `everyOptions`. |
| `runOn` | Optional: `"any"` (the default) or `"preferPhone"`; see [below](#prefer-phone). |
| `enabledBy` | Optional: the key of one of your `toggle` settings; see [below](#enabled-by). |
| `perProfile` | Optional, apiVersion 17 (`true` or `false`, always with `runOn: "any"`): one run per profile of the device with your plugin on; see [below](#per-profile). |

Any other key of a job is ignored. The texts a manifest is refused with:

| Problem | Text |
| --- | --- |
| `jobs` without `schedule` | `The "jobs" field needs the "schedule" capability` |
| `schedule` without `jobs` | `The "schedule" capability needs a "jobs" list with 1 to 3 jobs` |
| `jobs` is not a valid list | `The "jobs" field must be a list of 1 to 3 jobs` |
| `id` | `Each job needs an "id" of 1 to 24 characters: a-z, 0-9 and -` / `Two jobs have the same "id"` |
| `label` | `Each job needs a "label" object whose "es" is 1 to 40 characters ("en" optional, the same limit)` |
| `everyOptions` | `Each job's "everyOptions" must list 1 to 6 different whole numbers of minutes from 15 to 1440` |
| `everyMin` | `Each job's "everyMin" must be one of its "everyOptions"` |
| `runOn` | `Each job's "runOn" must be "any" or "preferPhone"` |
| `enabledBy` | `Each job's "enabledBy" must name one of the plugin's toggle settings` |
| `perProfile` | `A "perProfile" job must use "runOn": "any"` / `A job's "perProfile" needs apiVersion 17` / `Each job's "perProfile" must be true or false` / `A "perProfile" job can't use "enabledBy": Kino's own row is its consent` |

### How it runs { #jobs-run }

- Kino runs `job(ctx)` headless, through Android's WorkManager, every `everyMin` minutes while the person has that job
  switched on: **each job starts off** (the person switches it on), and off again after any gap in its approval
  (uninstalled, an update without it, a reinstall).
- `ctx` is `{ id, reason, lastRunMs, attempt }`: `id` is the manifest's; `reason` is `scheduled` or `manual` («Ejecutar
  ahora»); `lastRunMs` is when it last ran on this device (`null` before the first run); `attempt` is 1 plus its failures
  in a row.
- **Its answer is never read and nothing of a job is shown**: write to `kino.storage` (or [`kino.shared`](#shared)) and
  let your screen read it when it opens (stale-while-revalidate).
- It never starts while your screen, panel or catalog call runs (it waits up to 30 s, then gives way).
- It needs a network and the battery not low; «Solo con Wi-Fi» is on by default (per plugin).
- It stops when the plugin is disabled, removed or updated (it then runs as a new work), when the job is switched off or
  paused, or when Kino switches plugin screens off.

### Caps per run { #jobs-caps }

| What | Cap |
| --- | --- |
| Time | 20 s (60 s with `ai`, see below) |
| Requests | 10, made one at a time (the next answers `rate_limited`); 20 with `ai` |
| Answer bodies | 2 MB in all (an answer that would cross it is refused with `too_large`, never handed over) |
| Written to `kino.storage` | 256 KB (UTF-8 bytes of keys and values; the next `set` throws `too_large`) |
| Runs | 96 a day per plugin (UTC), all its jobs together |

From apiVersion 17, a run of a plugin whose `ai` is approved and switched on has 60 s and 20 requests instead of 20 s and 10;
every other cap stands.

A cap crossed cuts the run and counts as a failure. A failure waits 15 minutes, doubling up to 6 h; **3 in a row pause the
job** until the person switches it off and on, or a manual run succeeds. Kino words the failure itself (`timeout`,
`cap_fetches`, `cap_bytes`, `cap_storage`, `network` only when `kino.fetch` itself failed to reach a site, `plugin_error`).

### A job's APIs { #jobs-apis }

An allow-list:

- `kino.fetch` (your declared hosts and every usual rule and quota), `kino.storage`, `kino.log`, `kino.config` (read),
  `kino.cookies`, `kino.crypto`, `kino.sleep`, `kino.html`, `kino.secret`, `kino.error`, `kino.rank`.
- [`kino.library`](rooms.md#library), with its own approval (the same 18+ rule, rounding and rate).
- [`kino.ai`](#ai), with its own approval; each ask is one of the run's requests (10, or 20 with `ai`).
- `kino.tmdb` (apiVersion 17): each call, a cached one too, is one of the run's requests.
- [`kino.shared`](#shared).
- [`kino.progress`](progress.md) (apiVersion 22), but not in a job that runs for a profile other than the active one.
- [`kino.notifications`](notifications.md) (apiVersion 15), with its own approval: typically the job posts what is new here.
- [`kino.seed`](kino-api.md#seed), under exactly its usual rules: the same telemetry consent, filter and caps. So a
  contribution may move from after Home into a job (with [`enabledBy`](#enabled-by) on your contribution setting, it runs
  exactly while the person leaves that setting on).
- The plain values: `kino.apiVersion`, `kino.appVersion`, `kino.lang`, `kino.device`, `kino.fetchAnyHost`, `kino.screen`.

Everything else (`kino.room`, `kino.qr`, `kino.browser`, `kino.ws`, `kino.meta`, `kino.nuvio`,
`kino.catalog`, `kino.sync`, `kino.cloudstream` and any later API) answers `not_allowed` (logged). No UI, `go`, toast,
player action or room can come out of a job. Once a run is over (it answered or was cut), every API refuses whatever its
evaluation still tries.

### Kino's rows in Ajustes { #jobs-rows }

In your plugin's tab in Ajustes Kino draws, for each job (you draw nothing): its switch, its frequency (only your
`everyOptions`), «Solo con Wi-Fi», the last run and «Ejecutar ahora» (`reason: "manual"`, the same caps; with the
permission off not even a manual run goes). The person's choices (on, frequency, Wi-Fi only) sync between their devices.

An update never makes a job that is on run more often than before: the person's choice stays while it is still an option,
else the nearest option at least as slow as both the new `everyMin` and the period it ran at; when no option is that slow,
the job is switched off and its row asks the person to choose again.

### `runOn: "preferPhone"` { #prefer-phone }

`runOn: "any"` (the default): every device that has the plugin runs its own job, for its own `kino.storage`.

`runOn: "preferPhone"`: **ONE** of the person's linked devices runs it, a linked phone first:

- A TV never runs it while a phone that ran it **successfully** within two of its periods can. With no phone, or no
  successful run on the phone for two periods (its job paused or switched off there, no Wi-Fi with «Solo con Wi-Fi», the
  app force-stopped), the device that has the plugin (the TV) runs it itself.
- Each device decides by itself from a synced record (no voting); on a device whose turn it is not, the firing skips at
  once (no network, never a failure). A rare overlap runs it twice, harmless with last-writer-wins results.
- Write the result with [`kino.shared`](#shared) so the TV's screen reads it, and read `kino.device` in the job to do a
  lighter batch when the TV does run it (Kino enforces nothing extra; the job's caps apply).
- Kino's row adds «Hacer el trabajo en» ("Do the work on") with two choices, «Este aparato» ("This device") and «El
  celular si está vinculado» ("The phone, if linked", the default), and «Última ejecución en: {device}» ("Last run on:
  {device}"). «Ejecutar ahora» runs on the device where it is pressed.

### A setting that switches it on (`enabledBy`) { #enabled-by }

A job may name one of your own `toggle` settings, `"enabledBy": "contribute"`: that setting is then the person's on/off for
the job instead of the job's own switch (no second switch to find).

- The job is on while the setting is on (its `default` counts) and the job's row in Ajustes holds no OFF of the person's:
  the row still switches it off, and that OFF wins until the person switches the row on again. With the setting off the
  job never runs.
- Kino's row says which setting drives it: «Lo enciende y lo apaga el ajuste «{label}» del plugin; aquí también puedes
  apagarlo.» ("The plugin's “{label}” setting turns it on and off; you can also switch it off here.")
- Anything but the key of one of your `toggle` settings refuses the manifest (`Each job's "enabledBy" must name one of the
  plugin's toggle settings`); in an `enhancements` block, the block is dropped.
- The consent line, the permission switch, the frequency, «Solo con Wi-Fi» and every cap stay as above.

### One run per profile (`"perProfile": true`) { #per-profile }

From apiVersion 17 (always with `runOn: "any"`), Kino runs `job(ctx)` once for each profile of the device with your plugin on,
one at a time, oldest result first, each as its own run: its own caps, `lastRunMs`, `attempt`, backoff and pause, and one of the
96 runs a day.

- What does not fit the worker's nine minutes continues in the next period. A failure pauses that profile's turn, not the
  others'.
- `ctx` is unchanged: your code gets no profile id or name and cannot tell them apart.
- `kino.library`, `kino.shared`, `kino.storage`, `kino.config` and `kino.cookies` (with `kino.fetch`'s jar) answer for that
  profile only. For a profile that is not the one in use the runtime is opened for that run alone, so nothing in memory crosses:
  never count on a module variable from one run to the next.
- There, `kino.notifications`, `kino.coins`, `kino.seed` and `kino.progress` have no per-profile home and answer `not_allowed`: catch it.
  `kino.log` stays out of the Registro and of reports, `kino.tmdb` uses Kino's key only, and hosts, `kino.lang` and typed
  servers are that profile's; code at module level there only reads.
- **Consent is Kino's own row.** A `perProfile` job may not declare `enabledBy`: consent is Kino's own job row in Ajustes, off by
  default, device-wide and synced, covering every profile of the device and linked devices. Ask on your screen, saying what
  runs and what leaves the device, and answer the person's tap with `{ enableJob: "<jobId>" }` ([answers](screens.md#answers)):
  it turns the row on, only after a tap, with the plugin's approvals in place; no answer turns it off.
- `kino.jobOn("<jobId>")` answers `true` or `false` in `screen` and `screenEvent`, so you know whether to ask; it is refused in a
  job.
- **«Incluir este perfil» / "Include this profile".** Each profile also has Kino's own row, on by default: a profile that
  leaves itself out gets no turn, and its data is not read. `kino.jobOn` reads the first row; nothing tells you about the
  second: with no turn the job simply does not run for that profile.
- A person who switched the first row off keeps it off: `enableJob` is dropped and Kino tells them to turn it on in your tab.
  `enableJob` applies only to a job without `enabledBy`. Do not rename a `perProfile` job's id: both rows go by it, so a new id
  loses the person's choice and every profile's left-out mark.
- It must use `runOn: "any"` (a TV may hold profiles the phone lacks): each device serves the profiles it holds; share a result
  through `kino.shared` and skip the work when a fresh one already arrived.
- «Ejecutar ahora» runs the profile in use only, even one left out, since the person pressed it.
- The consent line says it works for every profile of the device and linked devices, and an update that adds `perProfile` asks
  again.

### Trying it with the kit { #jobs-kit }

```
node sdk/run.mjs <folder> job [jobId] [scheduled|manual]        # one job run, with Kino's caps
node sdk/run.mjs --device phone <folder> job refresh manual      # the job, as the phone
node sdk/run.mjs --device tv <folder> screen                     # ...then read what the job shared, as the TV
```

## Results shared between devices (`shared`) { #shared }

A declarative capability (no export) that never stands alone, with a **plain** consent line (not red, never waiting: the
person's own data on the person's own devices; an update that adds only `shared` applies without a sheet).

```js
kino.shared.set("digest", { at: Date.now(), items: top });  // true when stored, false when it was already that value
const digest = kino.shared.get("digest");                   // the value or null; never throws for a stored value
kino.shared.set("digest", null);                            // removes it
```

- `kino.shared.get(key)` answers the value or `null` (it never throws for a stored value: one this engine cannot read
  answers `null`). `kino.shared.set(key, value)` answers `true` when stored and `false` when it was already that value
  (nothing written or sent); `set(key, null)` removes it.
- Synchronous, like `kino.storage`, from screens, panels, settings and jobs (in a job it does not count against its
  `kino.storage` cap, but against these limits).
- Feature-detect it with `typeof kino.shared === "object"`.

### Limits { #shared-limits }

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Keys | up to 4 per plugin, `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,40}$` |
| A value | strict JSON of at most 64 KB (UTF-8) and 16 levels |
| The whole plugin | 128 KB of values |
| Writes | 30 a minute per plugin (`rate_limited`) |
| Travel | a key's new value travels at most once a minute, and at most 4 of your keys a minute |

- Values sync between the person's linked devices, both ways, **per profile** (a TV that carries several people's
  profiles never hands one person's values to another's phone); last writer wins by a clock Kino assigns. A scheduled job
  (device-wide) writes to the profile in use. Reads on this device see the new value at once.
- A device not linked to any other keeps them as an ordinary local store.
- They go (on every linked device) when the plugin is removed. Each plugin reaches only its own keys.
- Errors (thrown as Kino errors): `not_allowed` (no capability, the plugin off, a sealed value), `bad_request` (a bad key,
  a value that is not JSON, a secret-like key), `too_large`, `rate_limited`.

!!! warning "Never a secret in `shared`"
    Never put a token, a password, a cookie or a session there: it is copied to every linked device. A key with a word
    like one (`token`, `secret`, `password`, `cookie`, `session`, `auth`, `apiKey`, plurals too; `author` is fine) is
    refused, and so is a value holding a sealed secret. Those belong in `kino.storage` or your settings.

!!! warning "What `get` answers is untrusted"
    Another device wrote it, maybe with another version of your plugin. Validate its shape, sizes and every field before
    you use it.

### Trying it with the kit { #shared-kit }

`--device phone` and `--device tv` are two simulated devices sharing `.kino-shared.json`:

```
node sdk/run.mjs --device phone <folder> job
node sdk/run.mjs --device tv <folder> screen
node sdk/run.mjs <folder> shared                                 # what the simulated phone and TV hold
```

## Kino's text AI (`ai`) { #ai }

`kino.ai.ask({ prompt, system?, json?, maxChars? })` sends one short text to Kino's text AI (Kilo's free models, the same
fixed destination as Kino's own assistant; no key and no server of yours) and answers `{ ok: true, text, model }` or
`{ ok: false, error, message }`. **It never throws.**

```js
const answer = await kino.ai.ask({
  system: "Classify each headline as sports, politics or other.",
  prompt: headlines.map((h, i) => `${i}. ${h.title}`).join("\n"),
  json: true,
  maxChars: 1000,
});
if (!answer.ok) return fallback(); // unavailable, rate_limited, too_large, timeout or refused
```

- One-shot: no memory between asks, no streaming, no tools, no images or files; Kino adds no persona and keeps nothing (its
  logs carry sizes and codes only).
- `model` is only the name of the model that answered: never an address, a key or a header. `message` is Kino's English
  detail for you, never for the person.
- `json: true` only **ASKS** for JSON (Kino adds an instruction to the system text); the text comes back as the model
  wrote it, parseable or not.
- Feature-detect it with `typeof kino.ai === "object"`.

### Limits { #ai-limits }

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt` | non-empty, at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes |
| `system` | at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes |
| `maxChars` | 1 to 4096 (default 2048): the reply is cut there |
| Per plugin | 10 asks in any minute, 100 a day (UTC), one at a time (the next is `rate_limited`, never queued), 20 s each |
| The whole device | 300 a day and 2 at once for every plugin together, so plugins never starve Kino's own assistant (which shares Kilo's anonymous quota) |

The errors: `unavailable` (no model could answer: no internet, every free model busy), `rate_limited`, `too_large`,
`timeout`, `refused` (anything else: not approved, switched off, the plugin disabled, the wrong origin, a malformed
request).

### When it can ask { #ai-when }

- **Only after the person's own press**: a settings `action`, a `panelAction`, a `screenEvent` that follows a tap or a
  submit. Never from a screen's `open`, a tick, a load-more, a change, a `playerEvent`, Home, search or play.
- **Or from your [job](#jobs)**: each ask is one of the run's 10 requests, and is refused once the run is over.
- A screen event is still bounded by its session's own 60 s: ask once per event and batch items into one prompt.

!!! warning "The reply is untrusted data"
    The model read whatever you sent, and text you took from the web or from the person can steer it (prompt
    injection). Validate every field against what you sent (drop ids and categories you did not ask for), never execute
    it, never follow instructions found in it, never open a URL from it without checking it, and keep a fallback for when
    the AI is off or unavailable. Kino never shows a reply by itself: your screen shows what you decide.

What you send leaves the device: say so in your own UI.

### Trying it with the kit { #ai-kit }

The kit answers canned text. The variables `KINO_AI_REPLY` (the reply), `KINO_AI_ERROR` (an error) and
`KINO_AI_REVOKED=1` (the capability switched off) play what happens on the device.

## Limits in one place { #limits }

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Jobs (`schedule`) | 1 to 3 jobs, every 15 to 1440 minutes; one run at most 20 s, 10 requests made one at a time, 2 MB of answers and 256 KB written to `kino.storage`; 96 runs a day per plugin; a failure waits 15 minutes, doubling up to 6 h, and 3 in a row pause the job; from apiVersion 17 a plugin with `ai` approved gets 60 s and 20 requests |
| `kino.shared` | 4 keys of at most 40 characters per plugin; a value at most 64 KB and 16 levels, 128 KB in all; 30 writes a minute; a key's new value travels at most once every 60 s |
| `kino.ai` | a `prompt` at most 8192 bytes, `system` 2048; the reply cut at `maxChars` (1 to 4096, default 2048); 10 asks in any minute, 100 a day and 1 at a time per plugin; 300 a day and 2 at a time for every plugin of the device together; 20 s an ask |


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/enhancements/ (docs/enhancements.en.md) -->

# Screens and newer features without raising your apiVersion { #enhancements-page }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.74"
    Available from Kino 0.9.74. Only Kino 0.9.74 or later reads the
    `enhancements` block; an older Kino **ignores it**, like any key it does not know, and keeps installing and running
    your plugin as always: it never refuses it because of this block.

A plugin that raises its `apiVersion` to 14 is refused by every older Kino («Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de
Kino»). To keep those people, leave your `apiVersion` as it is and offer [screens](screens.md) and the other apiVersion 14
features in an optional block only a newer Kino reads.

## The `enhancements` block { #enhancements }

```json
"apiVersion": 8,
"capabilities": ["search", "home", "resolve"],
"enhancements": { "14": { "capabilities": ["screen", "library"], "screen": { "label": "Inicio", "menuOpens": "both" } } }
```

An older Kino ignores the key and never calls `screen`/`screenEvent` (the JS stays one file); this Kino merges the block and
checks it with apiVersion 14's rules. A block that fails is dropped and logged, **never a refusal**.

Another example, with a background job:

```json
"apiVersion": 8,
"enhancements": { "14": {
  "capabilities": ["screen", "schedule", "shared"],
  "screen": { "label": "Mi plugin", "opensFrom": ["settings"] },
  "jobs": [{ "id": "refresh", "label": { "es": "Actualizar", "en": "Refresh" }, "everyMin": 180, "everyOptions": [60, 180, 360] }]
} }
```

### How Kino reads it { #merge }

- **The keys** are the `apiVersion` that brought the feature: today, `"14"`. A Kino that knows the key merges its block
  over the manifest, keys in numeric order. A key above that Kino's apiVersion is ignored.
- **`capabilities` are added.** Only `screen`, `library`, `playerPanelTab`, `playerControl`, `room`, `schedule`, `shared`,
  `ai`, [`files`](files.md) (key `"21"`), [`progress`](progress.md) (key `"22"`) and [`playerSlot`](player-slot.md) (key `"23"`, with its `slot` block, which replaces the manifest's) can be added this way.
- **`screen`, `settings` (the whole list), `panel` and `jobs` replace** the manifest's. `playerPanelTab` and a `panel` with
  `"contributes": true` come together in one block, and so do `schedule` and its `jobs` (each needs the other). Only a
  block brings `jobs`: a top-level `jobs` below apiVersion 14 is never read.
- Then **everything is checked at that apiVersion**, with the very same rules as the plain fields:
  [`screen`](screens.md#manifest), [`jobs`](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs-manifest), [`panel`](player-panel.md#contributed-tab),
  the [capabilities](screens.md#consent).
- **Your `apiVersion` never moves**, so nothing else changes behaviour.
- **Key `"20"` (Kino 0.9.81): `provides` and `consumes`**, the [plugin protocol](protocol.md#versions). They replace the
  manifest's and are checked with apiVersion 20's rules: `"apiVersion": 7, "enhancements": { "20": { "provides": { … } } }`
  opens a door on Kino 0.9.81 and later while the plugin keeps installing as before on every older Kino (that is how TMDB
  1.3.0 and later opens its `movies` door).
- **Key `"20"`: `visualBrowser`** (`true`), the manifest key for [a browser window the person drives](visual-browser.md). It replaces
  the manifest's and is checked with apiVersion 20's rules, so a plugin that keeps an older `apiVersion` offers the window only
  to a Kino that has it: `"enhancements": { "20": { "visualBrowser": true } }`. Check `kino.visualBrowser?.available` before using it.

### When a block is dropped { #dropped }

Your plugin is **never refused** because of an `enhancements` block. The block is dropped (with a log line) and the plugin
runs as its own manifest says when:

- it fails those rules (a bad screen, a capability that cannot be added, any other field);
- its key is at or below your own `apiVersion` (declare each feature once);
- its `settings` change the type of a setting your manifest declares (keep the list a superset of yours: values sync by key
  with devices on an older Kino);
- its `screen.replaces` names Categorías and your own apiVersion lacks them (below 6);
- your script lacks an export the block newly needs (`screen`/`screenEvent`, `job`, or `settingsStatus`/`action` for such
  settings). Kino checks it at install and at every start;
- a job with [`enabledBy`](jobs-and-shared.md#enabled-by) does not name one of your `toggle` settings.

`node sdk/validate.mjs` reports every block Kino would drop as a problem.

### Consent { #consent }

It is a plain manifest's. The red lines of `library`, `playerPanelTab`, `playerControl`, `room`, `schedule` and `ai` are
asked at install and on the update that adds them (shown first and open, [below](#updates)), never approved by Kino on its
own, and unticked in a kit import; `shared` is a plain line.

Their features follow the block: your jobs run, and `kino.shared` and `kino.ai` exist, only on a Kino that read it.
`kino.library` exists on every apiVersion 14 Kino, but until the person approves the line its calls reject with
`permission_denied`: someone who installed your plugin on an older Kino and then updated Kino is asked only with **your
next version**. So `typeof kino.library === "object"` is not enough: catch the refusal and work without it.

On an older Kino none of it exists: keep the work your plugin does without background jobs where it already is.

### A `settings` list in a block { #settings-in-block }

A `settings` list inside a block is read at the block's apiVersion: its English texts (`labelEn`, `hintEn`, `confirmEn`),
`devices`, `linkOnly`, `help`, `link` and `qr` items, `"sync": false` and `unlockWith` all apply on a Kino that read the
block, and are ignored on an older one, which reads your base list. So:

- Keep every key of the base list with its type (else the block is dropped: `settingRetyped`) and its `sync`
  (`"settings" changes "sync" of the setting "<key>"`, also dropped: a value that syncs on one Kino and stays on the device
  on another would differ between the person's devices). A NEW key may say `"sync": false`.
- The two runtime features that depend on what the list may declare follow the list too: a `settingsStatus` answer's
  `hide` and an action's `setSettings` filling a `password` (both from apiVersion 13) are read at the block's apiVersion
  when the block replaced `settings`, and at your own apiVersion otherwise (a block that only adds a screen changes nothing
  for them).
- `setSettings` still fills only a `password` the list in effect declares, still refuses the whole field for an undeclared
  key or another type, never moves an `unlockWith` setting off its default, and the form saves the value as a typed one
  (sealed, never shown back, device-only with `"sync": false`).
- What else reads your own apiVersion stays so on purpose: the sealed `secrets` limit, the cipher key rules, Categorías,
  and every feature outside `settings`.

See also [the settings form](settings-form.md).

## Updates: new consents come first { #updates }

When an update of your plugin adds a red line (one of the capabilities above, `"fetchHosts": "any"`, `browser`,
`tracking`...) or a new host, Kino's update sheet shows it **first and open**, under «Nuevo en esta actualización»:

- By severity: any-host first, then the other capabilities, one grouped line for new insecure hosts, then the new hosts.
- Each line is a D-pad stop on the TV, with a «Hay más abajo» cue.
- What the person already approved stays behind «Ver detalles».

So one tap never approves something unseen. The update waits for the person; a plain line (`shared`) does not hold it back.
On a first install everything stays behind «Ver detalles», as before.

Describe in your release notes why you need the new reach. See also [What people see](what-people-see.md) and
[Publish](publish.md).


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/themes/ (docs/themes.en.md) -->

# App themes (apiVersion 18) { #themes }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.81"
    `appThemes`, `go.useTheme`, `go.setExperience` and `activeTheme` arrive with `"apiVersion": 18`, which
    `contract.json` ties to Kino 0.9.81. Every older Kino refuses an
    apiVersion 18 manifest with «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino», and `appThemes` is not offered
    through [`enhancements`](enhancements.md). Below apiVersion 18 the field is ignored.

A plugin may offer **whole-app looks**: colours, a background, corner radii, type sizes, shadows, motion, player
control sizes and its own logo, and from apiVersion 26 [painted surfaces, a background picture, a font and TV layouts](#level2), for every screen of Kino on the phone and the TV. A theme is **data in the manifest**: no
code runs, no network is used, no capability is needed. The person picks one theme in **Ajustes ▸ Apariencia** (or with a
button on your own screen), may adjust what you allow, and the choice is per profile and syncs between their devices.

This is not the apiVersion 6 [`theme`](section-theme.md#theme) field, which only colours *your* section, Ajustes tab and
player accent. Both may live in the same manifest.

## A theme-only plugin { #theme-only }

```json
{
  "id": "theme-neon",
  "name": "Neón",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 18,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Un tema oscuro con acentos neón",
  "hosts": [],
  "categories": ["themes"],
  "appThemes": [
    {
      "id": "neon",
      "name": { "es": "Neón", "en": "Neon" },
      "colors": { "accent": "#00E5FF", "onAccent": "#000000", "background": "#0A0A14", "surface": "#14142A", "surfaceHigh": "#1E1E3A", "railPanel": "#101026" },
      "background": { "type": "gradient", "colors": ["#0A0A14", "#1A0A2E"], "angle": 180 },
      "shape": { "cardRadius": 14, "channelRadius": 14, "buttonRadius": 24, "chipRadius": 20, "dialogRadius": 20, "inputRadius": 12 },
      "typography": { "scale": 1.1, "titleScale": 1.05, "bodyScale": 1.0 },
      "tv": { "typography": { "scale": 1.0 } },
      "adjustable": {
        "colors.accent": { "swatches": ["#00E5FF", "#7C4DFF", "#FFB300"] },
        "shape.cardRadius": { "min": 0, "max": 20 },
        "typography.scale": { "min": 1.0, "max": 1.3 },
        "background": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`plugin.js` can be empty (`export {};`): Kino loads it and calls nothing. Rules for such a plugin:

- **No capabilities.** A plugin whose only content is `appThemes` may leave `capabilities` out (or add only `screen`, for a
  presentation page: see [Turning a theme on from your screen](#use-theme)).
- **`"hosts": []`** is allowed from apiVersion 18 in a plugin that only ships `appThemes`: it reaches nothing, and its card
  says it doesn't connect to the internet.
- **`"categories": ["themes"]`** lists it under **Temas** in Kino's plugin store. `themes` is one of the nine marketplace
  values (`movies`, `series`, `anime`, `live`, `radio`, `subtitles`, `utilities`, `themes`, `adult`).
- It plays nothing, so it does not open the way past Kino's first source picker.
- No consent line: activating a theme is the person's consent, and a theme grants nothing (no network, no code, no data).
- Any other plugin (a catalog, a live TV plugin) may also carry `appThemes` beside its capabilities.

## The fields of a theme { #fields }

`appThemes` is a list of **1 to 8** themes. Each one:

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Required. `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$`, unique in the plugin. Never change it once published: the person's choice and adjustments hang off it. |
| `name` | Required. `{ "es", "en" }` (one may be missing: it takes the other) or one string for both; at most 40 characters. |
| `colors`, `shape`, `typography`, `elevation`, `motion`, `player` | The token groups below. Every token is optional: what you leave out stays Kino's. |
| `background` | `{ "type": "solid", "colors": [one] }` or `{ "type": "gradient", "colors": [2 to 8], "angle": whole degrees }` (default angle 180). `image` (apiVersion 26): `{ "asset", "fit", "dim" }`, see [a picture behind the app](#image) (an older Kino refuses it). |
| `tv`, `phone` | The same groups and `background`, overriding the theme on that form only. |
| `adjustable` | What the person may change in Ajustes ▸ Apariencia ▸ Personalizar (at most 48 tokens): `true`, `{ "swatches": ["#RRGGBB", …] }` (colours only) or `{ "min", "max" }` (numbers only). |
| `pluginColors` | `"respect"` (default) or `"override"`: what happens to other plugins' own apiVersion 6 `theme` colours. |
| `price` | Optional `{ "kinos": 1 to 1000, "payTo": "<64 lowercase hex>" }`. No `price` is a free theme. See [Priced themes](#price). |
| `experience` | Optional `"light"` or `"full"`: the whole-app experience the theme looks best with. See [The experience](#experience). |
| `logo` | Optional `{ "wordmark"?, "mark"?, "decor"? }` (at least one), vector only. See [Your own logo](#logo). |

**A format error refuses the whole manifest**: an unknown field or token, a wrong type (a number where a colour goes), a bad
`id`, two themes with the same `id`, more than 8 themes, a `name` over 40 characters, a malformed `price`, `experience` or
`logo`. **A value out of its range does not refuse anything**: Kino drops that one token with a warning and keeps its own
value, so the theme still works. `node sdk/validate.mjs .` prints those warnings for the phone and the TV.

## Tokens and ranges { #tokens }

The 47 tokens, with the ranges `contract.json` (`manifest.appThemes`) enforces:

| Group | Token | Type and range | Kino's own value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colors` | `accent` | `#RRGGBB` | `#E50914` |
| `colors` | `onAccent` (text and icons on the accent) | `#RRGGBB` | `#FFFFFF` |
| `colors` | `background` | `#RRGGBB` (or the `background` field) | `#0E0E0E` |
| `colors` | `surface` (cards, panels) | `#RRGGBB` | `#181818` |
| `colors` | `surfaceHigh` (raised panels) | `#RRGGBB` | `#242424` |
| `colors` | `textPrimary`, `textSecondary` | `#RRGGBB` | `#F5F5F5`, `#B3B3B3` |
| `colors` | `focus`, `onFocus` (the TV focus treatment) | `#RRGGBB` | `#FFFFFF`, `#000000` |
| `colors` | `outline`, `railPanel`, `placeholderTop`, `placeholderBottom`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `favorite`, `scrim` | `#RRGGBB` | Kino's |
| `colors` | `border` (the colour of borders, see [Borders](#borders)) | `#RRGGBB` | none: `outline` is used without it |
| `shape` | `cardRadius`, `channelRadius`, `buttonRadius`, `chipRadius`, `dialogRadius`, `inputRadius` | number, 0 to 32 | Kino's |
| `shape` | `dialogBorder`, `menuBorder`, `headerBorder`, `cardBorder`, `panelBorder` (width in dp, see [Borders](#borders)) | number, 0 to 4 | 0: Kino draws no borders |
| `shape` | `heroRadius`, `railItemRadius` (apiVersion 26: corners of the framed hero and the floating rail, see [Painted surfaces](#level2)) | number, 0 to 32 and 0 to 24 | 16 and Kino's |
| `typography` | `scale`, `titleScale`, `bodyScale` | number, 0.85 to 1.3 | 1 |
| `elevation` | `cardShadow`, `dialogShadow` | number, 0 to 1 | Kino's |
| `elevation` | `heroScrim` | number, 0.3 to 1 | Kino's |
| `motion` | `focusZoom` | number, 1 to 1.15 | Kino's |
| `motion` | `crossfadeMs` | number, 0 to 800 | Kino's |
| `motion` | `heroDrift` | `"on"` or `"off"` | Kino's |
| `player` | `buttonScale` | number, 0.8 to 1.4 | 1 |
| `player` | `playButtonScale` | number, 0.8 to 1.6 | 1 |
| `player` | `seekBarScale` | number, 0.8 to 2 | 1 |
| `player` | `labelScale` | number, 0.85 to 1.3 | 1 |
| `player` | `buttonShape` | `"circle"`, `"rounded"` or `"square"` | Kino's |

The token is named by its path: `colors.accent`, `shape.cardRadius`, `player.buttonShape` (that is how `adjustable` names
them). `typography.scale` multiplies the system font scale (the combination is capped). On the phone a player button may
look smaller, but its touch target never goes below 48 dp; on the TV the focused button keeps Kino's focus treatment, only
recoloured with `focus` and `onFocus`.

## How Kino resolves a theme { #resolution }

Lowest to highest priority, per token:

1. Kino's own value.
2. The theme, then its `tv` or `phone` block.
3. The person's adjustments, only on tokens in `adjustable`, clamped to its `min`/`max` (or one of its `swatches`) and to
   the ranges above.
4. **The device.** With reduced effects (Ajustes ▸ Experiencia visual) the `motion` tokens do nothing; whether TV cards
   are rounded at all stays the person's "Esquinas redondeadas" switch (off by default on TV for performance; Apariencia
   offers to turn it on when a theme uses a radius). A theme never decides what a device can draw.

### The legibility guardrails { #guardrails }

The same thresholds as the apiVersion 6 `theme` (`minTextContrast` 4.5, `minUiContrast` 3), read on the **effective**
colours (Kino's where your theme changed only one side). A pair that fails falls back to Kino's values on the side your theme
set, with a warning:

| Pair | Needs | When it fails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The background (every gradient stop) | dark (relative luminance at most 0.05) **or light, when the theme brings its own `textPrimary` and `textSecondary` that read on the background and on `surface`** (Kino 0.9.82; a light background used to be refused always) | Kino's background (and its `accent` if needed) |
| `accent` on the background | 3:1 | Kino's `accent` and `onAccent`, as a pair |
| `onAccent` on `accent` | 4.5:1 | Kino's `accent` and `onAccent`, as a pair |
| Kino's accent on your background | 3:1 | Kino's background |
| `textPrimary` and `textSecondary` on the background and `surface` | 4.5:1 | Kino's text colours |
| `textPrimary` on `surfaceHigh` | 4.5:1 | Kino's `surfaceHigh` (then the text colours) |
| Text on your `surface` | 4.5:1 | Kino's `surface` |
| `focus` on the background; `onFocus` on `focus` | 3:1; 4.5:1 | Kino's `focus` and `onFocus` |

Unlike the apiVersion 6 `theme`, `appThemes` has no "not close to Kino's red" rule. The person's own adjustments go through
the same checks: Apariencia refuses a colour that would not read, in Kino's words.
