### What a theme never restyles { #never }

Kino draws in its own look, whatever theme is active: Ajustes ▸ Apariencia itself, its preview, the purchase and experience
questions, the plugin install and update consent sheets, the 18+ code and setting locks, the `go.url` sheet, the lock screen,
and every other screen that asks the person for a decision. Kino's own logo stays on the splash, the gate and those decision
screens. QR codes stay black on white, and what is drawn over video or artwork keeps its colours.

## `pluginColors` { #plugin-colors }

Other plugins may have their own apiVersion 6 `theme` colours. With `"respect"` (the default) their pages and their player
accent keep them; with `"override"` the active theme's colours win everywhere. The person always has the last word: Apariencia
shows a **Colores de los plugins** switch for every theme, whatever you declared.

## Priced themes (`price`) { #price }

A theme may cost **kinos**, Kino's free coin (the person earns them by watching: 1 every 10 minutes, at most 20 a UTC day).

```json
"price": { "kinos": 50, "payTo": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" }
```

- `kinos` is a whole number from 1 to 1000; `payTo` is **your** coins account: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Both are
  required together; anything else refuses the manifest.
- Before a priced theme turns on (from Apariencia, from your plugin's manage sheet or from your own `go.useTheme`), Kino shows
  its own purchase sheet: «Comprar «name»», «Cuesta N kinos.», the person's balance («Tienes N kinos.»), and **Comprar por N
  kinos**, enabled only when the balance covers it («Te faltan N kinos para comprarlo.» otherwise). A failed purchase charges
  nothing. Apariencia shows the price on the list and on the preview button, and the balance next to priced themes.
- The kinos go to `payTo`. One purchase per theme and account, valid on every device of the person.
- Your plugin never sees the purchase, the balance or the coins session: **you need no `coins` capability to sell a theme.**
  Declare [`coins`](kino-api.md#coins) (apiVersion 16, a red consent line) only if your own screen wants to show the balance
  with `kino.coins.balance()`; when it rejects with `disabled`, show nothing about kinos.
- The price and the account are in your public manifest: they are what Kino charges and pays, not a lock on your files.
- **Your account.** A coins account is the same 64-hex identifier Kino Social calls the author's `user_key`: the coins service
  derives it from the person's Telegram identity with a secret, and never stores the Telegram id. It is the id of the person
  who signed in to Kino with Telegram, so `payTo` must be the account of the person who is paid. From Kino
  0.9.81 you read and copy it in **Ajustes ▸ App ▸ Tu cuenta de kinos** (it needs the Kinos switch on and
  your Telegram sign-in): tap the row to copy the whole 64 characters.
- **Your own theme.** The service refuses a purchase whose buyer and `payTo` are the same account (`self_purchase`): nothing
  is charged. To test the purchase flow, use a second account, or the kit's mocks and a debug build.
- **Refunds.** There are none: a purchase is final, the kinos are already in the author's balance, and the service has no
  refund operation. What a person never pays is a failed purchase: it charges nothing, and buying the same theme twice charges
  once.

## The experience (`experience`, `go.setExperience`) { #experience }

Kino has two whole-app presets in Ajustes ▸ Experiencia visual: **light** (no shadows, no effects, square corners) and
**full** (every effect on, rounded corners).

- A theme that looks best with one says so with `"experience": "light"` or `"full"`. When the person turns the theme on,
  Kino asks («Este tema se ve mejor con la experiencia completa. ¿La usamos también?», with «Usar la completa» and «Dejar la
  actual»). Nothing changes without their yes, and nothing is asked when the app already has it.
- Your own screen may ask too: `go: { setExperience: "light" | "full" }`, only from the person's own press or submit on your
  screen (never `open`, a timer, a change, a load-more, an `onClose`, a panel or a notice). Kino asks first, naming your
  plugin («Tu plugin» pide la experiencia completa. ¿La usamos?). Any other value drops the `go`, logged.

## Your own logo (`logo`) { #logo }

A theme may draw its own logo in place of Kino's in the phone's side menu and header and in the TV's rail. Vector only (no
image file, no network):

```json
"logo": {
  "wordmark": { "size": [120, 30], "paths": [{ "d": "M0 0 L26 15 L0 30 Z", "fill": "accent" },
                                              { "d": "M40 4 H52 V26 H40 Z", "fill": "textPrimary" }] },
  "mark": { "size": [30, 30], "paths": [{ "d": "M15 0 L30 15 L15 30 L0 15 Z", "fill": "accent" }] }
}
```

- At least one of `wordmark` (the long logo: phone menu and header, the TV's open rail) and `mark` (the square one: the TV's
  collapsed rail). What you leave out stays Kino's.
- `size` is `[width, height]`, whole numbers from 1 to 1000, at most 8 times wider than tall (or the reverse).
- 1 to 8 `paths`, each `d` up to 2,000 characters of SVG path data (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`, numbers, spaces, commas, signs);
  `fill` is `accent`, `onAccent`, `textPrimary`, `textSecondary` (they follow the theme and the person's adjustments) or a
  fixed `#RRGGBB`.
- `decor` (Kino 0.9.82) does not replace Kino's logo: it is drawn **over** it, in the wordmark and in the mark, in the space of the "o". It is `{ "paths": [...] }` (1 to 8, the same format). Its centre is the origin (0, 0), y grows downwards, and the ring's outer radius is 100. A hat on the "o" sits at y < -100, something covering the whole "o" is a disc of radius 100, and the dot of the "i" is near (-353, -132). Use it to play with Kino's own logo (Luffy's straw hat, the arc reactor as the "o").
- Kino keeps its own logo on the splash, the gate and every screen that asks for a decision.

## Borders (`colors.border`, `shape.*Border`) { #borders }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.82"
    No new `apiVersion`: an older Kino ignores these tokens and draws no borders.

Kino has no borders. A theme may ask for them, as a width in dp (0 to 4; 0 or absent = none) per kind of element, plus a colour:

| Token | Frames |
| --- | --- |
| `shape.dialogBorder` | dialogs and bottom sheets |
| `shape.menuBorder` | dropdown menus |
| `shape.headerBorder` | headers: a line along their lower edge |
| `shape.cardBorder` | cards |
| `shape.panelBorder` | panels |

The colour is `colors.border`; when the theme gives none, `outline` is used. A border follows the element's corners (`dialogRadius`, `cardRadius`…). A theme that asks for no borders looks exactly as before.

```json
"colors": { "border": "#8624A0" },
"shape": { "dialogBorder": 2, "cardBorder": 1, "headerBorder": 1 }
```

## Painted surfaces, layouts and files (apiVersion 26) { #level2 }

!!! note "Next Kino release, not published yet"
    Everything in this section arrives with `"apiVersion": 26` (Kino 0.9.87, provisional: the number moves if the release does).
    A theme that uses them must declare `"apiVersion": 26`: a Kino that does not know 26 then refuses the whole manifest ("Este
    plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino") instead of misreading it. **Do not** put these keys in a theme that declares a
    lower apiVersion: Kino 0.9.87 skips them there, but an older Kino refuses a theme with an unknown field. With none of these
    keys a theme looks exactly as before, on every Kino.

Level 1 colours, shapes and sizes. Level 2 lets a theme **paint**: a gradient or glossy fill, a gradient outline and a soft glow on
the elements Kino draws, a background **picture**, its own **font**, and two TV **layouts** (a framed hero and a floating
rail). It is still data: no code runs, no network is used at runtime, and the pictures and fonts ship in your plugin's own repository.

### `surfaces`: fill, stroke and glow per element { #surfaces }

`surfaces` is an object whose keys are the elements below; each value is `{ "fill"?, "stroke"?, "glow"? }`. An element you do not
list keeps Kino's own look.

| Element | Where it paints |
| --- | --- |
| `button` | the primary filled button (a dialog's confirm, the hero's "Continuar viendo") |
| `buttonGhost` | the secondary button next to it (Cancel, "…") |
| `navItem`, `navActive` | the top menu's pills and the rail's items, inactive and active (the focused or chosen one) |
| `rail` | the rail's panel: its fill and outline |
| `iconButton` | the round corner buttons (profile, bell, reload) and the plugins button |
| `card`, `cardFocus` | a poster or wide card at rest and focused: stroke and glow (the fill is the picture, so a card has none) |
| `focus` | the focus ring of everything else focusable: a stroke and a glow, never a fill |
| `hero` | the framed hero's card (stroke and glow; its corners are `shape.heroRadius`) |
| `progress` | the filled part of a continue-watching progress bar |

The three value types:

| Value | Shape | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fill` | `{ "type": "solid", "color": "#RRGGBB" }` or `{ "type": "gradient", "colors": ["#RRGGBB", …], "angle": degrees }` (angle default 180) | 2 to 8 colours; a gradient outside that is dropped with a warning |
| `stroke` | `{ "width": dp, "color": "#RRGGBB" }` **or** `{ "width": dp, "gradient": { "type": "gradient", … } }` (exactly one of the two) | width 0 to 4 |
| `glow` | `{ "color": "#RRGGBB", "radius": dp, "alpha": 0 to 1 }`, a blurred halo behind the element | radius 0 to 24 |

```json
"surfaces": {
  "button":     { "fill": { "type": "gradient", "colors": ["#D9232F", "#A8060F"], "angle": 180 }, "stroke": { "width": 1, "color": "#FF7B83" } },
  "navActive":  { "fill": { "type": "solid", "color": "#2A0D12" }, "stroke": { "width": 1.5, "color": "#E50914" }, "glow": { "color": "#E50914", "radius": 10, "alpha": 0.55 } },
  "cardFocus":  { "stroke": { "width": 2, "color": "#F2E8EA" }, "glow": { "color": "#E50914", "radius": 14, "alpha": 0.45 } },
  "card":       { "glow": { "color": "#E50914", "radius": 10, "alpha": 0.22 } }
}
```

A theme's `tv` and `phone` blocks may carry their own `surfaces`; the block wins over the theme on that form only. The phone paints
`button`, `buttonGhost`, `iconButton`, `card` and `progress`; the rail, the top menu and the framed hero exist on the TV only.

### `style.gloss`: a glossy look from one number { #gloss }

`"style": { "gloss": 0 to 1 }`. An element with **no explicit `fill`** gets a lighter-top to darker-bottom gradient derived from its
base colour (the accent for `button` and `navActive`, `surfaceHigh` for `iconButton` and `buttonGhost`), and `button`, `navActive` and
`cardFocus` get a glow derived from the accent. Anything you write explicitly wins over the derived value. `0` or absent = Kino's flat
look. A value outside 0 to 1 is clamped with a warning.

### `layout`: a framed hero and a floating rail (TV) { #layout }

`"layout": { "hero": "fullBleed" | "framed", "rail": "strip" | "floating" }`, both optional; `tv` and `phone` blocks may carry it.

- `"hero": "framed"` draws the Home's hero as an inset rounded card (with `surfaces.hero`) instead of a picture bleeding to the
  screen's edges. Its corners are `shape.heroRadius` (0 to 32, default 16).
- `"rail": "floating"` keeps the TV's left rail as a rounded panel at all times (with `surfaces.rail`), closed or open, with equal
  air on both sides; its items take `shape.railItemRadius` (0 to 24).
- **TV only.** The phone ignores both keys and keeps its own layout. An unknown word refuses the manifest; the device's switches below
  turn each layout off.

### `assets` and `background.image`: a picture behind the app { #image }

A theme lists the files it ships in `assets`, each `{ "id", "path", "sha256", "bytes" }`: `id` `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$`, `path` a
relative path inside your plugin's repository, `sha256` 64 hexadecimal characters, `bytes` the exact size. At most **16** files.

```json
"assets": [ { "id": "background", "path": "assets/background.webp", "sha256": "0ed54aa7…", "bytes": 8276 } ],
"background": { "image": { "asset": "background", "fit": "cover", "dim": 0.35 } }
```

- `background.image` is `{ "asset": id, "fit": "cover" | "top", "dim": 0.3 to 1 }`: `cover` fills the page and is centred, `top`
  anchors it to the top edge, and `dim` is how much black goes over it. `colors.background` stays **required** as the fallback
  (while the picture loads, when it fails, and for the contrast checks). A `tv` or `phone` block may name a different picture.
- Kino fetches each asset **at install** from the same address your manifest came from (never from a new host), checks the size and
  the sha256, and keeps the files with the plugin: an update replaces them, removing the plugin removes them. A picture is at most
  **2,000,000 bytes** and 3,840 x 2,160 pixels, a font at most **1,000,000**, all the files together **6,000,000**.
- A file that is missing, fails its hash, is over a cap or cannot be decoded is **left out**, with a note in the log: the plugin
  and the rest of the theme still install, and the page shows the fallback colour (or Kino's font). It never refuses the install.
- The text contrast is checked against the fallback colour **darkened by `dim`**; the picture itself is trusted beyond that, so test
  it in Kino. Pictures are decoded once, at the window's size, off the main thread.

An asset can be installed from a repository address (GitHub, a manifest URL); a plugin imported from a `.kinoplugin` file or
packaged by hand does not carry its theme files yet.

### `typography.fontFamily`: your own font { #font }

`"typography": { "fontFamily": { "regular": "<asset id>", "bold": "<asset id>" } }`: `bold` is optional, and both name entries of
`assets` (a TTF or OTF file of at most 1,000,000 bytes). Every text Kino draws with its own scale takes the family, and the scales
(`scale`, `titleScale`, `bodyScale`) keep working on top. A font that is missing or that Android cannot read leaves Kino's font.

### The two new shape tokens { #new-shapes }

`shape.heroRadius` (0 to 32) and `shape.railItemRadius` (0 to 24) join the table in [Tokens and ranges](#tokens). Below apiVersion 26
they are skipped without a word.

### Guardrails for what you paint { #level2-guardrails }

Every rule drops **that value** with a warning (`node sdk/validate.mjs .` prints it, and so does Kino's log); it never refuses the
manifest, so a theme with one bad number stays usable:

- **Text must stay readable on a fill.** The text colour Kino puts on a fill (`onAccent` on `button` and `navActive`, the page's text
  elsewhere) must keep 4.5 : 1 against **every stop** of a gradient. A fill that fails is dropped: "surfaces.navActive.fill: the text on
  it isn't readable on every stop (at least 4.5:1); dropped".
- **Focus is never invisible.** A `focus` or `cardFocus` stroke too close to the page colour is dropped and Kino keeps its own ring.
  `focus` has a stroke and a glow, never a fill (a `fill` there is dropped with a warning).
- Colour count, angle, width, radius, alpha and `dim` are held to the ranges above (clamped or dropped, with a warning).
- With `background.image`, `dim` is at least 0.3.

### The person's switches { #switches }

The device always wins over a theme. In **Ajustes ▸ Experiencia visual ▸ Personalizar uno por uno** (also reachable from the
**Rendimiento** tile of the plugins panel on the TV) the person can turn each of seven effects off on its own, keeping your colours,
shapes and type: glows, gradient fills, gradient outlines, the background picture, the framed hero, the floating rail and the theme
font. They are per device. On a weak TV, "all effects off" turns all seven off. So design every effect as an **addition**: a theme
with the seven off must still look right.

### A complete example { #crimson }

[`kinotvapp/kino-plugin-theme-crimson`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-theme-crimson) is a small, unsigned theme using every
key of this section: gloss and gradient buttons, a dark pill with a red ring for the active menu, a soft glow on the cards, a
framed hero, a floating rail and a background picture. Install it from Plugins ▸ Agregar with `kinotvapp/kino-plugin-theme-crimson`.

## Turning a theme on from your screen (`go.useTheme`, `activeTheme`) { #use-theme }

The person activates a theme in **Ajustes ▸ Apariencia** (Tema de Kino is always the first option; a preview shows a Home
row, a dialog and the player controls before **Usar este tema**), from your plugin's manage sheet («Ver temas», «Activar tema
de …»), or from a button on **your own [screen](screens.md)** (the `screen` capability, apiVersion 14+, which a theme plugin
may declare to present its theme):

```js
export async function screen({ activeTheme }) {
  const on = activeTheme === "neon";
  return { type: "ElevatedButton", labelText: on ? "Desactivar" : "Activar", labelTextEn: on ? "Turn off" : "Turn on",
    onPressed: { go: { useTheme: { theme: on ? null : "neon" } } } };
}
export async function screenEvent() { return null; }
```

- `screen` and `screenEvent` receive **`activeTheme`**: the id of your theme active now, else `null`. Kino calls `screen`
  again after any change (one made in Apariencia too), so one button can flip.
- `go: { useTheme: { theme } }`: `theme` is one of your `appThemes` ids (it does what Apariencia's button does: the same
  per-profile choice, the same sync, the person's adjustments kept) or `null` (back to Kino's theme, only while one of yours
  is active: you can never reset another plugin's).
- Only from the person's own press or submit on your screen: dropped, logged, from `open`, a timer, a change, a load-more, a
  pop-up's `onClose`, a panel or a notice, and below apiVersion 18. Refused, logged, with nothing changed, when Apariencia
  does not list that theme as yours (another plugin's id, your plugin off in this profile, 18+ while locked).
- A priced theme the person has not bought opens Kino's purchase sheet first; a theme with `experience` asks about it.
- Kino shows its own toast, «Tema aplicado» or «Volviste al tema de Kino», and repaints the whole app, your screen included.
- A presentation screen that needs no menu icon can open from your settings page only:
  `"screen": { "label": "Neón", "opensFrom": ["settings"], "settingsButton": { "label": "Ver presentación", "labelEn": "See presentation" } }`.

## The person's side { #person }

- One theme is active at a time, per profile; the choice and the adjustments sync between the person's linked devices, both
  ways.
- **Personalizar** lists only what you marked `adjustable` (swatches and a written `#RRGGBB` for colours: swatches are what
  work with a remote; a stepper for numbers), plus «Volver a los valores del tema».
- Disabling or removing your plugin returns to Kino's theme; the choice is kept and comes back on reinstall. An update
  re-resolves the theme, and adjustments to tokens no longer `adjustable` are dropped.
- Any failure resolving a theme gives Kino's own look, never a crash.

## Test it with the kit { #kit }

```
node sdk/validate.mjs .                                                   # format, plus each theme's warnings on phone and TV
node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"activeTheme":"neon"}' . screen              # your presentation screen with your theme on
node sdk/run.mjs . screenEvent activate --trigger tap                     # what Kino does with go.useTheme / go.setExperience
```

`validate.mjs` prints lines such as `appThemes neon (tv): shape.cardRadius: 40.0 is outside 0.0..32.0; Kino's is used` and
`appThemes neon (phone): background: is too light (the background must be dark for now); Kino's is used`: the app's own
warnings, word for word. `screen` prints the tree with any malformed `go` dropped, and `screenEvent` says when a `go.useTheme` in an answer would be dropped (not a tap, not one of your ids, `null` with
none of yours active). The kit draws no colours: look at the theme in Kino (Ajustes ▸ Apariencia ▸ the preview).

## Checklist { #checklist }

- [ ] `"apiVersion": 18` and the person knows it needs Kino 0.9.81 or later.
- [ ] `node sdk/validate.mjs .` passes and prints no warning you did not expect, for phone and TV.
- [ ] Every theme `id` is final; `name` has `es` and `en`.
- [ ] The background is dark, or light with your own readable text, and every pair in [the guardrails](#guardrails) reads.
- [ ] `adjustable` offers swatches (not only free colours) so a TV remote can use it.
- [ ] A `price` has your real `payTo`; you did not add `coins` just to sell.
- [ ] A screen that turns the theme on reads `activeTheme` and uses `go.useTheme` only from a tap.
- [ ] Level 2 keys (`surfaces`, `style`, `layout`, `assets`, `background.image`, `typography.fontFamily`) only in a theme that declares `"apiVersion": 26`; every asset's `sha256` and `bytes` match the file, and the picture is at most 2 MB.
- [ ] The theme looks right with the seven effects off (Ajustes ▸ Experiencia visual): colours and shapes carry it, effects only add.
- [ ] `"categories": ["themes"]`, and `"hosts": []` when the plugin only ships themes.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/theme-creator/ (docs/theme-creator.en.md) -->

# Theme creator { #theme-creator }

Build an [app theme](themes.md) while you watch it take shape, with an AI assistant that also **draws its logo in SVG** (the
theme's icon). On the left is Kino (Home, the side menu, search and a dialog) with sample data and, below it, the logo as the app
would show it; on the right, the theme's values; below, the code as it gets written. It starts from Kino's own theme: every value
you move changes the view at once, and whatever Kino would drop (for contrast or range) is dropped here too and explained
underneath, in the kit's own words.

Press the three-line menu to open the side menu and **Home** to go back to Home. With **TV** you see the side rail and the focus.
You can also type or paste the JSON below: the controls follow what you write.

<div id="kino-theme-creator" data-lang="en" data-gh-proxy="https://kino-theme-creator-oauth.kinotv.workers.dev"><noscript>The creator needs JavaScript.</noscript></div>

## The logo and the AI assistant { #logo-ai }

A theme's logo ([`logo`](themes.md#logo)) is **vectors only**: a `wordmark` (the long logo of the menu and the header), a `mark`
(the square in the TV rail) and a `decor` drawn over the "o" of Kino's own logo. The creator really draws them: in the phone's
header and menu, in the TV rail, and in the **Your logo in the app** strip under the preview.

Ask the assistant in your own words ("a neon lightning icon", "a wave mark for my blue theme") and it writes the paths. While it
works you see **which step it is on**: preparing the request, asking the AI, reading the answer, checking the values and updating
the preview. Every value it proposes is checked against the contract's rules before it is applied: 1 to 8 paths of up to 2,000
characters each, only SVG path commands (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`), a canvas of at most 1,000 × 1,000 and at most 8 times wider than
tall, and a fill of `accent`, `onAccent`, `textPrimary`, `textSecondary` or a `#RRGGBB`. Anything that does not fit is not applied
and the reason is shown underneath.

The logo can also come in the JSON you paste, and it is included in the code and in the `kino-plugin.json` you download. In the
**Logo and icon** section on the right you can see each piece's size and path count and remove them one by one.

## Publishing the plugin from the creator { #github }

The **Publish to GitHub** panel uploads `kino-plugin.json`, `plugin.js` (with `export {};`) and a `.gitignore` to a repository of
**yours that already exists**, without leaving this page. It also writes the repository's description and, if you leave the box
ticked, adds the **`kino-plugin`** topic: the only way Kino discovers a plugin, and it must be a public, non-fork repository
([Publishing your plugin](publish.md#appear-in-the-app)). The description you type in the panel is also the text of your plugin's card in Kino (up to 300 characters), and your GitHub username becomes the author. When it finishes it tells you the `owner/repo` to type in Kino.

It does not create repositories or ask you to sign in with your account. You set it up once:

1. On GitHub, create an empty **public** repository, with no README.
2. At `github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens` create a **fine-grained** token. Under *Repository access* pick *Only select
   repositories* and tick just that repository. Under permissions set **Contents: Read and write** and **Administration: Read and
   write** (the latter is for the topic and the description).
3. Type the repository in the panel and paste the token.

The token only reaches that repository: if it leaked, nothing else in your account is exposed. It is kept in that tab, wiped when you
close it (or with **Forget the token**), and the browser sends it only to `api.github.com`: it does not pass through any server of
this site or of a third party. If you would rather not use a token, download `kino-plugin.json` and upload it yourself.

**Sign in with GitHub** (optional) saves you creating the token: the page shows a code, you type it at
`https://github.com/login/device` and approve. It is more convenient but **less strict**: the scope is `public_repo`, which reaches all
your public repositories, and the token **passes through a Kino proxy** (a Cloudflare Worker, code in
[`github-oauth-worker/`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugins/tree/main/github-oauth-worker)) that stores and logs nothing,
does not forward the refresh token and only answers this page. If you would rather nothing passes through it, use the
one-repository token.

## Using the result { #use }

1. Download `kino-plugin.json` (or copy the code) and put it in a new GitHub repository, with a `plugin.js` that only says
   `export {};`, or let the **Publish to GitHub** panel do it for you. A plugin that only ships themes needs no capabilities and no
   hosts: [A plugin that only brings themes](themes.md#theme-only).
2. Give the repository the `kino-plugin` topic and [publish it](publish.md).
3. Validate with `node sdk/validate.mjs .` (the [kit](test-locally.md)): it prints the same warnings you see here.

The preview is an approximation of Kino made with HTML and CSS: it is good for choosing colors, shapes and borders, but the app has
the last word. The **Player** values are kept in the theme even though the preview only shows a small bar. The price (`price`), the
experience (`experience`) and the person's adjustments (`adjustable`) are written by hand in the code: see
[App themes](themes.md).


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/section-theme/ (docs/section-theme.en.md) -->

# Your own section, categories and colors (apiVersion 6)

Three optional widenings, all from `"apiVersion": 6` (Kino 0.9.50). None of them needs a capability of
its own. A complete example of the three is `plugins/sdk/test/section-demo` in Kino's repository (its
`highlight` fails on purpose so you can see the fallback).

## A section of your own { #section }

Declare `"section": { "label": "Demo" }` (1 to 20 characters) and export `section({ tab })`:

```js
export async function section({ tab }) {   // tab is null the first time
  const tabs = [{ id: "pelis", label: "Películas" }, { id: "series", label: "Series" }];
  const chosen = tabs.some((t) => t.id === tab) ? tab : "pelis";
  return {
    tabs,                                    // optional, at most 8, labels at most 24 characters
    tab: chosen,                             // the tab this answer is for
    hero: { title: "Destacado", text: "…" }, // optional; also image (http or https); text at most 300 characters
    rows: [{ id: `${chosen}-a`, title: "Destacadas", ref: `${chosen}-a`, items: [/* KinoItem */] }],
  };
}
```

- `rows` are exactly the rows of `home` (same shape, same checks and limits); a row with a `ref` gets
  "Ver más", which calls `browse(ref, null)`. Return `rows: []` for an empty tab: Kino says there is
  nothing there.
- Choosing a tab calls `section({ tab })` again with that tab's `id`. 20 s per call.
- Where it shows: on the **TV**, an entry in the sidebar after "Categorías" (at most 3 plugins have
  one); on the **phone**, a chip in the strip at the top of Inicio (scrollable, at most 8). Only plugins
  that are enabled, usable and need no setup appear: one that is off, or still asks for a required
  setting, gets no entry. Entries are ordered by label, then by plugin id. A call that fails shows an
  error inside the section and never touches the rest of the app.
- A manifest that declares `section` must export it: the install fails otherwise, like any other
  required export.
- `adult: true` entries follow the [18+ lock](contract.md#adult), and a `userMessage` on `not_found`,
  `unavailable` or `rate_limited` is shown in the section ([your own sentence](contract.md#user-message)).

## Your own categories { #categories }

Export `categories()` (needs the `browse` capability; no manifest field, Kino sees the export):

```js
export async function categories() {
  return [{ id: "accion", title: "Acción", ref: "accion", art: "https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500/x.jpg" }];
}
```

- At most 24 tiles, shown in your order; `title` at most 40 characters, `ref` at most 4,096, `art` an
  image URL (the Images rule of the [contract](contract.md#validation): `http` or `https`, not checked
  against `hosts`).
- They appear in Categorías as one group named after your plugin, and each tile opens
  `browse(ref, null)`, paged like any `browse`.
- If `categories()` fails or times out you simply contribute no group. 20 s per call.
- A tile with `adult: true` is shown only while the person's 18+ code is unlocked on that device, like
  any [18+ entry](contract.md#adult); a group left with only such tiles is not shown.
- A tile's "Ver más" page has a search field; with [`scopedSearch`](contract.md#scoped-search) you
  answer it yourself.

## Your colors (`theme`) { #theme }

!!! tip "Restyling the whole app"
    `theme` colours only your own pages. To offer a look for the **whole app** (every screen, the player, the logo), see
    [App themes](themes.md) (`appThemes`, apiVersion 18).

`"theme"` takes up to five colors, each `#RRGGBB`, each optional:

```json
"theme": { "accent": "#3D5AFE", "onAccent": "#FFFFFF", "background": "#101820", "surface": "#1A2733", "highlight": "#F7C948" }
```

| Token | What it paints |
| --- | --- |
| `accent` | in your section and your Ajustes tab: selected chip and tab, buttons, focus, the "Ver más" arrow; in the player: the progress bar, the slider, active states and the TV focus border |
| `onAccent` | text and icons drawn on top of `accent` |
| `background` | the screen behind your section and your Ajustes tab |
| `surface` | in your section: the cards, the "Ver más" card and the tabs that are not selected |
| `highlight` | emphasized text there; in Categorías, the title of your group |

Scope: your section, your Ajustes tab, the title of your group in Categorías (only that title, in
`highlight`; its tiles and background stay Kino's) and, while your content plays, the player's `accent`
and `onAccent` only (the player keeps Kino's background and surfaces). Nothing else in Kino changes, and
**errors are always shown in Kino's red**, whatever your theme says.

Kino protects readability, so each color is checked when it is used:

- `background` must be dark (relative luminance at most 0.05).
- `surface` must be dark (at most 0.12) and at least 1.05:1 apart from the background.
- `accent` must reach 3:1 against the background.
- `onAccent` must reach 4.5:1 against `accent`.
- `highlight` must reach 4.5:1 against the background.
- No color may be close to Kino's red `#E50914` (CIE76 distance below 25).

Kino's own colors (the fallbacks) are `accent` `#E50914`, `onAccent` `#FFFFFF`, `background`
`#0E0E0E`, `surface` `#181818` and `highlight` `#F5F5F5`. A color that fails falls back to Kino's own for that token only (`accent` and `onAccent` are judged and
fall back **as a pair**); the install still succeeds and the other colors stay. A color that is not a
valid `#RRGGBB` is refused at install time. Preview it, with the ratios and the warnings Kino would
print, before publishing:

```
node sdk/run.mjs . theme
node sdk/run.mjs . section [tab]
node sdk/run.mjs . categories
```

`sdk/validate.mjs` shows the same warnings.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/categories/ (docs/categories.en.md) -->

# Home categories { #home-categories }

Kino can show a **Home by categories**, in the style of streaming apps: a single list of rows by
category (Action, Comedy, Anime, Kids...), with **one card per title**. It is optional and off by default: the person turns it on in Ajustes ▸ App ▸ "Home por categorías (experimento)" ("Home by categories (experiment)" in English).
It is built **only from what your Home rows already left cached** (it does not search on its own or call your plugin), so
what you declare in `home()` decides where your content lands. This page explains how to declare it. Items and rows are
in [the contract](contract.md).

!!! note "Any category on a Home row"
    A Home row's `genre` used to accept only ten closed ids. Now it accepts **any category**
    (below). Earlier versions keep ignoring a value that was not in the list of ten.

## What the Home does with your categories { #how }

- **Rows by category, all in one list.** The Home no longer has type tabs: it is a single list of rows, one per
  category, with everything mixed (movies, series, anime...). Each row shows at most 30 titles.
- **Genre rows, merged across types.** Kino groups video titles by each item's `genres` (`["Drama", "Suspenso"]` puts
  the title in the Drama and Suspenso rows) and by the row's `genre` when it is a genre id (`accion`) or a new
  category. One "Acción" row holds every video title with that genre, whether movie, series or anime.
- **Thematic type rows, complete.** When a title's type is `anime`, `doramas`, `infantil`, `documentales`, `clasicos`,
  `deportes` or `noticias`, the title is also in that type's row ("Anime", "Infantil"...), which holds **every** title
  of that type, with a genre or without (they may repeat in their genre rows). The type comes from the row's `genre`
  when it is a type id (`anime`); otherwise from the item's `kind` (`movie`, `series`, `music`, `podcast`). With no
  `genre`, Kino reads the row title: one that names a known genre ("Terror", "Comedia") gives that genre, and the guess
  is skipped when the row already names a known genre; only `anime`, `infantil`, `documentales`, `deportes`,
  `noticias` and `musica` can be guessed as a type. A title's type is decided by the first row it appears in.
- **Generic types, only the leftovers.** `peliculas`, `series`, `entretenimiento` and `otros` get a row only for the
  titles with **no genre at all** (and no thematic type), named after the type ("Películas", "Series"...). A title
  with a genre appears in its genre rows and not in this one. The old single "Más títulos" ("More titles") row is gone.
- **One title, one card.** When several sources have the same title, one card is shown. Identity is, in this order: the
  **TMDB id** (movie and series kept apart), else the **normalised title plus year**, else just the title. Movies and series are kept apart even without a TMDB id. Then Kino joins copies of the same title (and the same kind, movie or series) when there is no doubt: a copy without ids joins the only one with a TMDB id when the years match or one of them has no year, and a year-less copy joins the only dated one. With two TMDB ids or two different years for that title, the copies without ids stay apart: Kino never guesses. Tapping a video
  card makes Kino search that title across every source that has it; an audio card plays that plugin's own item directly.
- **Nothing empty:** a category with no titles is never shown.
- **Fixed order:** rows always come in the [order below](#order); Kino does not change it per plugin and it cannot be customized yet.
- **18+:** `adult: true` content stays hidden while the person's 18+ code is locked.
- **Audio apart:** music and podcasts go in their own rows, at the end of the list and with square covers: the row of
  each audio genre the item has (`pop`, `rock`...) or, with none, the row of its audio type (`radio`, `podcasts`,
  `audiolibros`, `conciertos`, `musica`). Audio and video never share a row. Those rows are for audio items that are
  **not** live (`music`, `podcast`).
- **Live is not in it:** live channels (`kind: "live"`), **radio stations included**, stay in "En vivo" and this Home does
  not paint them. So a station never reaches the `radio` row.
- A **"Fuentes"** link opens the sources (your plugins).

## Group your content in these categories { #prefer }

!!! tip "Rule"
    Preferably group your content in the categories in the tables below: set `genre` on each `home()` row and `genres` on
    each item using ids from that list, and **invent a new category only when nothing fits**.

That way your content lands in the right place and sits together with other plugins' instead of in a lone row.

## Vocabulary { #vocabulary }

The **id** is what you write. Kino shows the Spanish name (or the English one if the person uses Kino in English). The
"Also understood" column holds aliases Kino maps to the id; case, accents and punctuation do not matter, and the names
shown on screen work too (note: English "Sports" is the name of both `deportes` and `deportivo`, and maps to `deportes`).

## Row order { #order }

The order is fixed and set by Kino, not by your plugin. A category with no titles is not shown, and the order cannot
be customized yet. From top to bottom:

1. The video rows of this list (genres and thematic types interleaved):

1. `accion`
2. `comedia`
3. `drama`
4. `terror`
5. `suspenso`
6. `ciencia-ficcion`
7. `animacion`
8. `anime`
9. `aventura`
10. `romance`
11. `doramas`
12. `crimen`
13. `fantasia`
14. `infantil`
15. `familia`
16. `misterio`
17. `documentales`
18. `belica`
19. `historia`
20. `biografia`
21. `musical`
22. `western`
23. `reality`
24. `deportivo`
25. `deportes`
26. `noticias`
27. `clasicos`
28. `shonen`
29. `isekai`
30. `mecha`
31. `escolar`
32. `slice-of-life`

2. Unknown categories (those not in the tables), in the order they arrived.
3. The generic type rows, holding only the titles with no genre: `peliculas`, `series`, `entretenimiento`, `otros`.
4. Audio, at the end and with square covers: first the audio type rows (`radio`, `podcasts`, `audiolibros`,
   `conciertos`, `musica`), then the audio genre rows (`pop`, `rock`, `urbano`, `tropical`, `electronica`,
   `clasica`, `jazz`, `regional`, `religiosa`).

## Declaring it in your plugin { #declare }

`genre` goes on the **row** `home()` returns; `genres` goes on each **item** (up to 5 free-text names, each at most 30
characters; see [the contract](contract.md)). For a title to merge well with other sources' copies, also send `ids`
(with the TMDB id if you have it) and `year`.

```js
export async function home() {
  const movies = await getMovies();   // your code
  return [
    {
      id: "peliculas",
      title: "Películas recientes",
      genre: "peliculas",              // the type
      items: movies.map((m) => ({
        id: String(m.id),
        ref: String(m.id),
        kind: "movie",
        title: m.title,
        year: m.year ? String(m.year) : undefined,  // helps merge the same title across sources
        ids: { tmdb: m.tmdbId },
        poster: m.poster,
        genres: m.genres,              // e.g. ["Drama", "Suspenso"]: its genre rows
      })),
    },
  ];
}
```

`genres` only places titles into genre rows: a type id there (`genres: ["Anime"]`) is ignored; the type goes on the row's `genre` (or comes from the `kind`). Both `genre` and `genres` accept the table ids **or** names and aliases (`"Action"`, `"Acción"`, `"Thriller"`,
`"Sci-Fi & Fantasy"`): Kino maps them to the id. Your genres can come straight from the source.

## What happens to an unknown category { #unknown }

A row's `genre` is no longer limited to the old ten ids. Kino **canonicalises** it:

1. If it is a known id or alias (Spanish or English), it goes to the table's id.
2. Otherwise it is kept as a **slug**: lowercase ASCII `[a-z0-9-]`, at most 40 characters.

A category that is not in the tables is a **genre row** (not a new type): every item of that row goes into it, the type comes from each item's `kind`, and the row is **appended after the known ones** (before the generic type rows and the audio), in the order it arrived, shown with your plugin's own text. It helps when nothing really fits. Rows are grouped by slug, not by plugin: it merges with another plugin's row only when the spelling matches, so use it sparingly.

**Live categories** and **playlists** keep the closed ten-id vocabulary; see [Live channels](live-channels.md).

## Tips so titles merge { #dedupe }

- Send `ids` (especially the TMDB one, `ids: { tmdb: 603 }`) and `year` on every item. A copy with TMDB and one without never merge, so always send `ids.tmdb`; without TMDB, title plus year merges best.
- Keep the title identical across rows and sources; do not append "(HD)", the year or the language.
- Declare `genres` on every item: without them a title of a generic type appears only in its type row ("Películas", "Series"...), not in the genre rows.
- Mark 18+ content `adult: true`: it stays hidden while the code is locked.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/player-panel/ (docs/player-panel.en.md) -->

# The player panel (apiVersion 9)

From **Kino 0.9.55** your plugin can open **its own panel from the player**: a surface you describe in JavaScript
for what is playing right now (movie, episode, copy, position), with text, images, buttons and inputs, whose
values are kept per video or for your whole plugin and synced across the person's devices. The same panel can
**drive the player** (seek, speed, picture size, markers, an end-of-episode countdown) and, with `playerEvent`,
you can learn what happens during playback. All of it needs `"apiVersion": 9`; below that, or on Kino 0.9.54 and
older (which refuse a manifest with `"apiVersion": 9`), none of it exists. Your plugin **must not depend on it
to play**.

A complete example with every element, both tabs and every action is [`sdk/test/panel-demo`](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk/tree/main/sdk/test/panel-demo) in the
kit's repository; there is [a small one](#example) below.

From `"apiVersion": 14` (Kino 0.9.74) the panel can also be built with the screen kit, a tab can live in another plugin's
panel or on a live channel, and the person can pin it next to the video: see
[The panel built with the screen kit](#screen-kit).

From `"apiVersion": 23` (the next Kino release) a plugin can also keep up to three small elements in the top-right corner of
the TV player, and a button there can open this panel (`openPanel`): see [The player slot](player-slot.md).

!!! note "What is not in this version"
    `ai` (Kino's AI) and `chat` do not ship in Kino 0.9.55; they come in a later version. If your panel includes
    an `ai` or `chat` element, Kino drops it and writes "needs a newer Kino" to the log. There is no `kino.socket`
    either.

## Where it appears { #where }

- A button with the name and icon from your manifest, **next to the subtitles one** ("Audio y subtítulos"), only
  **while a title from that plugin plays**. On the phone it sits in the icon row at the bottom, beside the
  subtitles one (if the row does not fit it scrolls, and the panel button is among the first); on the TV, right
  after the subtitles button, reachable with the remote's D-pad.
- It does not appear if the plugin is off or damaged, if its `apiVersion` is below 9, if the manifest does not
  declare `panel`, or if the plugin does not export `panel`. On the TV, a plugin's live channel has no on-screen
  buttons, so it has no panel; channels in the En vivo tab do not either (on the phone, a plugin's live channel does
  have it).
- **The video never pauses** while the panel is open. Back, or the X, closes it; it also closes when the app goes
  to the background and when the app's language changes.
- While the panel loads the person sees "Cargando el panel…". If the first call fails they see the message and
  "Reintentar" / "Cerrar"; if a panel was already showing, the error appears as a red line and the panel stays.

## The manifest: `panel` { #manifest }

```json
"apiVersion": 9,
"panel": { "label": "Opciones", "labelEn": "Options", "icon": "tune" }
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | 1 to 24 characters: the button's name. |
| `labelEn` | Optional, 1 to 24: the name when the app is in English (`label` is used when it is missing). |
| `icon` | Optional: one of Kino's 16 icons: `info`, `tune` (the default), `settings`, `star`, `bolt`, `language`, `subtitles`, `list`, `magic`, `heart`, `movie`, `tv`, `sports`, `music`, `bookmark`, `help`. An unknown name draws `tune` (and `validate.mjs` warns you). |
| `iconFile` | Optional: your own icon, a file in your plugin's repository next to the manifest (relative path, `.png`). A **PNG of exactly 96×96 px, with an alpha channel, at most 24 KB**. Kino draws **only its alpha** and tints it with the button's colour (focused or not), so a full-colour image shows as its silhouette. Kino downloads it on install and on update; if it does not qualify the install fails with "The panel icon must be a 96×96 px PNG with a transparent background, at most 24 KB". If it later fails to load, the button draws `tune`. |

`icon` and `iconFile` do not go together (the manifest is refused). Declaring `panel` requires exporting `panel`;
`panelAction` and `playerEvent` are optional (an action without `panelAction` shows the plugin's error in the
panel). An empty `label`, one over 24, a `panel` that is not an object, or an `iconFile` that is not a relative
path to a `.png` are refused at install. Below apiVersion 9 the field is ignored. See also
[the manifest](manifest.md#panel).

## `panel(context)`: what you receive { #context }

```js
export async function panel(context) { /* returns a Panel */ }
```

Kino calls it when the panel opens, when a tab is pressed (with `context.tab`) and every `refreshMs`. The context
carries **exactly** these keys (an optional field Kino does not know is left out):

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"movie"`, `"episode"` or `"live"`. |
| `ref` | the `ref` of the title playing, exactly as you gave it. |
| `title`, `year?` | the title and the year. |
| `season?`, `episode?`, `episodeTitle?` | only for an episode. |
| `ids` | the ids Kino knows for the title: `tmdb`, `imdb`, `mal`, `anilist` (`tvdb` and `kitsu` exist in the type, but Kino does not send them today). |
| `playing` | the copy playing: today Kino fills only `label` (the name the person sees in "Servidor"); `lang`, `quality` and `server` exist in the type and are not sent. |
| `positionMs`, `durationMs?`, `paused` | the position; the duration (absent for live or while the player does not know it); whether it is paused. |
| `seekStepMs` | the back/forward step in effect (10,000 by default). |
| `stats` | read-only stats, only what the player knows: `width`, `height`, `videoCodec`, `audioCodec`, `bitrateKbps`, `bufferedMs`, `droppedFrames`, `network` (`wifi`, `ethernet`, `cellular` or `other`), `stallsThisSession`. |
| `device` | `"tv"` or `"phone"`. |
| `lang` | the app's language, `"es-CO"` or `"en-US"`. Use it for your own texts. |
| `tab?` | the tab the person asked for (absent the first time). |
| `values` | what the person (or you) saved: `{ video: {…}, plugin: {…} }`. |
| `player` | the player's properties in effect: `seekStepMs`, `speed?`, `resize?` (`"fit"` if nobody changed it) and your `autoNext?` if you set one. |
| `features?` | **Kino 0.9.64, additive**: what this Kino draws beyond apiVersion 9's panel; `"loading"` means it understands the `loading` element. Absent on an older Kino, which drops it as an unknown type: check it before you answer with one. |

The context carries nothing about other plugins or the person's account.

## `Panel`: what you return { #panel }

```js
return {
  presentation: "panel",       // "modal" (default) or "panel"
  title: context.title,        // up to 60 characters (also titleEn)
  accent: "#2E7D32",           // optional, #RRGGBB
  refreshMs: 10000,            // optional, 2000 to 60000
  tabs: [{ id: "info", label: "Info" }],   // optional
  tab: "info",
  elements: [ /* elements */ ],             // at most 40 at the top level
};
```

- **`presentation`**: accepted for compatibility and no longer read: every panel draws the same way, as a
  **drawer** over the whole player (from the right on the TV and on a phone held sideways, from the bottom on
  a phone held upright), with the video visible and still playing behind it. Any value (`"modal"`, `"panel"` or
  none) looks the same.
- **`accent`**: a `#RRGGBB` that paints the top bar, the states and the focus. It follows the same contrast rules
  as [`theme`](section-theme.md#theme)'s `accent`; if it fails, Kino's own is used and the panel stays.
- **`refreshMs`**: asks Kino to call `panel(context)` again every so often while the panel is open (2000 to
  60,000, clamped). Calls never overlap (the next waits for the previous one and for any action); one that fails or
  times out is skipped without showing an error; refreshing stops when the panel closes or the app goes to the
  background.
- **`title`** and the other texts have an `...En` twin (`titleEn`, `labelEn`, `textEn`…) shown when the app is in
  English, like [the settings form's texts](settings-form.md#english).
- Everything is validated. An invalid element is dropped with a line in the plugin's log; a panel that is not an
  object shows nothing.

## Elements { #elements }

Every element may also carry `enabled: false` (shown dimmed, focus skips it) and `hidden: true` (not drawn). A
`key` is 1 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -` and **is unique across the whole panel** (a second element
with the same key is dropped). Anything that can be pressed or holds a value carries a `key`.

| `type` | Fields | Notes and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `section` | `title`, `text?` | a heading with optional text; `title` up to 60, `text` up to 1000. |
| `text` | `text` | multi-line text, up to 1000 characters; not selectable and does nothing. |
| `status` | `text` | a highlighted status line, up to 200 characters. |
| `image` | `url`, `aspect?`, `alt?` | `https` only, on a public address: Kino never reaches the device's or the home network's addresses (the one exception is a server the person typed in your plugin's settings); `aspect` is `16:9`, `2:3`, `1:1` or `banner`; `alt` up to 200. If it fails to load it takes no room and never breaks the panel. |
| `button` | `key`, `label`, `confirm?` | pressing it calls `panelAction` with `trigger: "press"`. `label` 1 to 40 (longer, and the button is dropped). With `confirm` (up to 160) Kino asks first. |
| `toggle` | `key`, `label`, `scope`, `hint?`, `autoSave?` | a switch. Calls `panelAction` with `trigger: "change"`. |
| `select` | `key`, `label`, `scope`, `options`, `hint?`, `autoSave?` | a list of 1 to 20 options `{ value, label }` (each 1 to 40, values distinct; one bad option drops the `select`). |
| `text-input` | `key`, `label`, `scope`, `hint?`, `placeholder?` | a text field. Calls `panelAction` with `trigger: "submit"` only on confirm (the TV keyboard's "Listo", the phone keyboard's action), **never per keystroke**. `placeholder` up to 40. |
| `qr` | `url`, `label?` | a QR code plus the link's text; `https` only, up to 512 characters, on a public host **with a dot** (or a public IPv4 address): never the device or the home network (no local or single-name host, private address or IPv6 literal). On the TV it is read with the phone's camera; on the phone, tapping it opens the link. Kino never opens it by itself. `label` up to 40. |
| `loading` | `text?` | **Kino 0.9.64, additive (any apiVersion)**: a spinner with `text` beside it (if missing, Kino's "Cargando…"). Answer at once with the tab's shell and this element, and set `refreshMs` so Kino asks again once you are done. Send it only when `context.features` includes `"loading"`: an older Kino drops it as an unknown element (answer with a `status` there instead). |
| `episodes` | `ref` | the list of the playing series' episodes with the current one highlighted; choosing one plays it, through the same path as "next episode". It may be empty (a movie, for example) and then takes no focus. |
| `row`, `col`, `card` | see [layout](#layout) | containers. |
| `ai`, `chat` | | **not in this version**: dropped ("needs a newer Kino"). |

Rules for the elements that hold a value (`toggle`, `select`, `text-input`):

- `scope` is `"video"` (one value per title; for a series, **per episode**) or `"plugin"` (one for all your
  titles; the default when you leave it out). Any other value drops the element.
- The value on screen comes from `context.values[scope][key]`.
- `hint` up to 80 characters; the label 1 to 40; with `autoSave: true` (only when it is exactly `true`) each
  change saves itself (see [Persistence](#persistence)).
- `toggle` and `select` report 300 ms after the last change (several in a row merge into one).

## Layout: rows, columns and cards { #layout }

You build the panel with containers, never with pixels: only weights, gaps and an image's `aspect`, so nothing
overflows on a TV or a phone.

```js
{ type: "row", gap: "small", children: [
  { type: "col", weight: 4, children: [{ type: "image", url: "https://…/poster.jpg", aspect: "2:3" }] },
  { type: "col", weight: 8, children: [{ type: "text", text: "…" }] },
] }
```

| Container | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `row` | `children`, `gap?` (`none`, `small`, `medium`, `large`; 0, 8, 16 or 24 dp), `align?` (`start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`), `stackOnNarrow?` (default `true`). Puts its children side by side. |
| `col` | `children`, `weight?` (1 to 12; any other value is 1), `gap?`, `align?`. A column inside a row takes `weight` shares of its width. Any loose element in a row weighs 1. |
| `card` | `children`, `title?` (up to 60), `style?` (`plain` with no border or padding, `outlined` with a border, `filled` with a background). A framed group. |

- **Limits**: nesting at most **4** levels deep (containers count), at most **6** children per row, at most
  **120** nodes in the whole panel (containers count; a dropped one does not spend any). Anything over is trimmed
  with a log line (at most 10 lines per panel, then "N more problems not logged"), and never breaks the panel.
- **Narrow screens.** A row with `stackOnNarrow` (the default) stacks its children vertically, in order, when the
  panel's space is under **480 dp** (a phone held upright, or a narrow strip). `stackOnNarrow: false` keeps them
  side by side. `align: "stretch"` in a row aligns to the top (it does not equalise heights); in a column it makes
  the children fill the width.
- **Dimmed and hidden.** A container with `enabled: false` dims everything inside it and takes it out of focus; one
  with `hidden: true` is not drawn (a row whose children are all hidden leaves no gap).

## Scroll and focus { #focus }

- The panel **scrolls** when the content does not fit: by touch on the phone; on the TV the focused
  element is always brought into view, with a margin (D-pad up/down moves focus and scrolls).
- Text, sections, images and status lines take no focus (they are scrolled past). Buttons, inputs, `episodes`
  and `qr` do.
- **TV**: focus starts on the first element that can take it (the close X if there is none); inside a row,
  left/right; between rows, up/down, in reading order. **Focus does not leave the panel** and Back closes it: to
  reach the player's controls, close it first. While the panel is open the player does not
  steal focus. The whole panel body is reachable with the D-pad (the QR and long text blocks are focus stops so they
  scroll into view) and, if the focused control disappears when your answer replaces the panel, focus returns to
  the first control.
- **Phone**: the panel does not take focus on its own, so a text field does not raise the keyboard. The strip
  fits between the top bar and the bottom controls while they are shown.
- An action's answer may ask for `focus: "<key>"` to move focus; it only applies on the TV, once per answer (a
  refresh does not repeat it).
- A busy button (waiting for your `panelAction`) shows a spinner and ignores another press without dropping focus.

## Tabs { #tabs }

`tabs: [{ id, label }]` (at most 6; `id` like a key, `label` up to 24, duplicates are dropped) and `tab` (the
current one; the first if it does not exist). They draw as a strip at the top (left/right on the TV). Pressing one
calls `panel(context)` again with `context.tab`: **you build each tab's content**. There is no `tab` trigger: the
tab arrives in the context.

## `panelAction(event, context)`: your JavaScript is in charge { #panel-action }

```js
export async function panelAction(event, context) { /* returns an answer, or null */ }
```

It is called with **two arguments**. Kino only draws what you return and tells you what the person does; you can
read any field, compute, call `kino.fetch`, `kino.tmdb`, `kino.meta`, `kino.storage`, and answer with a new panel,
values and player actions.

```ts
event = {
  key: string,                                  // the element that fired
  trigger: "press" | "change" | "submit",       // "tab" and "open" are reserved: this version never sends them
  values: Record<string, Value>,                // the CURRENT value of every input on screen, saved or not
  value?: Value                                 // the new value of `key` on "change" and "submit"
}
```

`press` is a button; `change` a `toggle` or `select`; `submit` a confirmed `text-input`.

### What the answer may carry { #answer }

Every field is optional; `null` (or nothing) means "nothing to do".

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `panel` | replaces the whole panel (same rules as `panel(context)`). |
| `patch` | `{ "<key>": element }`: replaces just those elements in place (only elements that have a `key`: `button`, `toggle`, `select` and `text-input`; to change a `text`, a `status` or an image, return a whole `panel`). At most 40 keys; each entry is a single node, validated like any element and with its own 120-node budget. Kino drops it (with a log line) if the key names no element on screen, if it repeats another element's key in the panel, or if the resulting panel passes 120 nodes or 4 levels. |
| `values` | `{ "<key>": value }`: changes what the inputs show (clear one, fill one from another). At most 120 keys; each value is a string of up to 500 characters, a boolean, a finite number or `null`. **It does not save.** A key that is not an input on screen is ignored. |
| `save` | `["<key>", …]`: saves those inputs, each with the `scope` it declared (at most 50). Only keys of inputs that are on screen are saved. Also, the `toggle` or `select` with `autoSave: true` that fired the action saves itself, without you listing it. |
| `focus` | the key to move focus to (TV). |
| `message` | a short notice for the person, up to 160 characters, that Kino shows as a brief message. It goes through **the same rules as a [`userMessage`](contract.md#user-message)** (Kino shows it as "Message from <your plugin>: …" ("Mensaje de <your plugin>: …" in Spanish), and if your plugin's name cannot introduce it, for example `Cuevana3`, it is dropped); if it does not pass, it is dropped with a log line. |
| `player` | actions on the player: the [table below](#player). |

Kino applies, in this order, `panel` or `patch`, `values`, `save`, `focus`, `player` and, last, `message`.

While your `panelAction` runs, the control that fired it shows it is busy; **there is one action in flight** and
the others wait their turn (in order). An error or a timeout shows as the plugin's error line inside the panel,
without closing it, and **never leaves anything half-saved**: values are written only after your action returns
without error. A `save` that spans both scopes is saved whole or not at all.

## Driving the player: `player` { #player }

A `panelAction` or `playerEvent` answer may carry `player: { … }`. Any other key inside `player` is ignored with a
log line (the rest of `player` still applies). A value outside its range is clamped or dropped, also with a log line.

| Property | Values | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seekToMs` | a number; clamped to 0 up to the duration | seeks to that position, through the same seek the other controls use (also when casting). Ignored for live. Never pauses or restarts playback. **At most one seek per second per plugin**, counting the panel and the events together; the rest are dropped. |
| `seekStepMs` | 5000 to 120,000, in whole seconds | the back/forward step (remote, keyboard, double tap and buttons); the on-screen labels follow the value ("−30", "+30"; at 10 s the usual icons stay). |
| `speed` | 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 or 2 | the playback speed. |
| `resize` | `"fit"`, `"fill"`, `"zoom"`, `"4:3"`, `"16:9"` or `"21:9"` | the picture size. |
| `skip` | `{ openingStartMs, openingEndMs, endingStartMs }` | the skip intro/outro button for **this video**, with the same rules as `Stream.skip`. |
| `markers` | up to 30: `{ atMs, label }` (`label` up to 24) | dots on the progress bar ("Goal 63'"), also in the markers menu; choosing one seeks there. Replaces the video's list; an empty list clears it. |
| `autoNext` | `{ enabled, countdownS, nextRef? }` | the end of an episode: see below. |

**`autoNext`** controls what happens when a chapter of your plugin ends:

- No `autoNext`, or `countdownS: 0` with no `nextRef`: it moves to the next one at once, as always.
- `{ enabled: false }` (needs no `countdownS`): the player stays at the end, without advancing.
- `{ enabled: true, countdownS: 1..30 }` (with `enabled: true`, `countdownS` is required; 0 to 30): a card at the
  bottom right says "Siguiente en N s" with "Ver ahora" (TV focus starts there) and "Cancelar" (Back also cancels and
  leaves the player at the end). At zero, or on "Ver ahora", the next one plays. If the person seeks back or
  resumes, the countdown is cancelled.
- `nextRef` suggests which one is next: it is used only if it is the `ref` of an episode in the series' list;
  otherwise Kino's own next one plays and a log line is written. With `countdownS: 0` and a valid `nextRef`, it plays
  at once with no card. The countdown starts only where Kino would have advanced anyway (where a next chapter
  exists).

### Who wins { #wins }

Everything applies **only while your plugin's content plays**, and **what the person does by hand always wins**:

- **Speed and size**: if the person taps the speed button or the player's zoom, your `speed` or `resize` is ignored
  for as long as that playback screen lasts. The person's own speed cycle **does not change** (0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5 and
  2); your 0.5 and 1.75 are applied and shown, and the next tap moves to the next step of the person's cycle. The TV
  has no speed button, so there the person cannot override yours.
- **Skip intro/outro**: a manual correction by the person (the "No tiene intro/outro" button, or adjusting the
  times) wins over your `skip`. It is not saved for live channels or 18+ titles.
- The rest (step, `autoNext`) you save and the person sees as part of the plugin; "Restablecer" undoes it.
- The context (`context.player`) tells you what is really in effect: the person's speed if they changed it, else
  yours, else 1; and for `resize`, `"zoom"`/`"fit"` if the person touched the zoom.

## Persistence and sync { #persistence }

- Values with `scope: "video"` are stored **per plugin and per title** (the title's key is the playing item's: for
  a series, the episode); those with `scope: "plugin"`, per plugin.
- The player properties are stored the same way, without you writing anything: `seekStepMs`, `speed`, `resize`
  and `autoNext` **per plugin**, and `markers` **per video**. `skip` goes to that episode's skip button.
- Limits: at most **50 keys per scope** and values of at most **500 characters**; over that, the whole write is
  refused with "Couldn't save: …" (in Spanish "No se pudo guardar: …"). Kino also keeps at most 1500 live values
  in total on the device (all scopes and all plugins); past that, the oldest per-video values go.
- **It syncs both ways** across the person's devices, like everything of theirs (last write wins per key). A value
  that arrives from another device updates the open panel.
- It is removed when the plugin is **uninstalled**.
- Every panel has the **"Restablecer"** button at the bottom, which Kino provides (not you): it asks "¿Qué quieres
  dejar como estaba?" with "Solo este video" (clears that title's values, its markers and the `skip` that came from
  your plugin) and "Todo lo de este plugin, en todos los videos" (clears every value of the plugin and the step,
  speed, size and `autoNext` return to their defaults; skip-intro times already saved stay).

## `playerEvent(event, context)`: learning what playback does { #player-event }

Export `playerEvent` (it needs no `panel`) to know what happens while one of your titles plays. It is
fire-and-forget: Kino expects nothing back and never blocks on it.

```js
export async function playerEvent(event, context) {
  if (event.type === "ended") return { player: { autoNext: { enabled: true, countdownS: 8 } } };
  return null;
}
```

The event is flat, `{ type, ...detail }`, and the context is the panel's own (with `values`):

| `type` | When | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `started` | the first time the title is ready. Another copy of the same title does not repeat it. | |
| `paused`, `resumed` | when the person pauses or resumes (the intent to play changes). Buffering or a seek sends nothing. | |
| `ended` | once per title, only at the real end (a stream cut midway does not count), never for live. | |
| `failed` | **an error happened** (it does not mean playback is over: a copy switch or a reopen may follow). | `kind`: for video, the player's error code name (such as `"ERROR_CODE_IO_BAD_HTTP_STATUS"`) or `"UNREACHABLE_SERVER"`; for live, the error class. For live it is sent per error, within the reopen budget. |
| `copyChanged` | the copy playing changed. | `automatic` (`true` if Kino switched, `false` if the person chose), `label?` (the new copy) and, when automatic, `kind` (why the previous one failed). |

- Only **`started`, `paused`, `resumed` and `ended` from the regular player** are sent: a download that plays from
  the service and casting to another screen (Chromecast, DLNA) do not send them. `failed` and `copyChanged` still
  go. Channels in the En vivo tab send no events.
- **They do not overlap.** There is at most one call in flight per plugin; while it runs, only the **latest** event
  that arrived is kept and sent when it ends (a waiting `failed` or `ended` is not replaced by a `paused` or
  `resumed`). A waiting `failed` can be replaced by a later `copyChanged`.
- **5 s** limit per call; past it the event is dropped with a log line and the next one goes.
- Of your answer only `player` and `message` count (through the same rules as above, and the same limit of one
  seek per second per plugin, panel included); anything else is ignored. An error, a timeout or an invalid answer
  is logged and dropped: **it never stops the video**.
- An answer that arrives after the person changed title is dropped.

## `settingsLayout`: arranging your settings { #settings-layout }

Your plugin's form (Ajustes ▸ your plugin) can use the same containers. It is **backward compatible**: `settings`
stays as always (keys, types, defaults, `required`, `validateSettings`…) and the layout only **places** settings
that already exist, by key.

```json
"settings": [ …as always… ],
"settingsLayout": [
  { "type": "card", "title": "Idioma y calidad", "titleEn": "Language and quality", "children": [
    { "type": "row", "children": [ { "setting": "preferred" }, { "setting": "maxQuality" } ] } ] },
  { "type": "text", "text": "Todo lo demás va debajo.", "textEn": "Everything else goes below." },
  { "type": "image", "url": "https://example.com/banner.png", "aspect": "banner" }
]
```

- The leaves are `{ "setting": "<key>" }`, `{ "type": "text", "text" }` (with `textEn`) and
  `{ "type": "image", "url" }` (`https`, with the panel's image rules). The containers are `row`, `col` and
  `card` (with `title` and `titleEn`) with the same limits and look as in the panel; in the form `enabled` and
  `hidden` are ignored.
- **A layout never hides anything**: a setting you do not name is appended at the end, in manifest order. A key
  that is repeated or does not exist is ignored at run time (with a line in the plugin's log) and `validate.mjs`
  flags it as a problem.
- Without `settingsLayout` the form is exactly as always, and an older Kino ignores the field and shows the usual
  list. A `settingsLayout` that only lists the settings in manifest order, with no containers, looks the same as
  the list. Below apiVersion 9 it is ignored.
- The `section` setting type keeps working; a `card` with a `title` is its richer version.

## The panel built with the screen kit (apiVersion 14) { #screen-kit }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.74"
    Available from Kino 0.9.74. This section needs `"apiVersion": 14`; an older
    Kino refuses these plugins with «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino»; to keep reaching people on an
    older version use `enhancements` (see [Screens without raising your apiVersion](enhancements.md)). Everything above
    stays valid as it is for apiVersion 9 to 13.

From apiVersion 14 the player panel can be built from the same nodes as a [screen](screens.md), a tab can live in
**another** plugin's panel or on a live channel, and the person can pin the panel next to the video. The reference example
is **Party Chat** (<https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-watch-party>): a tab it contributes to any title's panel, with
a room and a chat.

![The panel in screen mode, on a phone](assets/ui/panel-phone.png)
![The panel in screen mode, on a TV](assets/ui/panel-tv.png)

### Legacy panel and screen mode { #screen-mode }

`panel(context)` may return `{ format: "screen", root, title?, titleEn?, tabs?, tab?, refreshMs?, accent?, player?, layout? }`:
the same drawer (its title, tabs, `refreshMs` and accent follow the rules above; a `tabs` entry may also carry the shared
[`badge`](screen-components.md#badge), `"dot"` or `{ text, textEn?, color? }`, drawn beside its label) with a body that is
a screen tree. A result without `format` is the legacy panel, read and drawn exactly as before; the format may change from
one call to the next, and below apiVersion 14 a screen result is read as a legacy panel (logged).

```js
export async function panel(context) {
  if (!(context.features || []).includes("screen")) return { title: "Party Chat", elements: [{ type: "status", text: "Actualiza Kino" }] };
  return { format: "screen", title: "Party Chat", root: { type: "Column", children: [{ type: "ElevatedButton", labelText: "Sincronizar", onPressed: "sync" }] } };
}
```

| What | In a panel in screen mode |
| --- | --- |
| Result | `{ format: "screen", root, title, titleEn, accent, refreshMs, tabs, tab, player, layout }` |
| Tree | depth 6, 200 nodes; `AlertDialog`, `BottomSheet` and `PopupMenuButton` not drawn, unless it has an `anchor` (a popover inside the drawer, see [anchor](screen-forms.md#anchor)); no `every` |
| Context adds | `state`, `size`, and `features` holds `"screen"` while screens are on |
| `panelAction` triggers | `press`, `change`, `submit` |
| Answer fields kept | `state`, `toast`, `toastEn`, `ui`, `config`, `go`, `close`, `focus`, `player`, `message`, `pause`, `panel` |
| Answer fields dropped | `dialog`, `sheet`, `menu`, `route`, `share`, `enableJob`; legacy-only `patch`, `values`, `save` |

Differences from a full screen:

- **Limits**: depth 6 and 200 nodes. A `popup` node is dropped (pop-ups belong to the screen, not to the drawer) unless it
  has an `anchor`, and `every` is dropped: `refreshMs` (2,000 to 60,000 ms, only while the panel is open) is THE periodic
  call.
- **Calls**: renders call `panel(context)`; the person's events call `panelAction({ event, context })` with
  `event = { key?, trigger, name, arg?, value?, values }` (`trigger` is `press`, `change` or `submit`; `tab` and `open`
  stay reserved); there is no reserved `open` event. An apiVersion 14 plugin's `context` carries `state` (Kino's, kept for
  this title's playback) and `size` (the drawer's classes; Kino's estimate until it measured itself) **in every call, the
  first one included**, because Kino cannot know the format before your answer. See [state](screen-reference.md#state) and
  [per-size values](screen-reference.md#per-size-values).
- **Answers**: `state`, `toast`, `ui`, `config`, `focus`, `go` (every shape; all but `screen` and `close` close the panel
  first), `close`, and the legacy `player`, `message`, `pause` and `panel` are kept; `dialog`, `sheet`, `menu` and `route`
  are not honoured, and `patch`, `values` and `save` are legacy-only (dropped, logged). A `playerEvent` answer's `panel`
  (either format) shows in that title's open panel, but its `state` is never applied: keep that in your own variables or
  `kino.storage`. See [answers](screen-reference.md#answers).
- **Detect the format**: answer a screen result only when `context.features` includes `"screen"`. Kino puts it there only
  while plugin screens are switched on; when they are off a screen result shows no panel, so answer a legacy one then.
- **Errors**: a failed event shows the drawer's error line at once; three in a row show the panel's error state.
- **TV**: a [toast](screen-components.md#toast)'s action runs from the remote's Menu or Play/Pause key (the drawer has no
  Down-to-toast). The panel's text is a step smaller than a full screen's (the drawer and the dock are 360 to 480 dp wide):
  `h1` draws at a screen's `h3` size, `h2` at `h4`'s, `h3` at `h5`'s, `h4` and `h5` at the large body size, `p` at 15 sp;
  the phone's sizes do not change.
- **TV focus**: in any panel, legacy or screen mode, only what does something takes focus and Kino's ring: buttons,
  toggles, selects, fields, the episode list, the tabs, pin and close. A text, a section, a status, an image or a QR is
  never a focus stop and never boxed: Up and Down page through them. When an answer's new tree no longer has the focused
  node (a QR view replacing the pressed button), focus goes to the focusable now at or after its place; with none, the body
  itself takes it (no ring) so Up and Down still scroll it. An answer's `focus` wins.
- Kino's own tab about the title shows, top to bottom, the poster with the title and its facts, the synopsis, the details,
  the images and last the cast (three cards a row, two on a panel under 360 dp), each part only when TMDB has it.
- **Kit**: `node sdk/run.mjs --state '<json>' --screen <folder> panelAction <ref> <name> <press|change|submit>`.

### Layout fill: a chat tab { #layout-fill }

A panel's body scrolls by default (`layout: "scroll"`): the tree has no height limit, so a
[`ListView`](screen-components.md#list-view) draws flat and `flex` does nothing, and a row after a list sits right under
its last item. A chat wants the opposite: the messages take the room and the input row stays at the bottom of the panel,
like any chat app. Answer `layout: "fill"` (chosen per result: beside `root` in a `panel()` result, on the root object of a
`screen()` answer): the root is drawn at the body's size with no body scroll, `flex` shares the height left, and a
`ListView` with `flex` is lazy and scrolls itself.

```js
export async function panel(context) {
  const messages = ((context.state || {}).messages || []).map((m, i) => ({ type: "Text", key: "m" + i, text: m }));
  return { format: "screen", title: "Party Chat", layout: "fill", root: { type: "Column", gap: 8, children: [
    { type: "Text", text: "Sala 1234", style: "h4" },
    { type: "ListView", key: "chat", flex: 1, stickToBottom: true, items: messages,
      empty: { type: "Text", text: "Sin mensajes", textEn: "No messages", color: "muted" } },
    { type: "Row", gap: 8, children: [
      { type: "TextField", key: "msg", flex: 1, hintText: "Escribe…", hintTextEn: "Type…" },
      { type: "IconButton", icon: "send", labelText: "Enviar", labelTextEn: "Send", onPressed: "send" },
    ] },
  ] } };
}
```

- **Where the bottom row goes**: at the bottom of the panel, docked (pinned) or in the drawer, upright or sideways, however
  many messages the list holds; when the panel opens again (a return to Kino, a rotation) it is there too. The phone's
  keyboard lifts it: the dock and the drawer end above the keyboard, and the list gets the height left.
- **`stickToBottom`**: the list opens at the last message and follows new ones while the person reads the end; scrolled up
  to read older ones, it stays put until they come back down.
- **TV**: Up and Down page through a list with nothing to focus (messages), and leave it at its ends toward the controls.
- **Too tall**: when the parts without `flex` alone are taller than the panel (a short window, a big keyboard), Kino draws
  that render in the scroll layout and logs `screen: layout fill does not fit, using scroll` once; it tries `fill` again
  when the size or the root's children change. A `panel` root's own `layout` is ignored (logged): put it beside `root`.
- **Full screens** already draw the root at the screen's size with no scroll of their own (what `fill` does), whatever
  `layout` says. Any other value is logged and read as `scroll`.

### A tab in another plugin's panel (`playerPanelTab`) { #contributed-tab }

```json
"apiVersion": 14,
"capabilities": ["playerPanelTab"],
"panel": { "contributes": true, "label": "Party Chat", "icon": "mood" }
```

`"panel": { "contributes": true, "label"?, "labelEn"?, "icon"? | "iconFile"? }` with the capability `playerPanelTab` (each
needs the other; it exports `panel` and may stand alone) adds **your tab to the player panel of any plugin's title**. A
missing `label` is your plugin's name (cut to 24 characters).

- The drawer becomes a tab host: Kino's own information tab first (fixed), then the playing plugin's panel (with its own
  tabs), then the contributed tabs in the person's order (Ajustes, «Paneles del reproductor»; install order by default), at
  most 6. Each tab shows its plugin's name and icon, never Kino's info icon; a name that reads like "Kino" is shown as
  «Plugin «name»». The id `kino` is reserved. Without a contribution the drawer is exactly as before.
- **When you are called**: only while your tab is the selected one and the drawer is open (`refreshMs` only then), and
  `playerEvent` only while your tab is open (`copyChanged` without its label). Nothing runs in the background: when the
  person switches tabs or closes the drawer, you stop ([pin the panel](#pinned) to keep running).
- **What you see** (an allow-list): `kind`, `title`, `year`, `season`, `episode`, `episodeTitle`, `ids`, `positionMs`,
  `durationMs`, `paused`, `seekStepMs`, `stats`, `device`, `lang`, your `tab`, `values`, `features`, `state` and `size`;
