  of `player`, only `seekStepMs`, `speed` and `resize`; plus `foreign: true`, `source: { pluginId, name }` (the plugin that
  provides the stream) and `ref`, an **opaque** id: `"foreign:"` and 32 hex characters, the same for the same title on this
  install for your plugin, different for another plugin or install. It is opaque, **not secret**. Never the owner's
  `playing` copy or its `autoNext`.
- **Where not**: never on an 18+ title, any title of an 18+ plugin (an 18+ contributor only while the code is unlocked),
  your own titles (there you are the owner), M3U lists, own channels or other non-plugin content.
- **What you may do**: your `go.title` and `go.play` are dropped (you cannot open the playing plugin's content); `search`,
  `browse`, `section`, `categories`, `screen`, `titleByIds`, `url` and `close` work (see [`go`](screens.md#go)). Your player
  actions count only in the answer to a `panelAction` after a **press** in your tab, and only `seekToMs`; with
  [`playerControl`](rooms.md#player-control) also `pause` and `speed`, from any origin. Your episode list draws nothing.
- **Kit**: `node sdk/run.mjs --foreign <source plugin id>[:<name>] <folder> panel <ref>` gives your calls the foreign
  context.

The texts a manifest is refused with:

| Problem | Text |
| --- | --- |
| `contributes` is not a boolean | `The "panel.contributes" field must be true or false` |
| `contributes` without the capability | `The "panel.contributes" field needs the "playerPanelTab" capability` |
| the capability without `contributes` | `The "playerPanelTab" capability needs "panel": { "contributes": true }` |

#### Consent { #contributed-tab-consent }

`playerPanelTab` needs the person's approval with a **red** line, at install and on the update that adds it (Kino never
approves it on its own; a kit import starts it unticked):

> «Su pestaña en el reproductor verá lo que estás viendo (título, año, identificadores y posición, o el canal en vivo)
> mientras la tengas abierta, y podrá enviarlo a sus servicios» ("Its tab in the player will see what you are watching
> (title, year, ids and position, or the live channel) while you have it open, and can send it to its services")

The person can hide it with «Mostrar en el reproductor» ("Show in the player", in your tab in Ajustes; it covers the whole
device and syncs to their other devices) or reorder it (Ajustes, «Paneles del reproductor»). See
[the consent model](screens.md#consent).

### Your tab on a live channel (`"kinds": ["live"]`) { #live-kinds }

Every En vivo channel has the same player panel (Right on the TV remote; the panel button in the live band on a phone),
with Kino's own **General** tab first (the favourite and the channel's brightness). Add `"kinds": ["title", "live"]` (or
`["live"]`) to your `"panel": { "contributes": true }` and your tab joins it after General (default `["title"]`: titles
only, as before). The consent is the same capability (`playerPanelTab`).

```json
"panel": { "contributes": true, "label": "Party Chat", "kinds": ["title", "live"] }
```

- **What you see**: `kind: "live"`, `live: true`, `channel: { provider, code, name }` (the plugin that lists the channel,
  its id there, its name), `foreign: true`, `source`, `device`, `lang`, your `tab`, `values` (`video` is one set for every
  live channel: the session stays open across zaps), `features`, `state` and `size`. No `ref`, title, ids, position,
  duration, pause, stats or `player`: live has no seek and no pause that matters.
- **When**: as on a title, only while your tab is selected and the panel open. On a zap Kino calls `panel` again with the
  new channel (the panel stays open); there is no `playerEvent` on live.
- **Where not**: a channel its provider's own listing has not confirmed as not 18+, a channel of an 18+ provider, «Mis
  canales» (the person's own M3U lists and channels) and saved legacy channels: your tab is not there.
- **What you may do**: every `player` action is dropped (`panel: player actions do nothing on a live channel, dropped
  (live_channel)`). [`go.liveChannel`](screen-forms.md#go-live-channel) `{ provider, code }` tunes the player to a channel
  after the person's press (in the panel on live it changes in place): how a room's guest watches the host's channel.
- **Kit**: `node sdk/run.mjs --live-channel <provider>:<code>[:<name>] <folder> panel -`.

| Problem | Text |
| --- | --- |
| `kinds` empty, unknown or not a list | `The "panel.kinds" field must be a non-empty list of "title" and "live"` |
| `kinds` without `contributes` | `The "panel.kinds" field needs "panel": { "contributes": true }` |

### The pinned panel { #pinned }

Kino's own, for every panel: «Fijar» / «Pin» in the panel's header (a pin icon alone on a TV) docks it next to the video:

- the right third on a TV or a landscape window of 600 dp or more; below the video on an upright phone, whose video then
  gets at least 300 dp or 38 % of the height for its controls;
- not offered in picture-in-picture, while casting, or in a narrow landscape window.

Docked, the video keeps playing and the panel's sessions, `refreshMs` and `playerEvent` keep running while Kino is in
front. The pin lasts for the playback: it survives a rotation and the next episodes played in the player, and a new
playback starts unpinned (it is not remembered, stored nor synced). The panel only opens when the person opens it.

On a TV: Right from the last control of the player's row (of either row) goes into the panel, on «Desfijar» first, and
with the controls hidden Right on the video does too; Left past its edge goes back to the controls; the first Back hides
the panel (it stays pinned: opened again, it docks again) and the next Back is the player's. A pop-up or dialog over the
panel takes that first Back. While the panel is docked on a TV or a phone held sideways, the player's two groups of buttons
sit one row under the other.

Nothing in the plugin contract changes; a plugin that must keep running (Party Chat) tells its people to pin it for the
playback.

## Robustness { #robustness }

- **A failure never stops the video.** The panel runs in the plugin's sandbox; an exception, a timeout or an
  invalid shape show a contained error state (with your `userMessage` if there is one) and the video keeps playing.
- **Time limits**: `panel` and `panelAction`, **20 s** each; `playerEvent`, **5 s**.
- **One `panelAction` in flight** (the others wait in order, refreshes too); quick changes to the same input merge
  into one (300 ms).
- **Validation**: everything you return is checked against the contract; what is invalid is dropped with a line in
  the plugin's log, and a wholly invalid panel shows the error state. Messages are cleaned like a `userMessage`.
- A late answer to an action that no longer applies (the panel closed, the title changed, or it was reset) writes
  nothing.

## Trying it with the kit { #kit }

The Node kit (`sdk/run.mjs`) runs the three functions with a fake context (a title "Demo", `tmdb: 550`, position
10:00 of 1:30:00, TV, `es-CO`) and validates the answer with the same rules and the same log texts as Kino:

```
node sdk/run.mjs . panel <ref> [tab]
node sdk/run.mjs . panelAction <ref> <key> <press|change|submit> ['<value json>'] ['<values json>']
node sdk/run.mjs . playerEvent <ref> <type> ['<detail json>']
node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"lang":"en-US","kind":"episode","device":"phone"}' . panel <ref>
```

- `--context` merges your JSON over the fake context (for example `lang`, `kind`, `paused`, `values`, `tab`).
- The validated answer goes to stdout; each dropped element goes to stderr as `· dropped: <reason>`. The exit code
  is 1 if the whole panel is invalid and 2 if an argument is wrong. `playerEvent` without that export says Kino
  will never call your plugin for events.
- `sdk/validate.mjs` checks the manifest: `panel`, the `iconFile` (96×96, alpha, 24 KB, from disk), an unknown
  `icon` (a warning), a panel or layout below apiVersion 9 (ignored) and `settingsLayout` (a repeated or unknown
  key is a problem).

See also [Test it locally](test-locally.md).

## A complete small example { #example }

`kino-plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "mi-plugin", "name": "Mi plugin", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 9,
  "entry": "plugin.js", "hosts": ["example.com"], "capabilities": ["search", "resolve"],
  "panel": { "label": "Opciones", "labelEn": "Options", "icon": "tune" }
}
```

`plugin.js`:

```js
export async function search() { return []; }
export async function resolve() { throw kino.error("not_found", "example"); }

export async function panel(context) {
  const en = context.lang.startsWith("en");
  const left = Math.max(0, Math.round(((context.durationMs ?? 0) - context.positionMs) / 60000));
  return {
    presentation: "panel",
    title: context.title,
    accent: "#2E7D32",
    refreshMs: 10000,
    elements: [
      { type: "status", text: en ? `${left} min left` : `Faltan ${left} min` },
      { type: "row", gap: "small", children: [
        { type: "button", key: "back30", label: "−30 s" },
        { type: "button", key: "faster", label: en ? "Speed 1.25x" : "Velocidad 1,25x" },
      ] },
      { type: "toggle", key: "remember", label: en ? "Remember this copy" : "Recordar esta copia", scope: "video", autoSave: true },
      { type: "text-input", key: "note", label: en ? "Note" : "Nota", scope: "video", placeholder: "…" },
    ],
  };
}

export async function panelAction(event, context) {
  if (event.key === "back30") return { player: { seekToMs: Math.max(0, context.positionMs - 30000) } };
  if (event.key === "faster") return { player: { speed: 1.25 }, message: "Velocidad subida" };
  if (event.key === "note" && event.trigger === "submit") return { save: ["note"], message: "Nota guardada" };
  return null; // "remember" (autoSave) needs nothing else
}

export async function playerEvent(event) {
  if (event.type === "ended") return { player: { autoNext: { enabled: true, countdownS: 8 } } };
  return null;
}
```

And what the kit prints:

```
$ node sdk/run.mjs . panel m1
{ "presentation": "panel", "title": "Demo", "accent": "#2E7D32", "refreshMs": 10000, "tabs": [], "tab": null,
  "elements": [ { "type": "status", "text": "Faltan 80 min" }, { "type": "row", … }, … ] }
$ node sdk/run.mjs . panelAction m1 back30 press
{ "player": { "seekToMs": 570000 } }
$ node sdk/run.mjs . panelAction m1 note submit '"hola"' '{"remember":true,"note":"hola"}'
{ "save": [ "note" ], "message": "Nota guardada" }
$ node sdk/run.mjs . playerEvent m1 ended
{ "player": { "autoNext": { "enabled": true, "countdownS": 8 } } }
```

Note: `remember` saves itself (`autoSave`), the note only when the person confirms it (`save`), and the message has
no digit glued to a letter ("Velocidad 1,25x" would have been dropped by the `userMessage` rule).

## What the kit cannot check { #kit-limits }

The kit runs each call on its own, without a player session's state. **Only Kino** applies these rules:

- The `patch` rules that need the panel on screen: that the key **names an element**, that it does not repeat
  another element's key, and that the resulting panel stays within 120 nodes and 4 levels. The kit validates each
  `patch` entry on its own (and notes it).
- The cap of **one seek per second per plugin**, counting `panelAction` and `playerEvent` together.
- `values` and `save` keys that **name no input on screen** (they are ignored), and whatever depends on what is
  stored: the scopes, the 50-key and 500-character limits, "Restablecer".
- That a `message` containing **one of the person's own passwords** is refused (the kit applies the other
  `userMessage` rules).
- Everything that depends on the device: the real context (the stats, the copy, the ids that are known), the layout
  and focus on the TV and the phone, how the icon looks, and who wins (the person's speed or zoom).
- The `tab` and `open` triggers: the kit accepts them because they are reserved, but Kino 0.9.55 never sends them.
- The real player events: with `playerEvent` you call them by hand.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/player-slot/ (docs/player-slot.en.md) -->

# The player slot (`playerSlot`, apiVersion 23) { #player-slot }

!!! note "Next Kino release, not published yet"
    apiVersion 23 arrives with the next Kino release (provisionally 0.9.83), which is not published yet. A Kino that does not
    have it refuses a manifest with the `playerSlot` capability or the `slot` block ("Este plugin necesita una versión más
    nueva de Kino"). To keep running on older Kinos, keep your `apiVersion` and add both as an [enhancement](enhancements.md)
    (`enhancements["23"]`: `"capabilities": ["playerSlot"], "slot": { ... }`).

A plugin can put up to **three small things in the top-right corner of the TV player**: a clock, a score, a logo, a button
that opens the plugin's [player panel](player-panel.md). Kino calls two functions of yours, `playerSlot(context)` to fill the
elements and `playerSlotAction({ id, context })` when the person presses a button, and draws what you answer with its own look.
Like a [screen](screens.md), you describe and Kino draws: no views, no colours, no pixels.

- **TV only.** The phone's player is unchanged: no element, no call.
- **Movies, series and En vivo channels.** What changes on a channel is [below](#live).
- **Three elements on screen in all, across every plugin.** `fixed` ones first, then the ones that show with the controls;
  the person's plugin order (Ajustes, "Paneles del reproductor", the same list as the panel tabs) breaks ties and the rest are
  not drawn.
- **No new network destination.** The slot uses the hosts the plugin already declares; an `image` is loaded by Kino from any
  public https address.

The numbers on this page come from [`contract.json`](reference/contract.json) (`playerSlot`); the shapes are in
[`kino.d.ts`](reference/kino.d.ts) (`KinoManifestSlot`, `KinoSlotContext`, `KinoSlotAnswer`, `KinoSlotActionAnswer`).

## A first slot: a clock { #example }

The complete example is the **player clock** (version 1.1.0): the time and the date in Spanish or English, in one `overlay` text
element, with no network. The person dresses it in the plugin's settings: time zone (the device's own by default), size, weight,
colour, background and position (see [Dressing a text](#dress)). Its modules live in `src/` and are bundled into `plugin.js` by
`scripts/build.mjs` (Kino loads one file).

Downloads: [`kino-plugin.json`](slot-examples/player-clock/kino-plugin.json) ·
[`plugin.js`](slot-examples/player-clock/plugin.js) · [`src/clock.js`](slot-examples/player-clock/src/clock.js) ·
[`src/index.js`](slot-examples/player-clock/src/index.js) · [`scripts/build.mjs`](slot-examples/player-clock/scripts/build.mjs)

**`kino-plugin.json`** (the essentials; the download has the full settings form, with its English texts and every option)

```json
{
  "id": "player-clock",
  "version": "1.1.0",
  "apiVersion": 23,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": ["kinotvapp.github.io"],
  "capabilities": ["playerSlot"],
  "slot": { "elements": [{ "id": "clock", "kind": "text", "mode": "overlay" }] },
  "settings": [
    { "key": "timezone", "label": "Zona horaria", "labelEn": "Time zone", "type": "select", "default": "auto",
      "options": [{ "value": "auto", "label": "La del aparato (por defecto)", "labelEn": "This device's own (default)" },
                  { "value": "-5", "label": "UTC-5 · Colombia, Perú, Nueva York", "labelEn": "UTC-5 · Colombia, Peru, New York" }] },
    { "key": "size", "label": "Tamaño del texto", "labelEn": "Text size", "type": "select", "default": "normal", "options": [] },
    { "key": "weight", "label": "Grosor de la letra", "labelEn": "Letter weight", "type": "select", "default": "auto", "options": [] },
    { "key": "color", "label": "Color de la letra", "labelEn": "Letter colour", "type": "select", "default": "auto", "options": [] },
    { "key": "background", "label": "Fondo de la pastilla", "labelEn": "Pill background", "type": "select", "default": "default", "options": [] },
    { "key": "left", "label": "Horizontal", "labelEn": "Horizontal", "type": "select", "default": "0", "options": [] },
    { "key": "top", "label": "Vertical", "labelEn": "Vertical", "type": "select", "default": "0", "options": [] }
  ]
}
```

(`"options": []` stands for the list in the download: a `select` needs at least one option.)

**`src/index.js`** (the entry; `src/clock.js` turns a `Date` and `context.lang` into `"21:05\nWed Nov 4"`)

```js
--8<-- "slot-examples/player-clock/src/index.js"
```

- A plugin with only `playerSlot` and its `slot` block is complete: like `screen`, it plays nothing, so it needs neither
  `resolve` nor `search`.
- The manifest rules ask for at least one entry in `hosts`, so it names `kinotvapp.github.io`; the plugin never calls it.
- `playerSlotAction` is required by the capability even though the clock has no button (Kino never calls it here).
- `refreshMs: 60000` is the longest Kino allows: a clock that shows minutes asks once a minute.

```bash
node sdk/run.mjs player-clock playerSlot                              # the frame Kino would keep
node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"lang":"en-US"}' player-clock playerSlot  # in English
node sdk/validate.mjs player-clock                                     # an overlay-only slot shows no consent line
node sdk/run.mjs --config timezone=-5 player-clock playerSlot          # try a setting
```

## The manifest's `slot` block { #manifest }

```json
{
  "apiVersion": 23,
  "capabilities": ["playerSlot"],
  "slot": { "elements": [
    { "id": "clock", "kind": "text", "mode": "fixed" },
    { "id": "open", "kind": "button", "mode": "overlay" }
  ] }
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `elements` | 1 to 3 objects (a fourth is refused with `The "slot.elements" field must list 1 to 3 elements`). The count, the kinds and the modes are fixed here: your answers change content only. |
| `id` | Lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, starting with a letter, 1 to 24 characters (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,23}$`), unique in the block. Your answers use it as the key. |
| `kind` | `text`, `icon`, `image` or `button`. The answer for an element must be of its kind: a `text` element answered with an `icon` is dropped. |
| `mode` | `overlay`: floats over the video and shows **with the controls** (the controls of a movie or series; on a channel, the channel card). `fixed`: holds its place the whole time, paused or buffering too, and asks the person's approval ([consent](#consent)). |

- **The capability and the block need each other**: `The "slot" field needs the "playerSlot" capability`, `The "playerSlot"
  capability needs a "slot" block`. The capability exports `playerSlot` and `playerSlotAction`, both required (otherwise the
  install fails with "El plugin no carga: le falta ...").
- **`playerSlot` may be the plugin's only capability.** A slot-only plugin cannot declare `playerControl`: that one needs a
  `panel`.
- **When Kino draws nothing:** while a plugin panel is open, the audio and subtitles picker is open, a load error shows or the
  player is in picture-in-picture (an ordinary Kino dialog only dims the screen; the elements stay). An 18+ plugin draws only
  while the person's 18+ code is unlocked. `overlay` elements also wait for the controls: on a movie they hide with the
  controls, and while the screen is locked, a cast to a DLNA device is active or the person is marking a time.

## `playerSlot(context)`: what each element shows { #render }

```json
{ "items": [
    { "id": "clock", "text": "21:05\nmié 4 nov" },
    { "id": "mark", "icon": "star" },
    { "id": "logo", "image": "https://example.com/logo.png" },
    { "id": "open", "label": "Marcador", "icon": "tune" }
  ],
  "refreshMs": 30000 }
```

| `kind` | You answer | What Kino keeps and draws |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `text`: a string; newlines split lines | At most 2 lines (empty ones dropped, each trimmed), 2,000 characters before the split, control and direction characters removed. Never focusable. |
| `icon` | `icon`: one of Kino's [icon names](screen-components.md#icon-names) | The icon at 28 dp. An unknown name drops the item. Never focusable. |
| `image` | `image`: an https address on a public host (never an IP address, `localhost` or a local name) | Drawn small: about 40 dp high and at most 120 dp wide. Anything else drops the item. Never focusable. |
| `button` | `label` (at most 40 characters, control characters removed) and/or `icon` (a known name) | It needs at least one of the two valid. A round button (icon only) or a pill (with a label), focusable on the remote; icon-only reads "Botón del plugin" / "Plugin button" to a screen reader. |

- **`refreshMs`** is when Kino calls `playerSlot` again, counted from the end of the last call: below 2,000 it is raised to
  2,000, above 60,000 lowered to 60,000. Absent (or not a number) means it is never called again, which is fine for a button
  that does not change.
- **Nothing is repaired.** An id you did not declare, an item of the wrong kind, an unknown icon, a bad image and a button with
  nothing to show are dropped; a repeated id keeps the first valid one. If the answer is not an object with an `items` list,
  Kino keeps the last good frame (none the first time).
- **Items come out in declared order**, whatever order you answer in. An element you leave out is simply not drawn.

### Dressing a text and placing an element { #dress }

A `text` item may also say how it looks, and any item may say where it sits. The usual way is to offer them as ordinary
[settings](manifest.md) of your plugin, as the clock example does, and read them with `kino.config.get`.

| Field | On | Value | What Kino draws |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `text` | `"small"`, `"normal"`, `"large"` or `"xlarge"` | 12, 14 (the default), 18 or 24 sp, on a line that grows with it; the pill grows with the letters |
| `weight` | `text` | `"extralight"`, `"light"`, `"normal"`, `"medium"`, `"semibold"` or `"bold"` | Inter's weight (200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700) for every line. Absent: Kino's own, the first line Medium and the next Regular |
| `color` | `text` | `"#RRGGBB"` or `"#RRGGBBAA"` | The letters' colour. Never less than half opaque (a weaker alpha is raised to half) |
| `background` | `text` | `"#RRGGBB"` or `"#RRGGBBAA"` | The pill behind the text, instead of Kino's translucent black. `"#00000000"` (alpha 0) draws no pill |
| `left`, `top` | any item | whole numbers of dp | Nudges the element from its place in the row: `left` moves it right (negative: left), `top` moves it down (negative: up). Clamped to -400..200 and -40..300; anything that is not a number counts as 0 |

- **Each field is read on its own.** An invalid one (an unknown size or weight, `"red"`, `"#12345"`) is ignored: Kino draws
  its own for that field.
- **Kino keeps the text readable.** A `color` whose contrast against an opaque pill (or against Kino's dark one, when you give no
  `background`) is under 2:1 is dropped, and Kino's white letters turn black on a light opaque pill. A pill that is not opaque
  (alpha under 240) is never checked, because Kino cannot know what the video shows behind it.
- **A nudge keeps the space the element had**, so it can overlap its neighbour: nudge an element that sits alone.
- **The time zone is yours, not Kino's.** The clock example offers a "Time zone" setting whose default is the device's own
  clock; the others are fixed offsets from UTC (UTC-5, UTC+5:30...) that do not follow daylight saving time, because a plugin
  cannot rely on a time zone database in its sandbox.

### Timing, retries and the background { #timing }

- **Each call has 5 s.** Calls are serialized: never two at once for a plugin.
- **The first call can fail without losing the slot:** until Kino has one good answer it calls `playerSlot` again every 5 s, up
  to 4 more times, and then gives up for that playback. After the first answer, a failed or invalid call keeps the last frame
  and the `refreshMs` clock goes on.
- **Calls run unattended.** A `playerSlot` call (the first one included) never counts toward "No responde" (the strike of
  consecutive timeouts); a press does. So there is no breaker for refreshes either: a plugin whose `playerSlot` keeps timing out
  after its first frame is called again every `refreshMs` plus up to about 5 s, for as long as the playback lasts, keeping its
  last frame.
- **Not in the background.** Kino makes no `playerSlot` call while it is in the background (Home pressed, or a Kino page over the
  player) and calls again on return.

## `playerSlotAction({ id, context })`: a press { #action }

It runs when the person presses a button (OK on the remote); `id` is the element's id. Kino calls it only for a declared button
that is on screen. Answer `null` or `{}` to do nothing, or:

```json
{ "openPanel": true, "player": { "pause": true } }
```

| Key | What Kino does |
| --- | --- |
| `openPanel` | `true` opens your plugin's player panel (the one your `panel` export draws: it needs a `panel` block, or a [contributed tab](player-panel.md#contributed-tab)). If the panel is already open it is not switched to your tab. Without a panel of yours in that player it is logged and ignored. |
| `player` | An ordinary panel [`player` action](player-panel.md#player) (`seekToMs`, `pause`, `speed`, `resize`...), read by the panel's own reader and then by the same rules as a press in a panel: the plugin of the title playing keeps its fields, any other plugin only a seek (with the approved [`playerControl`](rooms.md#player-control) capability: a seek, `pause` and `speed`). Kino's gate applies (one seek or pause a second, nothing under a Kino dialog or while the person seeks, 30 controlled actions a minute), and a controlled action shows a notice naming your plugin. |

## The context { #context }

`context` is the player panel's context for the title playing (see [`panel(context)`](player-panel.md#context)) plus
`live: true | false`. Which one you get depends on what plays and who may know it:

| What plays | `context` |
| --- | --- |
| A title of **your own** plugin | The panel's full context: `kind`, `ref`, `title`, ids, position, your saved values... and `live: false`. |
| A title of **another** plugin (never 18+) | The contributed-panel context: an opaque `ref`, `foreign: true`, `source: { pluginId, name }`, and `live: false`. |
| A title that reaches no other plugin (18+, a title no plugin owns such as one of Kino's own sources, or a title Kino cannot confirm is the one playing) | The **bare** context: only `live`, `foreign: true`, `device`, `lang` and `features`. **No `kind`**, not even movie or series: code that reads `context.kind` must cope with it missing. |
| An En vivo channel its provider confirmed | The live panel's context (`kind: "live"`, `live: true`, `channel`, `foreign`, `source`...), see [Your tab on a live channel](player-panel.md#live-kinds). |
| Any other En vivo channel | The bare context with `live: true`. |

Read `live` and `lang` (`es-CO`, `en-US`...: a clock writes its date in it) and treat everything else as possibly missing.

## On an En vivo channel { #live }

- **`fixed` elements always show; `overlay` ones show with the channel card** (the card that comes up on a zap and hides after
  about 3 seconds), and fade with it.
- **Reaching a button: the Menu key.** Up and Down keep zapping channels, so they cannot enter the row. Menu brings the card up
  and focuses the first button; Left and Right walk the buttons, Down or Back return to the video (Back does not close the
  player). While a button has focus the card stays up. **A remote without a Menu key, such as the Chromecast with Google TV's,
  cannot reach a live button**: do not make a live-only function depend on one.
- **A press on a channel can do very little.** On a channel a plugin always counts as another plugin, so Kino keeps only a seek
  (or with `playerControl` also `pause` and `speed`), and a channel has no timeline: `seekToMs`, `seekStepMs`, `speed`, `skip`,
  `markers` and `autoNext` are dropped with a log line, and `resize` is never kept for another plugin. What survives is **`pause`
  (true or false), and only with the approved `playerControl` capability**, which a slot-only plugin cannot hold. `openPanel`
  has an effect only when the channel's player offers plugin panel tabs; on a channel without them (an own M3U channel, for
  example) it is ignored and logged.

## On a movie or a series { #vod }

With the controls up, **Up from the progress bar** reaches the first button of the row; Left and Right move between buttons and
Down returns to the bar. With no button on screen (only texts, icons and images, or no slot plugin) Up does exactly what it did
before. Text, icon and image elements are never focusable.

## How it looks { #look }

Kino draws every element with its own look, so none of the screen kit's style properties (`padding`, `color`, `style`...)
applies, and there is no focus `ring` or `key` to set.

- **A text** sits on a translucent dark pill: the player's small label size, white with a shadow (readable over bare video, since
  a `fixed` element shows with the controls gone), the first line Medium and the second Regular, with tabular figures so a
  ticking clock never changes the pill's width; past the width it ends with an ellipsis. Your answer may change the size, weight,
  colour and pill, and nudge it: see [Dressing a text and placing an element](#dress).
- **A button** is a round button (icon only) or a pill (with a label), on the same translucent fill until it has focus.
- **Order:** elements keep the order you declared, `overlay` ones to the left of `fixed` ones, so a fixed element never moves
  when the overlay ones come and go.

Kino's own type changed in the same release (lighter weights in its own screens); the slot keeps the look described here, and
[plugin screens](screens.md) keep the type scale they always had: headings are still bold.

## Consent and the switch { #consent }

- **`fixed` is the one that asks.** A plugin with a `fixed` element shows a red line on its install sheet: "Mostrará algo suyo de
  forma permanente en el reproductor mientras ves un video" ("Will keep something of its own on screen in the player while you
  watch a video"). An update that adds a `fixed` element asks again, marked as new, and Kino never approves it on its own; a kit
  import starts it unticked. An overlay-only slot shows no line and needs no approval.
- **Per device.** A `fixed` slot's approval never carries over from a peer device or a backup: the person approves it again on
  each device.
- **The person's switch**, in your plugin's tab in Ajustes: "Dejar que muestre algo en el reproductor" ("Let it show something
  in the player"). It covers the whole device and syncs to the person's other devices; off, Kino stops calling you at once.
- **A press is the person's own action; a `playerSlot` call is not.** The context follows the same privacy rules as a panel's,
  and the bare one is all a title Kino cannot share gets.

## Testing it with the kit { #kit }

```bash
node sdk/run.mjs <folder> playerSlot [ref]                         # the frame: items in declared order, refreshMs clamped; drops on stderr
node sdk/run.mjs <folder> playerSlotAction <ref> <button id>       # the request: { openPanel, player, controlled }
node sdk/run.mjs --foreign <plugin id>[:<name>] <folder> playerSlot <ref>   # a title another plugin owns
node sdk/run.mjs --bare <folder> playerSlot                        # a private title's context (no kind)
node sdk/run.mjs --live-channel tdt:la1:La 1 <folder> playerSlot - # an En vivo channel's
node sdk/run.mjs --bare --live-channel tdt:la1:La 1 <folder> playerSlot -   # a channel Kino cannot confirm
node sdk/validate.mjs <folder>                                      # also prints the red consent line of a fixed element
```

- `--context '<json>'` merges your JSON over the kit's fake context (for example `{"lang":"en-US"}`). The ref is `-` with
  `--live-channel` or `--bare`.
- `validate` checks the `slot` block against the contract and that the entry exports `playerSlot` and `playerSlotAction`, and
  (with `--run playerSlot`) calls the export and reads its answer as Kino does.
- The kit cannot say how a frame looks on a TV: for that, install the plugin on a device with a remote.

See also [Test it locally](test-locally.md) and [The player panel](player-panel.md).


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/customize/ (docs/customize.en.md) -->

# Customize your plugin

Everything a plugin can change in how Kino shows it, in one place, each with a short example and the
page that has the full rules. Most of it is new in `"apiVersion": 6` (Kino 0.9.50): declare 6 only if
you use one of those, because Kino 0.9.49 and older refuse an apiVersion 6 plugin.

## At a glance { #overview }

| What | Where the person sees it | How | apiVersion | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Name, description, author | the consent sheet and every card of your plugin | `name`, `description`, `author` | 1 | [The manifest](manifest.md) |
| Icon | your plugin's cards (Ajustes ▸ Plugins, Recomendados, "De la comunidad") | `icon`: a square `.png`, at most 128 KB | 1 | [The manifest](manifest.md) |
| Accent color | your plugin's tab and chips, your name over your search results | `color`: `#RRGGBB` | 1 | [The manifest](manifest.md) |
| Marketplace chips | the category chips of Recomendados, "De la comunidad", "Elige tus plugins" | `categories` in the manifest | any | [The manifest](manifest.md) |
| A settings form and its own Ajustes tab | Ajustes ▸ <your plugin> | `settings` (`list` from 4) | 1 | [The settings form](settings-form.md#types) |
| Headings, status lines, buttons, checks before saving | the same tab | `section`, `status`, `action` settings; `settingsStatus`, `action`, `validateSettings` | 6 | [The settings form](settings-form.md) |
| A help button and a button that opens an address | the same tab (and the Configurar form of a sync provider) | `help` and `link` settings | 12 | [Configuration aids](settings-form.md#aids) |
| "Is this you?" and filling your own settings | the same tab | an `action` that answers `link` or `setSettings` | any (Kino 0.9.74) | [The settings form](settings-form.md#link) |
| Your status line as a sync provider | Ajustes de todos los perfiles ▸ Sincronización ▸ Proveedor | `syncStatus` | 12 | [Sync providers](sync-providers.md#settings) |
| Colors | your section, your Ajustes tab, your group title in Categorías, the player's accent while you play | `theme` | 6 | [Your colors](section-theme.md#theme) |
| A look for the whole app | every screen of Kino, the player controls, the menu logo; picked in Ajustes ▸ Apariencia | `appThemes` (optionally `go.useTheme` on your screen) | 18 | [App themes](themes.md) |
| A section of your own, with tabs and a banner | TV sidebar, phone chip strip atop Inicio | `"section": { "label" }` + `section({ tab })` | 6 | [A section of your own](section-theme.md#section) |
| Tiles in Categorías | Categorías, a group named after you | `categories()` (with `browse`) | 6 | [Your own categories](section-theme.md#categories) |
| Home rows, "Ver más" and their genre | Inicio, Categorías | `home()` rows with `ref` and `genre` | 1 | [The contract](contract.md#paging) |
| Channels in your Home rows | Inicio | `kind: "live"` items in `home()` | 6 | [Live channels](live-channels.md#home-rows) |
| Search inside your "Ver más" pages | "Buscar en esta categoría" | `scopedSearch` | 6 | [The contract](contract.md#scoped-search) |
| 18+ entries | everywhere, only with the 18+ code unlocked | `adult: true` | 6 | [18+ content](contract.md#adult) |
| Names of the copies of a video | the player's Servidor menu | `Stream.label`, `alternatives` with `label` | 6 | [Labelled and lazy copies](contract.md#lazy-copies) |
| Skip buttons | "Saltar intro", "Saltar outro" | `Stream.skip` | any | [The contract](contract.md#stream) |
| Skip buttons on any title, from any source | "Saltar intro", "Saltar outro" | `segments` | 7 | [Where the intro and credits are](contract.md#segments) |
| Audio and subtitle names | the player's "Audio y subtítulos" menu | `audioTracks[].label`, `subtitles[].lang` | 1 | [The contract](contract.md#stream) |
| Your own sentence on an error | "Mensaje de <your plugin>: …" | `kino.error(code, detail, { userMessage })` | 6 | [Your own sentence](contract.md#user-message) |
| Subtitles for any title | "Buscar subtítulos en línea" | the `subtitles` export | any | [Subtitles for any title](contract.md#subtitles) |
| Info pages of other plugins' titles | a title's info page, where TMDB had nothing; from Kino 0.9.51 a logo instead of the name, other sites' ratings and the cast | `meta` (`logo`, `ratings`, `cast`) | 6 | [Describing other titles](contract.md#meta) |
| A tracker's switch and its status | "Enviar lo que veo" and "No pudo avisar a …" in your Ajustes tab | `tracking` | 7 | [Telling a tracker](contract.md#tracking) |
| Channels, logos, numbers, guide | En vivo, TV guide, channel drawer | `channels` | 3 | [Live channels](live-channels.md) |

## Your plugin's identity { #identity }

```json
{
  "id": "mi-cine", "name": "Mi cine", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 6, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Cine colombiano y latinoamericano, con subtítulos",
  "author": "ana", "homepage": "https://github.com/ana/mi-cine",
  "icon": "icon.png",
  "color": "#3D5AFE",
  "categories": ["movies", "series"],
  "hosts": ["api.example.com"],
  "capabilities": ["search", "home", "browse", "episodes", "resolve"]
}
```

- Write `name` and `description` in Spanish: they are what every card shows. `description` is at most
  300 characters, `name` 40.
- `icon` is a path next to the manifest, never `./icon.png`. A missing or too-big icon is skipped, never
  fatal.
- `color` paints your tab and chips and your name over your search results. `theme` (below) goes much
  further, from apiVersion 6.
- `categories` only tags your plugin for the marketplace chips. It is not the `categories()` export,
  which puts tiles inside Kino's Categorías.

## Your settings tab { #settings }

Every enabled plugin gets its own tab in Ajustes, with its [Modo debug](diagnostics.md#debug) switch; one
with `settings` shows their form there too. Eleven field types (`text`, `password`,
`url`, `toggle`, `select`, `list`, from apiVersion 6 `section`, `status`, `action`, and from apiVersion 12
`link` and `help`), defaults,
required fields, a check before saving and buttons that run your code:

```json
"settings": [
  { "key": "account", "label": "Tu cuenta", "type": "section", "hint": "Opcional" },
  { "key": "email", "label": "Correo", "type": "text" },
  { "key": "password", "label": "Contraseña", "type": "password" },
  { "key": "linked", "label": "Estado", "type": "status" },
  { "key": "logout", "label": "Cerrar sesión", "type": "action", "confirm": "¿Cerrar la sesión?" },
  { "key": "quality", "label": "Calidad", "type": "select", "default": "hd",
    "options": [{ "value": "hd", "label": "Alta" }, { "value": "sd", "label": "Ahorro de datos" }] }
]
```

```js
export async function settingsStatus() {
  return { linked: kino.config.get("email") ? "Cuenta vinculada" : "Sin cuenta" };
}

export async function action(key) {
  if (key === "logout") return { message: "Sesión cerrada", clearSettings: ["email", "password"] };
  return null;
}
```

Every type and attribute, `validateSettings` and a complete example: [The settings form](settings-form.md).
There are no conditional fields: every setting always shows.

## Your section, your tiles, your colors { #section-theme }

```json
"apiVersion": 6,
"section": { "label": "Mi cine" },
"theme": { "accent": "#3D5AFE", "onAccent": "#FFFFFF", "background": "#101820", "surface": "#1A2733", "highlight": "#F7C948" }
```

```js
export async function section({ tab }) {                 // tab is null the first time
  const tabs = [{ id: "pelis", label: "Películas" }, { id: "series", label: "Series" }];
  const chosen = tabs.some((t) => t.id === tab) ? tab : "pelis";
  return {
    tabs, tab: chosen,
    hero: { title: "Estreno de la semana", text: "Una película nueva cada viernes.", image: "https://img.example.com/hero.jpg" },
    rows: await rowsFor(chosen),                         // the same rows as home()
  };
}

export async function categories() {                     // needs the browse capability
  return [
    { id: "comedia", title: "Comedia", ref: "genre:comedia", art: "https://img.example.com/comedia.jpg" },
    { id: "terror", title: "Terror", ref: "genre:terror" },
  ];
}
```

Kino checks every color for readability when it uses it and falls back to its own for a color that
fails (`node sdk/run.mjs . theme` shows the ratios). Errors stay in Kino's red. The rules:
[Section, categories and colors](section-theme.md).

## Home rows { #home }

```js
export async function home() {
  return [
    { id: "nuevas", title: "Recién llegadas", ref: "nuevas", genre: "peliculas", items: newest },
    { id: "canales", title: "Canales de Colombia", genre: "noticias", items: [   // apiVersion 6
      { id: "canal-1", ref: "live:1", title: "Canal Uno", kind: "live", poster: "https://img.example.com/c1.png" },
    ] },
  ];
}
```

- A row with a `ref` (and the `browse` capability) ends in "Ver más"; with `scopedSearch` you answer the
  search inside it yourself.
- `genre` is how Categorías groups browsable rows of every plugin, and how the Home by categories places
  your content. On a row it accepts any category (an id such as `peliculas`, `series`, `anime`,
  `documentales`..., an alias, or a new one that is appended at the end); on a live category or a playlist it
  is still one of ten ids, and the older Categorías tab uses only those ten. Without it Kino guesses from the title. [Home categories](categories.md).
- Each item can carry `badges` (up to 3 chips such as `"Latino"`, `"4K"`), `quality`, `lang`, `rating`,
  `year`, `genres`, `overview`, a `poster` and a `backdrop`; `ids.tmdb` lets Kino complete its info page.
- `kind: "live"` items stay in Home rows from apiVersion 6, as channel cards with the "En vivo" badge.
- `adult: true` keeps an entry hidden until the person unlocks their 18+ code.
- Your rows come after Kino's own, under your plugin's name. Rules: [The contract](contract.md#validation).

## In the player { #player }

```js
export async function resolve(ref) {
  const servers = await listServers(ref);              // [{ id, lang, name }]
  const first = await resolveServer(ref, servers[0]);
  return {
    url: first.url,
    label: `${servers[0].lang} · ${servers[0].name}`,   // "Latino · Servidor 1" in the Servidor menu
    alternatives: servers.slice(1, 9).map((s) => ({ label: `${s.lang} · ${s.name}`, ref: `${ref}|${s.id}` })),
    audioTracks: first.dubs.map((d) => ({ lang: d.lang, url: d.url, label: d.name })),  // "Español (Latinoamérica)"
    subtitles: first.subs.map((s) => ({ lang: s.lang, url: s.url })),
    durationMs: first.durationMs,
    skip: { openingStartMs: 62_000, openingEndMs: 152_000, endingStartMs: 1_290_000 },
  };
}
```

- `label` and lazy `{ label, ref }` copies (apiVersion 6) fill the **Servidor** section of the player's
  "Audio y subtítulos" menu; a copy is resolved only when the person picks it or the automatic
  fallback reaches it ([Labelled and lazy copies](contract.md#lazy-copies)).
- `audioTracks[].label` is shown as is in the audio menu; without it Kino names the track from `lang`.
- `skip` puts "Saltar intro" and "Saltar outro" on screen; a correction the person makes by hand wins.
- With a `theme`, the player's progress bar, slider and focus border take your `accent` while your
  content plays.

## Your own words { #words }

```js
throw kino.error("not_found", "E404", { userMessage: "Este capítulo ya no está disponible." });
```

The person reads "Mensaje de Mi cine: Este capítulo ya no está disponible." instead of Kino's line, only
when the sentence passes [the safety rules](contract.md#user-message) (Spanish, at most 160 characters,
no links, never asking for money, credentials or contact data). Status lines and action messages of your settings
form are your words too ([The settings form](settings-form.md)).

## What you cannot change { #limits }

- Kino's own screens, fonts and layout, the order of Inicio (your rows go after Kino's own) and the
  player's background and surfaces.
- Error colors: always Kino's red, whatever your `theme` says.
- Conditional settings: every field always shows.
- Anything that runs outside your exports: no screens of your own, no notifications, no background jobs.
  Kino calls you; you answer with data.
- Whether the person's 18+ code is unlocked: you only mark entries `adult: true`, Kino decides.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/settings-form/ (docs/settings-form.en.md) -->

# The settings form (apiVersion 6)

The usual [settings](manifest.md#settings) hold values your code reads with `kino.config`. From
`"apiVersion": 6` (Kino 0.9.50) the form can also **show** and **do** things, and every installed plugin
gets its own tab in Ajustes. This page has [every field type](#types), the three types without
a value, the [two configuration aids](#aids) of apiVersion 12, the exports that fill and check them, and
[a complete example](#example).

!!! tip "For a new UI, use screens"
    From apiVersion 14 (Kino 0.9.74) the preferred way to build your plugin's configuration, onboarding
    or a dashboard is [screens](screens.md), which can also show this very form with the
    [`settings` node](screen-forms.md#settings-node). This form keeps working for compatibility.

## Its own tab in Ajustes { #own-tab }

Every installed plugin that is enabled gets **its own tab in Ajustes** (phone and TV), named after the
plugin, with its [Modo debug](diagnostics.md#debug) switch; when it has `settings` the tab holds their
form too, and Plugins ▸ Configurar opens the same form. That is why, from Kino 0.9.50,
the `auth_required` error reads "Configura {plugin} en Ajustes ▸ {plugin}" when your plugin declares
settings.

## Every field type { #types }

The form shows your settings **in the order of the manifest**, each with its `label` and, under it, its
`hint`. Eleven types, and a twelfth, `qr`, from apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74):

| `type` | What the person sees | What `kino.config.get(key)` returns | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | a text field (at most 500 characters) | the text, or `undefined` | apiVersion 1 |
| `password` | a hidden text field (at most 500), kept encrypted on the device | the text, or `undefined` | apiVersion 1 |
| `url` | an address field (at most 2,048): `http`/`https`; that server becomes a host your plugin may reach ([The person's own servers](manifest.md#own-servers)) | the address as typed, or `undefined` | apiVersion 1 |
| `toggle` | a switch | `true` / `false` (`false` when there is no `default`) | apiVersion 1 |
| `select` | a choice among `options` | the chosen `value` (the first option when there is no `default`) | apiVersion 1 |
| `list` | a list the person builds with "Agregar", each entry a dialog of the list's `fields` | an array of `{ [field key]: string }`, or `undefined` when empty | apiVersion 4 |
| `section` | a heading, with `hint` as its explanation | nothing | apiVersion 6 |
| `status` | a read-only line your `settingsStatus()` fills | nothing | apiVersion 6 |
| `action` | a button that runs your `action(key)` | nothing | apiVersion 6 |
| `link` | a button that opens an `https` address through the system, only when the person taps it ([Configuration aids](#aids)) | nothing | apiVersion 12 |
| `help` | a button ("Ayuda") that opens your instructions in a modal ([Configuration aids](#aids)) | nothing | apiVersion 12 |
| `qr` | a QR code drawn on the device from a text your `settingsStatus()` returns ([A QR code](#qr)) | nothing | apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74) |

What each entry may carry:

| Attribute | Types | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | all | required, `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,31}$`, unique in the list |
| `label` | all | required, 1 to 40 characters (optional on a `help`: without it the button says "Ayuda") |
| `type` | all | required, one of the eleven above |
| `hint` | all | optional, at most 80 characters: the example or explanation under the field. On a `section`, up to 300, wrapped over several lines (Kino 0.9.51; builds before 0.9.51 refuse one over 80) |
| `required` | `text`, `password`, `url`, `list` | optional `true`/`false`. A required setting with no value stops every call ("Falta configurar") |
| `default` | `text`, `password`, `toggle`, `select` | optional. Never on `url` or `list` ("… no puede tener valor por defecto: usa "hint"") nor on the types without a value; it must fit its type (a `select` default is one of its `values`) |
| `options` | `select` only | required: 1 to 20 `{ "value", "label" }`, `value` 1..40 characters and unique, `label` 1..40 |
| `fields` | `list` only | required: 1 to 4, each `{ key, label, type, hint?, required? }` with `type` `"text"` or `"url"`, no `default` ("Solo un ajuste de tipo list tiene "fields"") |
| `max` | `list` only | optional whole number 1..50 (default 20): how many entries |
| `confirm` | `action` only, apiVersion 6 | optional, 1 to 120 characters: asked before the action runs, with Cancelar focused ("Solo un ajuste de tipo action tiene "confirm"") |
| `url` | `link` only, apiVersion 12 | required: `https://`, no user name or password, at most 2,048 characters |
| `title`, `titleEn`, `body`, `bodyEn` | `help` only, apiVersion 12 | the modal's title (at most 60) and text (at most 2,000); `body` or `bodyEn` is required |
| `labelEn`, `hintEn`, `confirmEn` | those of `label`, `hint`, `confirm` | optional, apiVersion 9 (Kino 0.9.55): the same text in English, with the same limits ([English texts](#english)) |
| `devices` | all | optional, apiVersion 12: `["phone"]`, `["tv"]` or both, the devices that draw it ([one kind of device](#devices)) |
| `linkOnly` | `action` | optional `true`/`false`, apiVersion 12: never drawn, run only as a link's `confirm` ([linkOnly](#link-only)) |
| `sync` | `password`, `text` | optional `true`/`false`, apiVersion 13 (Kino 0.9.74): `false` keeps the value on this device ([sync: false](#sync-false)) |

Any other key in an entry is ignored. A manifest that breaks a rule is refused at install with a
message that names the setting (`El ajuste "quality" necesita opciones`); a `list` below apiVersion 4
a `section`/`status`/`action` below apiVersion 6 or a `link`/`help` below apiVersion 12 is refused too.
Limits: 12 settings with a value (`text`, `password`, `url`, `toggle`, `select`, `list`) plus, from
apiVersion 6, 16 without one (among them, from apiVersion 12, at most 4 `link` and 4 `help`).

There are **no conditional fields**: every setting is always shown, whatever another one holds. Use a
`section` with a `hint` to say which fields go together ("Opcional: sin cuenta ves el catálogo gratis"),
make them optional, and let [`validateSettings`](#validate) refuse a combination that makes no sense.

**`password` or sealed `secrets`?** A `password` setting is **the person's** credential: they type it,
your code reads it, it syncs to their other devices sealed end to end. A key that belongs to **you**, the
author (a fixed API key of the site's own player), goes in the manifest's sealed
[`secrets`](manifest.md#secrets) instead, and your code only ever holds a marker.

## English texts (apiVersion 9, Kino 0.9.55) { #english }

Kino speaks Spanish or English since 0.9.54 (Ajustes ▸ App ▸ Idioma). From Kino 0.9.55, with `"apiVersion": 9`, each
text of your form can carry its English version next to it, under the same key with `En` at the end:

| Where | English keys | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any setting | `labelEn`, `hintEn` | those of `label` (1 to 40) and `hint` (80; 300 on a `section`) |
| an `action` with `confirm` | `confirmEn` | 1 to 120, and only next to `confirm` |
| a `select`'s option | `labelEn` | 1 to 40 |
| a `list` field | `labelEn`, `hintEn` | 1 to 40 and 80 |
| the manifest's `section` | `labelEn` | 1 to 20 ([The manifest](manifest.md)) |

```json
{ "key": "quality", "label": "Calidad", "labelEn": "Quality", "type": "select",
  "hint": "La más alta gasta más datos", "hintEn": "The highest uses more data",
  "options": [{ "value": "hd", "label": "Alta", "labelEn": "High" }, { "value": "sd", "label": "Normal" }] }
```

- **The usual text is the Spanish one and the fallback**: with the app in English, Kino shows every English version
  there is and, where one is missing, the usual text (above, the "Normal" option reads the same in both languages).
  With the app in Spanish nothing changes.
- **Your code never notices**: keys, types, values and `default`s are the same in both languages, and `kino.config`
  returns the same. To know the language, read [`kino.lang`](kino-api.md#lang).
- **From apiVersion 9**: below 9 these keys are unknown and ignored without being checked, as on an older Kino (which
  does not take `"apiVersion": 9` either).
- **The same rules as the usual text**: an empty one, one over the limit or one that is not a text refuses the manifest
  at install ("\"labelEn\" del ajuste \"quality\" debe ser un texto de 1 a 40 caracteres"; on an option, "Una opción
  del ajuste \"quality\" no es válida"); `null` is the same as leaving it out. `confirmEn` only goes on an `action`
  ("Solo un ajuste de tipo action tiene \"confirmEn\"") and next to `confirm` ("…necesita también \"confirm\"").
- Kino only speaks Spanish and English: any other language key (`labelPt`, `labelFr`) is an unknown key and ignored.

`node sdk/validate.mjs` checks the same limits and, once your plugin uses an English version, tells you how many texts
have one and which do not.

## Three types that hold no value { #ui-types }

From apiVersion 6 there are three types that hold no value (never in `kino.config`, never `required`,
no `default`), at most 16 of them on top of the 12 valued settings:

```json
"settings": [
  { "key": "account", "label": "Tu cuenta", "type": "section", "hint": "Opcional: sin cuenta usas la sesión anónima" },
  { "key": "email", "label": "Correo", "type": "text" },
  { "key": "password", "label": "Contraseña", "type": "password" },
  { "key": "linked", "label": "Estado", "type": "status" },
  { "key": "logout", "label": "Cerrar sesión", "type": "action", "confirm": "¿Cerrar la sesión de esta cuenta?" }
]
```

- **`section`**: a heading; `hint` is its explanation.
- **`status`**: a read-only line. Kino calls your `settingsStatus()` when the form opens (10 s) and
  shows the text you return under that key: `{ linked: "Vinculada como ana@…" }` (at most 200
  characters). Until it answers the line reads "Cargando…"; a missing key or a value that is not a text
  shows "Sin información"; a timeout or an error shows "No se pudo consultar". The rest of the form keeps
  working either way. **Required export** when a `status` setting exists.
- **`action`**: a button. Kino calls your `action(key)` (30 s), one action at a time (the other buttons
  and Guardar wait), and shows the `message` you return (at most 300 characters) or "Listo"; if it throws
  or times out, the person sees the error text instead. Kino asks `settingsStatus()` again after every action (and when the form opens), so the status lines describe what it just did; `refresh: true` is still accepted and changes nothing.
  `confirm` (1 to 120 characters) asks first, with Cancelar focused. **Required export** when an
  `action` setting exists.

## A QR code: `qr` (apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #qr }

A fourth type that holds no value, counted among the 16: a QR code drawn on the form, on the device (nothing goes to a
network to draw it). It is how a TV shows a login code for a phone to scan.

```json
{ "key": "login", "label": "Escanéalo desde tu teléfono", "labelEn": "Scan it from your phone", "type": "qr", "refreshMs": 5000 }
```

- **Its text** is what your `settingsStatus()` returns under that key, like a `status` line, but kept whole: 1 to 512
  characters with no control character; an `http`/`https` address only https on a public host (never the home network);
  any other text (an app link such as `exampleapp://login?token=…`, a pairing code) is drawn as it is. A longer text, a
  non-text or one that holds one of your sealed secrets draws no QR, and a `qr` with no text draws nothing at all (no
  label, no placeholder line, no empty row), so a QR that only one step of a sign-in needs simply is not there in the
  others.
- **`refreshMs`** (2000 to 60000; only a `qr` setting has it): Kino asks `settingsStatus()` when the form opens, after
  every action and every that many ms while the form is on screen and the app in front. A refresh never starts while the
  previous call is still running, and the QR on screen stays up until the new text replaces it. That is how a code that
  expires every 30 s stays scannable, and how a status line next to it turns into "Listo" once the code was used.
- **Required export:** `settingsStatus`. Showing a QR needs no capability; scanning one (`kino.qr.scan`) needs `qrScan`.
  The whole two-device recipe: [QR codes](qr.md#recipe).

## Hiding items while they are not needed (`hide`, apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #status-hide }

Your `settingsStatus()` answer may carry `hide`: a list of keys of your own settings that the form (phone and TV) does
not draw while that answer is current. Use it for a form that changes with a step: the sign-in button, its QR and the
password step once the person is signed in, or "Cerrar sesión" while signed out.

```js
export async function settingsStatus() {
  if (signedIn()) return { status: "Conectado", hide: ["qr_login", "login_qr", "tg_password", "check_password"] };
  return { status: "Falta iniciar sesión", hide: ["logout"] };
}
```

- Their stored values stay and nothing is deleted; they still count for the form's own rules (a `required` one you
  hide still blocks Guardar).
- Unknown keys and non-strings are ignored, at most 32 entries are read, and a failed answer hides nothing.
- Kino asks `settingsStatus()` again after every action, so the form follows the step the action just reached.
- Below apiVersion 13 the key is ignored. `sdk/contract.mjs` exports `statusHide(answer, manifest)`, which gives the
  keys the app would hide.

## Configuration aids: `link` and `help` (apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74) { #aids }

Two setting types help the person configure your plugin. Neither holds a value (never in
`kino.config`, never `required`, no `default`), and both count among the 16 settings without a value.

```json
"settings": [
  { "key": "steps", "type": "help", "title": "Qué necesitas", "titleEn": "What you need",
    "body": "1. Crea un bot con @BotFather y copia su token.\n2. Pégalo aquí y toca Guardar.",
    "bodyEn": "1. Create a bot with @BotFather and copy its token.\n2. Paste it here and tap Save." },
  { "key": "botfather", "type": "link", "label": "Abrir @BotFather", "labelEn": "Open @BotFather", "url": "https://t.me/BotFather" },
  { "key": "botToken", "label": "Token del bot", "type": "password" }
]
```

- **`link`**: a button that opens `url` through the system **only when the person taps it** (on a
  phone, `https://t.me/...` opens the Telegram app when it is installed). Kino shows its own "Abrir
  enlace" and the host under the button, makes no request to that host, and does not count it as a
  network access of your plugin. On a TV (usually without a browser) the tap shows the address as text
  and as a QR to open on a phone. `url` must be `https://`, without a user name or password, at most
  2,048 characters; `label` is required. An address that holds one of your stored secrets is not shown.
  Kino opens the canonical form of the address (host in lower case), the same one it names. There is no
  other way for a plugin to have Kino open an address.
- **`help`**: a small button ("Ayuda" / "Help", or your own `label`) that opens a modal with your
  instructions, titled with your plugin's name. Plain text only: newlines are kept, markup is shown
  literally, nothing in it is tappable (use a `link` for an address). `title` at most 60 characters,
  `body` at most 2,000 (`body` or `bodyEn` is required); a missing Spanish or English text falls back to
  the other; everything is scrubbed of your secrets. On a TV it scrolls with the remote, focus starts on
  Cerrar and Back closes it.

A link's label and a help's label, title and body may not hold control characters (a body keeps its
line breaks), invisible formatting or direction overrides; the manifest is refused otherwise. At most 4
links and 4 helps per plugin. Older Kino builds refuse apiVersion 12, so a plugin that uses them
declares `"apiVersion": 12`.

**Keep the help short and practical**: what the plugin needs and where to get it, in a few lines. If
the plugin talks to a server the person runs, the help does not teach how to build it: add a `link` to
the complete guide (the technical cap of 2,000 characters is not a target).

## Settings for one kind of device (`devices`, apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74) { #devices }

Any settings item (a field, a section, a status, an action, a link or a help) may say which devices
draw it: `"devices": ["phone"]`, `["tv"]` or both; without it the item shows everywhere.

```json
{ "key": "botToken", "label": "Token del bot", "labelEn": "Bot token", "type": "password", "devices": ["phone"] }
```

It is only about drawing. On a device it leaves out, the form neither draws nor checks the item (a
hidden `required` field never blocks Guardar there), but its value is still stored, saved back
unchanged, synced to the person's other devices, handed over by `sync.provision` and read by your code
through `kino.config`. Use it for setup a TV cannot do well, like a token pasted on the phone: Sync-Gram
and Sync Servidor draw their setup only on the phone, and the TV receives the values with "Recibir
configuración" ("Receive settings"). An unknown device, an empty list or a repeated one refuses the manifest (`"devices" of the
setting "<key>" must be a list of different devices: "phone", "tv"`); below apiVersion 12 the key is
ignored. The Node kit renders no form: `validate.mjs` only checks the field.

## A setting the 18+ code guards (`unlockWith`, apiVersion 14, Kino 0.9.74) { #unlock-with }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.74"
    Available from Kino 0.9.74. Below apiVersion 14 the key is ignored.

A `toggle` or a `select` may say `"unlockWith": "adultCode"`: before the person moves it **away from its
`default`** (a toggle off its default, a select to any other option), Kino asks the device's 18+ code with its own
prompt (the «Código» field of Ajustes on the phone, the padlock's keyboard dialog on a TV; while the default code still
rules, the prompt says so, as every 18+ prompt does). The change applies only once the code is right; a wrong code says
«Código incorrecto» and keeps the old value, and Cancelar or Back leave the control as it was. Moving it back **toward**
the default never asks. Your plugin never sees the code, and giving it unlocks nothing else (no 18+ entry shows because
of it). Use it for a filter the person should not switch off on a whim, like the news example's «No mostrar noticias
+18» (default on).

```json
{ "key": "hideAdult", "label": "No mostrar noticias +18", "labelEn": "Hide 18+ news", "type": "toggle", "default": true, "unlockWith": "adultCode" }
```

It works in Kino's settings form wherever it is drawn: your tab in Ajustes, and a screen's or a panel's
[`settings` node](screen-forms.md#settings-node). Your own code may only move the setting toward its default: an
answer's `config` that moves it away is dropped (`is locked (unlockWith adultCode): only the person moves it away from
its default, in Kino's settings form`), an action's `setSettings` that does is refused whole, and a field may not
`bind` it (`bind "<key>" is locked (unlockWith adultCode): show it in a settings node`): show it with
`{ "type": "settings", "keys": ["<key>"] }`. The value syncs to the person's other devices like any setting (and
travels with «Enviar a otro aparato»); the code is asked on each device at the moment of the change. `unlockWith` on any
other type, or a value other than `"adultCode"`, refuses the manifest (`Only a setting of type toggle or select has
"unlockWith" ("<key>")`, `"unlockWith" of the setting "<key>" must be one of: adultCode`). The Node kit renders no
form: `validate.mjs` checks the field and `run.mjs` applies the same `config`, `bind` and `setSettings` rules.

## Actions only a link runs (`linkOnly`, apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74) { #link-only }

An `action` may say `"linkOnly": true`: it is never drawn on any device and runs only as the `confirm`
of another action's [`link`](#link), after Kino's own question. A "find, then confirm" pair then shows
the person one button (Sync-Gram's *Verificar mensaje en el chat*); without it the confirm action is a
second button. `linkOnly` on anything but an action, or not a boolean, refuses the manifest.

## Forgetting settings from an action (`clearSettings`) { #clear-settings }

An action may also **forget settings of your own** with `clearSettings`: up to 12 keys of your declared
valued settings (`text`, `url`, `password`, `toggle`, `select`, `list`). After the action returns, Kino
empties them exactly as if the person had emptied the fields and pressed Guardar (a `password` also
leaves the Keystore), closes your sandbox and forgets cookies and cached Home rows as for any saved
change (`kino.storage` survives), reloads the form and asks `settingsStatus()` again; your `message` is
still shown. It is how a "Cerrar sesión" button stops the next expired token from signing the person in
again with the saved account.

```js
export async function action(key) {
  if (key === "logout") {
    await api.logout();                       // tell the server first: a throw here keeps the saved account
    return { message: "Sesión cerrada", clearSettings: ["email", "password"] };
  }
}
```

(`email` and `password` must be optional settings here; mark the account `required` only if the plugin
cannot work signed out.)

Limits:

- Only the action's own plugin is ever touched.
- An entry that is not a string, is unknown, names a `section`/`status`/`action`, names a `required`
  setting (clearing it would make every later call fail), repeats, or comes after the twelfth is dropped
  with a log line (`run.mjs` shows `[dropped by Kino]`); a value that is not an array is ignored.
- An action that throws or times out clears nothing.

## Filling your own settings from an action (`setSettings`, Kino 0.9.74) { #set-settings }

An action may also **fill settings of your own** with `setSettings`: up to 8 keys of your `text` or
`select` settings, each with a string value. It is how a "Vincular" action stores the chat it found, so
the person types nothing. Kino trims each value, checks it like a typed one (length, one of the
options) and saves the values through the form's own Guardar: they reach the person's other devices and
stay in the profile in use like typed values, and your sandbox closes as for any saved change. It is
additive (no new `apiVersion`): an older Kino ignores it.

```js
return { message: "Vinculado", setSettings: { chatId: String(chat.id) } };
```

- **Never** a `url` (its value becomes a server your plugin may reach, so only the person types one),
  a `toggle`, a `list` or a setting without a value; a `required` setting is never emptied this way.
  A `password` only from `apiVersion` 13 ([below](#set-password)); below it the whole field is refused.
- Kino does **not** run your `validateSettings` on these values (you chose them), and it refuses a value
  that contains one of your stored secrets instead of copying it into a plain, synced setting.
- An unknown or secret key, a value that is not a string or fails its check, a key that is also in
  `clearSettings`, a value that holds one of your stored secrets, or more than 8 keys refuse the
  **whole** field: nothing is applied, your `message` still shows and Kino adds its generic error under it.
- It works from your settings form (any action, including the `confirm` action of a [link](#link)).

### Filling a password (`apiVersion` 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #set-password }

An action may fill one of your own `password` settings, for a value your plugin makes up instead of asking the person to type one:

```js
return { message: "Clave creada", setSettings: { syncKey: kino.crypto.randomBytes(32) } };   // 64 hex characters
```

Kino stores it exactly like a typed password: sealed in the Keystore, synced sealed end to end to the person's other
devices (or kept on this device only when the setting says [`"sync": false`](#sync-false)), and masked in the form. It
is never logged, and every password value your answer names is scrubbed from that same answer's `message` and `link`,
so it is never shown back on the page. The usual rules apply (at most 500 characters, a `required` one never emptied, a
value holding another of your secrets refused). Only an action the person ran fills a setting: a `settingsStatus` answer
is never read for `setSettings`. `node sdk/run.mjs . action <key>` prints such a value masked. A sync provider that only
needs a random key does not need this: [`sync.generateKey`](sync-providers.md#generate-key) makes Kino create it.

## Linking: "Is this you?" (`action.link`, Kino 0.9.74) { #link }

Use it when an action finds **who** to link and the person must say it is them: for example a
[sync provider](sync-providers.md) whose bot reads the latest message ("write something to your bot")
and finds `@ana`. Your plugin never links on its own: it answers a candidate, and Kino asks.

```js
export async function action(key) {
  if (key === "findMe") {
    const who = await bot.latestSender();          // null while nobody wrote yet
    if (!who) return { message: "Escríbele algo a tu bot y vuelve a tocar Buscar" };
    kino.storage.set("pending", who.id);
    return { link: { candidate: "@" + who.username, confirm: "linkMe" } };
  }
  if (key === "linkMe") {                           // runs only after the person confirms
    const chat = kino.storage.get("pending");
    return { message: "Vinculado", setSettings: { chatId: String(chat) } };
  }
}
```

- Kino shows **its own** question, "¿Eres tú, @ana?" / "Is this you, @ana?", and names your plugin in
  it by the `name` of your manifest. It has "Sí, soy yo" / "Yes, it's me" and Cancelar (Cancelar
  focused). You cannot change its words.
- **Cancelar runs nothing**: your plugin is not called and hears nothing. Only **"Sí, soy yo"** runs the
  `confirm` action, exactly once, like a press of that button (same settings, same 30 s). If it cannot
  start right then (another action or a save is running, or the person's unsaved edits cannot be
  saved), the question stays open and says so.
- `candidate`: a string, 1 to 64 characters after trimming, with runs of spaces collapsed to one. It may
  not hold control or invisible formatting characters, any space but the ordinary one, or the fillers
  that draw nothing (U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0, U+2800). It goes through the same secret scrubbing
  as your status lines and is shown as plain text.
- `confirm`: the `key` of **another** `action` setting of your plugin (not the one that is answering)
  that has **no `confirm` question of its own**: an action that asks "¿Borrar todo?" can never be
  presented as "Is this you?".
- Anything else refuses the link: your `message` is still shown, with Kino's generic error ("No se pudo
  completar. Inténtalo de nuevo.") under it.
- A `message` in the same answer is shown too. A `link` in the `confirm` action's own answer is ignored
  (no chains). One question at a time: a newer link replaces a waiting one, and leaving the form drops it.
- An older Kino ignores `link` (it is additive, no new `apiVersion`), so also say in `message` (or a
  status line) what to do.
- An action that only serves as a `confirm` can be hidden with [`"linkOnly": true`](#link-only): the person
  then sees one button, and only Kino's question runs the confirm action.

## Checking before saving (`validateSettings`) { #validate }

`validateSettings(values)` (optional, 20 s) runs **before** Kino saves. `values` holds only the valued
settings: strings trimmed, toggles as booleans, lists as arrays of objects.

- Return `null` to accept.
- `{ password: "La contraseña no es correcta" }` refuses with that text under the field (at most 200
  characters), or a text refuses with a general message. A key that is not one of your valued settings
  also refuses, its text shown as the general message.
- Nothing is saved on a refusal and the person keeps what they typed.
- If it throws, times out or answers something Kino cannot read (an array, a number…), nothing is saved
  either, and the form offers **"Guardar sin comprobar"**; that button is offered only then, never after
  a refusal with messages.

## Common rules { #rules }

- Texts you return are shown after Kino removes any of your stored secrets from them.
- These three exports run even while a `required` setting is still empty, so a status line can say what
  is missing.
- Saving any setting closes your sandbox, as always; `kino.storage` survives.
- If you declare `telemetry`, a failure of `settingsStatus`, `action` or `validateSettings` is reported
  like any other function's ([Logs and telemetry](diagnostics.md)).

Try them with the kit (it prints what the app would keep): `node sdk/run.mjs . settingsStatus`,
`node sdk/run.mjs . action logout`, `node sdk/run.mjs . validateSettings '{"email":"ana@x.co"}'` (or `node sdk/validate.mjs . --run …` with
the same arguments, which also says what Kino shows and flags a call it never makes; `--raw` prints your answer
untouched). The kit does not apply the app's secret scrubbing, and
`validateSettings` receives exactly the JSON you type: the app sends only valued settings, trimmed. A
working example is `plugins/sdk/test/settings-demo` in Kino's repository.

## A complete example { #example }

An account that is optional, a status line, a "Cerrar sesión" button, a quality choice, a switch and a
list of the person's own mirrors, all read the way [`kino.d.ts`](reference/index.md) declares them:

```json
{
  "id": "mi-cuenta", "name": "Mi cuenta", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 6, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": ["api.example.com"],
  "capabilities": ["search", "resolve"],
  "settings": [
    { "key": "account", "label": "Tu cuenta", "type": "section", "hint": "Opcional: sin cuenta ves el catálogo gratis" },
    { "key": "email", "label": "Correo", "type": "text", "hint": "ana@correo.com" },
    { "key": "password", "label": "Contraseña", "type": "password" },
    { "key": "linked", "label": "Estado", "type": "status" },
    { "key": "logout", "label": "Cerrar sesión", "type": "action", "confirm": "¿Cerrar la sesión de esta cuenta?" },
    { "key": "playback", "label": "Reproducción", "type": "section" },
    { "key": "quality", "label": "Calidad", "type": "select", "default": "auto",
      "options": [{ "value": "auto", "label": "Automática" }, { "value": "hd", "label": "Alta" }, { "value": "sd", "label": "Ahorro de datos" }] },
    { "key": "spanishSubs", "label": "Solo subtítulos en español", "type": "toggle", "default": true },
    { "key": "mirrors", "label": "Espejos propios", "type": "list", "max": 5,
      "fields": [{ "key": "url", "label": "Dirección", "type": "url", "required": true, "hint": "https://espejo.example.org" },
                 { "key": "name", "label": "Nombre", "type": "text", "hint": "Espejo de la casa" }] }
  ]
}
```

```js
const API = "https://api.example.com";
// Keyed by the account: settings can change under the plugin (another device, clearSettings).
const sessionKey = () => `session:${kino.config.get("email") ?? ""}`;

async function login(email, password) {
  const r = await kino.fetch(`${API}/login`, { method: "POST", body: { json: { email, password } } });
  if (r.status === 401) throw kino.error("auth_required", "login 401");
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", `login ${r.status}`);
  return r.json().token;
}

async function session() {
  await null;                                    // the first await before anything can throw
  const email = kino.config.get("email");        // undefined: signed out, free catalog
  if (!email) return null;
  const saved = kino.storage.get(sessionKey());
  if (saved) return saved;
  const token = await login(email, kino.config.get("password") ?? "");
  kino.storage.set(sessionKey(), token, { ttlMs: 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000 });
  return token;
}

export async function settingsStatus() {         // one text per "status" key
  const email = kino.config.get("email");
  if (!email) return { linked: "Sin cuenta: ves el catálogo gratis" };
  try {
    await session();
    return { linked: "Cuenta vinculada" };
  } catch (e) {
    return { linked: e.code === "auth_required" ? "El correo o la contraseña no coinciden" : "No se pudo revisar la cuenta ahora" };
  }
}

export async function action(key) {             // one call per "action" button
  if (key !== "logout") return null;
  const token = kino.storage.get(sessionKey());
  if (token) await kino.fetch(`${API}/logout`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
  kino.storage.remove(sessionKey());
  return { message: "Sesión cerrada", clearSettings: ["email", "password"] };
}

export async function validateSettings(values) { // before saving: null accepts
  await null;
  if (values.email && !values.password) return { password: "Escribe la contraseña de esa cuenta" };
  if (values.password && !values.email) return { email: "Escribe el correo de la cuenta" };
  if (values.email) {
    try {
      await login(values.email, values.password);
    } catch (e) {
      if (e.code === "auth_required") return { password: "El correo o la contraseña no coinciden" };
      throw e;                                    // the person may "Guardar sin comprobar"
    }
  }
  return null;
}

export async function search(query) {
  const token = await session();
  const r = await kino.fetch(`${API}/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query.q)}`,
    { headers: token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {} });
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", `search ${r.status}`);
  return r.json().results.map((x) => ({ id: String(x.id), ref: String(x.id), title: x.title, kind: "movie" }));
}

export async function resolve(ref) {
  const token = await session();
  const quality = kino.config.get("quality");    // "auto", "hd" or "sd": a select always has a value
  const r = await kino.fetch(`${API}/play/${encodeURIComponent(ref)}?q=${quality}`,
    { headers: token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {} });
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("not_found", `play ${r.status}`);
  const s = r.json();                            // { url, path, subtitles: [{ lang, url }] }
  const mirrors = kino.config.get("mirrors") ?? []; // [{ url, name? }]: each url is a server the person typed
  return {
    url: s.url,
    label: "Principal",
    subtitles: kino.config.get("spanishSubs") ? s.subtitles.filter((t) => t.lang === "es") : s.subtitles,
    alternatives: mirrors.slice(0, 8).map((m) => ({ url: m.url.replace(/\/+$/, "") + s.path, label: m.name || "Espejo" })),
  };
}
```

What the person gets: a tab "Mi cuenta" in Ajustes with two headings; "Estado" reads "Sin cuenta: ves
el catálogo gratis" until they type an account; Guardar checks the account before saving it;
