"Cerrar sesión" asks first, then empties the correo and the contraseña on every device of theirs; each
mirror shows up as one more copy in the player's Servidor menu.

## A value that stays on this device (`"sync": false`, apiVersion 13, Kino 0.9.74) { #sync-false }

A `password` may say `"sync": false` to stay on the device where the person typed it: use it
for a value that only makes sense once, on one device, such as a two-step verification password your plugin sends right
away and then clears (`clearSettings`). Without it a password reaches the person's paired devices, sealed end to end,
like every other password ([below](#other-devices)).

```json
{ "key": "tg_password", "label": "Contraseña de verificación", "type": "password", "sync": false }
```

- The value is never sent to a paired device, and a value another device sends never sets or clears it.
- It is in no backup and no kit.
- A sync provider's `sync.provision` may still name it, for a **one-shot secret** handed once to a new device (a TV
  that should not type a two-step password): see [Sync providers](sync-providers.md#one-shot). It can never be the
  `sync.keySecret` ("The \"keySecret\" of the \"sync\" field can't name a setting with \"sync\": false").
- Your plugin reads it with `kino.config.get` and clears it as any password.
- **A `text` may say `"sync": false` too**, for a value that must stay on the device but is no secret to hide, such as
  a phone number the person types to sign in on that device: it is drawn as a plain text field (nothing masked) and
  kept exactly like a device-only password (never synced, never in a backup or a kit). It may not appear in
  `sync.provision` ("The \"provision\" of the \"sync\" field can't name a text setting with \"sync\": false").
- `sync` on any other type refuses the manifest ("Only a setting of type password or text has \"sync\" (\"key\")"),
  and so does a value that is not `true` or `false`. Below apiVersion 13, and in a Kino build without it, the key is ignored
  and the password syncs as usual. `node sdk/validate.mjs` checks all of this like the app.

## On the person's other devices { #other-devices }

When the person pairs two of their devices (phone and TV), Kino keeps their plugins in step. What
crosses, and what does not:

- **Crosses:** install, updates, on/off, uninstall, and the host approvals. Each device fetches your
  code itself; only the address and the approval travel. The other device installs **silently** when
  what it fetched asks for nothing beyond what the person approved on the first one; if you now ask for
  more (a new host, permission or capability), it waits in "Plugins de tus otros aparatos" for the
  normal consent sheet.
- **Crosses:** the values of `text`, `select`, `toggle`, `url` and `list` settings (a `list` that has a
  `password` field does not travel), and `password` settings (except a `password` or `text` with `"sync": false`, apiVersion 13), sealed end to end with the key the devices
  agreed when they paired, never readable on the way.
- **Crosses:** clears. A field the person empties, or an action's `clearSettings`, empties it on their
  other devices too (passwords included). A `required` setting is never cleared remotely. A device
  running an older Kino build ignores clears and keeps its value.
- **Never crosses:** `kino.storage`, cookies, the cached Home rows.
- **A sync provider** can also hand its settings to another device with "Enviar configuración" (the
  ones its `sync.provision` names): see [Sync providers](sync-providers.md#provisioning).

A value that arrives this way is applied **without** your `validateSettings`, and, like any saved
change, closes your sandbox. So write the plugin as if a setting can change under it at any time: key
any session you keep in `kino.storage` by the account it belongs to, and never put a device identity in
a setting, because it would be copied to the other device.

```js
const sessionKey = `session:${kino.config.get("email") ?? ""}`;   // not just "session"
```

A [signed](signed.md) plugin installed from two different repositories on two devices counts as the
same plugin when both have the same `id` and the same author key: see
[The same plugin at two addresses](signed.md#two-addresses).


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/images/ (docs/images.en.md) -->

# Images from the plugin (`imageSource`, apiVersion 13) { #images }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.74"
    apiVersion 13 arrives in Kino 0.9.74, together with apiVersion 12. Every Kino before 0.9.74 refuses a manifest with
    `"apiVersion": 13` ("Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino").

Kino draws a poster, backdrop or still from a public URL. Some pictures have no such URL: the thumbnail a messaging
service attaches to a video file, the cover inside a private library, an image behind your service's login. With
`imageSource` your plugin hands Kino an **image reference** instead, and Kino asks your plugin for the bytes when the card
comes on screen. Use it when only your plugin can fetch the picture; a public URL stays the better choice when there is
one (Kino loads it itself, without waking your plugin).

## Declaring it { #declare }

`imageSource` needs `"apiVersion": 13` and the export `image`. No consent line and no approval: it
reaches nothing new, it hands Kino pictures. Below 13 the manifest is refused with "The \"imageSource\" capability needs
apiVersion 13"; without the export the install fails with "El plugin no carga: le falta image".

```json
"apiVersion": 13,
"capabilities": ["home", "search", "resolve", "imageSource"]
```

## The reference { #reference }

Wherever these fields are read, a plugin that declares `imageSource` may answer an object instead of
a URL:

```json
{ "source": "plugin", "handle": "thumb:1234" }
```

- Fields: an item's `poster` and `backdrop` (Home rows, search, "Ver más", your section's rows), an
  episode's `still`, the `poster` and `backdrop` of `episodes().series` and of a `details` answer, and a section hero's
  `image`. Anywhere else (a channel logo, a category's `art`, a `meta` answer, a layout image) a reference is ignored like a
  bad URL, and so is a reference from a plugin that does not declare the capability.
- `handle` is yours and opaque to Kino: 1 to 512 characters, no control character. A malformed reference is no image;
  the item itself stays.
- There is no per-answer cap on references: Kino asks only for the pictures that come on screen, one at a time.
- Strings are always URLs. Kino turns your reference into an address of its own that names your plugin, and only Kino's
  own parser can make one: a string that looks like it is ignored, so no plugin can make Kino ask another plugin for an
  image.

## The `image` export { #export }

Kino calls it with the handle you returned and expects the picture, base64-encoded:

```js
export async function image({ handle }) {
  return { bytes: "<base64 of the picture>", mime: "image/jpeg" };   // or "image/png", "image/webp"
}
```

- `bytes` is canonical base64 (the standard alphabet, padded, no whitespace or line breaks), at most 262,144 bytes
  (256 KB) once decoded. `mime` is `image/jpeg`, `image/png` or `image/webp`, and the bytes must really be that type (Kino
  checks their first bytes). A card's picture, not a photo: send the smallest size the service offers.
- It has 10 seconds. It runs in the background: nobody is asked anything, and a slow answer never marks your plugin "No
  responde".
- What it throws (any `kino.error` code), a wrong answer or a timeout: the card shows its placeholder, nothing more. The
  person never reads an error for a picture.

## What Kino does { #what-kino-does }

| What | How |
| --- | --- |
| When | When a card with a reference comes on screen (phone and TV alike), never ahead of it. A card scrolled away before its turn is never asked for. |
| One at a time | At most 1 `image` call in flight for your plugin; the next waits for it. Another plugin's images are asked alongside. |
| Playback first | No `image` call starts while one of your [byte streams](bytes.md) is open (on the phone or served to a TV), or while your `read` is queued or running or ended less than 2 s ago: the video keeps its turn. An image waits up to 20 s for that to end (it starts as soon as the stream closes), then is skipped (asked again the next time the card is drawn). A `read` that comes while an `image` call runs waits for that one call, so answer fast. A timed-out `image` call costs your plugin its sandbox: QuickJS cannot be interrupted, so Kino discards the runtime, and with it any socket or session it holds, and the next call starts a fresh one. |
| Once | The picture goes to Kino's image disk cache, under your plugin, its installed version and the handle: the same handle is not asked again until the cache drops it or your plugin is updated (an update asks again, so a fixed picture shows). |
| Failures | A handle that failed is not asked again for 5 minutes. 2 timeouts in a row pause all your images for 5 minutes (each timeout costs your plugin its sandbox, and the connection it keeps). |
| A call that started | Always runs to its end and is stored, even if the card went away meanwhile: cancelling it would restart your plugin. |

## Privacy { #privacy }

Kino keeps the reference wherever it keeps the title's poster: the library, the history, "Continuar
viendo", the person's lists. Those rows sync to the person's other devices and go into their backups, so never put a secret in a handle (a
token, a password, a signed URL): put an id there and the secret in a [sealed secret](manifest.md#secrets) or
`kino.storage`. A reference only loads on the device that read it from your answer; elsewhere (another of the person's
devices, a restored backup, a shared kit) it shows the placeholder. A reference is never sent to a Chromecast, a DLNA TV, the system's media controls or the TV launcher's rows: those get no
picture.

## Known limits { #known-limits }

- A title saved with a reference (library, history, "Continuar viendo", lists) keeps that poster as saved: on another of
  the person's devices, after a restore, or after this device lost its image key (a reinstall, the app's data cleared),
  that saved poster stays the placeholder. Kino does not rewrite saved rows; your Home rows, search and pages show the
  picture again, because they come from your plugin's new answer on that device.
- A picture Kino refused when the card was drawn (your plugin was switched off, not set up, being updated or not
  installed at that moment, or the address was not this device's) is not asked again while that card stays on screen; it
  is asked the next time the card is drawn.
- Only the pictures on screen are asked, one at a time: a long row of references fills in card by card.

## A complete plugin { #example }

A service whose thumbnails need the person's token: the item's `poster` is the public poster when
the service has one, and a reference otherwise. Kino asks `image` only for the second kind.

```js
// kino-plugin.json (the parts that matter): {"apiVersion": 13, "hosts": ["api.example.com"], "capabilities": ["home", "resolve", "imageSource"], "settings": [{"key": "token", "label": "Token", "type": "password", "required": true}]}
const API = "https://api.example.com";
const auth = () => ({ authorization: "Bearer " + kino.config.get("token") });

export async function home() {
  const videos = (await kino.fetch(API + "/videos", { headers: auth() })).json();
  return [{
    id: "latest",
    title: "Latest",
    items: videos.map((v) => ({
      id: "v" + v.id,
      ref: "video:" + v.id,
      title: v.title,
      kind: "movie",
      // A public poster when there is one; otherwise the thumbnail only this plugin can fetch.
      poster: v.posterUrl || { source: "plugin", handle: "thumb:" + v.id },
    })),
  }];
}

const MIMES = ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp"];

export async function image({ handle }) {
  const id = /^thumb:(\d{1,12})$/.exec(handle)?.[1];
  if (!id) throw kino.error("not_found", "unknown image handle");
  const r = await kino.fetch(API + "/videos/" + id + "/thumbnail?size=small", { headers: auth() });
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("not_found", "no thumbnail (" + r.status + ")");
  const mime = (r.headers["content-type"] || "").split(";")[0].trim();
  if (!MIMES.includes(mime)) throw kino.error("not_found", "not a JPEG, PNG or WebP picture");
  return { bytes: r.base64(), mime };
}

export async function resolve(ref) {
  const video = (await kino.fetch(API + "/videos/" + ref.slice("video:".length), { headers: auth() })).json();
  return { url: video.streamUrl };
}
```

A plugin that keeps the pictures itself (a thumbnail that came with a message it indexed) answers from `kino.storage`
instead: `const bytes = kino.storage.get(handle); if (!bytes) throw kino.error("not_found"); return { bytes, mime:
"image/jpeg" };`. Kino caches what you answer, so there is no need to keep a copy for Kino's sake.

## In the kit { #kit }

`checkOutput` keeps a reference of a plugin that declares `imageSource` as `{ source: "plugin", handle }`
and drops it otherwise, as Kino does. `askImage(plugin, manifest, ref)` from `sdk/kino-shim.mjs` asks your `image` the way
Kino does: the capability and the export, a valid reference, one call at a time, 10 s, and the answer's checks. It
resolves with `{ bytes, mime }` (a Buffer) or rejects saying why Kino would show the placeholder. It does not mirror
the wait behind playback, the 5-minute memory of a failed handle or the disk cache. From the terminal,
`node sdk/run.mjs --out poster.jpg . image <handle>` writes what your `image` answers (by default `image.<jpg|png|webp>` in
the plugin folder), and `node sdk/init.mjs my-plugin --host example.com --with images` scaffolds an apiVersion 13 plugin
with a working `image` example.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/qr/ (docs/qr.en.md) -->

# QR codes: showing one and scanning one (`qr` and `qrScan`, apiVersion 13) { #qr }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.74"
    apiVersion 13 arrives in Kino 0.9.74, together with apiVersion 12. Every Kino before 0.9.74 refuses a manifest with
    `"apiVersion": 13` ("Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino").

Some sign-ins are easier with a camera than with a keyboard, above all on a TV: the new device shows a QR code, and a
phone that already holds the account scans it and says "yes, let this device in". Kino gives you both halves, and
neither knows anything about your service:

- **Showing a QR:** the settings form's [`qr` setting](#qr-setting) draws one from a text your `settingsStatus()` returns,
  and asks for it again every `refreshMs`, so a code that expires is replaced in place. It needs no capability.
- **Scanning a QR:** `kino.qr.scan()` opens Kino's own camera scanner full screen on the phone and gives you the decoded
  text. It needs the `qrScan` capability.

## Declaring `qrScan` { #declare }

`qrScan` needs `"apiVersion": 13` and is declarative: nothing to export, no consent line, no approval
at install (the scanner only opens while the person is using your plugin, it names your plugin, and nothing is read
until they point the camera at a code). Below 13 the manifest is refused with "The \"qrScan\" capability needs apiVersion
13". Without the capability there is no `kino.qr` at all (`typeof kino.qr === "undefined"`), and `sign()` never has it.

```json
"capabilities": ["search", "resolve", "qrScan"]
```

## The call { #call }

`await kino.qr.scan({ title?, titleEn? })` resolves with the scanned text, or `null` when the person
closed the scanner (the close button, Back, or leaving the screen). `title` is your line under your plugin's name
(`titleEn` is shown instead when Kino speaks English); each is optional, at most 80 characters, shown on at most two
lines, and may hold no control, bidi or format character (no line break, no right-to-left override, no invisible
character), so it can never pass for one of Kino's own lines. Anything else you pass is dropped.

## What the person sees { #what-people-see }

The camera image with a frame to aim at and, at the top: "<your plugin's name> quiere leer un
código QR" ("… wants to read a QR code"), using the name of the plugin as installed (never a text you send), then your
`title`, then Kino's own instruction ("Apunta la cámara al código QR"), and a close button. The first code the camera
decodes that holds 1 to 4,096 characters answers your call and closes the scanner; a longer code is ignored, the
scanner says "Este código no es válido para <your plugin>" ("This code is not valid for …") and keeps looking. Without the camera permission Kino asks for it; if the person refuses, Kino explains why it needs
the camera, with Retry and Cancel.

## Where it works { #where }

Only on a phone or tablet with a camera, in Kino's phone interface: on a TV (and on any device
without a camera) the scanner never opens and the call fails with `unavailable`. A scan runs
only from a settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a `screenEvent` that follows the person's press, that is, when the person pressed one of your buttons: every other
call fails with `not_allowed` ("kino.qr.scan only runs from a settings action, panelAction or screenEvent the person pressed"), even one the person started (Home, a search, a play, a list, a title
page, your section, `settingsStatus`), so the camera never opens by itself while someone browses. In a [plugin screen](screens.md) (apiVersion 14, Kino 0.9.74: a root screen, a panel in screen mode, a tab you contribute in screen mode) only the event of the person's own tap or submit counts; the open event, a timer tick (`every`), a load-more, a change, a panel's `refreshMs` and a `playerEvent` never open the scanner. The settings node inside a screen runs its `action` exactly as Ajustes does. While the scanner is up, that call's own time limit stops (the 30 s of an `action` does not run out
while the person looks for the other device); the scanner itself closes after 120 s with `timeout`. One scanner on
screen at a time, for the whole app: a second scan while one is open, yours or another plugin's, fails at once with
`busy`. Kino checks, in this order: the request (`invalid_request`), the device (`unavailable`), where the call comes from
(`not_allowed`), and the open scan (`busy`).

| Error `code` | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `busy` | A scan is already open (yours or another plugin's). | Wait for it; do not loop. |
| `timeout` | Nothing was scanned in 120 s. | Say so, and let the person try again. |
| `unavailable` | This device cannot scan: no camera, or Kino's TV interface. | Show the code another way: a settings `qr` setting, or a typed code. |
| `not_allowed` | The call is not a settings `action`, a `panelAction` or a `screenEvent` after the person's tap or submit (Home, search, a play, `settingsStatus`, a screen's open event, timer tick or load-more…). | Scan from a button: an `action` setting, a panel button or a screen button. |
| `permission_denied` | The person did not give Kino the camera. | Tell them they can allow it in the phone's settings. |
| `invalid_request` | `title` or `titleEn` is not a string, is over 80 characters or holds a control or formatting character, or the argument is not an object. | Fix the call. |

## Privacy { #privacy }

You get only the text of the one code the person pointed the camera at, never an image or anything else the
camera saw. That text comes from the world: check it (its prefix, its length, its shape) before you act on it. Only your
plugin gets it, and only from the scan your call opened.

## Recipe: sign a new device in with a phone { #recipe }

The new device (say, the TV) shows a login code in its settings; the phone
where the person is already signed in scans it from an action. The service here is a made-up `api.example.com` with three
calls: create a login token, ask whether it was accepted, accept it with a session. Both devices run the same plugin:

```js
// kino-plugin.json (the parts that matter): {"apiVersion": 13, "hosts": ["api.example.com"], "capabilities": ["search", "resolve", "qrScan"], "settings": [{"key": "state", "label": "Cuenta", "labelEn": "Account", "type": "status"}, {"key": "login", "label": "Escanéalo desde tu teléfono", "labelEn": "Scan it from your phone", "type": "qr", "refreshMs": 5000}, {"key": "link", "label": "Vincular otro aparato", "labelEn": "Link another device", "type": "action"}]}
const API = "https://api.example.com";
const PREFIX = "exampleapp://login?token=";

async function api(path, body) {
  const r = await kino.fetch(API + path, body === undefined ? {} : { method: "POST", body: { json: body } });
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", path + " answered " + r.status);
  return r.json();
}

// The NEW device, not signed in: show a fresh login code, and keep the session once a phone accepted it.
// Kino calls this when the form opens, after every action and every refreshMs (5 s) while the form is on screen.
export async function settingsStatus() {
  if (kino.storage.get("session")) return { state: "Vinculado" }; // no "login" key: no QR is drawn
  let pending = JSON.parse(kino.storage.get("pending") || "null");
  if (pending) {
    const s = await api("/login/status?token=" + encodeURIComponent(pending.token));
    if (s.session) {
      kino.storage.set("session", s.session);
      kino.storage.remove("pending");
      return { state: "Vinculado" };
    }
  }
  if (!pending || pending.expires - Date.now() < 10000) {
    pending = await api("/login/token", {}); // { token, expires }: a new code before the old one runs out
    kino.storage.set("pending", JSON.stringify(pending));
  }
  return { state: "Esperando que lo escanees", login: PREFIX + pending.token };
}

// The phone, signed in: scan the new device's code and accept it with this phone's session.
export async function action(key) {
  if (key !== "link") return null;
  const session = kino.storage.get("session");
  if (!session) return { message: "Primero inicia sesión en este aparato" };
  let text;
  try {
    text = await kino.qr.scan({ title: "Escanea el código del otro aparato", titleEn: "Scan the other device's code" });
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code === "unavailable") return { message: "Este aparato no puede escanear: hazlo desde tu teléfono" };
    if (e.code === "permission_denied") return { message: "Permite la cámara a Kino en los ajustes del teléfono" };
    if (e.code === "timeout") return { message: "No se leyó ningún código: inténtalo otra vez" };
    throw e;
  }
  if (text === null) return { message: "Cancelado" };
  if (!text.startsWith(PREFIX)) return { message: "Ese código no es de inicio de sesión" };
  await api("/login/accept", { token: text.slice(PREFIX.length), session });
  return { message: "Listo: el otro aparato ya entró" };
}

export async function search() { return []; }
export async function resolve() { throw kino.error("not_found", "this example plays nothing"); }
```

What happens: on the TV the form shows "Esperando que lo escanees" and the QR; every 5 s Kino asks `settingsStatus()`
again, which swaps in a new code before the old one expires and notices when the phone accepted it. On the phone the
person presses "Vincular otro aparato", the scanner opens under the plugin's name, they point it at the TV, and the
action accepts the token. At the TV's next refresh the line turns into "Vinculado" and the QR goes away. Pressing the
button on the TV itself answers "Este aparato no puede escanear" (`unavailable`): the same plugin, no special case.

## The `qr` setting's rules { #qr-setting }

The [settings form](settings-form.md#qr)'s `qr` type, in full: its text is what `settingsStatus()` returns under its key, 1 to
512 characters, no control character; an `http`/`https` address must be https on a public host; any other text, such as
an app link like `exampleapp://login?token=…`, is drawn as it is; a text that would be longer, or that holds one of your sealed
secrets, draws no QR. `"refreshMs"` goes from 2000 to 60000 ms; without it the text is asked only when the form opens
and after an action. A refresh never cancels a `settingsStatus()` still running (that would restart your plugin and
close its sockets): the periodic one is skipped, and the one after an action waits for it and asks once more. The QR on
screen stays up until the new text replaces it.

## In the kit { #kit }

Node has no camera: `createKino(manifest, { qrScan })` takes a fake, `async ({ title, titleEn, invalid })
=>` the text "scanned", or `null` for a cancel; it may throw `kino.error("permission_denied")` and the like. Without one,
and with `device: "tv"`, `kino.qr.scan` fails with `unavailable`, as on a TV. The kit applies the same checks, in the same
order, with the same errors as the app: `not_allowed` unless the call is your plugin's `action`, `panelAction` or `screenEvent` (the kit
knows which export is running when it is called through `run.mjs` or `loadPlugin`), `busy` for a second scan while one is
open, `invalid_request` for a bad title. A code over 4,096 characters is ignored like on the phone: the kit asks your fake
again with `invalid: true` (the scanner keeps looking), and answers `timeout` after 10 ignored codes.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/notifications/ (docs/notifications.en.md) -->

# Notices in the bell { #notifications }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.77"
    `notifications` is `apiVersion` 15 and arrives with Kino 0.9.77. An older version refuses
    these plugins with «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino».

`notifications` lets your plugin leave **short notices in the Home bell**: «Beto y 2 más comentaron tu publicación». It is a
**declarative** capability (you export nothing new), cannot stand alone (a [screen](screens.md) or a
[background job](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs) uses it) and is not offered through [`enhancements`](enhancements.md).

```json
"capabilities": ["screen", "schedule", "notifications"]
```

## Posting and clearing { #api }

```js
await kino.notifications.post({
  id: "c123",                                            // 1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -
  title: "Beto y 2 más comentaron tu publicación",       // 1 to 80 characters
  titleEn: "Beto and 2 more commented on your post",
  text: "«Qué buena recomendación»",                     // optional, up to 160
  textEn: "“What a great pick”",
  go: { screen: { route: "post", args: { id: "123" } } }, // optional: where a tap goes
});

await kino.notifications.clear("c123"); // removes that notice
await kino.notifications.clear();       // removes all of yours
```

- **`id`** replaces an earlier notice with the same `id`, unread again: **group** your news under one `id` instead of posting
  one per event.
- **`title`** (1 to 80 characters) and **`text`** (up to 160) are plain, one line: Kino removes control and direction
  characters. `titleEn` and `textEn` are what shows in English.
- **`go`** is only `{ screen: { route?, args? } }` (a screen of **yours**, read like a screen's `go.screen`),
  `{ title: {…} }` or `{ titleByIds: {…} }` (with the screens' rules). Anything else drops the `go` (never the notice; it is
  logged) and a tap opens your screen's root. Today a title `go` also opens the root.
- Both functions resolve `undefined` or reject with an error carrying a `code`: `permission_denied`, `rate_limited` or
  `bad_request`.

## When you can call it { #when }

From your `screen`, a `screenEvent` or your **scheduled job** (`job`): typically the job asks your server what is new and
posts it. It is one of the few things a job may do besides `kino.fetch`, `kino.storage` and `kino.log`, and it counts against
no other quota.

## Limits { #limits }

Per plugin:

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Posts | 20 an hour (after that, `rate_limited`) |
| Notices kept | 30 (the oldest are dropped) |
| Life of a notice | 30 days |
| `title` / `text` | 80 / 160 characters |
| Request size | 8192 characters |

The exact numbers are in `contract.json` (`kinoNotifications.limits`).

## What people see { #what-people-see }

- The Home bell shows a badge with the **unread** notices plus the plugin updates waiting for approval.
- The list shows notices newest first, each with your plugin's icon and name, the title, the text and how long ago. A tap
  follows its `go` and marks it read; opening the list marks them all read.
- An 18+ plugin's notices show only while the 18+ code is unlocked.
- **Notices are not synced**: each device keeps its own (each device's job asks for its own), so let your server remember
  what was read.

## Consent { #consent }

The person reads, as a plain line (not red), on the install sheet and on the update that adds it:

- «Podrá mostrarte avisos en la campanita» ("Can show you notices in the bell").

And in your plugin's tab in Ajustes they can switch it off, for the whole device and their synced devices: «Mostrar sus avisos
en la campanita» ("Show its notices in the bell"). Switched off, its notices leave the bell and every call rejects with
`permission_denied`.

## Testing with the kit { #kit }

The kit keeps what you post in `<folder>/.kino-notices.json` and prints it:

```
node sdk/run.mjs --device phone . job notices      # runs the job and posts
node sdk/run.mjs . notifications                    # what has been posted so far
```

`KINO_NOTIFICATIONS_REVOKED=1` simulates the person switching it off. Add `.kino-notices.json` to your `.gitignore`, like
the kit's other local files. The contract is in `contract.json` (`kinoNotifications`) and the types in `kino.d.ts`.

## Worked example: Kino Social { #example }

**Kino Social** turns comments, likes and new followers into bell notices with a job that runs every 15 minutes or more (the
`notices` job in its manifest, which the person turns on and tunes). Each run asks its server for what is new, posts it oldest
first (so the newest ends on top) and moves its cursor only as far as the bell took, so one refused by the hourly cap comes
back on the next run:

```js
export async function postNotices() {
  if (typeof kino.notifications !== "object") return 0;        // a Kino without the capability
  const body = await call("/notifications?since=" + since);    // what is new, from its server
  const fresh = body.items.filter((n) => !n.read).sort((a, b) => a.createdAt - b.createdAt);
  for (const n of fresh) {
    try {
      await kino.notifications.post({
        id: "c" + n.id, title: titleEs, titleEn, text: excerpt,
        go: { screen: { route: "post", args: { id: String(n.postId) } } }, // a tap opens that post
      });
    } catch (_) { break; }                                     // the hourly cap: carry on next run
    since = Math.max(since, n.createdAt);
  }
}
```


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/what-people-see/ (docs/what-people-see.en.md) -->

# What people see

- **The consent sheet.** When someone types your address, Kino shows "Instalar <name>", your version
  and author, the description, the list of hosts under "Se va a conectar con:" (left out when
  `hosts` is empty), and the warning
  "Plugin no verificado: solo instálalo si confías en quien lo hizo." with "Instalar" and "Cancelar".
  If your manifest has a `password` setting it adds "Este plugin usa tu usuario y contraseña"; a `url`
  setting adds "Se conectará a los servidores que escribas en su configuración". Declaring `download`
  adds "Puede descargar videos para verlos sin conexión", `drm` adds "Reproduce video protegido (DRM)",
  `channels` adds "Agrega canales en vivo a la pestaña En vivo", `secrets` adds "Usa datos sellados por su autor", the `subtitles` capability adds "Agrega subtítulos a tus películas y series", each `insecureHttp` host adds, in red, "Conexión sin cifrar con <host>", `liveStreamHosts: "any"` adds, in red, "Puede reproducir canales desde cualquier servidor que indique su lista", and `streamHosts: "any"` adds, in red, "Puede reproducir video desde cualquier servidor que indique". From apiVersion 6, `migrate` adds "Revisar lo que tienes guardado (biblioteca, historial, favoritos) para pasarlo a este plugin", `telemetry: true` adds "Comparte registros de errores con Kino para corregir fallas" and `telemetry: "verbose"` adds "Comparte registros detallados de reproducción y errores con Kino para corregir fallas"; `"browser": true` adds, in red, "Puede abrir páginas web ocultas para encontrar el video" and `"browser": "pages"`, in red, "Puede abrir páginas web ocultas para mostrar contenido y encontrar el video" ([Hidden browser](browser.md#permission)). From apiVersion 7, `tracking` adds, in red, "Le contará a <your hosts> qué ves y cuándo lo terminas" ([Telling a tracker](contract.md#tracking)) and `segments` adds "Agrega el botón para saltar la intro y los créditos" ([Where the intro and credits are](contract.md#segments)). On an update, what is new carries a "nuevo" chip. Nothing of yours runs
  before they accept.
- **A long host list folds.** With more than 3 hosts the sheet says "Se va a conectar con N
  servidores:", lists the first 3 (on an update, the new ones first) and "y N más (M nuevos)", with a
  "Ver todos" / "Ver menos" toggle. The permission lines and the "Plugin no verificado" warning sit
  above the list and never fold; "Cancelar" and "Instalar" stay pinned below it while the body
  scrolls. A short list still reads better: declare what you use, not every mirror you ever saw.
- **Host dialogs.** A `kino.fetch` to an undeclared host during `resolve`/`episodes`, and an
  undeclared host of the video the player opens or meets mid-playback, ask the person ("Rechazar" /
  "Permitir"; the focus starts on "Rechazar"). For a movie's or episode's video, subtitles or audio
  the dialog also offers "Permitir video de cualquier servidor" ([the broad video
  permission](contract.md#broad-video)); once chosen, the plugin's details say "Puede reproducir video
  desde cualquier servidor" next to "Quitar permiso de video amplio". A plugin with remembered refusals
  also shows "Olvidar rechazos de host".
- **While `resolve` runs** the player shows "Resolviendo el video de <name>…", and after 5 s "…
  buscando enlaces (N s)".
- **When a stream can't play**, the player says why in Spanish, never the player's own English: for
  example "Este aparato no puede reproducir este formato de video (4K/HEVC)", "El servidor del video
  respondió con un error" or "No se pudo reproducir este video".
- **Configurar.** A plugin with `settings` has a "Configurar" button in Ajustes ▸ Plugins and, from
  Kino 0.9.50, its own tab in Ajustes with the same form ([The settings form](settings-form.md)). Until
  every required setting has a value its status is "Falta configurar" and nothing of it runs.
- **Ver más.** A Home row with a `ref` ends in a "Ver más" card, and a search page with a `next`
  shows "Ver más resultados de <name>": both open a grid that asks you for the next page as the
  person scrolls.
- **Search, Home and the library.** Your results appear in search under your plugin's name (with your
  `color`), next to the app's own sources; your `home` rows appear on Home after the app's own; your
  titles play in Kino's player and appear in "Continuar viendo" and the library. Titles of a plugin
  that declares `download` can be saved for offline viewing ([Downloads](manifest.md#downloads));
  Plugin titles can be sent to a TV (Chromecast and DLNA, see [Sending to the TV](#cast) below). A `live` item's card
  says "EN VIVO" and plays on tap, with no info page; a channel never enters "Continuar viendo" or
  the library ([Live channels](live-channels.md#live-items)). A plugin found through the `kino-plugin`
  topic carries the label "De la comunidad" on its card. In search, a live channel whose name has
  nothing to do with what was typed is left out ([the rule](contract.md#validation)); movies and
  series always stay.
- **Status of each plugin** in Ajustes > Plugins: "Activo", "Desactivado", "Falta configurar", "No
  responde — actívalo para volver a intentar" (three timeouts in a row; the person can re-enable it),
  "Actualización disponible — requiere tu aprobación", and "Archivos dañados, reinstálalo" (the
  installed file no longer matches what was installed).
- **Disable and uninstall.** A disabled plugin disappears from search and Home; its titles stay in
  the library and say "Activa el plugin <name> para ver esto". Uninstalling deletes the plugin's
  files, its storage and its cached Home rows immediately, but keeps the person's library titles and
  progress: opening one says "Esto venía del plugin <name>, que ya no está instalado", and installing
  the plugin again restores them. That is one more reason to keep `id` and `ref` handling stable.
  Titles already downloaded keep playing offline and can be removed from Descargas.

- **Signed plugins.** A signed plugin ([Signed plugins](signed.md)) shows the line "Firmado por su
  autor" on the consent sheet, a "Firmado" pill on catalog and community cards ("Activo · Firmado" on
  an installed one), and "Clave del autor: ABCD-EF01-2345-6789" in its details (phone: Gestionar; TV:
  the installed plugin's actions). Kino 0.9.45 and later.

## Sending to the TV (Chromecast and DLNA) { #cast }

Plugin titles can be sent to a TV from the player. Nothing in the manifest turns it on: Kino decides
per stream from what your `resolve` returns (`url`, `mime`, `headers`, `drm`):

| Your stream | What Kino does |
| --- | --- |
| mp4/webm (or another progressive file) with **no `headers`**, on a host your plugin may use | The TV fetches the URL itself; the phone moves no bytes. If the TV fails it, it is relayed through the phone. |
| HLS (`.m3u8`) | Through the phone (a Chromecast needs CORS on it): playlists are rewritten so every segment and key goes through the phone. |
| Any file **with `headers`** (Referer, cookies, tokens in headers) | Through the phone: it fetches with your headers and the TV only sees a local address. |
| A [request-signed](signed-streams.md#cast) stream (Kino 0.9.50) | Through the phone, which calls `sign()` for every playlist and segment the TV asks for. |
| DRM (Widevine or ClearKey), DASH, progressive MPEG-TS, or a format nothing tells apart | Not sent: the person reads "Este título no se puede enviar a la TV" (protected ones: "Este título está protegido y no se puede enviar a la TV"). |

What helps authors: return a real `mime` (`video/mp4`, `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`) or a URL that
ends in the right extension; Kino probes the first bytes of a stream nothing describes (a 1 KB ranged
read, 2 s) but that costs a request. Prefer links that need no `headers` (the lightest route); every
host involved must be one your plugin may reach (declared, typed, or covered by an "any" permission), over
https. While casting, the phone itself stays silent.

From Kino 0.9.54, an apiVersion 8 [`music` or `podcast`](contract.md#music-podcasts)
track goes to a Chromecast as music, with its title, artist, album and cover, and to a DLNA TV as an audio
item; an 18+ track sends only the app's name.

## External resolver apps (Kino 0.9.66) { #resolver }

When a plugin answers `external` instead of a `url` ([External resolver apps](resolver.md)):

- **The first time**, a dialog asks: "<plugin>" quiere usar "<app>" para resolver contenido de tipo "<protocol>".
  / Esta aplicación no es de Kino y actúa por su cuenta. ("Permitir" / "No permitir"). With several apps for the
  protocol, "Elige qué aplicación usar"; the pick is remembered.
- **While the app works**: "Abriendo con "<app>"" with its live progress (its own short text, or "Buscando...")
  and a "Cancelar" button.
- **When it fails**: "No se pudo resolver este contenido (<code>): <the app's own short sentence>."; with no app
  installed, "Este contenido necesita una aplicación externa que no tienes instalada." (or, when the plugin names
  one, a sheet that offers to download it from GitHub); after a "no", "No autorizaste resolver este contenido con
  ...". A later playback error the app explained reads "La aplicación que ofrece este video dijo: ...".
- **Their decisions** live in Ajustes, in the "Fuentes externas" section, where each can be revoked. Such a title
  can only be played, never downloaded.
- **Sending it to a TV** goes through the phone like any plugin title; it was tried on a real Chromecast (and DLNA on an LG
  webOS TV, with an HLS answer) ([Casting a resolver's title](resolver.md#cast)).

## Sync providers (Kino 0.9.74) { #sync-provider }

When a plugin declares `syncProvider` ([Sync providers](sync-providers.md)):

- **The consent sheet** says, in red, "Sincronizará tus datos a través de su servicio: el plugin y su
  servicio podrán leerlos" ("Will sync your data through its service: the plugin and its service can
  read it"). An update that adds the capability waits for approval.
- **Ajustes de todos los perfiles ▸ Sincronización ▸ Proveedor** lists "Red local" and every installed
  provider, each with a switch; only one is on at a time, or none. Turning one on asks "¿Sincronizar con
  <name>?" ("La sincronización por red local se apaga mientras uses <name>"; "Si <name> ya
  guarda datos de otro aparato, se combinan con los de este. Nunca se borra nada de ningún lado.") with
  "Combinar con este aparato".
- **The provider's row** shows "Sincronizado hace 3 min", "Esperando la primera sincronización", "Falló la
  última sincronización: <reason>", "Falta el token: escríbelo en Configurar" or "El token no
  coincide o los datos guardados no son de Kino", the plugin's own `syncStatus` line, and the buttons
  Configurar ("Set up"), Sincronizar ahora, Restablecer sincronización, Enviar configuración ("Send settings")
  and Recibir configuración ("Receive settings"); on a device that still lacks the settings, "Recibir
  configuración" leads and "Configurar" turns quiet.
- **Receiving on a second device**: a QR, an address and a 6-digit code for 3 minutes (and, when the
  Cloudflare quick tunnel opens, the words for "Otra red"), then "Recibido para <plugin>: ¿aplicar?" with the labels of the settings it got,
  never their values, and "Aplicar".

## Screens and apiVersion 14 (Kino 0.9.74) { #v14 }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.74"
    Available from Kino 0.9.74. An older Kino refuses these plugins with
    «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino»; to keep reaching people on an older version use
    `enhancements` (see [Screens without raising your apiVersion](enhancements.md)).

- **Screens.** A plugin with a [screen](screens.md) gets an entry on the TV sidebar (the first three plugin screens
  directly, the others under «Más pantallas») and a chip on the phone's Inicio strip, or a button at the top of its
  settings page; the screen opens with Kino's title bar (the plugin's name and a close button).
- **New red lines.** `library`, `playerPanelTab`, `playerControl`, `room`, `schedule` and `ai` each show their red line on
  the consent sheet and are asked at install and on the update that adds them; `shared` shows a plain line. The person can
  switch each one off in the plugin's tab in Ajustes ([Rooms, the library and player control](rooms.md),
  [Background jobs, shared results and AI](jobs-and-shared.md)).
- **The player slot.** A plugin with a `fixed` [player slot](player-slot.md) element shows «Mostrará algo suyo de forma
  permanente en el reproductor mientras ves un video» in red, asked on each device; its switch is «Dejar que muestre algo en
  el reproductor». On the TV its elements sit in the top-right corner of the player.
- **Updates.** An update that adds a red consent line or a new host shows it first, open, under «Nuevo en esta
  actualización».
- **Tabs in the player panel.** A plugin with `playerPanelTab` adds a tab to the player panel of any title; the person
  can hide it ("Mostrar en el reproductor") or reorder it (Ajustes, "Paneles del reproductor").
  [The player panel](player-panel.md#contributed-tab).
- **Exporting a plugin.** Plugins ▸ Instalados ▸ Gestionar ▸ "Exportar plugin" shares a `.kinoplugin` file that installs
  on another phone as a local plugin. [Exporting and importing a plugin file](plugin-files.md).

## Kino 0.9.77 (apiVersion 15) { #v15 }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.77"
    An older Kino refuses these plugins with «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino».

- **The Home bell.** A plugin with [`notifications`](notifications.md) leaves short notices: the bell shows a badge with the
  unread ones and the plugin updates waiting for approval; tapping a notice goes to the plugin's screen and marks it read.
  Each device keeps its own.
- **New consent lines.** `identity` shows, in red, «Podrá saber tu usuario de Telegram y enviarlo a sus servicios»;
  `notifications`, «Podrá mostrarte avisos en la campanita»; a store (`pluginStore`), «Agrega plugins de sus servidores a tu
  tienda» and, if it is live, also in red «Lo que busques en la tienda llegará a sus servidores». The person can switch
  `identity` and `notifications` off in the plugin's tab in Ajustes.
- **The plugin store.** Plugins shows one store built from the active stores (Kino Plugins ships with the app): the tabs «De Kino»
  (From Kino: Kino Plugins' default list), «De la comunidad» (Community: everything else, from every store, with the
  «Populares»/«Recientes» sort) and «Instalados» (Installed), a store filter and, on every card, «de <store>». A reload
  icon syncs the stores and ends with a toast, «Se actualizaron N plugins» or «Tus plugins están al día». Searching, filtering and paging are local; Kino
  applies its blocklist and the 18+ code to everything stores list, and keeps one plugin per `id` across stores. A plugin a store stops listing stays installed and
  Instalados says «Ya no está en ninguna tienda». [Plugin stores](plugin-stores.md).

## Kino 0.9.78 (apiVersion 16 and 17) { #v16 }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.78"
    `kino.coins` and `kino.sync.setActive` arrive with Kino 0.9.78; `kino.library.stats` and `"perProfile"` are apiVersion 17, in
    Kino 0.9.81. An older version refuses those plugins with «Este plugin necesita una versión más
    nueva de Kino».

- **Kino coins.** `coins` shows, in red, «Podrá ver tu saldo de kinos y regalar tus kinos». It has no switch of its own: the
  person revokes it by disabling or removing the plugin, and if they switch Kinos off in Kino's Ajustes the plugin must show
  nothing of coins ([`kino.coins`](kino-api.md#coins)).
- **The `library` line grew.** It now reads «Podrá leer lo que has visto y guardado en Kino, cuánto lo ves y a qué hora, y
  enviarlo a sus servicios», because with apiVersion 17 the plugin can read a month's aggregates
  ([`kino.library.stats`](kino-api.md#library-stats)). An update that raises a plugin already holding `library` to apiVersion
  17 asks the person again.
- **Switching sync provider from the plugin.** A provider may offer its own button; Kino always asks its own question with the
  plugin's name ([`kino.sync.setActive`](kino-api.md#sync-active)).
- **Per-profile jobs.** A `perProfile` job has, in the plugin's tab in Ajustes, the usual job row (off by default, covering
  every profile) and, for each profile, «Incluir este perfil», on by default
  ([Background jobs](jobs-and-shared.md#per-profile)).

## Kino 0.9.81 (apiVersion 20): plugins that use each other { #v20 }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.81"
    The [plugin protocol](protocol.md) is apiVersion 20, which arrives with Kino 0.9.81.

- **One plain line per door** on the install sheet of a plugin that uses another one's doors: «Usa datos de TMDB (Movie
  records from TMDB)», the provider's name and the door's summary (the repository, «Usa datos de
  kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb», while the provider is not installed). Not red, no switch, no approval of its own; on an update
  that adds a door the line is marked new. There is never a question per call.
- **An install button inside the plugin.** While the provider is missing, the consumer shows its own screen with a button;
  the button opens Kino's normal install sheet for the provider, with the provider's own consent lines, and nothing is
  installed until the person taps Instalar. If it is already installed Kino says «Ese plugin ya está instalado».
- **Removing the provider** leaves the consumer installed; it simply shows its install screen again.
- **A plugin that only provides** (no capability, no host) says on its card that it does not connect to the internet, and
  does not show up as a source in search or Home.
- **A screen-only consumer** (only `screen`, `"hosts": []`) says on its card that it does not connect to the internet only
  when it has no settings at all; its install sheet still shows the «Usa datos de …» line of each door it uses.

## Kino 0.9.81 (apiVersion 18): app themes { #v18 }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.81"
    App themes are apiVersion 18, which arrives with Kino 0.9.81. An older Kino refuses a plugin that declares `appThemes`
    with «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino».

- **Ajustes ▸ Apariencia.** Lists Kino's own theme and every theme of the installed plugins, each with the plugin it comes
  from. The person opens a preview (cards, a dialog, the player's controls), then turns it on; one theme is active at a time,
  per profile, and the choice syncs between their devices. «Personalizar» changes only what the theme's author allows.
- **No consent line.** A theme is data: no network, no code, no capability. It can never restyle what Kino asks the person to
  decide: Ajustes ▸ Apariencia itself, the purchase and experience questions, the gate and the splash keep Kino's own look.
- **A theme can cost kinos.** In the list the row says «Gran Tesoro · 50 kinos», on the preview the button reads «Comprar por
  50 kinos» and, above it, «Tienes N kinos.» (the person's balance). Pressing it opens Kino's own sheet with the price and the
  balance; «Comprar por N kinos» is enabled only when the balance covers it («Te faltan N kinos…» otherwise). It is bought once
  per account and works on every device; a failed purchase charges nothing. The same sheet appears when the plugin's own
  screen asks to turn the theme on. Free themes show none of this ([App themes](themes.md#price)).
- **The experience.** A theme may suggest the light or the full experience of the whole app; Kino asks the person first
  («Experiencia para “…”», «Dejar la actual» / «Usar la ligera» or «Usar la completa»), and a plugin's screen may ask the same
  with `go.setExperience` ([App themes](themes.md#experience)).
- **The logo.** A theme may draw its own logo in the side menu, the TV rail and the header.
- **Where the author is paid.** Ajustes ▸ App ▸ «Tu cuenta de kinos» shows the person's account (first and last 8 characters)
  and copies all 64 on a tap: the `payTo` of a theme's `price`.
- **A gift.** Kino announces «Te regalamos 100 kinos» in the Home bell, once, as its own notice (not a plugin's).

## Kino 0.9.74 (apiVersion 13) { #v13 }

With the apiVersion 13 capabilities ([What's new](changelog.md#v13)):

- **No new consent line**: `socket`, `byteSource`, `storageLarge`, `catalog`, `qrScan` and `imageSource` add nothing to
  the consent sheet (a socket reaches only the hosts the sheet already lists).
- **A byte stream plays like any video**, and casts to a Chromecast or a DLNA TV from the phone over the home network.
  When your `read` fails the person reads your error, or "El plugin no entregó los datos del video" for a wrong answer.
  Its titles show the download button, but such a video never downloads.
- **The QR scanner**: the camera full screen with "<plugin name> quiere leer un código QR", your `title`, "Apunta la
  cámara al código QR" and a close button; a code that is too long reads "Este código no es válido para <plugin>".
  Without the camera permission Kino asks for it, and explains why with Retry and Cancel if the person refuses.
- **A `qr` setting** is a QR code on the plugin's settings form, redrawn every `refreshMs`; with no text it reads "Sin
  información".
- **Images from the plugin** appear card by card as they come on screen; a picture that fails, or a title saved with one
  on another device, shows the usual placeholder. The person never sees an error for a picture.

## From Kino 0.9.54 { #v0954 }

With nothing new in your manifest, except where said:

- **Kino in Spanish or English.** The person picks the app's language in Ajustes ▸ App ▸ Idioma
  ("Automático" follows the device: Spanish on a Spanish device, English on any other). Kino's own texts
  follow it, the consent sheet and the messages Kino words for your plugin's failures included. What your
  plugin returns (titles, row names, settings labels, a `userMessage`) is shown as you wrote it: read
  [`kino.lang`](kino-api.md#lang), now `"es-CO"` or `"en-US"`, to word it in the person's language.
- **Catalog-only plugins.** With [`"catalogOnly": true`](contract.md#catalog-only) the consent sheet
  adds "Solo catálogo: no reproduce videos", the title page's button reads "Buscar dónde verlo", and
  the plugin is never offered as a source of a title.
- **Music and podcasts** (apiVersion 8, [the contract](contract.md#music-podcasts)): square covers in
  rows of their own, album and podcast pages with "Reproducir" and "Aleatorio", an audio player, a
  "Seguir escuchando" row for podcasts on Home, audio downloads and audio cast.
- **The title page is the same whatever order its sources answer.** TMDB comes first for the synopsis,
  year, genres, score and runtime; your item and the new [`details`](contract.md#details) export come
  before AniList and `meta` plugins for the synopsis and art.
- **A lighter copy after repeated stalls.** When playback keeps stopping to load, the player can say
  the connection is slow and, once, move by itself to a clearly lighter copy among your
  [alternatives](contract.md#stream) when their labels name the resolution.
- **Finding plugins.** "De la comunidad" lists 100 plugins a page, sorted by "Populares" or
  "Recientes", with "Cargar más" and "Buscar en GitHub" ([Publishing](publish.md#discovery-0954)).
- **CloudStream plugins.** People can add a CloudStream repository and install its plugins through a
  separate complement app ([CloudStream plugins](cloudstream.md)).

## From Kino 0.9.50 { #v0950 }

With nothing new in your manifest, except where said:

- **Play on the TV from the phone.** With two paired devices, "Reproducir en el TV" works for a title
  of any plugin: the TV opens it with **its own copy** of the plugin. If the TV can't, the phone says
  why: "Instala el plugin <name> en el TV para verlo allí", "Activa …", "Configura …",
  "Actualiza …", "Reinstala …", "En el TV hay otro plugin con ese nombre; instala el mismo desde su
  repositorio", "Desbloquea el contenido 18+ en el TV para verlo allí" or, for a TV on an older Kino,
  "Actualiza Kino en el TV para verlo allí". So keep your `id` and your refs the same on every device.
- **New chapters of the series the person follows.** Kino checks now and then (at most every 6 hours)
  the saved series of any usable plugin that declares `episodes`, calling your `episodes(ref)` with the
  saved `ref`, and adds the missing chapters. A failure leaves that series alone and moves on to the
  next. Keep your series refs stable.
- **"Para ti".** A recommendation that comes from a plugin's catalog is saved by its `ref`: a movie as
  a movie, a series with its first season (calling `episodes`).
- **18+ content.** `adult: true` entries of an apiVersion 6 plugin show only with the 18+ code unlocked
  ([18+ content](contract.md#adult)).
- **Channels on Home.** An apiVersion 6 plugin can put channels in its Home rows
  ([Channels in your Home rows](live-channels.md#home-rows)).
- **A section of its own** in the TV sidebar or the phone's Inicio strip, and a group in Categorías,
  for a plugin that declares `section` or exports `categories`
  ([Section, categories and colors](section-theme.md)).
- **Search inside a "Ver más" page.** Every "Ver más" page has "Buscar en esta categoría"
  ([`scopedSearch`](contract.md#scoped-search)).
- **Your own tab in Ajustes.** A plugin with `settings` gets a tab named after it, with its form, status
  lines and buttons, painted in its [`theme`](section-theme.md#theme) colors
  ([The settings form](settings-form.md)).
- **The Servidor menu.** When a Stream has two or more copies, the player's "Audio y subtítulos" menu
  starts with a **Servidor** section listing them by `label` ("Opción 2", "Opción 3"… without one); the
  person switches and keeps watching from the same spot ([Labelled and lazy copies](contract.md#lazy-copies)).
- **Your own sentence on an error.** A valid `userMessage` shows as "Mensaje de <name>: …" instead
  of Kino's line ([Your own sentence](contract.md#user-message)).
- **Subtitles from your plugin.** A plugin that exports `subtitles` is listed, under its name, in the
  player's "Buscar subtítulos en línea" for any title Kino knows by IMDb or TMDB id
  ([Subtitles for any title](contract.md#subtitles)).
- **Info pages filled by your plugin.** A `meta` plugin fills what TMDB and AniList left empty on any
  title's info page ([Describing other titles](contract.md#meta)).
- **Hidden pages.** A `"browser"` plugin's page is never on screen: the player shows its usual loading
  state while it runs ([Hidden browser](browser.md)).
- **Updates.** A badge on Ajustes ▸ Plugins counts the updates waiting for approval, and a failed call
  of a plugin with a pending update says so ([Updates](publish.md#updates)).
- **Community plugins.** The section carries the note "Plugins de la comunidad — Kino no los revisa ni
  responde por su contenido.", and an installed plugin taken down from the index says "Retirado del
  índice de la comunidad." ([Claims and plugin takedowns](claims.md)).

## Plugins on the person's other devices { #sync }

Kino keeps a person's plugins in step between their own devices (for example phone and TV): an
install, a switch on or off, an uninstall, an approval or a saved setting on one device is sent to
the others, and passwords travel encrypted end to end. Nothing in your plugin changes. What the
other device does: it installs **your plugin again from the same address**, silently when what it
fetches asks for nothing more than the person approved on the first one; if an update adds something
(a host, a capability), it waits in "Plugins de tus otros aparatos" for the person to approve it
there. So keep your repository public and your address stable.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/live-channels/ (docs/live-channels.en.md) -->

# Live channels

There are two ways to give Kino live TV, and a plugin can do both:

- **`live` items** (apiVersion 2): channels mixed into your "Ver más" pages and search results, next
  to your movies and series, and from apiVersion 6 into your Home rows too.
- **The `channels` capability** (apiVersion 3): your channels in Kino's own En vivo tab, TV guide,
  channel drawer and Home "Canales en vivo" row, given one by one or as an M3U playlist with an
  XMLTV guide that Kino downloads and parses itself.

Testing them with the Node kit is on [Test it locally](test-locally.md#live).

## Live channels (apiVersion 2) { #live-items }

With `"apiVersion": 2` an item may be a live channel: `kind: "live"`, in a `browse` page or `search`
result, next to your movies and series. Nothing to declare beyond the version. In a `home` row a
channel stays only from `"apiVersion": 6` ([below](#home-rows)).

```js
export async function home() {
  return [{
    id: "en-vivo", title: "En vivo",
    items: [
      { id: "canal-1", ref: "live:1", title: "Canal Uno", kind: "live", poster: "https://cdn.example.org/canal-1.png" },
    ],
  }];
}

export async function resolve(ref) {
  if (ref.startsWith("live:")) {
    const url = await freshPlaylistUrlFor(ref); // look the live link up here, never in home()
    return { url, mime: "application/vnd.apple.mpegurl" };
  }
  // ...movies and episodes as before
}
```

What Kino does with a `live` item:

- Its card wears an "EN VIVO" badge (Home, "Ver más", search, phone and TV), and tapping it goes
  **straight to the player**: no info page, nothing to read or pick. `resolve(ref)` gets the item's
  `ref`, exactly as for a movie.
- In **search**, a `live` item is kept only when its name matches what was asked (most of the words
  of 3 or more letters of the query, its `originalTitle` or one of its `altTitles`, like
  [`kino.rank.filterRelevant`](kino-api.md#rank)). A channel plugin that answers every search with
  its whole list when nothing matches sees those channels dropped; movies and series are never
  judged this way.
- The `Stream` plays as live: an HLS or DASH live manifest (`.m3u8`/`.mpd`) is what the player
  expects; a progressive file plays too but reads as a channel (no seek bar, no length). `headers`,
  `subtitles` and `expiresInSeconds` work as for any stream; `durationMs` and `audioTracks` are
  ignored (a separate audio file cannot follow a live window: put a channel's other languages inside
  its manifest, e.g. HLS `EXT-X-MEDIA` renditions, and the player's audio menu offers them).
- The player shows the live overlay (no progress bar, no seeking, no "next") and starts at the live
  edge. If it falls behind the live window, or the playlist resets or stalls, it re-joins the live
  edge in place without calling you (a few times a minute). On any other cut, or when your URL
  stops working, it calls `resolve` again with the same `ref` after 2 s, then 4 s, then 8 s: three
  reopens, replenished once the channel has played for five seconds. Only after the third failed
  reopen does the person read "Se cortó la señal de <canal> y no volvió". `expiresInSeconds` plays
  no part for a channel: a cut always re-resolves.
- A channel is never saved: no library row, no resume position, never in "Continuar viendo", and
  never downloadable (a plugin that declares `download` gets "Este contenido no se puede descargar"
  for it). `runtimeMinutes` on the item is ignored; a channel has no `episodes`.

Limits: a `live` item from a plugin on `"apiVersion": 1` is dropped silently, like any invalid
item (and a row left with no items disappears), so declare `2` before you return one. A channel
still counts against the same row and page sizes as any item. These channels appear in your rows,
with your plugin's name; to put channels in Kino's En vivo tab and its "Canales en vivo" row, use
the apiVersion 3 `channels` capability ([below](#en-vivo-tab)).

### Channels in your Home rows (apiVersion 6) { #home-rows }

From `"apiVersion": 6` (Kino 0.9.50) a `kind: "live"` item stays in a `home` row: it shows as a channel
card with the "En vivo" badge and opens like a channel from En vivo. A row of channels on Home (say, a
country's channels) is just a `home` row whose items are `kind: "live"`. Below 6 Kino drops channels
from Home. An `adult: true` channel follows the same [18+ lock](contract.md#adult) as any 18+ entry, and
a row left with nothing to show is not shown.

## Channels in the En vivo tab (apiVersion 3) { #en-vivo-tab }

Declare `"apiVersion": 3` and the capability `"channels"`, and export `liveCategories()` and
`liveChannels({ categoryId, cursor })` (and, optionally, `guide(...)` and `liveSearch(...)`, see [below](#live-contract)). Your channels then
appear in Kino's own En vivo tab, TV guide, channel drawer and Home "Canales en vivo" row, in a
section with your plugin's name. `channels` does not replace `search`/`home`: the manifest still
needs one of them (a plugin with only channels exports a `home()` that returns `[]`). Items of kind
`"live"` in your rows keep working; a plugin can do both. On install, and on an update that adds it,
the person reads and approves "Agrega canales en vivo a la pestaña En vivo".

## Channels from any server (`liveStreamHosts`, apiVersion 3) { #live-stream-hosts }

IPTV lists name their streams on servers you cannot know ahead of time, often plain `http` and
often a bare public IP. For that, and only that, a `channels` plugin may add:

```json
"apiVersion": 3,
"capabilities": ["home", "resolve", "channels"],
"liveStreamHosts": "any"
```

It is read only with `"apiVersion": 3` (an older manifest ignores it, like any field it does not
know). There, `"any"` is the only value and it needs the `channels` capability: otherwise the
manifest is refused with `El campo "liveStreamHosts" solo admite "any"` or
`"liveStreamHosts" necesita la capacidad "channels"`.

What it allows: **a live channel's stream** (the `url` of a channel's inline `stream`, or the `url`
`resolve` returns for a channel; items you mark as live are treated as channels) may be on **any
public host**, over `http` or `https`, a public IPv4 address included (not an IPv6 literal). The player then fetches that manifest and
its variants, segments and keys, and follows their redirects, under the same rule. The audio and
subtitle renditions the HLS manifest itself lists (`#EXT-X-MEDIA`) are part of that stream and follow
the same rule too; the `subtitles` and `audioTracks` you return in a `Stream` do not (see below).

What it never allows:

- the home network: private, loopback, link-local and carrier-grade NAT addresses, IPv6 literals,
  `localhost` and local names (`.local`, `.lan`, …), and a public name that resolves into any of
  them (refused when the player connects);
- other ports or schemes of a server the person typed: that server is reached exactly as typed,
  never "any";
- `kino.fetch`: your own requests still reach only your `hosts` and the person's servers;
- the playlist and XMLTV downloads a `{ playlist }` declaration asks Kino to make: those URLs must
  still be on your `hosts` (or the person's server);
- subtitles, audio tracks and a `drm` block's `licenseUrl`: still your `hosts` only, and every
  redirect they make is judged the same way;
- movies and episodes: a non-live `Stream` is checked exactly as before (unless your plugin declares
  [`streamHosts: "any"`](manifest.md#stream-hosts) or the person granted it the
  [broad video permission](contract.md#broad-video));
- images: the poster rule (http or https, never local) does not change.

The consent sheet shows it in red, "Puede reproducir canales desde cualquier servidor que indique su
lista", and an update that newly adds it waits for the person's approval, like a new host.

## The channel functions (apiVersion 3) { #live-contract }

With the `channels` capability ([above](#en-vivo-tab)) Kino calls up to
four more functions. Their arguments:

- `liveCategories()` gets `null`.
- `liveChannels({ categoryId, cursor })` gets the `id` of one of your categories, and `cursor` `null`
  for the first page or the `next` of the page before.
- `guide({ channelIds, from, to })` gets at most 50 of your channel ids and a window of at most
  24 hours: `from` and `to` are epoch milliseconds.
- `liveSearch({ query })` (optional) gets what the person typed in En vivo's search, trimmed, at
  least 2 characters.

They return:

```ts
LiveCategory = { id: string, title: string, country?: string, adult?: boolean, genre?: Genre }
Playlist     = { playlist: { url: string, format: "m3u", headers?: Record<string, string>,
                             streamHeaders?: Record<string, string>, genre?: Genre,
                             epg?: { url: string, format: "xmltv" }, refreshHours?: number,
                             hideGroups?: string[], resolve?: boolean } }
LiveChannel  = { id: string, title: string, categoryId?: string, ref?: string, stream?: Stream,
                 logo?: string, number?: number, adult?: boolean }
GuideEntry   = { channelId: string, title: string, start: number, end: number, description?: string }
```

A plugin can give its channels in three ways, and mix them:

1. **A channel with a `ref`.** The `ref` goes to `resolve(ref)` when the person plays it, exactly
   like a `live` item's, and its Stream plays as live.
2. **A channel with an inline `stream`.** A `Stream` checked by the same rules as `resolve()`'s
   answer ([The `Stream` rules](contract.md#stream)); it plays with no call to your plugin. A channel whose `stream` is refused is dropped. With
   both `ref` and `stream`, the stream plays and the `ref` is only the fallback (but a
   [request-signed](signed-streams.md) inline stream is set aside, and the `ref` plays). A channel with
   neither is dropped. Some channels only answer a known player: give the `Stream` a `headers` with
   the `User-Agent` (or `Referer`) it insists on, and the player sends it with every request for that channel.
3. **A playlist.** Put `{ playlist: { ... } }` entries next to your categories in the
   `liveCategories()` answer (or return one alone). Kino downloads the M3U list itself, and its XMLTV
   guide from `epg.url`, and groups the entries into categories. Both URLs must be `https` on one of
   your `hosts` (or `http` on one declared `insecureHttp`, or a server the person typed), always:
   a playlist on another host is dropped, and an `epg` on another host only loses the guide.
   `headers` go with those downloads. `streamHeaders` are what the **player** sends for every channel of
   the list, for the channels that only answer a known `User-Agent` (or a `Referer`): they are filtered
   like a Stream's `headers` and kept apart from `headers` on purpose, because those carry your list's own
   credentials and go only to the list's host, never to the many hosts the channels are on. A header an
   M3U entry names itself (`#EXTVLCOPT:http-user-agent=...`, `#EXTHTTP:{"User-Agent":"..."}`, a `url|User-Agent=...&Referer=...` suffix, or `#KODIPROP` stream headers) wins; only `User-Agent`, `Referer`, `Origin` and `Cookie` are kept, and a value with a control character is dropped. The list
   may be UTF-8, Latin-1 or UTF-16 (with or without a BOM); `#EXTINF` attributes may be double-quoted,
   single-quoted or bare (`tvg-id=abc`). A list over 20 MB, or a guide over 50 MB, is not refused: Kino
   keeps its start, up to its last whole line (`node sdk/run.mjs live playlist` says when). A guide
   `<programme>` without `stop` ends where the next programme of its channel starts, or one hour
   after its start when none follows. Kino versions before the one that added
   `streamHeaders` ignore the field, so the list plays without it. `refreshHours` is 1 to 168 (default 12); `hideGroups` lists
   group titles not to show (case doesn't matter, at most 50). With `resolve: true`, each entry plays
   through your `resolve(<entry url>)`, for lists whose links need a fresh token. At most 10 per
   answer.

    Each entry gets a channel code, the key of favourites and recents: its `tvg-id` when that is a
    valid id and the entry is the **first of the list to use it**, else one made from its URL and
    name. A later entry repeating a `tvg-id` never moves the first one's code, but it gets a
    URL-and-name code itself, which changes (and its favourites and recents stop matching) when its
    URL does; a copy inserted *before* the first one takes the `tvg-id` code over. Give every entry a
    stable, unique `tvg-id`; `node sdk/run.mjs live playlist <list>` lists the repeated ones.

The rules:

- Times are epoch milliseconds.
- At most 200 categories (playlists don't count), and at most 500 channels per `liveChannels` page.
  `id` follows the item `id` pattern; an `id` starting with `~` is reserved for Kino's own playlist
  entries and dropped. A repeated `id` in one answer is dropped. `title` is required.
- `country` is an ISO 3166 two-letter code (`"CO"`), informational; anything else is ignored.
  `number` is 1 to 9999 (anything else counts as no number); `logo` follows the poster rules;
  `categoryId` is optional and informational in `liveChannels` (a channel is listed under the
  category `liveChannels` was asked for); one that is not a valid id becomes empty. In a `liveSearch`
  hit it is how Kino knows whether the hit is 18+ ([below](#live-search-adult)).
- Kino pages `liveChannels` until `next` is missing, repeats, or brings nothing new. A category's
  first listing asks at most 10 pages; when the last one still has a `next`, Kino keeps it and asks
  5 more pages each time the person scrolls near the end of the list, up to 10,000 channels (or 200
  pages) per category. Kino 0.9.49 and older stop at the first 10 pages and never ask `liveSearch`.
- <span id="live-search"></span>`liveSearch` is optional, for a catalog too big to list whole. Kino
  asks it from En vivo's search (the phone's field, the TV guide's and the TV channel drawer's) when
  the person stops typing, only while some of your channels were never listed (a category not opened
  yet, or one with pages left), and keeps each answer 10 minutes per query. It returns channels
  exactly like a `liveChannels` page (`next` is ignored), at most 100 kept, with the same `id` a
  listed channel has, so favourites and recents match. Kino still shows only the ones whose name
  contains what was typed (or whose number is it). A channel found this way plays like a listed one,
  and a favourite Kino no longer has in memory nor in its cache is looked up again by name through
  `liveSearch` (one call) before the first pages of your first 10 categories; without `liveSearch`,
  only those first pages are looked at, never the pages after them. Its time limit is 15 s and it
  runs as a background call: a slow search never marks the plugin "No responde". Export it only when
  you can really search: an empty answer is taken as "nothing found", and Kino keeps saying some
  channels were not loaded. A preheat of the next channel (Kino resolving a neighbour ahead while one
  plays) never asks `liveSearch`: it looks only through your listings, and the zap itself asks when
  needed.
- <span id="live-search-adult"></span>**Mark every `liveSearch` hit** (apiVersion 6, when you have an
  18+ category): a hit names no listing, so give it `adult: true`/`adult: false`, or the `categoryId`
  of the category it belongs to. A hit with `adult: true` or the `categoryId` of an 18+ category is 18+;
  one with the `categoryId` of a plain category, or `adult: false`, is plain. A hit with neither counts
  as 18+ for a plugin that has any 18+ category, and, when your categories can't be read
  (`liveCategories` failed), every hit not marked `adult: false` counts as 18+. While the 18+ code is
  locked, Kino leaves those hits out of the search, does not open them and keeps them out of
  "Recientes". `node sdk/run.mjs <plugin dir> live search <query>` and `sdk/validate.mjs --run
  liveSearch` mark the hits the same way and warn about the ones that carry neither mark.
- Kino caches your categories and channels for 1 hour and your guide for 30 minutes.
- `guide` is optional. Kino keeps entries for the channels it asked for, with `end` after `start`,
  inside the window, at most 100 per channel and one per start time. A `guide` that fails or is not
  exported is simply not asked again for 30 minutes: your channels still list.
- `adult: true` on a category or a channel: from apiVersion 6 it marks an 18+ entry, shown only while
  the person's 18+ code is unlocked on that device (Ajustes ▸ Control parental) and hidden again when they lock
  it; below apiVersion 6 it is dropped. Every channel of an 18+ category counts as 18+, and an 18+
  channel never enters "Recientes". See [18+ content](contract.md#adult).
- While a channel plays, Kino may resolve the neighbouring channel ahead so zapping is quick (cancelled
  when the person leaves). That is one more call to your `resolve`: don't count it as a play.

A `liveSearch` for an API that can search its channels by name:

```js
export async function liveSearch({ query }) {
  const r = await kino.fetch("https://api.example.com/channels?q=" + encodeURIComponent(query));
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable");
  return r.json().items.map(c => ({ id: c.id, title: c.name, ref: c.id, logo: c.logo }));
}
```

Use the same `id` your `liveChannels` gives that channel. Test it with
`node sdk/run.mjs . live search <query>` ([Test it locally](test-locally.md#live)).

## Three recipes (apiVersion 3) { #recipes }

Three ways to fill the En vivo tab, from the least code to the most control. Each is a complete
plugin (see [Channels in the En vivo tab](#en-vivo-tab) and
[The channel functions](#live-contract) for the rules).

### 1. A plain M3U list the person types { #recipe-m3u }

The person pastes the address of their list (and, if they
have one, of its guide) in Configurar; Kino downloads it, groups it and plays each entry itself.

```json
{
  "id": "mi-lista", "name": "Mi lista", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 3, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": [],
  "capabilities": ["home", "resolve", "channels"],
  "liveStreamHosts": "any",
  "settings": [
    { "key": "lista", "label": "Lista M3U", "type": "url", "required": true },
    { "key": "guia", "label": "Guía XMLTV", "type": "url" }
  ]
}
```

`"hosts": []` is enough: the list and the guide are on servers the person typed. Their streams are
not: an IPTV list points at dozens of servers nobody can declare ahead of time, which is what
`"liveStreamHosts": "any"` is for ([Channels from any server](#live-stream-hosts)).
The person sees it on the consent sheet, in red: "Puede reproducir canales desde cualquier servidor
que indique su lista". Leave it out when every stream is on hosts you can declare.

```js
// Kino downloads the list (and the guide), groups it and plays each entry by itself.
export async function liveCategories() {
  const guia = kino.config.get("guia");
  return [{
    playlist: {
      url: kino.config.get("lista"),
      format: "m3u",
      epg: guia ? { url: guia, format: "xmltv" } : undefined,
      hideGroups: ["Compras"],
    },
  }];
}

// Every channel comes from the list: no categories of your own to page.
export async function liveChannels() {
  return { items: [] };
}

// The manifest needs search or home; a plugin with only channels has an empty home.
export async function home() {
  return [];
}

// A direct list never calls resolve: its entries play as they are.
export async function resolve() {
  await null;
  throw kino.error("not_found");
}
```

```
node sdk/run.mjs . --config lista=https://iptv-org.github.io/iptv/countries/co.m3u live categories
```

### 2. A token per channel { #recipe-token }

Your API lists the channels, and each play needs a freshly signed URL.
`liveChannels` returns `{ id, title, ref }` items; `resolve(ref)` signs the URL when the person
plays it. A channel's `expiresInSeconds` is ignored: when a live stream is cut, Kino simply calls
`resolve` again.

```json
{
  "id": "mi-tv", "name": "Mi TV", "version": "1.0.0", "apiVersion": 3, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": ["api.example.com", "cdn.example.com"],
  "capabilities": ["home", "resolve", "channels"],
  "settings": [{ "key": "token", "label": "Código de acceso", "type": "password", "required": true }]
}
```

```js
const API = "https://api.example.com";

async function api(path) {
  const r = await kino.fetch(API + path, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer " + kino.config.get("token") } });
  if (r.status === 401) throw kino.error("auth_required", "código de acceso inválido");
  if (!r.ok) throw kino.error("unavailable", "la API respondió " + r.status);
  return r.json();
}

export async function home() {
  return [];
}

export async function liveCategories() {
  const cats = await api("/categorias"); // [{ slug, nombre }]
  return cats.map((c) => ({ id: c.slug, title: c.nombre }));
}

// One page of a category. The ref is only the channel's id: the signed URL is made on play.
```
