- **Your own limits still apply.** The provider's `kino.fetch` stays on its own `hosts`, and Kino's services keep their limits
  ([`kino.tmdb`](kino-api.md#tmdb): 20 calls per 10 s per plugin on Kino's key). Design calls that cost one or two requests
  (TMDB's `byId` asks for the credits in the same request; `random` costs two).
- **Your manifest is the documentation.** Authors of consumers read your `provides` to know what to send and what comes back.
  Describe the door in your README too: what each call does, its errors, how often a stream changes.

### Changing a door later { #evolving }

Kino re-reads the provider's door at **every call**, never at install time of the consumer, so a change applies at once:

| Change in a provider update | What consumers see |
| --- | --- |
| A new call, stream or door | Nothing, until a consumer lists it in its own `consumes` |
| A new **optional** field in a type (`"rating": "number?"`) | Old consumers keep working; Kino passes the field once declared |
| A new **required** field in an `in` | Old consumers that do not send it get `bad_input`: avoid it, add an optional one |
| A call or stream removed or renamed | Every consumer that uses it gets `not_declared` |
| A field removed from an `out` type, or its type changed | Consumers that read it break silently or get `bad_output` |

So treat a published door like a public API: only add, and only optional fields. When you must break it, open a **new door**
(`movies2`) next to the old one and keep both for a while. A provider update that widens a door does not show the consent line
again to people who already have the consumer.

## The type language { #types }

A small, closed language, the same for `in`, `out` and `types`:

| Type | Means | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string`, `number`, `boolean` | the JSON primitive (`number` is a finite number) | `"id": "number"` |
| `T?` | optional: absent or `null` | `"director": "string?"` |
| `T[]` | an array of `T` | `"out": "Movie[]"` |
| `Name` | a type declared in the door's `types` | `"out": "Movie"` |
| `{ ... }` | an inline object of field to type | `"in": { "q": "string" }` |

Suffixes combine (`"string[]?"`: an optional list of strings; `"Movie?[]"`: a list whose items may be null). There is no
`any`, no union, no enum and no map: if you need a free-form value, send it as a `string` (JSON inside a string, if you must)
and document it.

| | Requests (`in`) | Answers (`out`, stream items) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Checked | **strictly** | **loosely** |
| An undeclared field | refused: `bad_input` | dropped silently |
| A required field missing | `bad_input` | `bad_output` |
| A wrong type | `bad_input`, never coerced (`"1990"` is not a `number`) | `bad_output`, never coerced |
| No argument at all | read as `{}` when every field of `in` is optional; else `bad_input` | — |
| Size | at most 64 KB of JSON (UTF-8 bytes) | at most 64 KB of JSON (UTF-8 bytes) |

Only the argument itself reads as `{}` when absent: a `null` nested inside it (an element of an `Opts[]`, say) is still
`bad_input`.

## The consumer in detail { #consumer }

### The `consumes` block { #consumes }

`consumes` maps a local alias to the door it stands for. **At most 8 entries.**

| Field | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| *key* (the alias) | Letters and digits, starting with a letter, at most 32. Only your code sees it |
| `repo` | Required. The provider's plain GitHub `owner/name` (no URL, no sub-path, no `@ref`), the same kind of string as `recommends`. A fork with another repository does **not** satisfy it |
| `door` | Required. The door's name in the provider's `provides` |
| `calls` | The call names you use, at most 16. A call not listed here answers `not_declared` even if the door has it |
| `streams` | The stream names you use, at most 8 |

Two aliases may point at the same door (rarely useful): the rate limit is per **provider door**, whatever alias reaches it.
A provider installed after the consumer simply starts working: nothing is resolved at install time.

### The consumer's `hosts` { #consumer-hosts }

Data that arrives through a door needs no host: `hosts` is only for what **your** plugin loads itself with `kino.fetch`. A
consumer whose only purpose is a screen that shows what its providers give is a **screen-only consumer**: `apiVersion` 20 or
later, a non-empty `consumes` and `capabilities` exactly `["screen"]`. It declares **`"hosts": []`** (`contract.json`,
`protocol.screenOnlyConsumer`), as Cine Trivia does.

- With no host its own `kino.fetch` calls are refused, unless it declares `"fetchHosts": "any"` (then they may reach any public
  https host, said in red on its install sheet) or has a `url` setting, alone or as a field of a `list` (the servers the person
  types). With no source capability it is no source.
- Drawing a picture needs **no** host declaration: an `Image` takes any public https address
  ([Image](screen-components.md#image): "no host declaration needed, as for every image in Kino"). The posters a provider hands
  you (TMDB's `posterUrl`) draw without `image.tmdb.org` in your manifest.
- With `"hosts": []` **and no setting at all**, its card in Plugins says it does not connect to the internet. Any setting rules
  that out (a typed address is a server, and what the person types could leave with a picture's address). It is still a
  consumer: its install sheet carries the «Usa datos de …» line of each door it uses.
- If your screen does fetch something of its own, declare that real host: the plugin keeps the screen-only status and the
  install sheet lists the host, so it must be true.
- Add any other capability (a catalog, `tracking`, a panel's `playerPanelTab`...), leave `consumes` empty, or stay below
  `apiVersion` 20 (with `consumes` only in `enhancements["20"]`), and the ordinary rule comes back: **at least one host**,
  unless it has a `url` setting (`The "hosts" field can only be empty if the plugin has a setting of type "url"`).
- Never publish a placeholder (`example.com`, a `.test` or `.invalid` name, a domain nobody runs): the person would read a
  host that is not true. `node sdk/init.mjs … --kind consumer` writes `"hosts": []` (or the host you pass with `--host`), and
  `node sdk/validate.mjs .` warns (`!`, still accepted) on `example.com`, `*.example.com`, `example.org`, `example.net` and
  anything under `.test`, `.invalid` or `.example`. For a screen-only consumer the warning reads `hosts: "example.com" is a
  placeholder host; a screen-only consumer needs no host: declare none ("hosts": []); its pictures from public https addresses
  need no declaration (see …)`; for any other plugin, `… is a placeholder host; declare a host the plugin really loads from`.

### A consumer that shows only text { #text-only-consumer }

A screen that shows only text (or pictures from public https addresses) and loads nothing of its own is a screen-only
consumer like any other: declare **`"hosts": []`**. There is nothing to invent and nothing to replace:

```json
{ "apiVersion": 20, "hosts": [], "capabilities": ["screen"], "consumes": { "recipes": { "repo": "owner/kino-plugin-recipes", "door": "recipes", "calls": ["byId"] } } }
```

The manifest needs real hosts again as soon as the plugin declares **any capability other than `screen`** (then list each host
its own `kino.fetch` really reaches). A `url` setting (alone or in a `list`) or `"fetchHosts": "any"` keeps `"hosts": []`
valid but opens the network: the first reaches the servers the person types, the second any public https host (said in red
on the sheet), and with any setting the card no longer says it connects to nothing. Images never need a host.

### A minimal consumer screen that draws clean { #minimal-consumer }

The smallest consumer that does everything right: the install gate, a `Scaffold` with one compact `AppBar`, a scroll, a button
that calls the door, an error sentence per code and a stream switch. It is checked with the kit: with the example provider,
`node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"installed":{"kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb":true}}' --provider <provider folder> . screen` prints no
`dropped` line, with `installed` `true` and `false`, with `--lang en` and with `--device tv`. `node sdk/init.mjs my-consumer
--kind consumer` scaffolds a bigger one with its own tests.

```json
{
  "id": "mini-trivia",
  "name": "Mini Trivia",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": 20,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Una pregunta de cine con las películas del plugin TMDB",
  "hosts": [],
  "capabilities": ["screen"],
  "screen": { "label": "Trivia", "labelEn": "Trivia" },
  "recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb"],
  "consumes": { "tmdb": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb", "door": "movies", "calls": ["random"], "streams": ["trending"] } }
}
```

```js
const TMDB = "kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb"; // exactly as written in "recommends"

const ERRORS = {
  provider_missing: ["TMDB está apagado o le falta configurarse: revísalo en Plugins.", "TMDB is off or needs setting up: check it in Plugins."],
  rate_limited: ["Demasiadas preguntas seguidas. Espera un momento.", "Too many questions in a row. Wait a moment."],
};
const OTHER = ["No se pudo traer la película. Intenta otra vez.", "Could not get the movie. Try again."];

const text = (es, en, more = {}) => ({ type: "Text", text: es, textEn: en, ...more });
const page = (children) => ({
  type: "Scaffold",
  appBar: {
    type: "AppBar", title: "Mini Trivia", titleEn: "Mini Trivia", mergeWithKinoBar: true, dense: true,
    leading: { type: "IconButton", icon: "close", labelText: "Cerrar", labelTextEn: "Close", onPressed: { close: true } },
  },
  body: { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Column", padding: 16, gap: 12, children }] },
});

export async function screen({ state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (installed[TMDB] !== true) {
    return page([
      text("Para jugar necesitas el plugin TMDB.", "To play you need the TMDB plugin."),
      { type: "ElevatedButton", key: "install", labelText: "Instalar TMDB", labelTextEn: "Install TMDB",
        onPressed: { go: { installPlugin: { repo: TMDB } } }, autofocus: true },
    ]);
  }
  const kids = [];
  if (state.movie) {
    if (state.movie.poster) kids.push({ type: "Image", url: state.movie.poster, aspect: "2:3", width: 160 }); // image.tmdb.org
    kids.push(text(`¿De qué año es ${state.movie.title}?`, `What year is ${state.movie.title} from?`, { style: "h3" }));
  }
  if (state.error) kids.push(text(...(ERRORS[state.error] || OTHER), { color: "error" }));
  kids.push({ type: "ElevatedButton", key: "play", labelText: "Otra película", labelTextEn: "Another movie", onPressed: "play", autofocus: true });
  kids.push({ type: "Switch", key: "live", labelText: "Tendencias en vivo", labelTextEn: "Live trending",
    value: state.protocol?.tmdb?.trending === true, onChanged: "live" });
  if (state.trending) kids.push(text(state.trending, state.trending, { style: "caption" }));
  return page(kids);
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, value, arg, state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (installed[TMDB] !== true) return null; // the gate: nothing works until the provider is installed
  if (name === "play") {
    try {
      const m = await kino.plugins.call("tmdb", "random", {});
      return { state: { movie: { title: m.title, year: m.year, poster: m.posterUrl ?? null }, error: null } };
    } catch (e) {
      return { state: { error: e.code || "provider_failed" } }; // provider_missing, rate_limited, timeout...
    }
  }
  if (name === "live") return { state: { protocol: { tmdb: { trending: value === true } } } };
  if (name === "protocol" && Array.isArray(arg?.items)) {
    return { state: { trending: arg.items.map((m) => m.title).slice(0, 5).join(", ") } };
  }
  return null;
}
```

Three traps that a Flutter habit walks into, and that the kit and Kino do not draw:

| You write | What happens | Write instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ type: "SingleChildScrollView", child: { … } }` | an **empty** scroll, and **no** `dropped` line warns you | `children: [ … ]`, a list, even for one child |
| `appBar: { title: "…" }` (no `type`) | `dropped: screen: scaffold appBar must be AppBar`: the whole bar is lost | `appBar: { type: "AppBar", title, titleEn, … }` |
| `{ type: "FilledButton", … }` | `unknown widget "FilledButton"`: the button is dropped | `ElevatedButton` (or `TextButton`) with `labelText` + `labelTextEn` and `onPressed` |

A `Text` whose `text` is `""` is dropped too (`text is empty`): leave the node out instead.

### `kino.plugins.call(alias, call, arg?)` { #call }

```js
const movie = await kino.plugins.call("tmdb", "byId", { id: 603 });
```

- `alias` is a key of your `consumes`, `call` a name listed there, `arg` JSON that matches the call's `in` (leave it out, or
  pass `{}`, when every field is optional).
- It resolves to the provider's answer, checked against `out`, or rejects with an `Error` whose `code` is one of the seven
  [error codes](#errors).
- **Where:** in `screen`, `screenEvent` and the other exports that can use Kino's services (a player panel's exports too).
  **Not** in a background `job` (it rejects with `not_allowed`) and not in `sign()`.
- **Feature detection:** `typeof kino.plugins === "object"`. Useful when a consumer offers the protocol through
  `enhancements["20"]` and keeps a lower `apiVersion` (see [Old Kinos](#versions)).
- Each call is independent: a screen's state lives in Kino, so a handler calls, answers with new `state`, and nothing has to
  stay alive between events. Do not cache answers in global variables expecting them to survive; put what you need in
  `state`, `kino.storage` or [`kino.shared`](jobs-and-shared.md#shared).

### Small recipes for a consumer { #consumer-recipes }

**The reserved `open` event.** It is the first `screenEvent` of every opening. While `installed[repo]` is not `true`, answer
`null`, like every other event: an `open` answer may not carry `go.installPlugin` (only the person's press or submit may), and
`open` drops every `go` except `go.screen`. When the provider is installed, `open` may load the first data (call the door and
answer a `state` patch) or answer `null` and wait for a press. After the person installs the provider, Kino calls `screen`
again with the new `installed`; it does **not** send a new `open`, so the main view must work with an empty `state` (a button,
or a `Skeleton` and a load on the first press).

**A search box** (three lines): a `TextField` with `kind: "search"` and `onSubmitted`; the event carries the typed text as
its `value` (not in `arg`).

```js
{ type: "TextField", key: "q", kind: "search", labelText: "Buscar", labelTextEn: "Search", onSubmitted: "search" }
// screenEvent({ name: "search", value }) -> value is the typed text: kino.plugins.call("recipes", "search", { q: value })
// kit: node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --provider <provider> . screenEvent search "" '"tomate"' --trigger submit
```

In `run.mjs` the value is the **third** word after `screenEvent` (`<name> [arg] [value]`, `""` for no `arg`) and it must be
JSON: `'"tomate"'` with the inner quotes, never `tomate` (`the value must be JSON`). `state.inputs.q` also holds what the
field shows; the full field is in [forms](screen-forms.md).

**A detail route.** Answer `{ route: { push: "detail", params: { id } } }` from the press; `screen` then gets
`route = { name: "detail", params: { id } }`; its `AppBar` `leading` is a back button whose event answers
`{ route: { pop: true } }`. Test the detail screen in the kit by giving the route in `--context`:

```sh
node sdk/run.mjs --context '{"installed":{"owner/kino-plugin-recipes":true},"route":{"name":"detail","params":{"id":1}}}' --state '{"item":{"id":1,"text":"Hola"}}' . screen
```

**A code you did not expect.** Keep a default sentence for any `code` your `switch` does not name (`provider_failed`'s, for
example): a newer Kino may add a code, and a missing case must not throw out of `screenEvent`.

**`focus` on a key inside a `ListView` item.** An answer's `focus` moves focus to the node with that key **only if a focusable
node with it is drawn at that moment**; otherwise it is ignored with no log. `ListView` draws its items lazily, so an item that
is off screen is not drawn and the `focus` does nothing; an item on screen with an `onTap` takes it. The kit accepts any key
and cannot tell: it is **not guaranteed**. Prefer `focus` on a key outside the list (a button) or on an item you know is
visible.

## Streams { #streams }

A stream is a subscription **Kino owns, tied to one of your screens**. Nothing runs in the background when no screen of yours
is open.

1. **Switch it on** with a state flag in your answer: `{ state: { protocol: { tmdb: { trending: true } } } }`, that is
   `state.protocol.<alias>.<stream> = true`. `false` switches it off. The `protocol` key is replaced whole like any other state
   key, so send all your flags together when you have more than one.
2. While that screen is **open, shown and Kino in front**, Kino calls the provider's `proto_<door>_<stream>(cursor)` every
   `everySeconds` (30 at least, 60 when the provider did not say), with the last cursor (`null` the first time).
3. Kino checks every item against the stream's `out` and drops the ones that do not match.
4. If there are new items, your `screenEvent` receives the event **`protocol`** with `arg` `{ alias, stream, items }`. Its answer
   is treated like an [`every` timer tick](screens.md#timers): only `state`, `toast`, `close` and `config` are kept.
5. Three failures in a row switch that subscription off for this opening of the screen. It never counts toward "No responde".

| Rule | Number |
| --- | --- |
| Live subscriptions per plugin | 4 |
| Flags read from `state.protocol` | 16 |
| Polls per provider door | 8 in any 10 s, shared by all its subscribers (separate from the 30 calls, so your calls never starve your polls) |
| Poll interval | `everySeconds` from 30 to 86,400; 60 by default |

Good to know:

- Closing the screen ends the subscription; nothing is persisted. Kino leaving the front stops every subscription.
- A feed's cursor is dropped when its last subscriber leaves: after a return the provider is polled from `null` again, and a
  batch already delivered **may arrive again**. Make your `protocol` handler idempotent (Cine Trivia only shows the newest
  title).
- A subscriber that joins a feed others already share gets only the items polled after it joined.
- Streams are for plugin screens, not for a player-panel session.
- The provider's cursor is its own business: an offset, a date, the list of ids already delivered (TMDB keeps up to 200 ids).
  It must be JSON, and small: it is part of the provider's answer, which may be at most 64 KB **together with the items**, and
  it comes back with every poll. Never put the items themselves in it.

## Errors { #errors }

`kino.plugins.call` rejects with an `Error` whose `code` is exactly one of these:

| `code` | When | What the consumer should do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider_missing` | The provider (the plugin of that repository) is not installed, is off or needs setup, or is 18+ while your plugin is not | Show the [install gate](#install-gate) (or "turn TMDB on") |
| `not_declared` | The alias is not in your `consumes`, the call or stream is not listed there, the provider's door lacks it, or the door is your own plugin's | A bug in your manifest, or the provider removed the call: log it, say "no disponible" |
| `bad_input` | Your argument does not match the call's `in`, is not JSON, or is over 64 KB | A bug in your code: check the provider's types |
| `bad_output` | The provider's answer does not match `out`, is not JSON, is over 64 KB, or holds one of its sealed secrets | The provider's bug: show a short error with "Reintentar" |
| `rate_limited` | More than 30 calls in any 10 s from your plugin to one door of one provider (whatever alias you use) | Slow down; never retry in a loop |
| `timeout` | The provider took more than 10 s | Offer "Reintentar" |
| `provider_failed` | The provider threw, or does not export `proto_<door>_<call>` | Offer "Reintentar"; if it keeps failing, the provider has a problem |

In a background `job`, `kino.plugins.call` rejects with `not_allowed`. The rejection is a normal `Error`: always `await` the
call inside `try`/`catch`, and show the person a sentence of your own, in Spanish and English, never the raw code alone.

```js
try {
  const list = await kino.plugins.call("tmdb", "search", { q });
  return { state: { results: list } };
} catch (e) {
  if (e.code === "provider_missing") return { state: { needsTmdb: true } };      // the screen draws the install button
  return { toast: { text: "TMDB no respondió, intenta otra vez", textEn: "TMDB did not answer, try again" } };
}
```

## Limits { #limits }

| What | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Doors per provider | 4 |
| Calls / streams per door | 16 / 8 |
| Door `summary` | 120 characters |
| Names (door, call, stream, alias) | `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,31}$` |
| Type names | `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,31}$` |
| `consumes` entries | 8; each lists at most 16 calls and 8 streams |
| Request and answer | JSON, at most 64 KB (65,536 UTF-8 bytes) each |
| Time per call | 10 s |
| Calls | 30 in any 10 s, per consumer and provider door |
| Stream interval | `everySeconds` 30 to 86,400, default 60 |
| Live subscriptions | 4 per consumer; 16 flags read from the state |
| Polls | 8 in any 10 s per provider door |
| Where | screens and the other exports; never a background `job` (`not_allowed`) nor `sign()` |

The same numbers are in [Limits and engine quirks](engine-limits.md#limits).

## A plugin that only provides { #provides-only }

A plugin whose **only** purpose is to open doors needs nothing else: `apiVersion` 20, a non-empty `provides`, no capability at
all (the `capabilities` field may be left out) and no settings. Such a plugin is **provides-only** and may declare
`"hosts": []`. It plays nothing, is no source and does not show up in search or Home. With `"hosts": []` its consent sheet
claims no network and no role, and its installed card says it does not connect to the internet: it reaches the world only
through Kino's services, such as [`kino.tmdb`](kino-api.md#tmdb). `node sdk/init.mjs my-provider --kind provider` scaffolds
one, with its test.

There is **no `providesOnly` field**: Kino derives it from those conditions, and `node sdk/validate.mjs` warns if you write one.

```json
{
  "id": "movie-facts",
  "name": "Movie Facts",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 20,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": [],
  "provides": {
    "facts": {
      "summary": "Short facts about a movie",
      "calls": { "forMovie": { "in": { "tmdbId": "number" }, "out": "string[]" } }
    }
  }
}
```

- **A provider that needs `kino.fetch`** (its own API instead of a Kino service) lists those hosts in `hosts`, like any plugin.
  That does not make it lose the status: with no capability and no setting it is still provides-only (no `resolve`, `search`
  or `home` to write), but its consent sheet now lists those hosts.
- Declare any capability or any setting, or put `provides` below `apiVersion` 20, and the ordinary rules come back (`resolve`
  and `search` or `home`, at least one host...).
- The other side has the same freedom: a [screen-only consumer](#consumer-hosts) (a non-empty `consumes`, `capabilities`
  exactly `["screen"]`) may declare `"hosts": []` too.

## Old Kinos: `apiVersion` 20 or `enhancements["20"]` { #versions }

| How you declare it | On Kino 0.9.81 or newer | On an older Kino |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"apiVersion": 20` with `provides` / `consumes` at the top level | Works | The plugin does not install («Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino») |
| A lower `apiVersion` with `provides` / `consumes` at the top level | **Refused**: `The "provides" block needs apiVersion 20` | Ignored |
| A lower `apiVersion` with `"enhancements": { "20": { "provides": … } }` | Works: the block is merged and checked as `apiVersion` 20 | The block is ignored; the plugin installs and works as before |

- A **provider** that already has users should use `enhancements["20"]` (TMDB's way): nobody loses the plugin.
- A **consumer** that only makes sense with its provider can declare `apiVersion` 20 (Cine Trivia's way). A consumer that has
  other uses can put `consumes` in `enhancements["20"]` and hide the feature with `typeof kino.plugins === "object"`.
- `recommends` and `installed` have no `apiVersion` of their own (Kino 0.9.81 reads them at any `apiVersion`, an older Kino
  ignores them); `go.installPlugin` is honoured from `apiVersion` 19 (below it, Kino drops it and logs it).
- A block inside `enhancements` that breaks a rule is dropped and logged, never refusing your plugin: run
  `node sdk/validate.mjs .`, which lists every drop. More in [Screens without raising your apiVersion](enhancements.md).

## What the person sees { #what-people-see }

- **On the consumer's install sheet**, one plain informational line per door it uses, not red and without a switch:
  «Usa datos de TMDB (Movie records from TMDB)» («Uses data from TMDB (Movie records from TMDB)» in English): the provider's
  `name` and the door's `summary`. If the provider is not installed yet, the line names its repository instead
  («Usa datos de kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb»).
- **On an update** that adds a door to `consumes`, the line is marked new (also in the notice of an update Kino applied on its
  own).
- **No prompt per call.** Having the provider installed is the consent.
- **Nothing installs silently.** A consumer can only show a [`go.installPlugin`](screen-forms.md#go-install-plugin) button;
  Kino opens its own install sheet with the provider's own consent lines, and only the person's Instalar installs it.
- **On its card in Plugins**, a screen-only consumer with `"hosts": []` and no setting says it does not connect to the
  internet; with any setting it does not.
- **Removing the provider** only makes its doors answer `provider_missing`; the consumers are not changed or uninstalled.
- **Nothing new is synced**: the protocol stores nothing. Keep your own state in `kino.storage` or `kino.shared` as usual.

## Security and privacy { #security }

!!! warning "Your arguments reach the provider"
    The consent line says that the consumer uses the provider's data; it says nothing about what the consumer **sends**.
    Every argument of every call reaches the provider, which may send it to its own `hosts` (or to any public host, with
    `"fetchHosts": "any"`). Never put in an argument what you would not hand to the provider's author: no tokens, no
    passwords, nothing the person typed in a private field.

- **18+:** an 18+ provider answers only an 18+ consumer. To any other plugin its doors answer `provider_missing`, so 18+
  content never crosses into a plugin that is shown with the 18+ lock closed.
- **Sealed secrets never cross.** An answer (or a stream poll) that holds one of the provider's [sealed secrets](manifest.md#secrets),
  in any form, or a secret marker, is `bad_output`, the same rule `kino.shared` applies.
- **No self-calls.** A plugin cannot use its own door: it answers `not_declared` (the call would wait on itself until the
  timeout). Two plugins that use each other's doors must not call back from inside an answer: the second call may wait on the
  first until `timeout`.
- **Hosts are not widened.** Receiving data from a provider gives the consumer no new host: what it fetches is still limited
  to its own approved `hosts`.
- **Only declared data leaves.** The provider decides in code what to answer; Kino drops every field the door does not
  declare.
- **Repository, not id.** A consumer names its provider by repository. A plugin that copies the provider's `id` from another
  repository (or a fork) is not that provider.

## Testing offline with the kit { #kit }

**Start from a scaffold.** Both have the right shapes from the first line and a test that passes as they come:

```sh
node sdk/init.mjs my-provider --kind provider
#   provides-only (apiVersion 20, "hosts": [], no capabilities), door "quotes" with a call and a stream, test/plugin.test.mjs
node sdk/init.mjs my-consumer --kind consumer --repo owner/kino-plugin-quotes --door quotes --call byId
#   a screen-only consumer with "hosts": [] (--host <a host it really fetches from> adds one), the install gate, one compact bar (mergeWithKinoBar + dense, a close leading), a detail route with a back,
#   an error per code, a stream switch and TV focus; test/provider is a STAND-IN provider with the same door/call names
node sdk/init.mjs --help
```

`--door`, `--call` and `--stream` (default `quotes`, `byId`, `latest`) take the **real door's names**, for a provider too, so
the consumer, its stand-in and the provider agree. `test/provider` is a **stand-in**, not the real provider (its
`README.md` says so): replace it with a copy of the real provider (the same door, call and stream names and types), then adapt
the argument and the fields your code reads, and the scaffold's test. The consumer's `description` comes out as a Spanish
`TODO:` to rewrite, `screen.labelEn` as an English label (the door's name: check it).

Then copy the kit next to the new plugin: `sdk/` **without `sdk/test/`** and `contract.json` (both required; `kino.d.ts` is
optional, only for your editor's typings: the kit never reads it; see [Test it locally](test-locally.md#copy-the-kit)), and
replace the scaffold's placeholder `your-user/...` with the provider's real repository. The consumer's `"hosts": []` is no
placeholder: leave it empty unless the screen fetches something of its own.

**A provider on its own**, with no consumer: `proto` sends one call or one poll through the app's checks (the argument strictly
against `in`, the answer loosely against `out`) and its error codes:

```sh
node sdk/run.mjs ./my-provider proto quotes.byId '{"id":1}'    # a call: prints the checked answer
node sdk/run.mjs ./my-provider proto quotes.byId '{"id":"1"}'  # ✗ bad_input: $.id: expected number
node sdk/run.mjs ./my-provider proto quotes.latest             # a stream's first poll (cursor null): prints { items, cursor }
node sdk/run.mjs ./my-provider proto quotes.latest '2'         # the next poll, from the cursor the last one printed
```

Exit code 0 with the answer on stdout; 1 with `✗ <code>: <message>` on stderr when Kino would reject the call (if your export
threw, its own message follows on a `·` line: the consumer never sees it); 2 for a wrong command (a door or call that does
not exist, which it lists; JSON that does not parse; a folder without `provides`).

**A consumer with its provider.** `--provider <folder>` (repeatable) loads the provider in its own sandbox and answers every
`kino.plugins.call` from its exports; without it every call rejects with `provider_missing`. Pass `installed` to `screenEvent`
too: a consumer with an install gate does nothing while it is `false`.

```sh
I='{"installed":{"kinotvapp/kino-plugin-tmdb":true}}'
node sdk/run.mjs ./cine-trivia screen                                    # the install gate: every recommends entry is false
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --provider ../kino-plugin-tmdb ./cine-trivia screen
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --lang en --provider ../kino-plugin-tmdb ./cine-trivia screen   # the English texts
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --device tv --provider ../kino-plugin-tmdb ./cine-trivia screen
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --provider ../kino-plugin-tmdb ./cine-trivia screenEvent play
# a stream: one poll, sent as the "protocol" event { alias, stream, items }; --cursor polls from a given cursor
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --state '{"protocol":{"tmdb":{"trending":true}}}' --provider ../kino-plugin-tmdb ./cine-trivia screenEvent protocol tmdb.trending
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --cursor '[603]' --provider ../kino-plugin-tmdb ./cine-trivia screenEvent protocol tmdb.trending
```

- **Read stderr.** A `· dropped: …` line is a node Kino would not draw. The exit code stays 0 when nodes are dropped, so a
  clean run is one with no `dropped` line. `node sdk/run.mjs` with no arguments prints every command.
- **`--cursor`** lets you send a cursor the provider already returned, to see what your `protocol` handler does with a batch
  it may have seen before (Kino can resend items after a return).
- **Which error codes the kit can provoke.** With a real provider folder only two: `provider_missing` (run without
  `--provider`) and `provider_failed` (a call the provider throws on, such as an id it does not have); `proto` also shows
  `bad_input` for a wrong argument. `not_declared`, `bad_output`, `rate_limited` and `timeout` need a broken manifest, a broken
  provider or real time, so test that your screen **draws** each one by putting the code in the state:
  `node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --state '{"error":"rate_limited"}' . screen` (and a made-up code, for your default).
- **Check that a prop is accepted.** The printed tree is the checked one and does not echo every flag (an `AppBar`'s
  `dense: true`, for instance, is not printed). A wrong value is: `dense: "yes"` prints
  `· dropped: screen: appBar dense "yes" is not true or false, ignored`. So a run with no `dropped` line means every prop was
  accepted; `--raw` prints the tree exactly as your plugin returned it. The app draws `dense` on a phone (4 dp above and below
  the bar's row) and ignores it on a TV and in a player panel ([One compact bar](screen-components.md#one-compact-bar)).
- **The kit ignores `repo`.** It has no repositories, so it serves each `consumes` entry with the **first provider that has
  its door**; the app matches the entry's `repo`. Check by hand that `repo` is the provider's exact GitHub `owner/name`
  (open `https://github.com/<owner/name>`), the same string in `recommends` and in the key your code reads from `installed`.
- The provider's own services work as usual in the kit: TMDB needs `KINO_TMDB_KEY` or a `KINO_TMDB_FIXTURE` for `kino.tmdb`
  ([Test it locally](test-locally.md#kino-services)).
- **`node sdk/validate.mjs <folder>`** reads `provides` and `consumes` (top level and in `enhancements`) the way the app does.
  It **fails** (`✗`, exit 1) when a declared call or stream has no `proto_<door>_<name>` export (Kino installs it, but every
  consumer's call to it answers `provider_failed`; the name is case-sensitive). It **warns** (`!`, exit 0: read each one) when a
  consumed repository is missing from `recommends` (the install gate would never open), when a stream's `everySeconds` is
  outside 30..86,400 (it says the value Kino uses), when the manifest has a `providesOnly` field (there is none) and when a
  `hosts` entry is a placeholder (`example.com`, `*.example.com`, `example.org`, `.test`, `.invalid`, `.example`; a
  screen-only consumer is told to declare none, see [the consumer's `hosts`](#consumer-hosts)).
- In your own tests, `createProtocolCaller` and `createKino(manifest, { protocol })` from `sdk/protocol.mjs` give you the same
  caller.
- `--provider` and `sdk/protocol.mjs` belong to the kit of Kino 0.9.81, and `proto`, `--cursor`, `--lang` and
  `init.mjs --kind` to its later copies. If `run.mjs` or `init.mjs` does not know one of them, or `validate.mjs` does not know
  `provides`, your copy of `sdk/`, `contract.json` and `kino.d.ts` is older: replace all three from
  [kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-plugin-sdk) (never silence the error by removing the blocks).

!!! warning "What only the app checks"
    The kit does **not** apply the 18+ rule, the refusal of sealed secrets in answers, nor the self-call refusal, and it does
    not match `repo`: those need the installed plugins, and only Kino has them. Before publishing, install both plugins in
    Kino 0.9.81 or newer and try the real flow: the install gate, a call, the stream switch, and removing the provider.
    More in [What the kit cannot copy](engine-limits.md#kit-protocol).

## Checklists { #checklists }

**Provider**

- `provides` at the top level with `"apiVersion": 20`, or in `enhancements["20"]` to keep your `apiVersion`.
- One export per call and per stream: `proto_<door>_<name>`, spelled exactly like the manifest (case included).
- Every answer matches `out`; a stream answers `{ items, cursor }`.
- Nothing private in answers or in thrown messages; no sealed secret anywhere in an answer.
- A short `summary` the person understands; the door described in your README.
- Changes after publishing only add (new calls, optional fields); a breaking change goes to a new door.
- `node sdk/validate.mjs .` shows no `✗` (a missing `proto_` export fails) and you read every `!`.
- Each call tried with `node sdk/run.mjs . proto <door>.<call> '<json>'` (also with a bad argument), each stream with
  `proto <door>.<stream>` and again from the cursor it printed.
- A provides-only plugin has no capability, no setting and no `providesOnly` field; its `hosts` are `[]` or the real ones its
  `kino.fetch` needs.

**Consumer**

- `consumes` with the provider's exact `repo`, `door`, and only the calls and streams you use.
- The same repository in `recommends`, and an install screen with `go.installPlugin` while `installed[repo]` is not
  `true`.
- Every `kino.plugins.call` in `try`/`catch`, with a Spanish and English message per case; no retry loops.
- Arguments carry nothing the provider's author should not see.
- No calls from a background `job`.
- A `protocol` handler that tolerates repeated items (try it with `--cursor`).
- `hosts` is `[]` for a screen-only consumer (only `screen`, a non-empty `consumes`), or the real hosts its own `kino.fetch`
  reaches; never `example.com` or another placeholder.
- `node sdk/validate.mjs .` shows no `!` about `recommends`; your `repo` checked by hand (the kit ignores it).
- The screen drawn with `installed` `true` and `false`, with `--lang en` and with `--device tv`, with no `dropped` line.
- Tried with `--provider` in the kit, and in the app with the real provider installed, switched off and removed.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/protocol-quick/ (docs/protocol-quick.en.md) -->

# The plugin protocol on one page { #protocol-quick }

The minimum an AI (or a person) needs to write a **provider** and a **consumer** of the plugin protocol (apiVersion 20, Kino
0.9.81). Every line points to the long page, [The plugin protocol](protocol.md), for the rest.

## Start from the scaffolds { #start }

```sh
node sdk/init.mjs my-provider --kind provider --door recipes --call byId
node sdk/init.mjs my-consumer --kind consumer --door recipes --call byId --repo owner/kino-plugin-recipes   # writes "hosts": []
```

Copy next to each plugin `sdk/` **without `sdk/test/`** and `contract.json` (both required; `kino.d.ts` is optional, only for
editor typings). The consumer's `test/provider` is a **stand-in**: replace it with a copy of the real provider
([Testing offline](protocol.md#kit)).

## Provider { #provider }

```json
{ "id": "recipes", "name": "Recetas", "version": "0.1.0", "apiVersion": 20, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Recetas para otros plugins", "hosts": [],
  "provides": { "recipes": { "summary": "Recetas con sus ingredientes",
    "calls": { "byId": { "in": { "id": "number" }, "out": "Recipe" } },
    "streams": { "latest": { "out": "Recipe", "everySeconds": 300 } },
    "types": { "Recipe": { "id": "number", "title": "string", "imageUrl": "string?" } } } } }
```

```js
export async function proto_recipes_byId({ id }) { /* return a Recipe, or throw: the consumer gets provider_failed */ }
export async function proto_recipes_latest(cursor) { return { items: [/* new Recipes */], cursor: 0 /* small JSON */ }; }
```

No capabilities and no settings make it **provides-only** (`hosts` `[]`, or the real hosts its `kino.fetch` reads). Names:
`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,31}$`. Types: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `T?`, `T[]`, a door type, an inline object
([types](protocol.md#types)). Test: `node sdk/run.mjs . proto recipes.byId '{"id":1}'`, `node sdk/run.mjs . proto
recipes.latest` (exit 0 answer, 1 `✗ <code>`, 2 bad command).

## Consumer { #consumer }

```json
{ "id": "recipe-picker", "name": "Recetario", "version": "0.1.0", "apiVersion": 20, "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Elige una receta del plugin Recetas", "hosts": [],
  "capabilities": ["screen"], "screen": { "label": "Recetario", "labelEn": "Recipes" },
  "recommends": ["owner/kino-plugin-recipes"],
  "consumes": { "recipes": { "repo": "owner/kino-plugin-recipes", "door": "recipes", "calls": ["byId"], "streams": ["latest"] } } }
```

`"hosts": []`: a **screen-only consumer** (a non-empty `consumes`, `capabilities` exactly `["screen"]`) declares no host, and an
`Image` needs no declaration. Add a real host only if the screen's own `kino.fetch` reaches it (any other capability brings back
"at least one host"); never `example.com` or a made-up name ([the consumer's `hosts`](protocol.md#consumer-hosts)).

The minimal screen (install gate, one compact bar with a real exit, a call, an error sentence with a default):

```js
const REPO = "owner/kino-plugin-recipes"; // exactly as in "recommends"
const t = (es, en, more = {}) => ({ type: "Text", text: es, textEn: en, ...more });
const page = (kids) => ({ type: "Scaffold",
  appBar: { type: "AppBar", title: "Recetario", titleEn: "Recipes", mergeWithKinoBar: true, dense: true,
    leading: { type: "IconButton", icon: "close", labelText: "Cerrar", labelTextEn: "Close", onPressed: { close: true } } },
  body: { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Column", padding: 16, gap: 12, children: kids }] } });
const ERR = { provider_missing: ["Recetas está apagado: revísalo en Plugins.", "Recipes is off: check it in Plugins."] };
const OTHER = ["No se pudo traer la receta.", "Could not get the recipe."]; // the default for any other code

export async function screen({ state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (installed[REPO] !== true) return page([t("Necesitas el plugin Recetas.", "You need the Recipes plugin."),
    { type: "ElevatedButton", key: "install", labelText: "Instalar", labelTextEn: "Install",
      onPressed: { go: { installPlugin: { repo: REPO } } }, autofocus: true }]);
  const kids = [];
  if (state.title) kids.push(t(state.title, state.title, { style: "h3" }));
  if (state.error) kids.push(t(...(ERR[state.error] || OTHER), { color: "error" }));
  kids.push({ type: "ElevatedButton", key: "next", labelText: "Otra receta", labelTextEn: "Another recipe", onPressed: "next", autofocus: true });
  return page(kids);
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (installed[REPO] !== true) return null; // the gate; `open` too
  if (name !== "next") return null;
  try {
    const r = await kino.plugins.call("recipes", "byId", { id: (state.n || 0) + 1 });
    return { state: { title: r.title, n: (state.n || 0) + 1, error: null } };
  } catch (e) { return { state: { error: e.code || "provider_failed", n: 0 } }; }
}
```

Test it (`I='{"installed":{"owner/kino-plugin-recipes":true}}'`; a clean run prints no `dropped` line):

```sh
node sdk/validate.mjs .                                                  # no ✗; read every !
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --provider ../my-provider . screen       # also --lang en, --device tv, and without --context (the gate)
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --provider ../my-provider . screenEvent next
node sdk/run.mjs --context "$I" --state '{"error":"timeout"}' . screen    # every code is drawn from the state
```

More: a [search box, a detail route, `open`, unknown codes and `focus`](protocol.md#consumer-recipes), [streams](protocol.md#streams),
[errors](protocol.md#errors), [the kit](protocol.md#kit).

## The five traps { #traps }

1. `SingleChildScrollView` takes `children` (a list): with `child` the scroll is empty and **no** `dropped` line warns you.
2. `appBar` must be `{ "type": "AppBar", … }`: without `type` the whole bar is dropped.
3. There is no `FilledButton`: use `ElevatedButton`/`TextButton` with `labelText` + `labelTextEn` and `onPressed`; and a
   `Text` with `text: ""` is dropped.
4. Without `--context '{"installed":{…:true}}'` the kit draws the install gate and a gated `screenEvent` answers nothing;
   without `--provider` every call is `provider_missing`.
5. A `run.mjs screenEvent` value is the third word and JSON: `screenEvent search "" '"tomate"'`, never `tomate`.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/share/ (docs/share.en.md) -->

# Sharing: to Kino Social and with cards { #share }

Any plugin can offer the person a **Compartir** (Share) button. This page has two parts:

- **[Sharing to Kino Social today](#social)** (Kino 0.9.81 or newer, with Kino Social 0.9.7 or later): your plugin proposes a
  post to Kino Social (a text and, if you like, the title the person is watching) through the `wall` door of the
  [plugin protocol](protocol.md). Kino Social keeps it as a **draft**; the person reviews it and posts it there. **Nothing is
  published without the person.**
- **[Share cards](#cards)** (Kino 0.9.84, not published yet): the pieces that let a plugin open another plugin's content from a
  card: [`go.plugin`](#go-plugin), [`openFrom.routes`](#open-from), [`ctx.caller`](#ctx-caller) and
  [`kino.image.thumbnail`](#thumbnail).

Look at Megaplay ([xuper-plugin/kino-plugin-megaplay](https://github.com/xuper-plugin/kino-plugin-megaplay), its
`src/browse/share.js`) as the published example: it shares from a title page and from the bar.

!!! tip "Not the `share` answer"
    A screen's `share` answer (apiVersion 17) opens the device's own share sheet. This page is about something else: sending
    something to Kino Social, or opening another plugin's content.

## Sharing to Kino Social today { #social }

!!! note "Kino 0.9.81 or newer, with Kino Social 0.9.7 or later"
    The `wall` door arrives in Kino Social 0.9.7 ([kinotvapp/kino-social](https://github.com/kinotvapp/kino-social)). It sits in
    its `enhancements["20"]`, so only Kino 0.9.81 or newer opens it. Your plugin uses it as a consumer of the
    [plugin protocol](protocol.md) (`apiVersion` 20, or `consumes` inside `enhancements["20"]`).

**What happens when your plugin shares:**

1. The person presses **Compartir** on your screen, types (or keeps) a text and sends.
2. Your plugin calls `kino.plugins.call("social", "share", { … })`.
3. Kino Social **publishes nothing**: it keeps the proposal as a draft on the device and answers
   `{ status: "draft", draftId, pending }`.
4. Kino's bell announces it («Megaplay quiere publicar en tu muro») and Kino Social's wall shows the draft at the top, with
   **Revisar** and **Descartar**. Revisar opens Kino Social's composer filled in (with the title's poster, if you sent one);
   the person presses **Publicar** themselves, or discards it.

### The manifest { #social-manifest }

```json
"consumes": { "social": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-social", "door": "wall", "calls": ["share"] } },
"recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-social"]
```

- `social` is your local alias, the first argument of `kino.plugins.call`.
- `recommends` names the same repository: `screen` and `screenEvent` then get `installed["kinotvapp/kino-social"]`, so you
  know whether to offer installing it.
- With `"apiVersion": 20` both sit at the top level. If your plugin keeps a lower `apiVersion` to keep installing on older
  Kinos, `consumes` goes inside `enhancements["20"]` and the feature hides behind `typeof kino.plugins === "object"`.
  Megaplay, for example, keeps `apiVersion` 9, declares its screen in `enhancements["14"]` and its `consumes` in
  `enhancements["20"]` (next to `"capabilities": ["screen"]`).
- Sharing needs no host: what you send reaches Kino Social through Kino, not over the network.

### The `share` call { #share-call }

```js
const r = await kino.plugins.call("social", "share", {
  text: "Estoy viendo «Frieren»",                                   // optional, up to 500 characters
  title: { kind: "series", tmdb: 209867, season: 1, episode: 3 },   // optional: a movie or series by its TMDB id
  link: "https://example.com/page",                                 // optional, https only
  from: "My plugin",                                                // optional: your plugin's name
});
// r = { status: "draft", draftId: "…", pending: 1 }
```

| Field | Type | What Kino Social does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string?` | The proposed text. Control characters out, extra blank lines folded, cut at 500 characters (its composer's limit) |
| `title` | `{ kind, tmdb, season?, episode? }?` | The title to attach. `kind` is `"movie"` or `"series"`; `tmdb` a positive whole TMDB id. `season` and `episode` (both positive whole numbers) count only on a series. On review, Kino Social fetches the name, year and poster from TMDB |
| `link` | `string?` | An `https` link (at most 500 characters, no user or password). It goes at the end of the text on review |
| `from` | `string?` | Your name, at most 40 characters. Shown in the notice («My plugin quiere publicar en tu muro») |

- **At least one** of `text`, `title` or `link`. **Text-only** sharing is valid: leave `title` out (Megaplay does so from its
  bar, or when the person switches «Adjuntar el título» off).
- Kino checks the types against the door: an extra field, or a wrong type (`tmdb: "209867"`), is `bad_input`. Kino Social
  checks the meaning: an empty proposal, a `kind` other than `movie` or `series`, or a non-https link is refused, and you get
  `provider_failed`.
- **The answer:** `status` is `"draft"`, `draftId` the draft's id and `pending` how many drafts wait (at most 5: the oldest
  goes). The same proposal twice (same text, title and link) keeps one draft. Drafts older than 14 days are dropped.
- `from` is your own word: Kino Social 0.9.7 does not know which plugin calls and shows what you send. Put your plugin's real
  name.

### Errors and what to do { #share-errors }

| What happens | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `typeof kino.plugins !== "object"` (Kino before 0.9.81) | Do not call: a toast «Actualiza Kino para compartir en Kino Social» |
| `provider_missing` and `installed["kinotvapp/kino-social"]` is not `true` | Kino Social is not installed: answer `go: { installPlugin: { repo: "kinotvapp/kino-social" } }` so Kino opens its install sheet (the person decides) |
| `provider_missing` with `installed[…] === true` | Kino Social is off or needs setting up: say so in a sentence (a `go.installPlugin` of an installed plugin only shows «Ese plugin ya está instalado») |
| `not_declared` | Your `consumes` does not list `share`, or the installed Kino Social is older than 0.9.7 and has no `wall` door: ask the person to update Kino Social |
| `bad_input` | A bug in your code: an extra field or a wrong type |
| `provider_failed` | Kino Social refused the proposal (empty, a bad title or link) or failed: «No se pudo enviar a Kino Social. Inténtalo de nuevo.» |
| `rate_limited`, `timeout` | Offer to try again; never retry in a loop |

Always keep a default sentence for a code you did not expect. The full list of codes is in [Errors](protocol.md#errors).

### Rules { #share-rules }

- **Only from the person's press.** Share when the person pressed Compartir and sent; never from `open`, a timer, a `job`
  (there `kino.plugins.call` answers `not_allowed`) or on your own.
- **Never publish on the person's behalf.** The door only leaves a draft; do not tell the person it was posted. Tell them it
  waits in Kino Social for them to review.
- **Let the person see and change the text** before it goes, and drop the title if they do not want to share it.
- **Nothing private.** What you send reaches Kino Social: no tokens, no setting values, nothing the person typed in a private
  field.
- **Texts in Spanish and English**, like everything the person reads.

### A complete minimal example { #share-example }

A screen with a **Compartir** button (in the bar, text only; and in the content, with the title), a sheet with the text and an
«Adjuntar el título» switch, and the send. Megaplay's shape, simplified.

```json
{
  "id": "mi-plugin",
  "name": "Mi plugin",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 20,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "hosts": [],
  "capabilities": ["screen"],
  "screen": { "label": "Mi plugin", "labelEn": "My plugin" },
  "recommends": ["kinotvapp/kino-social"],
  "consumes": { "social": { "repo": "kinotvapp/kino-social", "door": "wall", "calls": ["share"] } }
}
```

```js
const SOCIAL = "kinotvapp/kino-social";   // exactly as written in "recommends"
const SHEET = "shareSheet";
const TITLE = { kind: "series", tmdb: 209867, name: "Frieren" };   // the title this page shows

const en = () => String(kino.lang || "").startsWith("en");
const say = (es, english) => ({ toast: es, toastEn: english });

function shareSheet(share) {
  return {
    type: "BottomSheet", key: SHEET, title: "Compartir en Kino Social", titleEn: "Share on Kino Social",
    children: [{ type: "Form", key: "shareForm", onSubmitted: { event: "sendShare", timeoutMs: 15000 }, gap: 12, children: [
      { type: "TextField", key: "shareText", multiline: true, maxLines: 6, maxLength: 500,
        labelText: "Qué quieres contar", labelTextEn: "What do you want to say" },
      ...(share ? [{ type: "Switch", key: "shareTitle", value: true, labelText: "Adjuntar el título", labelTextEn: "Attach the title" }] : []),
      { type: "Text", style: "caption", color: "muted",
        text: "Llega a Kino Social como borrador: allá lo revisas y lo publicas.",
        textEn: "It reaches Kino Social as a draft: you review and post it there." },
      { type: "ElevatedButton", key: "shareSend", icon: "send", submit: true,
        labelText: "Enviar a Kino Social", labelTextEn: "Send to Kino Social" },
    ] }],
  };
}

export async function screen({ state = {} }) {
  return {
    type: "Scaffold",
    appBar: {
      type: "AppBar", title: "Mi plugin", titleEn: "My plugin", mergeWithKinoBar: true, dense: true,
      leading: { type: "IconButton", icon: "close", labelText: "Cerrar", labelTextEn: "Close", onPressed: { close: true } },
      actions: [{ type: "IconButton", key: "shareBar", icon: "share", labelText: "Compartir", labelTextEn: "Share",
        onPressed: { event: "openShare", arg: "" } }],                       // from the bar: text only
    },
    body: { type: "SingleChildScrollView", children: [{ type: "Column", padding: 16, gap: 12, children: [
      { type: "Text", text: TITLE.name, textEn: TITLE.name, style: "h3" },
      { type: "ElevatedButton", key: "share", icon: "share", labelText: "Compartir", labelTextEn: "Share", autofocus: true,
        onPressed: { event: "openShare", arg: "title" } },                    // from the title: with the title
      shareSheet(state.share || null),
    ] }] },
  };
}

export async function screenEvent({ name, arg, value, state = {}, installed = {} }) {
  if (name === "openShare") {
    const share = arg === "title" ? TITLE : null;
    const text = share ? (en() ? `I'm watching "${share.name}"` : `Estoy viendo «${share.name}»`) : "";
    return { state: { share, inputs: { shareText: text, shareTitle: !!share } }, ui: [{ open: SHEET }] };
  }
  if (name === "sendShare") {
    // The form's fields come as value; state.inputs holds them too.
    const v = { ...(state.inputs || {}), ...(value && typeof value === "object" ? value : {}) };
    return sendShare(v, state.share || null, installed);
  }
  return null;
}

async function sendShare(v, share, installed) {
  const text = String(v.shareText || "").trim().slice(0, 500);
  const withTitle = !!share && v.shareTitle !== false;
  if (!text && !withTitle) return say("Escribe algo o adjunta el título.", "Write something or attach the title.");
  if (typeof kino.plugins !== "object") return say("Actualiza Kino para compartir en Kino Social.", "Update Kino to share on Kino Social.");
  const arg = { from: "Mi plugin" };
  if (text) arg.text = text;
  if (withTitle) arg.title = { kind: share.kind, tmdb: share.tmdb };
  try {
    await kino.plugins.call("social", "share", arg);
    return { ui: [{ close: SHEET }], state: { share: null },
      ...say("Listo: tienes el borrador en Kino Social para revisarlo y publicarlo.", "Done: the draft waits in Kino Social for you to review and post.") };
  } catch (e) {
    const code = e && e.code;
    if (code === "provider_missing" && installed[SOCIAL] !== true) {
      return { ui: [{ close: SHEET }], go: { installPlugin: { repo: SOCIAL } },
        ...say("Instala Kino Social para compartir.", "Install Kino Social to share.") };
    }
    if (code === "provider_missing") return say("Kino Social está apagado o le falta configurarse: revísalo en Plugins.", "Kino Social is off or needs setting up: check it in Plugins.");
    if (code === "not_declared") return say("Actualiza Kino Social para compartir.", "Update Kino Social to share.");
    return say("No se pudo enviar a Kino Social. Inténtalo de nuevo.", "Could not send to Kino Social. Try again.");
  }
}
```

- The sheet is a [declared pop-up](screen-forms.md#popup): it lives in the tree with its `key` and the answer opens it
  (`ui: [{ open }]`), so it never shows the previous text.
- The `go.installPlugin` comes from the answer to the person's submit, which is exactly where it may come from
  ([`go.installPlugin`](screen-forms.md#go-install-plugin)).
- To try it in the kit without Kino Social:
  `node sdk/run.mjs --state '{"inputs":{"shareText":"hola"}}' . screenEvent sendShare --trigger submit`. Without
  `--provider` every call is `provider_missing` and `installed` is `false`, so you see the install path. Megaplay tests its
  `share.js` with a fake `kino.plugins.call` in `test/share.test.mjs`.

## Share cards { #cards }

!!! note "Available from Kino 0.9.84"
    Not published yet: this arrives with Kino 0.9.84. There is no new `apiVersion`: `go.plugin` and `openFrom` are
    `apiVersion` 20 and an older Kino drops or ignores them; `ctx` and `kino.image` simply do not exist on an older Kino (check
    before using them). Every number is in `contract.json` (`manifest.openFrom`, `manifest.screen.goPlugin`, `protocol.ctx`,
    `kinoImage`).

A plugin that shows other plugins' content (a wall of shared titles, a feed, a list) can carry a small card per item and let
the person open it in the plugin it came from, without knowing how that plugin lays out its pages. Four pieces fit together:

- **The sender** (the plugin that owns the content) puts its own address in the card: its `repo`, a `route` and `args` that
  mean something to it, and a `query` (usually the title) for when nothing else works.
- **The plugin that shows the cards** draws a button with [`go.plugin`](#go-plugin).
- **The target plugin** says in its manifest which of its screen routes may be opened from outside:
  [`openFrom.routes`](#open-from).
- A protocol **provider** knows who calls it through [`ctx.caller`](#ctx-caller), and whoever receives a picture's address
  shrinks it with [`kino.image.thumbnail`](#thumbnail).

**Kino Social will show these cards in a later version.** Until then, a plugin that wants to share uses the
[`share`](#social) call above. What you can do right away is declare `openFrom.routes`, so cards can open your content when
they arrive.

### `go.plugin`: opening another plugin's content { #go-plugin }

From `apiVersion` 20 (Kino 0.9.84): a button on your screen that opens another plugin's screen, or its search, from its GitHub
repository.

```js
{ type: "ElevatedButton", labelText: "Ver en Mi anime", labelTextEn: "Open in Mi anime", onPressed: { go: { plugin: {
  repo: "your-user/kino-plugin-anime", route: "detail", args: { id: "frieren" }, query: "Frieren" } } } }
```

| Field | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| `repo` | Required. A GitHub `owner/name`, with an optional sub-path (`owner/name/plugins/x`), at most 200 characters. A URL (anything with `://`) or an `@ref` drops the `go`, logged |
| `route` | Optional. A route as [`go.screen`](screen-forms.md#go-screen) takes (at most 64 characters) |
| `args` | Optional. A JSON object, within the same cap as `go.screen`'s `args` (4,096 bytes) |
| `query` | Optional. A text of at most 200 characters for the fallback search |

Any other field drops the `go`, logged. It comes only from **the person's own press or submit on your screen** (a tap, a
submit, the answer to one, a pop-up's button): from `open`, a timer, a change, a load-more, a pop-up's `onClose`, a panel or a
notice it is dropped, logged. Below `apiVersion` 20 too.

**What Kino does when the person presses the button, in this order:**

1. The plugin is **not installed**: Kino shows its install sheet (the same one as `go.installPlugin`) and, once the person
   installs it, continues with the steps below.
2. The plugin is **18+** and adults-only content is locked: nothing opens, and Kino shows its own locked-content toast.
3. The plugin is **off**: Kino asks «¿Activar?» and, if the person accepts, continues.
4. `route` is in the plugin's `openFrom.routes`: that screen opens with `args`.
5. Otherwise, if you sent a `query` and the plugin has a search: Kino's search opens scoped to that plugin, with that `query`.
6. Otherwise (no `query`, or no search): Kino opens the plugin's section, or its screen's default page.
7. If none of that is possible: Kino shows a toast.

A route the target does not list is never opened (step 5 or 6 happens instead), and the card cannot reach any other of its
screens.

### `openFrom.routes`: what of your plugin may be opened { #open-from }

```json
"openFrom": { "routes": ["detail"] }
```

- `apiVersion` 20 and the `screen` capability (counting one from `enhancements`). With `"apiVersion": 20` it sits at the top
  level; with a lower `apiVersion`, inside `enhancements["20"]` (an older Kino ignores it without refusing the plugin). At the
  top level below 20 it is refused: `The "openFrom" block needs apiVersion 20`.
- 1 to 16 different names, each 1 to 64 letters, digits or `. _ ~ -` (the same names a `go.screen` `route` takes). A bad list
  refuses the manifest with a message naming `openFrom.routes`.
- **It says what may be opened, not how.** You decide later, in your screen, how each route reaches its content. So an old
  card keeps working even if you change how your pages are laid out.

**How the target reads the route.** Your screen opens at that route: `screen({ route })` gets `route.name` (the route) and
`route.args` (the card's `args`), and the reserved `open` event comes with the same `route`, so you load what the `args` name
there:

```js
export async function screenEvent({ name, route }) {
  if (name === "open" && route && route.name === "detail") {
    const id = route.args && typeof route.args.id === "string" ? route.args.id : null;
    if (!id) return null;                                   // args from another plugin: always check them
    const detail = await loadDetail(id);                    // your own loader
    return { state: { detail } };
  }
  return null;
}
```

The `args` come from the card, that is, from another plugin: treat them as outside data. Check the type, the length and that
they name something of yours, and have a view for an id that no longer exists.

### `ctx.caller`: who calls your door { #ctx-caller }

From Kino 0.9.84, every `proto_` export of a [provider](protocol.md#exports) gets a second argument, `ctx`, that Kino fills in
and the consumer can neither send nor change. `ctx.caller` is the calling plugin:

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The calling plugin's id |
| `repo` | The address it was installed from, as Kino keeps it: `owner/name`, with `/path` for a plugin in a sub-folder and `@ref` for a pinned branch or tag (`owner/name/dir@v2`); `null` when it came from a manifest URL or a file |
| `name` | Its display name |
| `adult` | Whether it is 18+ (the same test as the 18+ lock) |

```js
export async function proto_wall_share(arg, ctx) {
  const caller = ctx && ctx.caller;   // a Kino before 0.9.84 sends no ctx
  // caller = { id: "my-game", repo: "me/my-game", name: "My game", adult: false }
  return { ok: true, from: caller ? caller.name : null };
}
```

- Treat `repo` as an opaque key, or compare only its `owner/name` part.
- **Before using `repo` in a `go.plugin`, cut the `@ref` off**: `go.plugin` drops a `repo` with an `@ref`.
  `repo.split("@")[0]` leaves `owner/name` or `owner/name/path`.
- A provider that declares only `(arg)` keeps working: JavaScript ignores the extra argument.
- In the kit, `node sdk/run.mjs --repo me/my-game <provider folder> proto <door>.<call>` tries a provider as that plugin;
  the kit passes the same `ctx`: the consumer folder's manifest `id` and `name`, `repo` from `--repo <owner/name>` or that
  folder's git origin (otherwise `null`), and `adult` from its `categories`.

### `kino.image.thumbnail`: a small picture from an address { #thumbnail }

```js
let thumb = null;
if (typeof kino.image === "object") {          // Kino 0.9.84+
  try { thumb = await kino.image.thumbnail(card.image, { maxWidth: 200, maxBytes: 16384 }); }
  catch (e) { /* not_image, too_large, network...: show the card without a picture */ }
}
// thumb is "data:image/jpeg;base64,…" (or null): small enough to send inside a message.
```

A sender passes only a picture's address; the plugin that receives it asks Kino for a thumbnail and gets it as a `data:`
address. A plugin's JavaScript cannot decode and re-encode an image (a library for it runs a 1 GB TV box out of memory), so
Kino does it natively: it downloads the picture, reads it with a sample size (never the whole bitmap), scales it down (never
up) to `maxWidth`, and writes a JPEG at quality 85, 75, 65, 55, then 45 until it fits `maxBytes`. A transparent picture goes
over white.

| | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | An `https` address (at most 2,048 characters). Anything else is `bad_request` |
| `maxWidth` | A whole number from 32 to 400; default 200 |
| `maxBytes` | A whole number from 2,048 to 32,768; default 16,384 |
| The answer | A string `"data:image/jpeg;base64,…"` |
| The download | Follows **your plugin's own network rules**, exactly those of `kino.fetch`: your `hosts` (or `fetchHosts: "any"` approved by the person), https only, never the home network, and your request budget (in a scheduled job, each call is one of the run's requests). At most 5 MB |
| Rate | At most 20 calls a minute per plugin |
| Where | Every export that may use Kino's services (as `kino.tmdb`), a provider's `proto_*` call and a scheduled job included; never `sign()` |

**Errors** (`e.code`): `bad_request` (not https, or the options are out of range), `host_not_allowed`, `not_found` (404/410),
`network`, `timeout` (the download), `too_large` (the download is over 5 MB, or the picture cannot get under `maxBytes`),
`not_image` (not a JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF that Android reads), `rate_limited`, `not_allowed` (from `sign()`). Show the card
without a picture on any of them.

No new `apiVersion`: check `typeof kino.image === "object"`. Kino's telemetry counts calls by outcome only, never an address.
Under the Node kit there is no image codec: `kino.image.thumbnail` downloads with your fetch rules and answers the bytes **only
when they already are** a JPEG (or PNG) within `maxWidth` and `maxBytes`; anything else throws `kit_unsupported` with a warning
that the Kino app does it. With `KINO_THUMBNAIL_FIXTURE=<file>` it answers that file as the thumbnail, so you can try your
plugin offline.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/identity/ (docs/identity.en.md) -->

# Identity: knowing who the person is without a sign-up { #identity }

!!! note "Available with Kino 0.9.77"
    `identity` is `apiVersion` 15 and arrives with Kino 0.9.77. An older version refuses these
    plugins with «Este plugin necesita una versión más nueva de Kino».

`identity` lets your plugin's server know **who the person is without asking for a username or a password**. It is a
**declarative** capability (you export nothing new), cannot stand alone (a [screen](screens.md) or a
[panel](player-panel.md) action uses it) and is not offered through [`enhancements`](enhancements.md): the plugin declares
`apiVersion` 15 itself.

!!! warning "Only plugins signed with Kino's own author key"
    `kino.identity.telegram` **answers only plugins signed with Kino's own author key** (`07DA-B67F-2ACF-B4D3`; a debug build
    of Kino answers any author, for development). The token works as a login for every server that trusts Kino's bot and its
    payload names the Telegram account, so a community plugin gets `permission_denied` whatever the person approved. If your
    plugin is not Kino's, it needs another way in; a per-plugin bot key would lift this restriction.

```json
"capabilities": ["screen", "identity"]
```

## The call { #call }

```js
const { id, token } = await kino.identity.telegram();
```

- **`id`** is a **pseudonym of the person for your plugin**: the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256 of
  `"kino-identity-v1\n" + yourPluginId + "\n" + telegramAccountId`. It is the same on every install and every device of the
  person and **different for every plugin**. You never receive the Telegram id or the username.
- **`token`** is the token Kino's bot signed for this device (`base64url(payload).base64url(Ed25519 signature)`). Your server
  verifies it with the bot's public key. It still names the Telegram account, so treat it as a credential: **never log or
  show it**.

## With a challenge: binding the session to this device and to your code { #challenge }

```js
const who = await kino.identity.telegram({ challenge }); // the nonce your server issued
// who = { id, token, deviceKey, signature, author, codeHash }
```

`challenge` is a nonce from your server: 16 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. With it, Kino also **signs**
(SHA256withECDSA, curve P-256, with a non-exportable key of its own for **your plugin on this install**, held in the Android
Keystore, created on first use and never synced or backed up) the UTF-8 bytes of:

```
"kino-identity-v2\n" + yourPluginId + "\n" + challenge + "\n" + author + "\n" + codeHash
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `deviceKey` | The public key (X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER), base64url without padding. |
| `signature` | The DER signature, base64url without padding. |
| `author` | The fingerprint of the author key Kino verified and pinned when your signed plugin was installed (for example `07DA-B67F-2ACF-B4D3`), or `""` for an unsigned plugin. |
| `codeHash` | The lowercase hex SHA-256 of the entry file Kino runs (the runtime refuses a script whose bytes differ). |

`author` and `codeHash` come from Kino's record of the installed plugin, **never from your code**. So your server can:

1. issue a one-use `challenge`;
2. verify the `token` with the bot's public key;
3. verify the `signature` with `deviceKey` over the bytes above;
4. **require its own fingerprint in `author`** (and, if it wants, a known `codeHash`): a modified copy of your plugin cannot
   log in;
5. bind the session to `deviceKey` and refuse a replayed token.

Keys are per plugin, so two plugins cannot match the person by key. A reinstall makes a new key.

## When you can call it { #when }

Only inside a call **the person started**: what a `screen`, a `screenEvent` or a `panelAction` runs. Never from a screen
timer's tick, a [background job](jobs-and-shared.md#jobs), Home, search, play or sync. At most **10 calls a minute** per
plugin.

## Errors { #errors }

`kino.identity.telegram` rejects with an error carrying one of these `code`s:

| `code` | When |
| --- | --- |
| `permission_denied` | The person did not approve it or switched it off, the plugin is disabled, the owner's switch, the call is not one of the allowed ones, or the plugin is not signed with Kino's key. |
| `not_available` | This device holds no token (the person must validate again in Kino) or the key could not sign. |
| `rate_limited` | More than 10 calls in a minute. |
| `bad_request` | Options that are not an object, an unknown key or a `challenge` that does not match the pattern. |

Detect it with `typeof kino.identity === "object"` and **still** catch the errors. Always keep another way in without it (or
say what is missing): the person can switch it off whenever they want.

## Consent { #consent }

The person reads, **in red**, on the install sheet and on the update that adds it (Kino never approves it on its own; in a kit
import it comes unticked):

- «Podrá saber tu usuario de Telegram y enviarlo a sus servicios» ("Can know your Telegram user and send it to its
  services").

And in your plugin's tab in Ajustes there is a switch, for the whole device and their synced devices: «Dejar que sepa mi
usuario de Telegram» ("Let it know my Telegram user").

## Testing with the kit { #kit }

The kit answers with a fake account:

| Variable | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `KINO_IDENTITY_TG=<id\|none>` | The fake Telegram account id; `none` simulates a device without a token (`not_available`). |
| `KINO_IDENTITY_TOKEN=<text>` | The token it returns. |
| `KINO_IDENTITY_AUTHOR=<fingerprint>` | The `author` it attests (empty by default: the kit verifies no author signature). |
| `KINO_IDENTITY_REVOKED=1` | The person switched it off (`permission_denied`). |

```
KINO_IDENTITY_TG=401234567 node sdk/run.mjs --device phone . screenEvent open
```

The kit applies the same gates as the app (the capability, the call being the person's, `bad_request`, 10 a minute) but
**not** the Kino author-key rule: in the kit it answers any plugin, so try it in the app, with a signed plugin, before you
depend on it.

The contract is in `contract.json` (`kinoIdentity`) and the types in `kino.d.ts`.

## Worked example: Kino Social { #example }

**Kino Social** (a Kino experiment: a feed to tell what you watch) is a screen plugin that logs in like this, asking for
nothing. It has a server of its own (the plugin holds no key: Kino signs everything):

```js
// 1. When the person opens the screen: the server's one-use challenge
const { challenge } = await post("/session/challenge", {});
// 2. Kino signs the challenge with this device's key and attests who is asking
const who = await kino.identity.telegram({ challenge });
// 3. The server verifies token, signature, author fingerprint and code hash, and answers with its own session
const body = await post("/session", {
  token: who.token, challenge, deviceKey: who.deviceKey, signature: who.signature,
  author: who.author || "", codeHash: who.codeHash || "",
});
kino.storage.set("session", body.session, { ttlMs: SESSION_TTL_MS }); // the session is the server's, not the token
```

If `kino.identity` does not exist or the call fails, the screen says it cannot sign in instead of breaking. The session is
the server's: the Telegram token is neither stored nor sent again.


<!-- page: https://kinotvapp.github.io/kino-plugins/en/sync-providers/ (docs/sync-providers.en.md) -->

# Sync providers (apiVersion 12, Kino 0.9.74) { #sync-providers }

A **sync provider** is a plugin that carries Kino's own sync between a person's devices through a
service you choose, instead of the local network. Kino does all the syncing work and hands your plugin
one encrypted file to store and give back: your plugin only moves bytes.

## What it is good for { #ideas }

From `"apiVersion": 12` (Kino 0.9.74), anything that can keep one file of up to 4 MiB behind a public
`https` API can carry a person's library, history, progress and settings:

- **Your own server or NAS**, through a public `https` address (a tunnel): `kino.fetch` never reaches the
  local network directly.
- **A cloud drive or storage service** with an `https` API and a long random token per person.
- **A chat bot of the person's own**, like [Sync-Gram](#examples): the copy is a pinned file in their
  private chat with the bot.
- **The person's own chat account**, like [Sync-Gram Cuenta](#examples): the copy is a pinned file in their
  Telegram Saved Messages, reached over a WebSocket (`socket`, apiVersion 13).
- **A private Git repository**, the copy kept as one file written through the host's API.
- **A Raspberry Pi at home** running a tiny server like [Sync Servidor](#examples), behind an `https`
  tunnel.
- **A company or school server** with a public `https` address that gives each person a token.
- **Sync without sharing a Wi-Fi**: devices in different places stay in step, as often as the person
  picks (every 1 to 60 minutes).

## How it talks to Kino { #how-it-works }

```text
 phone / TV (Kino)                     your plugin                    your service
 ─────────────────                     ───────────                    ────────────
 builds the snapshot, encrypts it ──▶  syncPush({ blob, expectedVersion }) ──▶ stores the bytes
 merges what it reads back       ◀──  syncPull() → { blob, version }     ◀── returns the bytes
```

1. Kino builds one snapshot of everything it already syncs (every profile this device syncs),
   compresses it and encrypts it as a whole (AES-256-GCM).
2. It calls your `syncPull()`: you return the stored copy as base64 with a `version` string of yours,
   or `null` when nothing is stored yet. Kino opens it, merges it with the device's own data and
   builds the new copy.
3. It calls your `syncPush({ blob, expectedVersion })`: you store the bytes as they are and return the
   new `version`. If your service can tell that another device stored a copy since
   `expectedVersion`, you throw `kino.error("conflict", …)` and Kino pulls, merges and pushes again.
4. That is all your code does. Kino never hands it a row or the key; but the key is derived from one
   of your plugin's own `password` settings (the required [`sync.keySecret`](#sync-block)), which your
   code can read, so **the plugin and its service can read the data** and the consent sheet says so
   in red ([who sees what](#who-sees-what)).

What Kino does for you, with no code of yours:

- **Scheduling**: when to pull and push, a debounce after changes, at most 60 rounds an hour, back-off
  after failures, and the person's own **"Sincronizar cada"** (1 to 60 minutes) on your provider's card.
- **Merging and conflicts**: the rows of both sides are merged (newest wins, deletions kept); a
  `conflict` you report is retried up to 3 times.
- **Profiles**: every profile the device syncs travels in the same copy.
- **Another device**: **"Enviar configuración"** ("Send settings") hands your settings to a second device,
  which shows **"Recibir configuración"** ("Receive settings"), by QR or a typed code, over the local network or a temporary Cloudflare tunnel ([provisioning](#provisioning)).
- **Settings and screens**: your settings form, the provider list with your card, its status line
  (from your optional `syncStatus`), and a "Sincronización ▸ Proveedor" button on your plugin's page.

## Build yours in 4 steps { #build }

The example talks to a server of yours at `https://sync.example.com` with two calls: `GET /blob`
answers `200 { "blob", "version" }` (or `404` when empty) and `PUT /blob` with `If-Match: <version>`
answers `200 { "version" }` (or `409` when the stored version is another one).

**1. The manifest** (`kino-plugin.json`):

```json
{
  "id": "my-sync",
  "name": "My Sync",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": 12,
  "entry": "plugin.js",
  "description": "Syncs your Kino devices through my server.",
  "author": "me",
  "hosts": ["sync.example.com"],
  "capabilities": ["syncProvider"],
  "settings": [
    { "key": "token", "label": "Token", "type": "password", "required": true,
      "hint": "The long random token your account page shows", "devices": ["phone"] }
  ],
```
